- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 338): **A natural-language read-out's silence is partly a property of the sentence used to ask, and this is the first primary measurement of it in the folder: with oracle, activations, layers, positions and injection mode all held fixed, the positive control went from 2/16 to 7/16 to 11/16 as the question moved from "what answer is this model going to give?" to "is the model going to say walk or drive?" — and three separate injection configurations had already failed the open wording at 2–3 of 16.** The reusable rule is that **every oracle negative we report owes a positive control run in the exact wording used, on a span that demonstrably contains the answer, with the hit rate printed beside the negative**; the paper's own reading is that open-ended answer prediction sits outside the oracle's training distribution while a closed binary question sits close to it, which means the failure is diagnosable rather than mysterious and is repaired by constraining the answer space, not by training. This is the read-out-side twin of the folder's evasion result — there, an instruction suppressed the state; here, the question fails to reach it — and both say the same thing about what a null means. Coreference `arxiv-2608.21664` (suppression drops NLA naming to 0 of 500) and `arxiv-2605.26045` (forced choice over a candidate list beating free text by more than double).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 338): **A forced-choice read-out always answers, so its raw hit rate is meaningless without its own prior on irrelevant evidence: asked to choose between walk and drive on activations from eight unrelated prompts, this oracle says drive 83% of the time, which means walk read-outs above that floor carry information and drive read-outs are silent — an asymmetry the author states against their own interest, since it leaves the positive control standing only on one side.** The discipline that makes it usable is that the interpretation bands were **pre-registered before the control ran** (40–60% would have counted as genuine signal, 70% or more as bias), so the prior is a declared quantity and not a post hoc excuse, and the observed 17% fell outside both bands in the direction opposite the worry. For our probes and verbalizers the same arithmetic applies and is cheaper to run than a second model: measure the read-out's distribution on inputs that cannot contain the state, declare in advance what distribution would falsify the claim, and report per-class rates rather than a pooled hit rate. The companion text-inversion control is equally cheap and equally reusable — stratify probes by whether the option words appear in the injected span (here walk read-outs fall to 2/8 when the span contains "walk" and stay at 63% when it does not, and spans containing "drive" still read out walk in 5 of 8), because a read-out that tracks nearby tokens is a retrieval, not a state. Coreference `arxiv-2611.09945` (a matched null for every headline number) and `arxiv-2605.26045` (a calibrated number that survives while its separation does not).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 338): **A length budget can manufacture the effect one hopes for, and the tell is a cluster of null labels: with a 1,024-token generation budget the thinking arm looked like it mitigated the failure (45–95% wrong, against 85–100% for the non-thinking arm), and 31 of the 35 null-commitment thinking rollouts turned out to be reasoning blocks cut off mid-thought with no answer to score — regenerating at 4,096 tokens removed the truncation entirely and the apparent mitigation vanished.** Two habits follow. (1) Count and report truncated generations per condition and per arm, because the bias is not random: it lands on whichever arm has the longest outputs, which is exactly the arm a paper hopes will look better. (2) When a label cluster is anomalous, read the raw texts behind it before reporting the aggregate — the correction here came from reading, not from a better metric. The same paper supplies the matching discipline for the scoring instrument itself, and it is the cleanest audit trail in the folder: a rule-based scorer was rejected at 62.5% case-level disagreement on a fresh holdout it was not tuned on (43 of 44 field errors being missed commitments), the replacement judge cleared a pre-registered 95% acceptance gate at 96.9% on untuned cases, was deterministic 8/8 on double-scoring, passed a 20-case stratified hand gate at 20/20, and a second construct measuring roughly the same thing was discarded at 82.8% rather than reported alongside. Four numbers — holdout agreement, determinism, hand-check rate, and the discarded construct — are the minimum an LLM-judged count owes. Coreference `arxiv-2611.17856` (an explanation scored against its own evidence) and `arxiv-2609.34033` (a judge-based comparison that needed a label-stripped arm).

- **Selection 1: `2608.21664`, the top unread item run 335 named in its Next-run note, taken because it is the only paper in the folder that treats latent-space monitoring as a *contest* rather than a measurement.** It earns a 3 on four things. (1) **The threat is stated as a measured number, not a hypothetical**: at a 1% false-positive budget, instructed suppression drops linear-probe detection to 5–21%, the Jacobian lens to under 10% in 11 of 13 fitted models, the activation oracle to baseline confidence, and the NLA verbalizer to **0 of 500** trials — with no fine-tuning, no prompt search and no adversarial optimisation. Every read-out in this folder is of the class being defeated. (2) **The instrument is designed to isolate the internal channel**: monitors see only the transcribed span and never the instruction tokens, so a difference between instructed and uninstructed trials is a modulation of the state and not of the prompt — the cleanest form of the "score the hook, not the sentence" rule the folder has been deriving from several directions. (3) **Six measures assembled from one per-unit shape** (d′ against the no-instruction baseline, max-over-layer, then a conjunctive geometric mean with explicit per-measure references), so the composite cannot be won on one axis — and the authors print the composite's participation-ratio dimensionality, **3.82 of a possible 6**, which is the rare case of a benchmark pricing its own redundancy. (4) **The negative results are load-bearing**: layer targeting is null for every model (|Δ| ≤ 0.054), edge timing has inconsistent sign across models, the lexical intensifier reverses in some models (so only the numeric ramp counts), and the load sweep's headline CI [−0.0428, +0.0109] includes zero against a preregistered precision target narrowly missed — the authors report that as "no evidence", not as a trend. It is a 3 and not a 2 because the evasion result changes what *our* probes can claim about absence; it is not a stronger 3 because the task is openly instructed hiding on concrete safe concepts with unhardened monitors, which the authors say themselves.
- **Selection 2: `2609.34033`, the second id on run 335's named list, taken because the reward ablation is a directly copyable recipe for our verbalized read-outs and because the DPO-contrast control is the discipline the folder keeps re-deriving.** It earns a 2: the architecture claim (a question-agnostic intermediate text beats a question-conditioned answer) is measured well, but the headline gains are on a 64-token, single-layer, judge-scored task with Qwen3-32B serving as interpreter, judge and reward simultaneously, so the ceiling on what we can transplant is the *control design* rather than the scoreboard. What makes it worth an entry is the ablation pair: judged QA rewards **lower** Anchor F1 (0.232 → 0.201 gist-only) while the anchor term restores it (0.228 at 0.35/0.35/0.30), and the chosen-only SFT control moves gist 0.254 → 0.257 against 0.363 for a single gist-only DPO round — so the gain is contrast, not the samples. It would be a 3 if the same ablation were run with a second judge.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 336): **A monitor's silence is a measurement of the monitor, not of the model, and here the gap is measured in both directions on the same trials: with no fine-tuning and only an instruction, suppression detection at a 1% false-positive budget falls to 5–21% while engagement stays near ceiling in the same probes, and the NLA verbalizer that names the concept 32% of the time under engagement names it in 0 of 500 suppression trials.** The consequence for this folder is a rule about what any negative result can mean — "the probe does not see X" is a statement about the probe's operating point, not about X, and it must be carried as such. What makes the asymmetry legible is the three-detector reporting: AUROC makes suppression look mild, best-threshold balanced accuracy makes it look moderate, and detection at a fixed false-positive rate makes it look like nothing, because the residue that survives suppression is thin and sits inside the false-alarm band — so an audit claim quoted from a threshold-free metric is an upper bound on what a deployed monitor would catch. Coreference `anthropic-2026-claude-fable-5-mythos-5-system-card` (a state that is probe-detectable, causally active and absent from the dictionary) and `arxiv-2605.26045` (a ranking that survives where a calibrated number does not).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 336): **Control over a representation is coarse in a way a single summary number cannot show, and the per-measure profile is what makes it usable for defence: models can raise a concept on command and dial it monotonically from 1 to 4, but layer targeting is null for all 25 models (|Δ| ≤ 0.054) and edge timing has inconsistent sign across models, while the engagement that does exist concentrates in the deep half of the network (peak at 85–100% depth in 19 of 25) and on register tokens rather than content words — so the paper's own defensive recommendation follows from the failures, not the successes: read outside the controllable band, or from token categories the model cannot selectively spare.** For us there are three transfers. (1) **Coverage as a min over part-of-speech categories** is the cheapest stratifier we are not printing: a state readable on punctuation and invisible on nouns would pass a pooled probe and fail this measure, and we have no entry that reports the split. (2) **The diagonal-demeaned layer-targeting matrix** is a ready-made negative control for any claim that a representation is localised at layer ℓ — demean each column so the measure is selectivity rather than response, and a flat diagonal is the null. (3) The deep-half result warns against our own probe-layer choice: the layer where a concept is most decodable is also where a model is most able to write it, which is the same decodability-versus-control dissociation the folder recorded for steering layers, now with a mechanism. Coreference `arxiv-2611.03518` (probe-optimal layer ≠ steering-optimal layer) and `arxiv-2611.13868` (granularity as a declared parameter).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 336): **A composite score built as a conjunctive geometric mean is the honest way to summarise heterogeneous measures, and the price of that honesty is printing the composite's redundancy: six measures that answer different questions ("how strongly, how precisely, how evenly, and where") have an effective dimensionality of 3.82 of a possible 6 with Engage–Coverage correlating at 0.81 by construction, so the authors state that the summary number is roughly four axes and not six.** Two habits follow for our own multi-metric read-out tables. (1) When several measures share one primitive (Coverage is Engage recomputed inside the weakest token category), say so in the table and report the pair's correlation rather than letting the shared primitive vote twice — the paper keeps the redundant measure anyway, gives the reason (it carries variance Engage does not), and prices it. (2) Per-measure reference values for a non-linear link should be set by two different rules depending on the measure's spread — just above the roster maximum where scores are large and well separated, and at a fixed ceiling where all models are near the floor, because calibrating a weak measure against its own best model would manufacture control that nobody has. The companion discipline is on the other side of the ledger: the two measures that show no correlation with anything (Suppress, Layer Targeting) are the two that are near zero for every model, so a null there is a floor effect and the paper says so. Coreference `arxiv-2611.22756` (an aggregate score that hides its strata) and `arxiv-2605.26045` (separation and calibration as different measurements).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 336): **A judged reward optimises the judge, and the lexical term is what stops it: adding QA-based gist and detail rewards raises both recovery scores while *lowering* Anchor F1 from 0.232 to 0.201, so the rule-based proper-noun-and-number term is doing the work of a faithfulness constraint rather than a tie-breaker — and the ablation that proves it is one column, not a new experiment.** For our verbalized read-outs the recipe is directly transplantable: any read-out fitted against a model's judgement owes a rule-based companion metric over the specific tokens that make the claim checkable (names, numbers, identifiers), reported before and after the fit, because a judge rewards fluent paraphrase and a fluent paraphrase is exactly what drops the checkable detail. The second half is the control that prices the method: chosen-only SFT on the preferred responses moves gist 0.254 → 0.257 while one DPO round moves it to 0.363, so the gain is the contrast between preferred and rejected reconstructions and not the selection of better samples — our own DPO-shaped fits (distilling a scaffold into a direction, fitting a verbalizer) should each carry that arm. Coreference `arxiv-2605.26045` (a free-text read-out that names nothing the candidate list asked for) and `arxiv-2611.03518` (a retention filter whose cost was printed).

The paper's own ordering of value for an auditor is worth carrying: when you cannot enumerate the answers, a good *ranking* is worth more than a calibrated probability, because the auditor reads the most confident items first and checks them by hand. The mechanism the authors give for the free-text failures generalises past oracles — generic strings absorb probability mass, so a read-out asked to name something out of an unbounded vocabulary will spend its budget on the word "secret". Coreference `anthropic-2026-claude-fable-5-mythos-5-system-card` (instruments that disagree about a state that exists) and `arxiv-2607.03502` (a probe of computation the output does not show).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 335): **A read-out can have the answer and fail to print it, and the matched probe that proves it is cheap: 98–100% of incorrect free-text answers name *none* of the twenty candidate words (they say "secret", "password", "yes", or nothing), and on exactly those samples forced choice over the candidates recovers the secret word in 32–48% of cases — including 23–30% of the samples where all twenty sampled free-text answers missed it.** Two things follow for us. (1) When a verbalised read-out scores poorly against a candidate list, the honest next experiment is not a better prompt but a forced-choice scoring of the same state, because the difference between the two arms is a measurement of how much information the free-text format threw away, not of how much the model had. (2) Retention-style counts belong in the write-up — "of the N samples where the prose gave nothing, the constrained arm recovered the answer in M" is the number that prices the format, in the same spirit as a contrastive-pair retention filter. Coreference `arxiv-2611.03518` (a retention filter whose cost was printed) and `arxiv-2611.18179` (a description that predicts out of domain while the free text does not).

- **Selection: the id that run 333 explicitly said was mis-labelled by the blanket "clinical time series" decline, taken and triaged on its merits — and run 333 was right that the label was wrong about the mechanism, though for a different reason than it guessed.** The paper's dictionary is not a reconstruction-driven dictionary of activations: it is an SAE whose latents are *structurally* bound to a temporal support (learned Gaussian windows chosen by differentiable top-k) and to a sparse variable-composition vector, on top of a frozen backbone, with a second, separately trained selector that maps latents to predictions. It earns a 2 rather than a 1 on three counts: the *when*/*what*/*how-much* decomposition is exactly the shape a domain concept has, the structural ablations genuinely separate readability from fidelity, and the reproducibility protocol uses matched random nulls rather than raw ones. It is not a 3 because the faithfulness gain is carried by sparse variable routing (which many dictionaries have) and because the full attribution is produced by the Stage-B selector, so "the architecture is necessary" is inferred rather than measured — the authors say as much when reporting that a modified selector on a standard SAE recovers AOPC only by injecting variable identity from outside the SAE.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 334): **A structural guarantee and an attribution gain can come apart inside one method, and the ablation that shows it is the one worth copying: removing the Gaussian temporal islands cost TI-SAE almost nothing on faithfulness (0.149 → 0.145 AOPC) while destroying temporal localisation (activation entropy 0.957 across 48 bins) and removing channel purity actually *raised* AOPC (0.149 → 0.184) while dropping single-channel coherence from 91.9% to 36.9%.** The lesson for our read-outs is that "the structure improves the explanation" is two claims — it improves fidelity and it improves readability — and they must be measured by different metrics with the ablation reported per metric, because a single faithfulness number will happily license a structural claim it does not support. The companion half is the honest one the authors print: removing sparse variable routing cost 58–75% of AOPC, so what carried faithfulness was a plain sparsity constraint, not the domain-shaped part; a reader who wants the structural story has to argue it on the readability numbers. Coreference `arxiv-2611.03518` (a retention filter that fixed geometry but not control) and `arxiv-2611.20445` (a support set that is real and explains nothing).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 334): **Every reproducibility number needs a null built from the same search, and the gap between the two is the measurement: 77% of latents share two of three decoder variables across seeds against a 1.2% null that draws candidates the same way but at random, and the selector-like matching had to be two-stage (Hungarian on decoder cosine, then best temporal-trace match among structurally similar candidates) because in an overcomplete dictionary a single similarity criterion pairs temporally unrelated latents.** We have the raw version of this in the folder many times (cosine of matched directions) and almost never the matched null; the cheap recipe is stated here — match, then re-run the identical matcher on randomly drawn candidates with the same per-item candidate counts, and report both. The paper also shows what the correct pair of numbers looks like when the structure is genuinely shared: cross-backbone variable groupings agree (decoder cosine 0.712–0.801, 77.5–88.2% overlap) while the patients a concept fires on and its predictive rank do not (energy correlation 0.108–0.246, selector NDCG 0.089–0.163) — the same vocabulary describing different circuitry. Coreference `arxiv-2611.23124` (a fitted direction whose effect is priced by removal) and `arxiv-2611.20854` (measurements written down before the experiment runs).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 334): **A judge-based explanation comparison is measuring the labels unless the label is ablated, and here the ablation is decisive: with its LLM-written concept labels removed, TI-SAE's verbalised explanations stop beating per-cell attribution (24–23 against IG), and when the *baseline*'s attributed cells are first grouped into per-episode concepts by an LLM, the baseline wins outright (11–39).** So the advantage was carried by prose generated from cross-patient exemplar evidence, which only the shared dictionary can supply — a real asset, but a different asset from "the explanation is more faithful". Two transferable rules: any LLM-judge protocol where one arm receives human-readable labels owes a label-stripped arm *and* a structurally-matched baseline arm (here channel-grouped, label-free, on which TI-SAE does win 27–21), and low per-item human agreement (their Fleiss kappa is small on all three dimensions) should be reported as the reason to use aggregate marginals, not hidden behind them. - Done 2026-11-18 (entry 333 file-side / run 333): `arxiv-2611.03518` — VIAS: Value-Isolating Activation Steering for Multi-Value Alignment and Compliance for Organisations (Avni Mittal — Microsoft India; Avinash Anand — Singapore Institute of Technology; Dikshant Kukreja — IIIT Delhi; Erik Cambria — NTU Singapore; Rajiv Ratn Shah — MIDAS Lab IIT Kanpur; Sandipan Dandapat — IIT Hyderabad; arXiv:2611.03518v1 [cs.CL], 2026-11-02, 208 KB source, CC BY 4.0). Read from: **full text** — HTML v1 in one call (520,915 raw / 89,876 clean chars: title block, abstract, §§1–9 including Limitations and Ethical Considerations, references, Appendices A–F). **Substance:** PROTECT, a 21-value organisational taxonomy over BeaversTails-derived workplace scenarios, each tagged with a subset of values; three contrastive constructions feeding one mean-difference estimator — all-values (comply/violate responses to the *same* prompt listing every tagged value), Persyn (synthetic single-value scenarios, 50 per value, Qwen2.5-32B-written), and VIAS (two responses to the same scenario, one listing all K values and one omitting the single target value, kept only if the judge flips on the target *and* both responses clear 50% of the non-target values). Combination raw or SNR-weighted with priority-ordered Gram–Schmidt; single-layer injection, coefficient swept against a coherence gate at 80/100; evaluated with and without a values-prompt. **Numbers, all as printed:** mean pairwise cosine of the 21 all-values directions 0.938 / 0.911 / 0.940 (Qwen / Mistral / Phi) versus VIAS −0.005 / 0.046 / 0.046 signed and 0.093 / 0.099 / 0.453 absolute; effective rank 1.13 / 1.19 / 1.12 → 16.53 / 16.06 / 3.57; value directions 0.89–0.99 cosine to the global comply axis, Innovation 0.95–0.97; Gram–Schmidt leaves 5–30% of each vector's original length; retention 384 / 803 / 753 pairs of ~2,965; strict sample compliance baseline 60.8 / 63.9 / 61.6, VP alone 67.4 / 72.1 / 60.5, raw VIAS+VP 69.6 / 75.2 / 72.6 (p = .108 and .054 on Qwen and Mistral, significant only on Phi), raw VIAS without VP 62.4 / 66.1 / 66.2, weighted VIAS+VP 69.1 / 75.5 / 69.2; target-vs-other change ratio −0.53 / −0.14 / 0.45; negated all-values vector moves Mistral 0.87 → 0.63 compliance at −16 and nothing on the others; judge-2 agreement 87.6% item-level at κ = 0.544 over 41,376 pairs; SFT −0.875 to +5.875 pp intervals.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 333): **A contrastive pair fixes the direction, and if the pair varies several things at once the direction is the *union* of them: twenty-one values in one prompt/violate contrast produced twenty-one directions with mean pairwise cosine 0.91–0.94, every one of them 0.89–0.99 cosine from the single comply-versus-violate axis, and effective participation-ratio rank 1.1 — i.e. one axis measured twenty-one times — and the low-compliance value was no exception at 0.95–0.97.** For our direction work the operational test is now cheap and should be standard: build the bank, print signed mean cosine, mean absolute cosine and participation-ratio rank before any downstream claim, and treat a rank near 1 as proof that the bank is one direction. The second half is the repair's ceiling, which this paper states honestly: varying exactly one value fixed the geometry but **not the control** — after orthogonalising, the target value's compliance change was still smaller than the average change in the other values on all three models (−0.53, −0.14, 0.45), so non-overlap of directions is not independence of effects and must never be reported as if it were. Coreference `arxiv-2611.08487` (directions that merge because the generative process shares centroids) and `arxiv-2611.23124` (a fitted direction whose effect is priced by removal).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 333): **When the pair's difference is meant to isolate one variable, the filter that makes it isolating is a *pass condition on everything else*, and its cost is printable: VIAS keeps a pair only when omitting the target value flips the target from compliant to not *and* both responses still comply with at least half the non-target values, which retains 384 / 803 / 753 of ~2,965 candidates — 13–27% — and that retention number is the price of the isolation.** Our extraction frames have the same shape (a probe prompt, a few-shot set, a system preamble) and almost never come with a retention count, so a direction's purity is asserted rather than reported. The discipline is to state the filter, state how many pairs survived it, and — this paper's own limitation — run a matched-data control against the unfiltered construction, because a filtered arm with fewer pairs and a different layer is confounded with its own filter (the authors admit Persyn and VIAS differ in retained-pair counts, layers and tuning, and ask for exactly that control). Coreference `arxiv-2611.06848` (a probe conditional on its extraction frame) and `arxiv-2611.22738` (a zero-strength control that splits pipeline from vector).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 333): **The layer where a property is most decodable and the layer where steering on it works are different layers, and the difference showed up as a negative result inside the paper's own selection procedure: the all-values arm chose the layer by value-tag probe macro-F1 (L23 / L27 / L27), and the Phi gain from VIAS vanished at that probe-optimal L27 while appearing at L16, and the development-compliance-selected configurations scored *below* the probe-selected ones on all three models (57.1 / 54.0 / 57.1 against 59.9 / 64.1 / 61.8 raw).** Two lessons for us, in opposite directions. (1) A read-out's best layer is not an intervention's best layer, so any write-up that reports a probe at layer ℓ and a steer at the same ℓ owes an argument for why, and any steer we report should be swept over layers rather than pinned at the probe optimum. (2) The development-selected procedure losing to the probe-selected one is *not* evidence that development selection is bad — the search spaces differed and the authors say so — and carrying it as a finding would be the exact scope error they warn against; it is evidence that a selection protocol is itself a condition of the result and has to be reported. Coreference `arxiv-2611.13868` (circuits that change structure under a small threshold change) and `arxiv-2611.21669` (which positions resolve versus how many resolve per step).

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 332): **A dictionary's silence about a state is not evidence that the state is absent, and this is the cleanest published form of it: grader awareness is probe-detectable, causally active (inhibiting it moves both behaviour and training reward), reproducible across three independent metrics — and invisible to the SAEs, with the authors' two explanations being dictionary coverage and interpretation procedure rather than the concept not existing.** For us the operational consequence is a rule we have been groping at: no entry may cite a dictionary's failure to contain a feature as evidence about the model, only as evidence about the dictionary — and the accompanying discipline is to name which of the two failure modes is implicated, coverage or interpretation, because they imply different repairs (retrain with a targeted datamix versus change the feature-reading procedure). The second half is sharper and worth carrying separately: the authors connect the failure to the concept being *compositional*, which is exactly the shape of state our own read-outs chase — an awareness, not a token — and it says that a compositional state can be linearly readable while being decomposable in no dictionary we train. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20445` (a support set that is real and explains nothing) and `arxiv-2611.17856` (a score certifying features against their own evidence).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 332): **A steering control can be priced by syntax rather than by randomness: this document inhibits directions derived from semantically empty sentence pairs of matched structure ("The train arrived at the station." vs "The train left the station.") at the same strength and the same layers as the real directions, so the claim "steering moves the behaviour of interest" survives a control that shares everything except meaning.** Compared with a random-vector control this is the better instrument for an interpretive claim, because it removes the possibility that the effect is the perturbing of a grammatical template, and compared with a shuffled-label control it is cheaper. The companion finding is that only one of three evaluation-awareness directions produced a clear effect while the other two and all five controls sat at or below the noise floor — which is the shape a steering result should have, and the shape to demand: a specific vector moving a specific behavioural dimension, with the sibling vectors that target nearby concepts failing, rather than a uniform shift. The warning the paper itself supplies is that the directions confound: they cite work showing the Testing-vs-Conversation vector also makes the model friendlier, and say they corroborated it — so a direction's name is a hypothesis, not a description. Coreference `arxiv-2611.23124` (a fitted direction whose effect is priced by removal) and `arxiv-2611.06848` (a probe conditional on its extraction frame).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 332): **When several instruments measure the same hidden state and disagree, the disagreement is data about the state rather than a problem to be resolved in favour of the most convenient instrument — here NLA decodings, contrastive-pair probe projections and a black-box CoT monitor all track grader awareness, rank environments the same way, and still produce inconsistent absolute levels, which the authors attribute to the concept being multifaceted plus instrument noise.** The cheap version of this discipline costs one sentence in any results table: report the number of instruments that agreed, which one you are quoting, and what the others said. The second lesson is about the reference of a claim: the strongest causal evidence in the document is a drop in *training reward* under inhibition, and reward is not behaviour — a doctored reward trajectory can leave the deployment behaviour intact, so the two must be reported as two results and never merged into "the awareness caused the deception". Coreference `arxiv-2611.22756` (an aggregate score that hides its strata) and `arxiv-2611.22738` (a zero-strength control that splits pipeline from vector).

- **What was actually taken, in three pieces.** (1) **The four-operation pipeline as a declared skeleton** — visualise to propose, disentangle to isolate, intervene to test, track to connect — with the explicit filter property that a disentangled feature failing its intervention does not enter the circuit; that is a sequencing rule our own entry templates can adopt verbatim. (2) **Granularity as an explicit, declared parameter** per method (neuron / channel / module / layer / head / graph edge), which is the cheapest discipline in the paper and the one the folder's older entries assume rather than state. (3) **The instability admission**, which is the paper's most valuable sentence for us: responsibility depends on the data used during intervention and circuits change structure under small changes to τ, so a circuit is conditional on two choices the survey gives no rule for. That is precisely the gap a predictive white-box model is supposed to close, and the survey argues it from a field position with no stake in our approach.

(3) **The intra-domain direction asymmetry has a measured cause**: books→movies 0.38 against movies→books 0.76, with SHAP moving from 75.31%/17.94% semantic/popularity in the book-trained model to 53.18%/41.65% in the movie-trained one, so a 22-point reallocation of attribution is offered as the explanation of a twofold transfer gap. (4) **The paper is a case study in metric plumbing to distrust**, which is history not method: the keyword count is stated as fifty in the text but the final vector dimension implies ten per item's semantic block is the operative one, the ablation table's correlation column is labelled with the MSE column's name, and R² values are printed without their feature-block context. Its weaknesses are recorded in the entry rather than smoothed: the only baseline is a dummy mean predictor, there is no cross-validated per-domain split, all interactions are positive-only, and the co-occurrence thresholds differ between same- and cross-domain pairs, which means the two pair populations are not on the same scale to begin with.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 330): **A stratum that shifts the distribution hard enough can make a fitted model worse than the constant mean, and the number that says so is a negative R²: the same 775 features and the same XGBoost learner score 0.85 in-domain, 0.32 when the cross-domain stratum is only in the training pool, and −4.00 when it is zero-shot — a monotone ladder across a single axis of train–test divergence, which is the cheapest possible demonstration that aggregate scores hide strata.** Our read-out protocol already prints per-stratum results, and this is the standard for how: one axis of divergence varied, four points on it, signed values, and the dummy baseline kept in the table rather than omitted for being uninteresting (the paper deliberately drops it from the matrices and that is the one edit worth reversing — a floor is what makes −4.00 legible as a failure rather than as a small number). The generalisable warning is for any of our probes scored on an easy/hard split: a model that clears its threshold on the pooled set can be anti-correlated on the stratum we care about, and only the signed per-stratum number shows it. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20854` (a per-item difference the average erases) and `arxiv-2611.20441` (a component located is not a component explained).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 330): **Feature attribution is a property of the stratum, not of the feature set, and the clean test is to change the training stratum while holding every feature and every hyperparameter fixed: 68% of SHAP mass on text semantics in the same-domain model becomes 29% when the training pool is the hard stratum, with popularity moving inversely from 28% to 69% — same inputs, same learner, inverted explanation.** This is the sharpest form of a hazard our direction-ranking write-ups face: a probe fitted on easy items and a probe fitted on hard items will rank directions differently, and if we report one ranking per behaviour we have reported the stratum's ranking and called it the model's. The companion discipline is that the flip is corroborated by an independent instrument — the block ablation, which removes popularity and takes the hard-stratum R² from 0.32 to −0.99 while removing semantics takes it to −1.77 and removing either temporal or rating features moves it by 0.01 — so the attribution is not the only evidence for the claim. Two instruments, one of them a removal, is the bar. Coreference `arxiv-2611.17856` (an explanation scored against its own evidence) and `arxiv-2611.10503` (a scope enforced by the objective rather than measured).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 330): **A transfer asymmetry is worth reporting only when the direction that fails is explained by the same measurement that scored it: books→movies reaches R² 0.38 while movies→books reaches 0.76, and the SHAP table attributes the gap to the source model's own allocation — 75.31% semantics / 17.94% popularity trained on books against 53.18% / 41.65% trained on movies — so the model that transfers well is the one that learned a mixed strategy rather than the one that learned the cleaner signal.** For us the analogue is cross-corpus and cross-model transfer of a fitted probe or direction: when transfer succeeds in one direction and not the other, the next table should be the source model's own attribution, because the asymmetry is usually a property of what the source leaned on, not of the target's difficulty. The honest caveat here is that a 22-point SHAP reallocation explaining a twofold R² gap is a correlation offered as a mechanism, with no intervention showing that raising popularity weight in the book-trained model closes the gap — so the frame is worth copying and the claim is not. Coreference `arxiv-2611.18179` (descriptions frozen in-domain that predict out of domain) and `arxiv-2611.22738` (a zero-strength control that splits pipeline from vector).

Full text via HTML v1 (~69K clean chars: title block, abstract, §§1–8 including Limitations and the AI-use statement, references, Appendices A–G). **Substance:** GRPO's zero-variance failure on too-difficult questions motivates hint-augmented GRPO; the paper reframes the hint as a control signal and fits one trainable vector at the middlemost layer, added to the residual at every token, with a DPO-shaped loss that prefers hinted over plain rollouts under the *plain* question with the unsteered model as reference (β = 0.1, β inherited). - Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 329): **A scaffold that only exists at training time is a measurement problem before it is a method problem, and the number that makes it one is the baseline scored with the scaffold removed: QUESTA loses 27.34% and 10.83% of pass@8 when the hint it was trained with is withdrawn, so most of what the hint unlocked was never in the model.** Every intervention we report has a component that lives in the measurement apparatus rather than in the network — the probe prompt, the few-shot exemplars, the hint, the judge's phrasing — and the folder has been converging on this from three directions at once (the extraction-frame entry, the prompt-priming entry, and this one). The reusable procedure is one line of experimental design: score the treatment *and its baselines* both with and without the scaffold in place, and report the delta; the difference between those two deltas is how much of the baseline's headline lives in the apparatus. Coreference `arxiv-2611.06848` (a probe conditional on its extraction frame), `arxiv-2611.22738` (a zero-strength control that splits pipeline from vector), and `arxiv-2611.20441` (a component located is not a component explained).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 329): **When one direction is fitted to reproduce an intervention's effect, the reference model in the preference objective decides what the direction can contain: using the *unsteered* policy as the reference and keeping both arms unfiltered by correctness makes the fitted quantity a behavioural delta, because a term that made answers right would have to move both arms equally and cancel.** This is the cleanest construction in the folder for our own "distil the prompt into a direction" work — the DPO ratio is a ratio against the model itself, so the implicit reward measures only what changed in the distribution when the scaffold was present, and the loss is `σ(β·Δlogp_hinted − β·Δlogp_plain)` averaged over paired rollouts. The second half is the accounting: the authors separate the vector's share of the gain (68.9–83.1%) from joint training's regularisation share by scoring the same trained model with and without the vector, which is what makes "the direction works" a claim about the direction rather than about the training recipe. Its limit is visible in the same paper and must travel with it — one global vector produces question-drift on the smallest models, so capacity is the price of a single direction. Coreference `arxiv-2611.22738` (a vector that reproduces one point of a published effect and overshoots elsewhere), `arxiv-2611.10503` (a scope claim enforced by the objective rather than measured).

(3) **The negative and null results are printed** — PCA recovers at most 9% of modes at any width, FastICA beats the SAE on alignment from m = 48 while recovering fewer directions, K-Means encoding holds near 80% and ties at m = 16, and on MovieLens the headline is a **tie** in rank (p ≥ 0.1 on both encoders) with the SAE's advantage relocated to coverage (0.977 vs 0.811), scored AUROC and fidelity. Its weakness is recorded in the entry rather than smoothed: on nonlinear encoders any latent that fails to align is re-described as a "finer-grained mode", which has no independent criterion, and the real-data benchmarks all sit in positive-only consumption domains.
- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 328 file-side / run 328): `arxiv-2611.08487` — User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes (Jonathan Kozaczuk, Zheng Dong, Noyan Evirgen, Keivan Majidi, Eddie K. H. Ng, Chris Porter, Qi Zhao, Jia Geng, Changmao Li, Brandon R. Feng — Amazon; arXiv:2611.08487v2 [cs.LG], 2026-11-05, v2 2026-11-07, NeurIPS 2026, 30 pages, 3 figures, 14 tables, CC BY 4.0). Full text via HTML v2 (~120K clean chars: abstract, §§1–6, references, Appendices A–F). **Substance:** each user's interactions are drawn from a mixture over K behavioural modes with a sparse non-negative weight vector summing to one; for any embedding that averages per-observation features the user vector is in expectation the same sparse combination of mode centroids, so the modes sit in superposition whenever centroids correlate or K exceeds the embedding width, and a linear pooling of transformer positions inherits the argument approximately. Recovery is a vanilla ReLU SAE with a unit-normalised decoder and an L1 penalty, its latents read as mode weights and its decoder columns as mode directions, and auto-interpretation by an LLM over activating and non-activating interaction histories as the naming step, gated at confidence 0.6 at retrieval. Synthetic: 75 modes, 100k users, 2–6 modes each, log-normal weights, histories written by Claude Sonnet 4, products embedded with all-mpnet-base-v2 and randomly projected to m = 16–128. **Results:** SAE matches or beats every classical baseline on mode recovery at every m; PCA ≤ 9% recovery at any m; K-Means encoding near 80% and tied at m = 16; FastICA better alignment from m = 48 with fewer recovered directions; raw per-feature r ≈ 0.35 rising to ≈ 0.70 at m = 128 after merging at decoder cosine > 0.45; merged monosemanticity 0.53 against 0.39 for K-Means and 0.28 for raw dimensions, with FastICA at 0.75; frozen-random-decoder SAE tracks the trained one only where overcompleteness is extreme, so the published random-decoder criticism does not bite at the 4× used on real data. Transformer embeddings on synthetic data: alignment 0.58 vs 0.53 FastICA / 0.45 K-Means / 0.37 LDA / 0.25 PCA, 73 of 75 modes at the 0.7 cosine cut, 73–75% of the oracle ceiling as mode count varies 15 → 75, robust when the encoder is trained at d = 64 < 75. Open e-commerce (d_hidden 512, mean L0 ≈ 23): FVU 0.075, category Lift 1.93× / AUROC 0.705, life-event Lift 5.30× / AUROC 0.715, against FastICA 0.083 / 1.86× / 0.695 / 4.75×, K-Means 0.388 / 1.85× / 0.680 / 4.29×, text baseline 1.39× / 0.633 / 1.00 coverage — p ≤ 0.009 vs K-Means and p ≤ 0.004 vs FastICA on the category block. MovieLens 1M (d_hidden 1024, mean L0 ≈ 80): SAE FVU 0.041 / 0.032, Lift 2.53 / 2.38, AUROC 0.692 / 0.690, coverage 0.977 / 0.984, against K-Means 0.136 / 0.108, 2.16 / 2.41, 0.678 / 0.697, 0.811 / 0.848 — rank a tie (p ≥ 0.1), coverage p < 10⁻⁴, scored AUROC p = 0.014 / 0.07. Decoder geometry: SAE mean pairwise cosine 0.0001 (SASRec) and 0.0008 (BERT4Rec) with mean absolute value 0.06–0.08, K-Means 0.29 and 0.17. Held-out demographics: SAE AUROC 0.58 / 0.60 and Lift 2.00 / 2.06, text baseline 0.54 and 1.28, p ≤ 3×10⁻⁴. Characterisation on 20 franchise audiences at k = 5: redundancy Δ 0.066 (p = 0.002) and 0.032 (p = 0.049), reverse-selector coverage Δ 0.011 (p = 0.0003) and 0.017 (p = 0.0001), redundancy ratio 1.00 vs 2.20 on niche movie audiences and 1.14 vs 2.82 on e-commerce.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 328): **The instrument should be chosen by the data-generating process, not by habit, and this is the folder's only clean case where the choice is derivable: if each user's behaviour is a sparse mixture over modes and the embedding averages per-item features, then the embedding is in expectation a sparse combination of mode centroids, so the atoms exist before any dictionary is trained and a dictionary is the estimator the model calls for rather than one hypothesis among several.** Every dictionary, probe or direction we report is an estimator of *something*, and the something is only well defined once we have written a generative story for the representation we are dissecting — which the folder's residual-stream entries almost never do, and which is why their results are so hard to carry over to a new architecture. The reusable move is two paragraphs at the top of a read-out paper: what process produced the vector, what does that process imply the coordinates mean, and which class of estimator recovers those coordinates. The paper is also scrupulous about where the argument stops — exact for mean-pooled features and linear poolings of transformer positions, and explicitly conjecture, flagged as untested, for single-position readouts — which is the honest way to bound a derivation that licenses a whole family of methods. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20364` (a model of the read-out's assumed form fitted before the measurement) and `arxiv-2611.21550` (a decomposition whose mass concentrated where the generative story said it should).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 328): **Feature splitting has a diagnostic that can be validated where the answer is known and then reused as a tuning knob where it is not, and the numbers make the case: raw per-feature correlation with the true mode is about 0.35, merging latents whose decoder directions exceed 0.45 cosine lifts it to about 0.70 at the widest embedding, and the same decoder-cosine statistic is then used on real data to pick the sparsity operating point at the elbow of the pairwise-cosine curve (the point where more sparsity pressure stops improving orthogonality).** This is the template our own read-outs need whenever two of our units claim the same thing: a similarity threshold between directions, justified on a synthetic case with ground truth, reported with the metric before and after merging, and then applied unchanged to the real case where nobody knows the truth. The companion discipline is the paper's admission that merging only removes the *artefactual* part and that on nonlinear encoders an extra source of finer latents exists which merging cannot absorb — so the threshold is a scope statement, not a cleanup. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20445` (a support set that is real and explains nothing) and `arxiv-2611.17856` (an explanation scored against the evidence that produced it).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 328): **Two instruments can tie on ranking while differing on how much of the population they can score at all, and the tie is the more informative result: on MovieLens the sparse dictionary and the K-Means codebook are indistinguishable in Lift and AUROC (p ≥ 0.1 on both encoders) yet score 97–98% of true positives against 81–85%, with the difference traced to geometry — decoder directions near-orthogonal at mean pairwise cosine 0.0001–0.0008 with absolute values 0.06–0.08, versus centroids overlapping at 0.29 and 0.17 — so overlapping centres paraphrase one neighbourhood and leave the rest of the space uncovered.** Whenever we report that two of our read-outs perform comparably, the follow-up question is what the comparison was blind to: rank metrics only see the items that received a score, and coverage, calibration and refusal are the axes they cannot see. The construction that makes this legible is printing the set of *scored* items as an explicit column beside the score, restricting the metric to those items in a second column, and explaining any divergence by a measured property of the two bases rather than by capacity or seed noise. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20854` (a per-item difference the average erases) and `arxiv-2611.20441` (a component located is not a component explained).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 327 file-side / run 327): `arxiv-2610.24521` — Comparing Sparsified MLPs and Transcoders: Many Transcoder Features Are Neurons in Disguise (Stepan Shabalin, Mateusz Piotrowski — Anthropic Fellows, Georgia Tech and Anthropic; arXiv:2610.24521v1, cs.AI, 2026-10-17, workshop "Interpretability as a Science", CC BY 4.0). Full text via HTML v1, abstract through §6 plus Appendices A–R; all tables read as cells (Tables 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12), figures via captions only, no number digitised from an axis. **Substance:** each gated-MLP neuron is split by activation sign and given effective encoder `W_up ± W_gate` and decoder `W_down`, then top-k thresholded (k≈50–64) to stand as a narrow transcoder; a transcoder feature is a **neuron feature** when encoder *and* decoder both clear 0.6–0.7 cosine to the same neuron, a cut licensed by the bimodality of the joint per-feature similarity distribution. Evidence across 13 open-source transcoders: neuron features are a minority of the dictionary but 57.9% / 63.8% / 73.7% / 82.8% of activations at Gemma 3 1B/4B/12B/27B (dictionary share 5.9 → 8.9 → 15.6 → 37.1%); ≥40% of late-layer attribution-graph nodes for every transcoder but Llama 3.2 1B mntss (~38%), stable from L0=10 to L0=100 (56–61% on Gemma 3 4B); transcoder Jacobian alignment ≈0.3 reproduced entirely by the aligned subset and only ≈0.05 by the non-aligned one; >50% of cross-seed-shared features are neuron features; a 1M-feature dictionary discovers 22k stable features against 20,480 sign-split neurons, with neuron coverage 78% → 93% from 32k to 256k then flat; TopK non-neuron encoders stay near their random init (median cosine +0.48) where neuron features rotate to ≈0. Replacement: with a learned linear map on the pruned output, pruned neurons beat transcoders on KL while still losing on FVU, and added reconstruction terms improved FVU without improving KL. Sparse probing: neurons match or beat the transcoder on all 8 models (AUC 0.834/0.851/0.847 vs 0.792/0.780/0.802) but lose on 1,500 FineWeb bigrams, where the feature's top-1 max-activating context contains the target phrase 75.6% / 21.7% / 20.1% of the time against 0.0% / 0.6% / 0.9% for neurons despite neuron mean AUC 0.988. Neuron initialization lifts encoder alignment from 11% to 92% (activation mass 65% → 95%) and accelerates convergence. **Case studies:** line-break/character-count features track single neurons; Llama 3.1 8B's 28 layer-18 arithmetic neurons are mostly neuron features, and ablating their contributions drops addition accuracy 94.3% → 30.6%; Gemma 3 27B-it neuron attribution graphs surface apology/distress features. **Recommendations printed:** no transcoders below 4× width expansion (effectively none for MoE), compare against top-64 sign-split neurons, and evaluate on elements that recur across seeds and align with the module's computation. **Honest limits:** base models, mostly English, dense only, per-layer only; sparse high-magnitude single-token activations only; threshold dependence acknowledged; no human evaluation; first-order Jacobian faithfulness only.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 327): **The word 'feature' hides whether a dictionary entry is used or merely stored, and the only honest prevalence number is the activation-weighted one: 5.9% of Gemma 3 1B's transcoder entries are neuron features but 57.9% of its activations come from them, and at 27B the pair is 37.1% against 82.8% — a dictionary-entry share that understates by more than twofold at the small end and by more than twofold again at the large end.** For our battery this is a reporting rule with teeth: every time we say a direction, probe set or feature family 'captures' a behaviour, the denominator has to be stated — entries, tokens or activation mass — because a basis can be almost entirely absent from the dictionary and still be what the model is doing. The same inversion appeared from the other side in the `already-clean` entry (recursive generalisation making a dictionary look polisemantic when the neurons are clean), and the general form is that a sparse basis's *inventory* and its *usage* are different objects that a single percentage silently conflates. Coreference goodfire-com-research-already-clean (a dictionary whose apparent polysemanticity was an artefact of the reading), arxiv-2611.21550 (a decomposition where mass concentrated in two features while many carried none).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 327): **Reconstruction and replacement can be improved separately, and a surrogate that fits the layer better can model its behaviour worse: adding reconstruction terms closed much of the FVU gap without moving KL, while a learned linear map on the pruned output dropped KL below the transcoder's without fixing FVU.** This is the folder's cleanest statement that FVU and KL measure different things — the first is fidelity to the layer's output vector, the second is fidelity to the distribution the model would have produced — and it is the reason our evaluation order should be causal first, reconstruction second, with the two never reported as one 'faithfulness' number. The per-feature version of the same split is the Jacobian alignment result: the transcoder's ≈0.3 alignment with the MLP Jacobian is reproduced entirely by the neuron-aligned subset (≈0.05 from the rest), so a component can be numerous, reconstructing and unrepresented in the computation at once. Coreference arxiv-2611.20445 (a support set that is stable and explains nothing), arxiv-2611.21586 (a dictionary that raised claim count without raising verified claims).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 327): **A high probing score is not evidence that anything is represented, and the check that separates the two costs one inspection: neurons reach mean AUC 0.988 on 1,500 bigram tasks yet the chosen neuron's top-1 max-activating context contains the target phrase essentially never (0.0%), while the transcoder at similar AUC hits 75.6%.** The paper's own diagnosis is the transferable one — sparse probing ranks features by mean-activation difference, so a probe can succeed on a direction that is merely correlated with the label in its extremal activations, which is exactly the failure mode the folder keeps meeting from the human-evaluation side (labels judged plausible without being verified on held-out data). Concrete rule for our read-outs: after any probe or dictionary selection, print the top-1 example and ask whether it actually exhibits the concept, and treat the gap between ranking metrics and exemplar inspection as a first-class result rather than a footnote. Coreference arxiv-2611.21586 (a hypothesis verifier that demands an exact quotation before counting a claim), arxiv-2611.20441 (a component located is not a component explained).

- **Selection: the first entry in the folder whose thesis is that the field's founding evidence for the object we are trying to predict is an artefact of observation, and it is the strongest available counter-position to our own vocabulary.** `goodfire-com-research-already-clean` earns the slot on four things. (4) **It names the failure mode of our own read-out family in one sentence**: a dictionary's units on the last layer were 88% near-copies of single neurons, and removing every direction that matches no neuron left accuracy unchanged, so the decomposition was not recovering anything the original basis lacked. Evidence: the V-shape re-reading of 4e:55; the 480→10 mixed3b squeeze with an SAE that cannot recover the ten curve detectors; Qwen3-32B at ~90% one-job poles (~97% on strong activations) and GPT-2 XL going from <2% to ~70% in 500 papers; blind maximum beating the best example in 10B tokens; 76%/11% on 200 pre-registered explanations; 88% of last-layer SAE activity being near-copies of single neurons; umbrella→bee learned in nine steps as an off-ramp between existing circuits; weakest-75% versus strongest-7% activation deletion at matched mass (72→71 against 72→4).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 326): **The test that makes "the model hid it elsewhere" falsifiable is a capacity squeeze plus a decomposition, and this essay is the folder's cleanest instance: cut a layer from 480 to 10 channels with no bypass, retrain, then train a dictionary on the squeezed layer and ask whether the missing units reappear anywhere in it — they do not, with shape correlations of 0.52–0.72 and photo matches of 0.09–0.14 against 0.96–1.00 for a dictionary of the intact layer, every one of the 91 most responsive features firing at the opposite angle, and a nonlinear readout ceiling of 0.29–0.48.** Every claim of the form "the information is still there, just distributed" needs this construction, and the reason it works is that the squeeze removes the capacity while leaving the task, so a fold-elsewhere strategy has somewhere specific to show up. For us the mirror is a read-out that underperforms at small width or sparse k and is then defended as "differently encoded": the defence is testable by giving the wider or denser model the same probe and seeing whether the missing selectivity returns. The companion discipline is that the squeezed model was still scored on the task (58.35/81.14), so the units were absent from an accurate model rather than from a broken one, and a squeeze experiment that destroys accuracy proves nothing. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20253` (a learned block the decoder never uses beside blocks that behave) and `arxiv-2611.20445` (a support set that is real and explains nothing).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 326): **A neuron's label is a claim about the observer as much as the model, and the movable part is the description's grammar: the canonical cat-and-car neuron is a bilateral-pointed-shape detector whose negative pole is a round O, so the honest label is a distinction (V versus O) rather than a list of nouns, and the same group of responses becomes evidence for arbitrary packing under one grammar and evidence for generalization under the other.** This is the sharpest form of a failure our own probe write-ups are prone to, because a linear probe's positive class is always reported as a noun phrase ("vehicle-ness", "sentiment") and almost never as a contrast; the repair costs nothing and is three questions — what is the shared pattern in the inputs that drive this unit, what is its negative pole, and does the pattern predict a fourth group of nouns the original set did not contain. The essay's own tell is that both human and automated interpreters default to noun groups, and the author's experience is that mid-layer neurons are more often verbs. The second half is the architectural version of the same lesson: when a characteristic fills the top of a ranking for 4% of units (the SwiGLU −×− echo, 131 of 133 responses in the p75–p99 band) and ablating it raises most benchmarks while lowering some reasoning ones, the ranking is reporting the gate's sign algebra, not the model's concepts. Coreference `arxiv-2611.17856` (an explanation scored against the evidence that produced it) and `arxiv-2611.20897` (a support set certified about the wrong object).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 326): **There is a pre-registered behavioural test of an explanation that costs one agent run and cannot be gamed by fitting to the corpus: give an agent only the written explanation and ask for five inputs that should drive the unit and five near misses that should not, commit the examples before measuring anything, and score firing against a fixed fraction of the corpus maximum — 76% of new examples against 11% of near misses on 200 neurons, 164 wins to 15 ties and 4 losses, is what a real explanation buys, and blind maximum (a second agent writing one maximally activating sentence from the explanation alone, which beats the strongest of ten billion corpus tokens) is the single-item version of the same construction.** For us this replaces agreement-with-the-probe as the way to certify a written explanation: a description that generalises to inputs the model was never searched for has done work, and one that only re-describes the top activations has not. The threshold matters and must be printed (here 30% of the neuron's corpus maximum), and the scoring must be committed before the examples are run, because otherwise the agent is searching the corpus the same way the original analysis did. Its own limit is honest and transferable: 4 of 200 explanations lost outright and 15 tied, so the test is a filter, not a certificate. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20854` (measurements written down before the experiment runs) and `arxiv-2611.10503` (a scope enforced by the objective rather than measured).

- **Selection: the standing invite from run 323, taken deliberately as the run that wants a diffusion-generation entry — and the first folder entry whose object of explanation is the SAMPLER rather than the network.** `2611.21669` earns the slot on four things. (1) **A genuinely new unit for the folder** — every prior steering entry intervenes on what the model predicts (activations, logits, guidance); this one intervenes on which provisional predictions become permanent and how many per step, which is a decoding decision autoregressive models do not have, and it formalises that policy as a scoring map plus a budget map so the two axes can be swept separately. (2) **The sweeps are single-variable by construction** — order is swept with budget fixed at one token per step so every point uses identical denoising cost, budget is swept with ranking fixed to confidence, and the conclusion the design licenses is exactly the one drawn: movement along each curve is not bought with compute. (3) **The principal baseline is the right one** — a scorer-free stochastic schedule with the same confidence ranking whose budget distribution was chosen post hoc from step counts alone to match average steps, so state-dependent adaptation is separated from average cost; and random commitment order serves as a null that separates "the mechanism works" from "leaving the default works", with the shape a null should have (worst perplexity of any policy, 13.1, for a target move of 0.35 → 0.41). (4) **The target-type generalisation is the paper's real claim** — because both controls need only a scalar score on a provisional completion, they apply to example-specific proxies (NLI entailment, CLIPScore) that correspond to no reusable direction, which is the case the folder's direction-based entries cannot address. Its weakness is recorded in the entry rather than smoothed: the knob is ranked by the target scorer itself, so the re-scoring check carries more weight than the monotonicity does; one seed; one strength per steering method, with the authors explicitly declining the commitment-versus-steer-harder comparison; ~49% latency overhead for counterfactual ordering; and the authors' own proposed fix (a surrogate that preserves the ranking) concedes the on-the-fly measurement is impractical.

- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 325): **A knob whose ranking function is the target scorer is a property of the optimiser, not a read-out of the model, and this is the cleanest case in the folder because the knob and the objective are the same quantity separated by one step — every rank in the counterfactual map is a scored provisional completion, so the sweep cannot distinguish "this control surface is meaningful" from "the scorer's preferences are being hill-climbed", and the check that does distinguish them is not the monotonicity but the independent re-scorer.** For us the mirror is our own calibration-by-agreement work and any probe-based selection that uses a held-out score to choose which directions to test: the ordering along the sweep is guaranteed by the objective, so the evidence has to come from somewhere the objective never touched — a different scorer, a different dataset, a behavioural read that was not optimised. The structural tell is stated honestly in the paper's own name for the method: *counterfactual* here means a local span deletion on the current completion, not the downstream causal effect of the commit, which is exactly the substitution we keep needing to police in our own vocabulary. Coreference `arxiv-2611.17856` (a faithfulness score certifying incoherent features) and `arxiv-2610.41661` (a perplexity check blind to the side effect it audits).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 325): **The compute-matched null is the baseline that makes a "the mechanism works" claim admissible, and this paper builds the right one — same confidence ranking, budget sampled from a state-independent distribution with its parameters chosen post hoc from step counts alone, so only state-dependent adaptation differs from the treatment — then adds a second, cheaper null in random commitment order that separates the mechanism from merely departing from the default, and the pair is what makes the result legible: random order pays the largest perplexity of any policy (13.1) for a target move of 0.35 → 0.41, where the target-aware order reaches 0.63 at 10.6.** Nearly every intervention or instrument we report is compared against another intervention rather than against an account of its own cost, and the two-null protocol is cheap: match the compute, randomise the mechanism, and report both against the default. The companion discipline in the same paper is that the comparison is framed as non-domination rather than dominance and the authors print the cells where the adaptive point merely matches (Dream NLI, same score at 1.1 lower perplexity, read as a match not a win) — which is the honest form of a fifteen-setting claim. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20854` (measurements written down before the experiment runs) and `arxiv-2611.20445` (a support set that is real and explains nothing).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 325): **Sampling and probing have the same two independent axes, and separating them is what makes each sweep interpretable: this paper splits the commitment policy into *which* positions resolve (a scoring map) and *how many* resolve per step (a budget map), lets exactly one vary at a time with the other pinned, and gets two orthogonal, monotone curves instead of one confounded one.** Our probing designs conflate the same pair constantly — which units or positions we measure next versus how many we measure, which feature we interrogate versus how often — and a design that varies both at once cannot attribute its curve to either. The operational form is one sentence per experiment: name the selection rule, name the rate, and state which of the two the intervention changed. The second half is the cost of a state-dependent rule: conditioning each step on the current state bought the ordered curve at +49% wall-clock for order and +8.5% for budget, and the authors' proposed fix is a surrogate that only has to preserve the ranking — which is worth carrying as the standard shape of a cheap approximation to an expensive per-step measurement: keep the order, drop the magnitude. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20840` (a relevance metric maximised over its own tuning parameter) and `arxiv-2611.20364` (a tie set that decimals conceal).

- **Selection: the folder's first entry whose explanation is a surrogate fitted to another model's OUTPUTS and whose own table is candidly in-sample, taken because that is precisely the failure mode our calibration-by-agreement work keeps risking.** `2611.22515` earns the slot on four things. (1) **The object is different from everything the folder's other linear entries hold** — twenty-one entries carry the `replacement-model` tag, but those are additive models and low-order depth dynamics fitted to a network's internals; this fits a discriminant to a black box's *binary predictions* and never inspects it, which is our black-box-on-both-sides case rather than our white-box case. (2) **The scope claim is measured, not asserted** — the one exception in the covariance-pooling table (Genbase, per-label 0.999 against shared 0.980) is explained by the condition number (5.72e6 shared against 3.54e7 per-label, i.e. its binary Prosite features are near-singular), so the paper shows its own regularity condition failing in exactly the dataset it predicts it should fail in. That kind of exception-with-a-number is the honest form of a scope claim and we have been asking for it. (3) **A real controlled comparison with one variable** — shared against per-label covariance, "identical in every respect except covariance scope", same ridge rule, same right-hand side, same attribution protocol, giving +0.180 AUC on Enron's 53 labels where per-label matrices are about 184,000× worse conditioned and each label has on average 64 positives in 1,001 dimensions. (4) **A diagnostic validated against a disagreement measure chosen per feature type** — top-1 match on the two binary-feature datasets, correlation-cluster-aware top-1 on Yeast and Scene, full-vector Spearman on Emotions, averaged over all fifteen classifier pairs; all five signs are in the predicted direction and only Enron (ρ = −0.568, p = 0.001) and Genbase (−0.545, p = 0.029) reach significance, which the authors print rather than smooth. Its weakness is recorded in the entry rather than smoothed: **fidelity is fit and scored on the same predictions throughout**, so no number in the paper bounds out-of-sample reproduction; the Pareto comparison puts an in-sample curve beside out-of-sample tree and Lasso curves; the concentration correlations rest on 6 to 32 labels, so three of five are uninformative rather than negative; Theorem 1 bounds separability in the *surrogate's* feature space and is not a claim about any internal direction; and the whole study is classical classifiers on five small benchmarks with no neural network and no two-sample sufficiency test for the concentration statistic.

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 319 file-side / run 324): `arxiv-2611.22515` — Right Labels, Wrong Reasons: Signed Feature Attribution for Multi-Label Explainability (Kenton White — AC Online, Algonquin College; arXiv:2611.22515v1 [cs.LG, cs.AI], 2026-11-17, Accepted at IEEE SSCI 2027, 7 pages, 43 KB source, replication code released). Full text via PDF extraction (~41K chars: abstract, §§I–VII, references). **Substance:** FLEX fits **one** Fisher linear discriminant to a black box's binary prediction matrix. Per label, positive and negative predicted-group centroids give the right-hand side; **one** within-class covariance is pooled over every label's positive group, ridge-regularised at the median diagonal floored at 1e-6, and a single batched Cholesky solve yields all label weight vectors at once. A feature enters a label's list only if a two-sample F-test between that label's predicted-positive and predicted-negative groups survives Bonferroni correction within the label (α = 0.05); the sign sorts it into a positive or a negative list. Two diagnostics follow: the weight-vector norm bounds separability (Theorem 1: two-sided bound by the Whitened centroid gap scaled by the extreme eigenvalues of the regularised pooled covariance, hence a cross-label proxy up to the square root of its condition number), and concentration (largest weight over mean weight) is a black-box signal that the label rests on one dominant feature. Six classical classifiers (BR-LR, BR-RF, BR-XGB, ECC, ML-kNN k = 10, RAkELo) on five Madjarov benchmarks (Yeast, Emotions, Scene, Genbase, Enron; 6–53 labels, 1.07–4.24 labels per instance), 50/50 iterative-stratification splits, ten seeds, explainer given only the feature matrix and the predictions. **Results:** surrogate AUC ≥ 0.90 in all 30 cells and > 0.96 in 25 (lowest ML-kNN 0.901 and BR-XGB 0.911 on Yeast); recall ≥ 0.77, = 1.00 on Genbase; precision from 0.876 (BR-LR Yeast) to 0.245 on Genbase; shared covariance beats per-label AUC in 4 of 5 datasets, by **+0.180** on Enron where per-label condition number is 6.32e7 against 3.44e2 and each label has on average 64 positives in 1,001 dimensions; Genbase reverses (0.999 per-label vs 0.980 shared) at condition numbers 3.54e7 vs 5.72e6; budget sweep monotone for FLEX (best AUC of any method at full budget on 0.964/0.969/0.984/0.995) while trees peak and decay (0.858→0.764 Emotions, 0.828→0.741 Yeast) and Genbase's tree is already 0.993 at one feature; concentration correlates negatively with cross-classifier explanation disagreement on all five datasets, significant only on Enron (ρ = −0.568, p = 0.001) and Genbase (−0.545, p = 0.029), against mean pairwise prediction discrepancy of only 0.4–10.7%, i.e. the classifiers agree on which instances to label and diverge in how.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 324): **A surrogate's fidelity and a surrogate's scope are separate claims, and the tell that a paper conflates them is a caption saying the surrogate was fit and scored on the same items — here every one of the 30 fidelity cells is in-sample, and the Pareto figure then places an in-sample curve beside two out-of-sample baselines whose fitting sets differ, so the comparison is between reconstruction and generalisation rather than between methods.** This reads like a technicality and is not one: AUC 0.98 on the items you fitted a linear discriminant to is close to arithmetic, and the number that would actually license "the surrogate explains the model" is the same AUC on held-out instances. The rule is one clause in the caption we refuse to omit — *fitted on X, scored on Y, and whether they intersect* — plus the discipline of never drawing an in-sample curve and an out-of-sample curve on one axis without marking which is which. Under our setting this bears directly on any calibration-by-agreement study: if we fit a read-out to reproduce a model's behaviour and then report agreement on those same probes, we have measured our own optimiser, not the model. Coreference `arxiv-2611.17856` (an explanation scored against the evidence that produced it) and `arxiv-2611.10503` (a scope claim enforced by the objective rather than measured).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 324): **Pooling a nuisance estimate across groups is a bias-variance trade whose break-even point is a condition number, and this paper shows both sides of it with numbers: pooling scatter across 53 email labels buys +0.180 AUC where per-label covariances are rank-deficient (184,000× worse conditioned, ~64 positives per label in 1,001 dimensions), and costs 0.019 AUC on Genbase where the labels are near-orthogonal binary features that a shared covariance blurs.** Every estimate we borrow across strata to make it well-conditioned — a noise ceiling, a covariance for whitening directions, a shared decoder baseline, a normalisation constant — sits on exactly this trade, and the generalisable lesson is that the borrow is safe when the per-stratum estimate is underdetermined and unsafe when the strata differ in the *structure* the estimate is meant to capture. The operational form is cheap: report the condition number of both estimates per stratum group beside the downstream score, so a pooled estimate that silently degraded one group is visible as an anomaly in that group's condition number rather than as an unexplained dip in results. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20253` (a learned block the decoder never uses beside blocks that behave) and `arxiv-2611.20854` (a per-item difference the average erases).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 324): **Diffuse attribution is evidence about the model's reasons rather than about the explainer's quality, and the test that makes it a claim is cross-model: disagreement between classifiers' own internal attributions is low exactly where FLEX weights are concentrated (ρ = −0.568 on Enron, −0.545 on Genbase) while their *predictions* disagree on only 0.4–10.7% of instances — so a diffuse weight vector flags a decision reached by an arbitrary feature subset, not an unreliable explanation.** For us the mirror is direct: when two models, or two of our instruments, produce overlapping but non-identical direction sets for the same behaviour, the interior of that overlap is the content and the residual is the arbitrariness, and the honest report gives both. The construction worth copying is the concentration statistic as a *self-audit attached to the explanation* rather than a separate accuracy number — largest weight over mean weight costs one pass over the weights and can be printed in every read-out table. Its own limit is visible in the same table and must travel with it: with 6 to 32 labels per dataset, three of the five correlations are between −0.486 and −0.086 with p from 0.33 to 0.87, i.e. the sign is right and the evidence is not, and a claim of this shape needs the label count printed beside the coefficient. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20445` (a support set that is real and explains nothing) and `arxiv-2611.20897` (a support set certified about the wrong object).
