- **Selection: the folder's first entry that derives the geometry of a representation from an objective rather than measuring it, and the first to state in its own terms where its derivations stop being checkable.** `2611.19972` earns the slot on four things no other entry has together: a **closed-form law for the thing every latent-space reading assumes but never bounds** — a finite wall whose width shrinks only like the inverse log of the coupling, so a separation can be sharpened but never removed at finite regularization; **a binodal/spinodal pair of thresholds for rare states**, which separates "a distinct region is the better representation" from "training can reach it", giving the first in-corpus formalisation of the decodable-versus-used gap we keep writing around; **a stationarity identity with named failure conditions** (zero mean, identity second moment at any affine optimum — coordinatewise only for diagonal families, broken by fixed absolute resolution), which is a cheap falsifier for any read-out that claims to describe a geometry rather than a checkpoint; and **an explicit non-equivalence caveat** (the free-energy rewriting is exact but the responsibilities cannot be chosen independently, so the analogy is a dictionary, not a variational bound) plus a printed list of where the asymptotics are known to fail (the square-gradient expansion missing the wall cost by about a factor of three). It also does the one thing several recent entries were declined for not doing: it separates existence of a low-loss folded optimum from gradient accessibility of it, and reports the trained-network negative result plainly.
- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 308 file-side / run 310): `arxiv-2611.19972` — The structure of variational autoencoder latent spaces and its consequences for representation and optimization (Sergei V. Kalinin, Department of Materials Science and Engineering, University of Tennessee, Knoxville; arXiv:2611.19972v1, 2026-11-15). Full text via PDF text layer (~203K chars, 60 pages including SI; figures not inspected — every number below is quoted from prose or table text, not read off a plot). **Substance:** one-author theory paper; a reduced model (one Gaussian prototype per class, squared-error reconstruction, optimal decoder, standard-Gaussian prior) is mapped onto a standard VAE objective through three rewritings — responsibility-weighted optimal decoder, affine invariance of the reconstruction term, and a split of the class-averaged KL into aggregate-density and mutual-information parts — producing a regular-solution mixing functional whose interaction coefficients are the reconstruction couplings. Derived and numerically checked: two equal classes separate at coupling one half with square-root onset and inverse-square-root wall broadening (fitted exponent 0.504; condensation gain exponent 2.007 with prefactor 1.00; Widom combination 0.997 at a coupling one-thousandth above threshold); wall width falls like the inverse of twice the log coupling; centroid separation grows only logarithmically in prototype dissimilarity; the KL acts as a harmonic trap on centroids whose stiffness is class frequency, so frequency behaves as mass; a rare class is compressed toward the prior tail and under-weighted in prior allocation (5% data frequency receiving 18% of a proportional prior share at one coupling and 4% at a sharper one), with four distinct fates (own island, adsorption inside the wall between two common classes, dissolution into a common class, own layer) separated by binodal and spinodal thresholds; dimensionality needs m+s−1 latents for m continuous factors with s classes, m+k−1 for k factors in m dimensions, with oversubscribed cases favouring a folded staircase whose preferred strand count grows like the square root of the excess factor's strength; pair-model layouts agree with the full objective to 4×10⁻⁴ with a 0.001–0.007 junction excess. Checks: multistart L-BFGS-B over three posterior families (isotropic, diagonal per class, full covariance via Cholesky) plus structured starts; trained 2-D VAEs on digits 0/1 (8×8, 128-unit tanh hidden, Bernoulli reconstruction, three seeds, four regularization strengths), ten-class MNIST, rotated digits for orientation winding, and a synthetic rotation-plus-shear card set, largely used for qualitative illustration; a nonparametric per-datapoint-Gaussian encoder supplies low-loss layouts; a DKL and a hybrid VAE–DKL arm test the predictive-objective contrast. **Honesty ledger:** the paper calls the free-energy correspondence a dictionary rather than an equivalence; states the encoded-mean proxy omits encoder variance precisely where the wall-width law is hardest to verify, and calls its own trained two-class measurement qualitative; reports that the third synthetic factor was suppressed or entangled in trained 2-D networks rather than folded, and reads that as an optimisation-accessibility result; notes higher-dimensional winding was never tested with trained networks; and explicitly refuses to fit the asymptotics to heterogeneous trained networks. **Read relevance 2:** no benchmark, no leaderboard, no intervention test — but three transferable instruments (see the Pattern lines) and the closest theory-side statement of the multi-region latent picture our probes keep measuring.

- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 310): **When a derivation says a separation exists but not that it is reachable, the interval between those two thresholds is a quantity, not a footnote.** The paper separates a binodal (a distinct region is the lower-loss layout) from a spinodal (the mixed layout loses local stability) and then uses that gap to explain why initialisation decides whether a rare state is resolved. Every claim of the form "the model represents X" that our folder contains collapses two thresholds into one: decodable and used. Reading them apart is cheap — hold the representation fixed, vary only the initialisation or the training path, and ask whether the region's presence moves while the inputs do not — and the width of the interval is then the honest bound on how much of the claim is about the data and how much about the optimisation.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 310): **A read-out that describes a geometry must be checked against the identity its own objective implies, and the check fails for reasons that are stated in advance.** Zero mean and identity second moment hold at any affine optimum; the paper shows the identity is only coordinatewise under a diagonal posterior family and is broken outright by a decoder with fixed absolute resolution. Both are exactly the shortcuts our probes take — a fixed smoothing scale, a diagonal or factorised family, a probe fitted at a finite checkpoint — so the identity is not a nice-to-have but a test that returns "checkpoint, not geometry" on the configurations we most often use. This recurs with run 300's entry on allocation-vs-attribution and with `arxiv-2611.13548` on denominators deciding what a number means.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 310): **Similarity is a metric choice, and the corpus now has the geometric version of the denominator lesson.** Switching from pixelwise to smoothed comparison moved a rare prototype between the "island" and "adsorbed" fates at identical frequency and coupling — the representation did not change, the metric did, and the reported structure changed with it. On our side the equivalent move is a probe whose similarity notion (cosine over a residual stream, dot product over a fixed direction, a nearest-neighbour metric in an SAE feature space) is stated as a choice beside every structural claim rather than left implicit as the definition of similarity.

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 307 file-side / run 309): `arxiv-2611.20111` — When Valid Decisions Are Not Enough: Evaluating Structural Constraints in Knowledge-Guided Generative Systems (Josef Pavlíček, Petra Pavlíčková — CTU Prague FIT; Martin Molhanec — CTU Prague FEE; arXiv:2611.20111v1 [cs.AI], 2026-11-15, arXiv perpetual non-exclusive licence). Full text via HTML (~44K clean chars: abstract, §§1–8, references). **Substance:** a deterministic two-level ablation on a hand-built harmonization system, not a neural model. Four configurations — baseline, repetition (weight 0.12), functional (0.06), combined — share one candidate generator and one iterative Viterbi-style dynamic program (four-iteration cap, best complete-objective path retained, no global-optimum guarantee) over a fixed hand-written local score; motif links span distant positions so the structural term is scored against the previous iteration's assignment. Reference annotations are never visible to the optimizer. 19,745 HookTheory/SheetSage records (17,911/1,821 processed for development/held-out), 143,634 motif pairs (131,117/12,517). Two measures on identical outputs: record-macro exact chord agreement, and pair-weighted reference root-interval agreement stratified retrospectively into four contexts (untransposed-same-root, untransposed-changed-root, transposed-tracking, transposed-non-tracking). Work-clustered bootstrap, 1,000 resamples per contrast plus 5,000 for simultaneous intervals across all 12 contrasts (common half-width 3.09 points); 3 × 3 weight grid on the development split only. **Results:** aggregate moves are negligible — 18.32% → 18.38% on the development split, 18.97% → 19.03% held-out, all held-out intervals spanning zero, combination never beating repetition alone. Context effects are large and opposed: combined configuration +5.00 (same root) / −0.99 (changed root) / −8.93 (transposed-tracking) / +4.18 (non-tracking) points held-out, with the development split within 0.08 / 0.53 / 0.13 / 0.05 points; simultaneous intervals exclude zero for three of four (the changed-root contrast does not); all four directions hold at all nine weight settings (36/36). Blame: repetition alone reproduces −8.93 of the −8.93 tracking effect while functional alone is −2.44, so the bundle's damage is one component's.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 309): **An aggregate metric and a stratified effect computed on the same outputs can differ in sign while the aggregate looks null, and the gap here is two orders of magnitude: exact chord agreement moves +0.07 points while the same runs move root-interval agreement +5.00 and −8.93 points in different strata — so "no effect on the headline" was never evidence of no effect, it was evidence the headline cannot see the relationship the intervention targeted.** Every probe or circuit metric we publish that is averaged over positions or prompts has this shape, and the average is the metric we report first. The copyable procedure is three lines: choose strata from a property the instrument *cannot see when it acts* (here, whether the human reference tracks the melodic transposition, known only at evaluation), print each stratum's effect and interval beside the headline number, and label the strata retrospective so the result reads as a diagnostic rather than a controller. The specific trap the paper warns about and then avoids is numerical cancellation: the aggregate is not the sum of a benefit and a cost that cancel — the measures have different units and different denominators, so the correct sentence is not "the effects cancel" but "the aggregate is blind to this dimension". Coreference `arxiv-2611.20364` (a rank order that a tie set forbids) and `arxiv-2611.21232` (a responsibility table naming each module's characteristic failure in advance).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 309): **A matched intervention ladder in which nothing but the treatment varies is what makes an attribution safe, and it is available without any model at all — here the segmenter, candidate set, scoring function, optimizer, iteration cap and determinism are identical across all four arms, no reference information touches generation, and there is no seed noise, so the contrast is the constraint weight and nothing else.** This is the control our own ablation batteries approximate and rarely achieve: a probe versus a patched ablation differs in extraction, fitting and intervention at once, whereas a ladder that holds three of four fixed licenses a sentence about the fourth. The companion discipline is the **component decomposition inside the bundle**: because the combined configuration does not decompose into its parts (the arms are optimized independently, and combined-effects are explicitly not additive), the only way to know which term did the damage is to run each alone — repetition alone accounts for essentially all of the −8.93 in the tracking context, so a report of the bundle would have credited the wrong term half the time. Corollary for us: never publish a multi-component intervention as a single arm when single-term arms are one run away. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20678` (the matched ladder where denoising and pruning each buy a great deal and learned selection buys the last 0.09) and `arxiv-2611.21331` (a targeted-versus-random control at matched spend).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 309): **A rule can be meaningful and misinterpreted in the same breath, and the paper's separation of meaning from applicability is the portable part: transposition alone does not determine whether the rule helps — the constraint hurts where the reference *tracks* the transposition (−8.93) and helps where it does not (+4.18), so the operative feature is not the surface property (melody moved) but the relationship between the surface property and the reference's behaviour.** That is the difference between a stratifier and an explanation, and it is the exact error our read-outs are prone to: splitting results by an easily-computed surface variable (prompt length, position, layer depth) and calling the resulting table a mechanism, when the variable that matters is the relation between that surface feature and what the reference does with it. The paper's own framing — constraints have an *applicability condition*, not just a meaning — translates directly: a probe that fires on a feature has an applicability condition we almost never state, and the condition is usually a property of the input the probe cannot observe. The stated limit keeps this honest: the stratifier here is retrospective and reference-dependent, so it cannot be deployed as a selector, and the paper refuses to present it as one. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20111`'s own §6.1 and `arxiv-2611.20364` (a post-hoc disagreement reported rather than resolved).

Three feature libraries (tsfresh efficient configuration, TSFEL statistical+temporal, tsfeatures with periodicity features off) over six channels → 3,286 features per window; Boruta all-relevant filter → RFECV (LightGBM, ~5% removed per step) and iterative SHAP pruning (weakest quartile per round, smallest set within one SE of the best) with their **intersection** kept as 18 features. Fourteen classifiers, 5×5 repeated stratified CV, Friedman omnibus then Nemenyi and Nadeau–Bengio corrected paired t-tests with Holm adjustment; out-of-fold predictions for all reported confusion, per-class and AUC statistics. **Results:** three-way task Rotation Forest 99.98% ± 0.04 (CI 99.96–100.00), but ET/RF/XGBoost/GB/CatBoost/LightGBM/SVM-RBF/MLP all within 0.12 points and Holm p > 0.95 — nine ties; Ridge 86.14, NB 80.84, LSVM 94.88, LR 96.46 are the separable failures (Δ 19.14 / 13.84 / 5.10 / 3.52 points, all Holm p < 10⁻¹⁰); k-NN 0.25 down, p 0.02 uncorrected → 0.16 corrected. Friedman χ² = 262.26, p = 1.81 × 10⁻⁴⁸. Binary task SVM-RBF 97.97% ± 0.80 (CI 97.63–98.31), eleven ties, only NB (9.11 down) and Ridge (1.33 down, p = 0.030) separable; Nemenyi additionally flags ET, GB, k-NN, MLP and ROF there; Friedman χ² = 151.88, p = 8.63 × 10⁻²⁶. Out-of-fold 97.82% accuracy with class 1 recall 96.15% / precision 99.73% and class 2 the mirror, AUC 99.34% both classes. SHAP: top features are autocorrelation lag 10 of the first difference (0.05), max R² of a linear trend over 5-sample chunks (0.04), variance of trend intercept over 50-sample chunks (0.04), variance of trend standard error over 5-sample chunks (0.04), mean R² of a 10-sample trend (0.04), AR(10) coefficients (0.03, 0.02, 0.02), down to a spectral centroid at 0.01; trend and autocorrelation dominate over spectral descriptors. Fit times: 12.73 s (ROF) against 1.35 s (ET), 0.97 s (XGBoost), 0.24 s (SVM-RBF) on task A; 0.09 s (SVM-RBF) against 4.79 s (LightGBM) on task B. Limits named by the authors: one 9-bus system, ideal conditions, no measurement noise, no inverter-based resources, no larger test system.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 308): **A comparison run properly yields a tie set, and the tie set is the result worth reporting — here nine of fourteen classifiers sit within 0.12 points of a 99.98% leader with Holm-adjusted p above 0.95, on a second task eleven of fourteen are inseparable from a 97.97% leader, and only the linear and probabilistic families are ever separable; with fit times printed beside the scores, the tie is what makes the paper useful, because the leader takes 12.73 s where a tied rival takes 0.24 s.** Our read-out tables are built the other way round — one best number per instrument, a rank order, and a claim that the winner is better — which is exactly the movement a tie set forbids. The copyable procedure is three lines: an omnibus test whose only job is to say the comparison is not noise, a paired figure with a variance correction and a multiple-comparison adjustment for the pairwise claims, and then a sentence that names the tied set explicitly ("these eight are not distinguishable from the best") rather than leaving the reader to infer a difference from decimal places. The second, sharper lesson is that an omnibus *rejecting* barely licenses anything: on the binary task the Friedman test is decisive (χ² = 151.88, p = 8.6 × 10⁻²⁶) while the same data supports only two separable pairwise differences, because at these accuracies the omnibus is detecting the spread of the whole field around a leaderboard position — which is why the paper's own conclusion reads the significance as "at least one classifier differs meaningfully from the rest" and not as evidence about the winner. Coreference arxiv-2611.20983 (a TOST margin used to refuse a verdict on a plateau) and arxiv-2611.21586 (a verification count that rose by 30% with nothing surviving correction).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 308): **Two post-hoc tests over the same accuracies can disagree, and when they do the disagreement is information rather than a fault to be silently resolved: on the binary task Nemenyi flags five extra classifiers as different from the leader (ET, GB, k-NN, MLP, ROF) that the Nadeau–Bengio corrected paired t-test leaves tied, and the paper names the cause — a rank test compares average positions across all fourteen models at once and reacts to small but *consistent* rank swings, while a paired test compares score magnitudes with a variance correction for non-independent folds, so report both and say which one your claim rests on.** For our battery the practical consequence is that a rank-based instrument (which layer ranks highest across seeds, which feature ranks highest across prompts) and a magnitude-based one (mean score difference with seed variance) are answering different questions and will sometimes order things differently; the wrong response is to pick whichever supports the claim, and the nearly-wrong response is to average them. The right response is the one used here: a single sentence in the results that states the divergence, its mechanism, and that the conservative reading is adopted — and the divergence itself is a diagnostic, because a large gap between rank evidence and magnitude evidence usually means the scores are packed tightly and the ranks are being carried by very small consistent differences.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 308): **An importance ranking produced from 3,286 candidates, cut to eighteen, where the top entry carries 0.05 of total importance and no selected feature is ever deleted to see whether the model notices, is a description of the fitted model and not evidence about the signal — and the tell is that the paper's interpretive claim ("trend and autocorrelation rather than spectral information alone") is supported only by that ranking.** Every SHAP or attribution table our read-outs publish has the same gap: the measure says how much of the *model's output variation* the feature carries in this reference distribution, and it says nothing about whether the behaviour survives the feature's removal, which is the difference between a correlate and a cause. Two cheap additions close it, both already in the folder's vocabulary elsewhere: ablate or perturb the top-k features and re-measure the decision (the intervention test rather than the attribution score), and publish the importance mass's distribution rather than only its order, because eighteen features averaging 0.055 with a 0.05 maximum is a flat ranking being read as a decisive one — a support set that is real and explains nothing, the same shape as `arxiv-2611.20445`'s stable-but-uninformative support. The companion is the selection caveat the paper leaves unstated: features chosen under one label and reused under another are a transfer, and what the reused set gives up is measurable by re-running selection on the second target. Coreference arxiv-2611.20441 (a component located is not a component explained) and arxiv-2611.20897 (a support set certified about the wrong object).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 305 file-side / run 307): `arxiv-2611.21331` — TRIAGE-CPG: A Cross-Model Study of Budgeted Static Malware Triage with Large Language Models (Paul-Andrei Sava, Alexander Küchler, Daniel Kowatsch — Fraunhofer AISEC; Bernhard Grill, Jennifer Pullman, Yanick Fratantonio, Luca Invernizzi — Google Zurich; AISec '26 workshop, ACM DOI 10.1145/3847352.3848112, arXiv:2611.21331v1 [cs.CR], 2026-11-16, CC BY 4.0, artifact on Zenodo). Full text via HTML (~82K chars: abstract, §§1–7, Appendices A–D). **Substance:** 1,000 VirusTotal Windows PE binaries (500/500, stratified over five size quantiles; benign = 0 detections, malicious ≥ 10, 1–9 excluded), splits 200/200/600, the test split touched once. Ghidra → CPG, but only the function-level call-graph projection is queried, plus PE metadata. Stage 1 seeds with an untrained Evidence Priority Score (reverse PageRank + boundary flag + normalised log body length; deployed weights 0.50 / 0.25 / 0.25, zero on forward PageRank and API rarity), 10% of functions with floor 10 and cap 75; stage 2 is a 30-read exploration agent over callers/callees/API lookup; stage 3 adjudicates the **frozen** dossier under a 20-action read-only allowance into benign / suspicious / malicious. Eight models, identical zero-shot protocol, temperature 0, no per-model tuning. **Results:** best model Gemini 3.1 Pro, strict balanced accuracy 0.805, **tBA 0.855** at ~40 of a mean 1,000 functions; 65% of malware flagged, 7.3–12% escalated, 93.7% of benign cleared. Models occupy different operating points with no provenance split — Gemma 4 26B commits 88% of malware at 0.370 specificity; GLM 5.2 is the best open-weight model at 5.3 tBA points below the leader and agrees with it on 78.3% of verdicts; Gemini 3.5 Flash and Gemma 4 26B agree on only 48.2% against 91% run-to-run agreement for one model repeated, and that repeat spans 1.5 balanced-accuracy points, which is the paper's stated noise floor. Suspicion queues are model-specific: Flash 12.0% coverage at 0.875 precision, DeepSeek V4 Pro 41.0% at 0.443. Selector comparison (exploration off): EPS 0.775, out-degree 0.785, largest body 0.765, random mean 0.724 — EPS chosen for frontier position (0.92 recall at 0.63 specificity). Seed cap 50 → 0.820, 75 → 0.790, 100 → 0.790. Exploration on vs off, pooled over nine configurations: benign 30 corrected / 11 hurt, malware 9 corrected / 18 hurt; agent-guided vs random targeting at matched actions: no significant accuracy difference, agent stops at 5.2 reads against 11.3–25.4. Full pipeline reconverges specificities to 0.70–0.72 while recall gaps persist (EPS misses 11/100, largest-code 18, random 13). PE metadata alone has strict recall 0.010 and marks 72.5% suspicious; adding it to code cuts false positives 56 → 30. Cascades: Pro 44-sample queue → Flash 35 at 0.943 precision with 2 additional misses; GLM 5.2 103 → Gemma 4 26B 25 at 0.840 with 1 additional miss; best cascade tBA +0.005. Reports judged against VirusTotal intel: capabilities 75–96%, role 66–83%, type 56–76%, **family only 1–6%**; under-claim 45–56% vs over-claim 13–22% on malware; 35% over-claim on benign. Wrappers 31% of the test set, 44% of both missed malware and false positives, 61% of escalated malware against 29% baseline.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 307): **A metric that an always-abstaining instrument cannot game is a one-line construction, and publishing it beside the strict version turns the *gap* into the informative quantity: defining tBA as the balanced accuracy of clear-versus-not-clear makes escalate-everything score exactly 0.5, and reporting strict balanced accuracy (0.805) beside tBA (0.855) localises the whole difference in how much the model defers — DeepSeek V4 Pro's recall jumps 0.603 → 0.967 under the triage reading while its specificity collapses 0.790 → 0.333, so its high triage number is bought almost entirely with escalation.** Every instrument in our battery with a "don't know" band or a threshold has the same hole: an abstention rate can be pushed to hide errors, and a single aggregate rewards it. The copyable form is (a) state the score an always-abstain instrument achieves and assert it is no better than the base rate, (b) report the committed-only and abstention-credited readings *side by side with their denominators*, and (c) treat the gap between them as the headline secondary number, because it is the direct measure of how much of the performance is deferral rather than measurement. Coreference arxiv-2611.20983 (a selector and a refuser are separate capabilities averaged away by one accuracy) and arxiv-2611.20432 (a predicted-versus-observed pair reported together so neither half can stand alone).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 307): **Reading order has an asymmetry that accuracy does not, and the asymmetry is what should set the price of a false positive: an unread region is unrecoverable downstream — the adjudicating stage can only work from the dossier it is handed — while a spurious flag is retractable, which is why the cheap seeder is deliberately tuned recall-first (0.92 recall at 0.63 specificity, chosen over out-degree's 0.785 balanced accuracy because it misses fewer) and why the expensive explorer is trusted only to remove false alarms (30 benign corrected vs 11 hurt; nothing consistent for malware at 9 vs 18).** Our probes perform the same function — they decide which heads, layers or activations get a second, more expensive look — and the standing rule is that the first pass must over-fire and must never be optimised for precision, because precision at that stage is bought out of quantity that no later stage can recover. The evidence here is also a caution about the second stage: it buys specificity (specificity converging to a 0.70–0.72 band across all seeders under the full pipeline) but *cannot close a recall gap*, since EPS's 11 missed malware, largest-code's 18 and random's 13 stay ordered exactly as they were seeded. Coreference arxiv-2611.20983 (a guardrail that takes the right candidate when one is present but cannot reject an all-wrong pool) and arxiv-2611.11398 (a first-pass null that decides which later scores count).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 307): **A smarter acquisition policy can be worth nothing while the budget is worth everything, and the test that shows it is random targeting at matched spend: agent-guided exploration reads 5.2 functions with balanced accuracy 0.800–0.820, action-matched random reads 11.3 for 0.760–0.815, full-budget random reads 25.4 for 0.775–0.805 — no difference reaching significance — so the agent's entire measurable contribution is stopping, not choosing.** This is the cleanest instance in the folder of a scheduling claim collapsing against its control, and it pairs with the selector null in the same paper (seven rankings within two points, random seeding only five down) to make a general rule: before reporting that a search or acquisition *strategy* beats a baseline, run the same strategy with the choice replaced by a random draw at the same spend, and report realised spend separately from accuracy, because an early-stopping policy will otherwise take credit for the budget it did not use. The practical corollary for our read-outs: if a "which features to probe first" ordering cannot beat random ordering at matched compute, the ordering is decorative — and the honest paper prints exactly that, in the same section that argues for its own heuristic. Coreference arxiv-2611.20678 (a matched-control ladder where the last learned stage buys 0.09 of a 0.91 margin) and arxiv-2611.21405 (a mean published beside its range).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 304 file-side / run 306): `arxiv-2611.20678` — UNIDE: Cross-PDE Learning for Noise-Robust Discovery of Governing Equations (Xiaoyu Xie, single author, Independent Researcher; arXiv:2611.20678v1, math.NA, 2026-11-16, 30 pages, 9 figures, arXiv perpetual non-exclusive licence). Full text via HTML (~82K clean chars: abstract, §§1–7, Appendices A–H). **Substance:** three stages over six one-dimensional periodic PDE families (advection, diffusion, advection–diffusion, Burgers, a stabilised KdV and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky), 2,400 simulated fields from 20 coefficient settings × 20 random initial conditions per family, 501 stored frames on 1,000 grid points, a twelve-term library of which five are ever active. A residual dilated CNN with circular spatial padding is trained with a blind-spot objective (masked entries replaced by a randomly offset neighbour, loss only at masked entries, fresh noise realisation per step) so no clean target is required; a shared encoder (per-frame spatial CNN → time-tagged frames → 2-layer, 4-head transformer → attention pooling fused with a metadata MLP, ~0.5M parameters) predicts per-term presence probabilities from the denoised field and is trained **on denoised features**; coefficients are never predicted and come from a weak-form least-squares solve on the predicted support with greedy backward pruning under a validation-tuned tolerance. One denoiser+encoder specialist per noise level. **Results:** exact match 0.866 at 1% noise, 0.960 at 10%, 0.924 at 80% against WSINDy 0.820 → 0.003 and SINDy/PySR at 0.00–0.01; clean-data PySR reaches 0.953 and UNIDE's clean variant 0.999, so the gap is a noise phenomenon. Coefficient accuracy inverts at low noise — WSINDy is better up to 5% and the two are close at 10% (4.99% vs 6.19%, five-seed mean 7.3%), UNIDE ahead only from 20% (8.04% vs 43.01% at 80%). Matched controls at 80% noise with identical denoiser, terms, windows, pruning and validation partition: weak STLSQ 0.010 raw → 0.484 with denoiser → 0.834 with pruning → 0.924 with learned selection, with **no consistent coefficient winner** among them. Ablations at 10%: no pruning 0.960 → 0.670 (coefficient error improves 4.99% → 4.73%), no denoiser 0.667, clean-trained encoder 0.393, pointwise least squares 0.670 exact with 48.85% coefficient error. Per-loss-term ablation: removing any one of the four auxiliary losses leaves exact match at or above the full objective (0.679–0.711 unpruned vs 0.670). Coefficient extrapolation at 10% noise: 0.906 exact match vs WSINDy 0.494, but 9.88% vs 4.98% coefficient error, almost all of it Burgers. Inference 0.45 s per trajectory (faster than WSINDy and PySR; only pointwise SINDy is faster and it fails under noise); fully frozen 10%-trained transfer falls 0.960 → 0.489 exact match from 10% to 80% noise while Term F1 holds at 0.696. **Named failures:** Burgers substitutes the convective term for the advective one (a whole-family swap that removal-only pruning cannot repair), and pruning deletes KdV's small fixed stabilising term on up to 29 of 150 trajectories.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 306): **The matched-control ladder is the whole instrument, and the ladder is what makes a pipeline claim legible: holding denoiser, candidate terms, windows, pruning and validation partition fixed and swapping only the selector gives 0.010 → 0.484 → 0.834 → 0.924 exact match at 80% noise, so denoising and pruning each buy a great deal on their own (0.010 to 0.834 is almost the entire margin) and learned selection buys the last 0.09 — a decomposition no end-to-end "ours versus baseline" comparison could have produced.** Every read-out comparison in our battery has the same shape and none of them are laddered: a probe versus a surrogate versus a patched ablation differ in extraction, in fitting and in the intervention all at once, so the reported gap is attributable to nothing in particular. The copyable form is one table with one row per cumulative addition, every shared component held fixed, and the *increments* quoted rather than only the endpoints — plus this paper's honesty in the same table, that the classical selector is actually better on coefficients at 10% noise (3.28% vs 4.99% relative error after pruning) while losing badly on structure, which means a single aggregate would have reported the wrong winner. Coreference arxiv-2611.21586 (three arms with the reader and budget held fixed) and arxiv-2611.20983 (the same candidate pools, only the selector swapped).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 306): **Two metrics that fail asymmetrically are worth more than one that fails symmetrically, and this paper states the asymmetry in advance so the pair works as a diagnostic: a spurious extra term lowers structure but is invisible to coefficient error because that error is computed only on the true active terms, whereas a missing true term lowers both — so a high coefficient score beside a low exact match is not a near-miss, it is the signature of over-selection.** For our probes the same split exists and is rarely reported: an instrument that fires on features the target does not contain and an instrument that stays silent on features it does contain produce the same F1 and support opposite conclusions, and the two are separable by reporting structure and magnitude accuracy side by side with their denominators stated. The paper's own data shows the pair earning its keep twice — at 10% noise learned selection wins on structure while sparse regression wins on coefficients, and under coefficient extrapolation UNIDE's 0.906 exact match sits next to a 9.88% coefficient error that WSINDy beats at 4.98% — so publishing both columns is what stops the reader from believing either alone. Coreference arxiv-2611.20983 (a ranked-correct rate and an all-wrong-rejection rate that average to one misleading number) and arxiv-2611.21405 (a mean published beside its range and split).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 306): **An auxiliary loss that can be deleted for free is a claim that has not been tested before it was published as a mechanism, and the ablation here is unambiguous: removing any one of the four auxiliary objectives — coefficient MAE, residual consistency, L1 sparsity, family cross-entropy — leaves exact match at or above the full objective (0.679 to 0.711 against 0.670), so the weighted term loss is doing all the structural work and three of the four additions buy nothing on the metric the paper headlines.** The transfer is a standing rule for any multi-term training or scoring objective in our battery: ablate each term singly against the primary metric *before* describing the objective as a design, and when the answer is "the extra terms are inert", say so — this paper does say so, in one sentence, but keeps the four-term objective in the method section and in the title of the ablation table, which is the compromise a reader has to notice. The companion finding in the same table is the one worth remembering: dropping the residual or family loss does raise coefficient error (5.30% and 6.34% vs 4.73%), so the inert terms are not inert on everything — the honest statement is "these terms matter for magnitude accuracy and not for structure", which is exactly the kind of per-metric attribution our read-outs should carry. Coreference arxiv-2611.20840 (a relevance metric maximised over a tuning parameter with no held-out split) and arxiv-2611.20311 (a derivation that must transpose to new data before it counts).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 303 file-side / run 305): `arxiv-2611.20983` — GRACE: Parallel Best-of-N Multi-Agent Analysis of Closed-Form Questions over Dataframes with Guardrail Selection and Adaptive Retry (Fabio Picariello, Salvatore Cipolla, Susanna Bonura, Vito Morreale — Engineering Ingegneria Informatica S.p.A., Roma; arXiv:2611.20983v1, cs.AI/cs.LG, 2026-11-16; ITADATA 2026, CEUR Workshop Proceedings, CC BY 4.0). Full text via HTML (~64K clean chars: abstract, §§1–7, Tables 1–3, acknowledgements, references). **Substance:** a label-free best-of-N selector for dataframe code. A description agent writes one authoritative schema from a 20-row preview; N code agents run concurrently under a three-clause output contract (one dict entry holding one pandas DataFrame, chart artefacts stored outside it with provenance links, a meaningful frame name) with internal self-repair so only runnable contract-satisfying candidates reach judging; diversity from four fixed personas plus a neutral anchor (agent 1 identical to N=1), one-step persona rotation per retry, and a temperature schedule 0.65 → 1.0; for N ≥ 3 a single-elimination pairwise tournament halts at two survivors so both finalists keep an advice channel; a guardrail judges program plus artefact preview jointly and either selects the least-defective candidate (narrative stripped of any reference to the selection process) or rejects the pool with global root-cause advice plus per-agent critique; rejection re-diversifies the whole pool and every retry must add a new invariant, assertion or state variable; budget exhaustion returns a diagnostic narrative. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (35B/3B-active MoE, 262k context, BF16) for all roles, Qwen3.5-9B dense as a downscaling probe; DAEval M = 246 and a fixed 400-question DataBench subset; answer match under 1% relative / 0.01 absolute tolerance; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples), BH at q = 0.1, TOST equivalence against margins equal to each benchmark's median measurement resolution. **Results:** DAEval 39.0% → 71.0% (N=2, r=4), 95/96 kept and 79/150 recovered; N=4 with no retries 61.8%; every non-baseline cell significant; 9B 37.8% → 63.4% (N=4, r=4) with 82/93 kept and 74/153 recovered, and unlike the 35B still gaining from agents under a generous retry budget; DataBench 69.8% → 85.0% (N=4, r=10), equivalence for 2 of 4 plateau steps (the other two small but not declarably equal); same 263 pools: selector 66.9% vs 77.6% oracle, voting 63.1% (+3.8 pp, CI [+0.3,+7.3], p = 0.03), random 62.9% (+4.0 pp, p = 0.02), voting vs random +0.2 pp p = 0.66 with 63.9% of pools showing no agreement and a majority cluster in 34.2%; conditioned on pool-contains-correct 176/204 = 86.3% selected correctly (17 wrong, 11 rejected) and on all-wrong pools 53/59 = 89.8% false-accepted, only 10.2% rejected; cost ~1.1× baseline tokens for N=1 with a moderate retry budget, ~2× for N=2 at the best accuracy, four agents paying for nothing, latency near baseline because agents run concurrently. **Limits they name:** abstention is the weak link and the next target; the input table is authoritative, so upstream extraction error is untested; arms are not compute-matched; no per-component ablation of personas, rotation, temperature, invariant forcing or the tournament; answer match cannot separate interpretation, computation, formatting and abstention errors; DataBench's baseline is partly a typed-answer floor effect.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 305): **A selector and a refuser are two capabilities, and an aggregate accuracy number can only ever publish their average — the split is one conditioning variable and it is the most useful table in this paper: given a pool containing a correct candidate the guardrail takes it 86.3% of the time, given an all-wrong pool it rejects the pool 10.2% of the time, so the system is strong at ranking and nearly blind to "none of these".** For our battery this is the missing breakdown behind every hit-rate we report: a probe that ranks candidate directions correctly when the right one is among them, and a probe that fires confidently on inputs where no direction is appropriate, produce the same aggregate score and support opposite claims. The reporting rule is cheap and exact — split the confusion on whether a true answer was available *to the instrument*, publish both conditional rates with their denominators, and stop describing the aggregate as a capability. It also tells you where to spend the next experiment: here the paper says plainly that the remaining gain is in the refusal half, not in more generators, and the reason is structural — a wrong rejection can still be recovered by retry while an all-wrong pool accepted has no path back. Coreference arxiv-2611.20583 (correct refusal with no retained evidence scores zero, the same asymmetry from the logging side) and arxiv-2611.21405 (a half-and-half split hidden inside a mean).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 305): **A consensus score over a population that never agrees carries no information, and the diagnostic is the agreement rate itself: here majority answer-agreement voting is statistically indistinguishable from picking at random (+0.2 pp, p = 0.66) because in 63.9% of decisions no two candidates agree at all and a majority cluster of size ≥ 2 exists in only 34.2% — with 3.66 valid candidates per pool, 2.32 of them correct.** Voting is the default reconciliation step in this literature and in ours: average the readouts across seeds, take the direction most probes agree on, keep the component that two methods both rank high. This paper is the clean refutation of running that step without first measuring whether agreement exists — when members are diverse by construction (and this pipeline diversifies deliberately), the vote is noise with a plausible name. Two measurements make the failure visible in advance: the pairwise agreement rate of the members and the modal cluster's size, both of which are one pass over the same data the vote was computed from. The companion move from the same section is the one that lets the paper make this claim at all: **hold the pool fixed and swap only the selector**, so selection quality is measured with the candidate-generation budget identical and the oracle ceiling printed beside the realised score — the control our own "probe versus baseline" comparisons should run before any claim about a read-out being informative. Coreference arxiv-2611.15168 (routing at 100% per grain and 76.69% pooled — the same aggregation cost, measured) and arxiv-2611.21586 (claim count rising 30% under a dictionary with no gain in verified recurrence).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 305): **A non-significant difference is not equality, and the instrument that says so is a two one-sided test against a margin the benchmark chooses in advance: four plateau comparisons here are tested by TOST with margins set to each benchmark's own median measurement resolution (±5.7 pp on DAEval, ±3.75 pp on DataBench), two clear it and two do not — and the paper reports the two that do not as *not declarably equivalent* — small differences that fail the margin, which is a different sentence from *no difference*.** Our entries routinely turn a lost p-value into a claim of equal performance between two read-out variants, and that move is exactly what this paper refuses. The operational detail worth copying: the margin is not a round number but a property of the measurement — the median resolution of the metric — so an equivalence claim on a probe score would have to be bounded by the score's own quantisation or seed spread, not by a conventional 0.05. Two further transfers from the same design: report the TOST interval rather than its verdict, and when the aggregate plateau hides a surviving increment at one factor level (DataBench keeps a small significant retry gain at N ≥ 2 where DAEval has none), say so inside the equivalence paragraph rather than in the appendix. Coreference arxiv-2611.20311 (a validated derivation record that must transpose to a new corpus) and arxiv-2611.21159 (a stochastic read-out's own noise floor as the unit for any "no change" claim).

convergence to cosine 0.99 at 56 of 720 prompts; both nulls pass by 10.66× and 12.76× their 95th percentiles (minima 7.22 and 5.96). **Restrictions the licence prints rather than hides:** the profile moves with the mixture (re-weighting 2.34 twin units against ~1 for a redraw, only 4 of 188 within one unit); eight statements length-sensitive, `With` 55% and `For` 49% of neurons flagged; companion matching fails for all eight compound statements (0.19–0.68 against a 0.15 cap) and costs 2.95 (`For`) / 5.50 (`With`) twin units where it can be re-weighted; `Try` 5.95 nats on a 0.088-nat baseline, `Lambda` 4.99 on 1.40. **Structure:** `for`-as-loop vs `for`-in-comprehension share 0.250–0.266 of carriers (0.198 `AsyncFor`) against 0.050 chance and a 0.872 ceiling; indented vs module `for` share 0.494 against scope ceilings 0.837/0.850, running 0.44 (`Match`) to 0.71 (`Try`) across the twelve scope pairs. Shared neurons cluster by **inventory** category — exception classes purity 1.000, warning classes 1.000, builtin functions 0.86, builtin types 0.73, comprehensions 1.000 (p = 0.004) — and *not* by grammatical category; surviving under a pooled-cell yardstick (38 of 189 tests significant, all inventory). **Probe comparison:** linear probe at the same read site 0.653 / 0.802 untrained on residual stream / hidden units, then 0.998 / 0.999 median at the first and last trained checkpoints, 145–148 of 164 at ≥0.99, minimum 0.902, AUC median 1.000 — unable to order anything, while its margin moves 13.8 → 16.5 → 14.8. **Three self-caught artefacts:** twin unit too small for intervals (corrected agreement above 1 for ~150 of 188), standardised size rises while raw falls (144 vs 148 of 169; `for` raw 15.7 → 184.5 → 143.0 → 96.0, standardised 30.2 → 239.6 → 270.9 → 251.5), peak layer moves for 41% of constructs when the last layer is excluded.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 233): **A reading's licence can be run before the effect is read, and the seven restrictions it prints are each a named class of claim it forbids — this paper is the first in the folder to invert the order, so the caveats arrive as constraints rather than as an apology, and the two that bite hardest were both found by the instrument's own checks: re-weighting the logged stimulus factors to a different mixture moves the profile 2.34 twin units when a fresh redraw of the same battery moves it about one, so "this construct's response is such-and-such" is licensed only *relative to a declared distribution*, and eight statements are length-sensitive at more than 5% of their neurons (`With` 55%, `For` 49%), so comparisons across prompt lengths are simply not available for them.** The form is worth copying exactly: two of the nine checks are hard gates (scrambled-label and split-half nulls must be cleared or nothing is read at all — cleared here by 10.66× and 12.76× their 95th percentiles, minima 7.22 and 5.96), and the other seven are *reported* regardless of outcome, each with the claim class it restricts written beside it. That is a cheaper discipline than a limitations section, because it is enforceable: our own battery already produces the artefacts — a mixture, a length dependence, an interval width — and the only change is to compute them before the headline number and print them next to the claims they bound. A second lesson sits in the appendix: the licence was re-run after a fault in how per-prompt vectors were joined to their prompts, and the corrected numbers *improved* the two null margins (10.1 → 10.7 and 9.6 → 12.8), which is the shape a healthy re-run takes — the instrument was understating itself, and the paper says so. (arxiv-2611.09196, arxiv-2611.05655, arxiv-2611.08438)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 233): **Standardising a reading against a baseline that itself drifts turns a shrinking effect into a growing one, and the paper catches it in its own headline statistic: the yardstick's spread narrows over training, so the standardised norm rises for 144 of 169 constructs while the raw norm falls for 148, and on the worked construct the raw response goes 15.7 → 184.5 → 143.0 → 96.0 while the standardised version goes 30.2 → 239.6 → 270.9 → 251.5 — the two curves disagree on the direction of the last two-thirds of training.** This is the folder's denominator lesson in its temporal form, and it is the one instance where the *corrected* value is the one that looks worse: every other entry's fix made a number look smaller and more honest, whereas here raw units make the model's response look like it is decaying. The stated rule is to report size on the raw form and concentration on the standardised one, because the two answer different questions and `σ0` is the only channel through which set C enters. The paired artefact is that the twin unit cannot serve as the interval width — the twins share their cores, so their disagreement measures surface variation only, and correcting agreement by it yields values above 1 for roughly 150 of 188 constructs, with intervals therefore taken from a core bootstrap whose coverage is itself checked (calibrated at the median, but optimistic by up to 7.17× for 33 constructs). For any metric we compute across checkpoints: print the raw series, the standardised series and the noise unit's own calibration factor, because a cross-checkpoint trend that inverts between two normalisations is not a trend yet. (arxiv-2611.09196, arxiv-2611.13548, arxiv-2611.05655)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 233): **A probe's accuracy saturates exactly where the interesting comparisons live, and the saturation is total rather than partial — 0.653 median on the residual stream and 0.802 on hidden units at initialisation become 0.998 at the first trained checkpoint and 0.999 at the end, with 145–148 of 164 constructs at or above 0.99 on a 0.902–1.000 range, so 169 constructs, 24 layers and 61 checkpoints cannot be ordered by it, the AUC median is a flat 1.000, and a harder two-role contrast (same token, loop role versus comprehension role) saturates just as completely at 0.999 against 0.68–0.75 untrained.** The reading that makes this a result rather than a complaint: at initialisation the probe is *partly* separating a contrast it should not be able to see at all, which is the random-feature-map effect the folder already has theory for, and after training it separates everything, so the probe's accuracy is measuring the model's competence at the task the stimuli define and not the geometry of the concept. The instrument that keeps resolving is the profile's carrier overlap, which is *low* on precisely the contrast the probe calls perfect, and each number carries a ceiling to be read against — 0.250–0.266 overlap for the two `for` roles against a 0.050 chance rate and a 0.872 twin maximum, and 0.494 for one role across two tokens against scope-restricted ceilings of 0.837 and 0.850. So the honest form of "the model represents X" is an overlap with a chance rate and a same-instrument ceiling, not an accuracy: the first can distinguish five-times-chance from under-a-third-of-ceiling, and the second cannot distinguish anything from anything. (arxiv-2611.09196, arxiv-2611.15735, arxiv-2611.13548)

Full text via HTML (~51K clean chars: abstract, §§1–7, conclusion, references). **Substance:** a design-oriented review, not a system — no model is trained or measured. Twenty core sources (arXiv 2023–2026, CNKI Chinese-language journals and theses, ACL Anthology, Home Assistant engineering posts) are searched to 2026-11-08 along three term dimensions plus memory and security/privacy and snowballed by reference, then field-coded on ten fields and mapped onto nine recurrent responsibilities of the home local server: device connectivity and capability registration, perception and event extraction, home state, memory management, model serving, agent orchestration, safe execution, cloud-edge collaboration, and feedback and auditing. Four distinctions are fixed before comparison (local-first vs fully offline; home state vs home memory; model vs agent; generative planning vs deterministic execution), and the recommended pipeline separates proposal from execution: models interpret and plan, state/memory/registry supply structured context, a policy layer routes and confirms, deterministic verifiers, graph constraints or time-limited execution leases confine actions to a legal space, device adapters execute and write audit records. Deployment styles are grouped into three routes (models and profiles local; state/orchestration/authorisation local with hosted inference; models embedded in devices), with the conclusion that what matters is which stages the home node holds rather than whether all inference runs offline. **Results:** none of its own; the framework's outputs are the module set, a five-dimensional evaluation framework (architectural capability, system resources, privacy, safety and reliability, human experience), six design principles (separate generation from execution, state precedes intelligence, layer memory and govern its lifecycle, orchestrate by responsibility, tier permissions by risk, ensure end-to-end auditability) and a research agenda. Quoted from the surveyed work: an on-device home-assistant model holding accuracy at 16-bit and 8-bit with a noticeable 4-bit drop on device service classification and 80–86% on noisy/out-of-domain instructions at 5–6 s per response; invalid multi-device commands as a pervasive failure hotspot across 13 models; memory retrieval alone failing to resolve elliptical commands while environment state and preferences are jointly required (bounded by the authors to that benchmark's tasks and tools); a graph-constrained conflict resolver tested on 203 rules across 70 apartment configurations; an edge tool-chain monitor at sub-second latency. **Honest concessions:** a single author with no screening/exclusion counts, no claim of exhaustive coverage, a CNKI corpus, a dated cutoff, no real-home deployment, and two judgments stated against its own framing — local deployment is not inherently safer, and technical continuity does not establish companionship's social or medical effects.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 304): **A responsibility table is a pre-registration device, and the version worth copying has three columns rather than one: name the module, name the way it specifically fails, name the number that catches the failure — capability misdescription → registration failure rate, state staleness → update latency, memory contamination → pruning coverage, quantisation degradation → TTFT and memory footprint, unauthorised execution → unauthorised action rate and refusal rate, missing or tampered logs → audit completeness.** This survey's Table 2 is nothing more than nine modules in three columns, and it is the cheapest discipline in the folder: our battery writes read-out tables that say what a component *is* and what it measured, and almost never says in advance what its characteristic failure mode is, which is why a null result has to be re-argued per paper instead of read off a grid. Written first, the table also fixes the comparison — a probe that fails by staleness cannot be rescued by a better extraction metric, and a circuit claim that fails by unauthorised action cannot be rescued by a larger faithfulness number — and it makes the negative result legible as "this module failed in its own way" rather than as a generic score drop. Coreference arxiv-2611.20583 (a refusal recorded nowhere is indistinguishable from an event that never happened) and arxiv-2611.20840 (a component whose relevance metric saturates because nobody named its failure mode first).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 304): **A review's most credible move is grading its own evidence per claim rather than at the top, and the tell is a quoted number that arrives with its own qualifier attached: this survey holds five evidence categories apart — reviews, prototypes, benchmarks, HCI/eldercare studies, vendor documentation — and uses each only for what it can support, so a platform's release note establishes functionality and never security, a prototype establishes an implementation path and never a longitudinal effect, and a benchmark's simulated home cannot be promoted into deployment evidence.** Two consequences for us. First, the failure it names explicitly is *substitution*: a simulated or virtual environment standing in for the real one, which is the exact error our own harnesses risk when a synthetic pair stands in for held-out data and a generated circuit stands in for a mechanism. Second, its two concessions run against its own thesis and are printed anyway — local deployment is not inherently safer, and a companion that talks every day has not thereby been shown to help — which is the discipline of stating what your framing cannot establish before a reader asks. Coreference arxiv-2611.21586 (a verifier that sees the text but not the group, the month, the method or the activation) and arxiv-2611.21405 (a mean published beside its range and the count on each side of the split).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 301 file-side / run 303): `arxiv-2611.21405` — Shaping AI's Beliefs Before It Generates: Human Sense of Agency in Creative AI (Zi Wang, Mahima Pushkarna — Google DeepMind; arXiv:2611.21405v1, cs.AI/cs.HC, 2026-11-16; NeurIPS 2026 Creative AI Track; CC BY 4.0). Full text via HTML (~102K clean chars: abstract, §§1–6, Appendices A–E). **Substance:** PaCC is a React/TypeScript front end over Gemini text, image and video models that interposes a belief-control phase before any media is generated — exactly three clarifying questions per cycle each with 3–5 options and a per-question "You Decide" delegation, a belief graph that draws user-stated entities solid and model-inferred entities dashed with typed relations and 2–3 candidate values per attribute (incremental JSON deltas, not regeneration), modality-level media attributes, a low/medium/high proactiveness tier, and a side-by-side prompt diff for approval — built from four design principles: intervene before generation, make assumptions visible, keep the possibility space open, calibrate AI autonomy. The backend estimates uncertainty over candidate attribute values and then withholds the numbers from the UI to avoid clutter. **Results:** eight participants from one institution (five AI researchers/engineers, two creative professionals, one UX researcher; AI artists excluded), 10-minute demo, 30-minute unconstrained multi-modal task, 20-minute questionnaire on a 1–5 scale (1 diminished, 3 preserved, 5 augmented): overall agency 4.09 (SD 0.84, range 2.5–5.0), control 3.89 (SD 0.69), ownership 3.22 (SD 1.49, range 1.2–5.0), authorship 2.75 (SD 1.13, range 1.5–5.0); greater/equal/lesser against their own tools 5/2/0 agency, 4/2/1 ownership, 6/2/0 control, 3/3/1 authorship; clarifying questions 8/0/0 on agency and prompt refinement 6/1/0 on ownership and 5/1/1 on authorship, the belief graph 4/0/2 and 3/2/2, attributes 4/2/0 and 3/3/1; half the participants (P1, P2, P3, P8) report high ownership and the other half (P4–P7) none; five of the six who rated both put authorship below control; expression is the lowest aspect on all four dimensions (authorship 2.77, beneath intent, process and outcome, whose values the prose gives in rough bands). **Stated as exploratory throughout, with one-sample effect sizes explicitly described as distance from the scale midpoint rather than treatment effects** — there is no control arm and the comparison is retrospective against familiar tools.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 303): **A polarised population summarised by its mean is a reporting failure, and the fix is three numbers plus a split rather than a better average: agency here reads 4.09 (SD 0.84) while ownership reads 3.22 with SD 1.49 over a 1.2–5.0 range, and the split that explains it — half the participants high, half none, four of them naming the interface's own option menus as the reason — is what a reader needs and what a mean deletes.** For our battery this is the standing hazard in every averaged read-out: a probe score of 0.7 computed as a mean over items or seeds can hide a population where some items are 0.95 and others 0.3 (a probe that fires on half the distribution), and a circuit metric averaged over prompts can hide the prompts where the mechanism is absent. The copyable reporting rule is the one this paper accidentally demonstrates: publish the mean, the standard deviation, the *range*, and the count of individual ratings on each side of the decision boundary — and if the range spans the whole scale, stop describing the result as an effect and describe it as a split. Coreference arxiv-2611.21159 (every stochastic read-out needs its own floor) and arxiv-2611.20445 (a dispersion number that has to be published beside the fidelity number).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 303): **Offering a reader a small set of candidate interpretations is not the same as giving them control — the constraint is the menu: four of the eight participants who felt no ownership over the result attributed it to being handed multiple-choice options at every step, and one said by the end they no longer knew whether it had been what they wanted in the first place.** This is the interaction-design twin of a hazard our own read-outs carry: an interface that presents three candidate hypotheses for a probe, three plausible circuits for a behaviour, or a shortlist of names for a feature has already collapsed a space before the person gets to speak, and the collapse is more persuasive than an opaque single answer because it looks like freedom. Two design consequences follow and the paper's own data supports both: keep an explicit delegation route ("you decide") so the person can hand a decision back deliberately rather than by omission, and score the near-miss *against* the presented set — the paper's half-and-half ownership split is measured against the participant's pre-formed intent, not against satisfaction with the tool. Coreference arxiv-2611.20432 (a read-out validated against an independent measurement rather than against its own output) and arxiv-2611.20441 (a component located is not a component explained).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 303): **The modality of an explanation changes what a reader can do with it even when the content is identical: the dialogue instruments (clarifying questions 5/1/1 and prompt refinement 5/1/1 on comparative authorship) beat the visualisation ones (belief graph 3/2/2, media attributes 3/3/1) while the belief graph drew both the "most useful" and the "least useful" votes from different participants — one because it confirmed a complex visual concept, four because its structure "did not reflect how I was thinking".** The folder has met this from the model side twice lately (a force-harness ladder where computing a quantity beat plotting it, and an additive summary whose readability depended on a uniqueness construction); this is the human-reader side of the same fact, and it is the argument for our published read-outs carrying a numeric form *and* an interactive or textual form rather than one polished visual. The specific warning to carry: a graph is an assertion about structure, so a reader whose mental structure differs rejects it as wrong rather than as partial, whereas a question is an invitation that can be answered without accepting the questioner's ontology. Coreference arxiv-2611.21099 (a presentation ladder that separates computing a quantity from formatting it) and arxiv-2611.21550 (an additive summary whose uniqueness had to be constructed before it could be read).

(3) **A failing case reported as the most informative row**: S-024 refused an unauthenticated Alert→Enforce attempt before any side effect but committed no audit entry for the refusal, scoring 0 on three of four components for Control = 0.250 — correct prevention with no retained evidence of the prevention. (4) **A dependency the composite hides and the paper surfaces**: the machine-verifiable audit chain is 0/36 → 35/36 yet is reported *outside* the four-component mean while still gating treatment traceability, which the authors flag rather than silently drop.

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 300 file-side / run 302): `arxiv-2611-20583-state-machine-governance` — State-Machine Governance of Adaptive Enforcement: Evidence from a Paired-Scenario Evaluation (Ifeanyi Williams Agbedo, Yanzhen Qu — Colorado Technical University; arXiv:2611.20583v1, cs.CR, 2026-11-16; IRB exempt and approved, 2026-07-20). Full text via PDF text layer (~38K characters: abstract, §§1–7, Tables I–V). **Substance:** an AI recommendation is held fixed as an input and only the *transition procedure* varies — a typed state-machine kernel (ZTGuard) over the states Monitor / Alert / Enforce, with block, deny and quarantine as actions inside Enforce, explicit guards before commitment, a seven-field attributable record (timestamp, actor, policy id, pre-state, post-state, evidence pointer, outcome) in a sequenced in-memory audit chain, a convergence check after enforcement, and a bounded rollback to the previous validated state — against a scripted operator baseline, on 36 matched scenarios (11 CICIDS2017, 11 CICIoT2023, 14 synthetic) run once per arm, with Check Point Smart-1 and Palo Alto Panorama represented by deterministic simulations. Control is the equal-weight mean of traceability, accountability, audit-chain completeness and reliable rollback (reversions must finish within 60,000 ms; no-reversion cases score 1). **Results:** 0.720 (SD 0.218) → 0.972 (SD 0.131), mean paired difference 0.252, medians 0.714 → 1.000, Shapiro–Wilk W = 0.891 p = .002, Wilcoxon V = 359 p < .001, Hodges–Lehmann 0.321 [0.295, 0.447], rank-biserial r = .899, 26 pairs better / 9 tied / 1 worse, retained-data recomputation p = 0.000042782; components 0.472 → 0.972 / 0.694→ 0.972 / 0.797→ 0.972 / 0.917→ 0.972; atomic consistency 34/36 → 36/36; audit chain 0/36 → 35/36 reported outside the composite; rollback timing on four cases per arm 1/4 → 3/4 within bound, median 21,015.5 ms → 741 ms, with S-036 breaching in both arms (143,720 / 120,561 ms).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 302): **When two arms of a comparison are scored by different rules, the honest report is the unmatched-predicate caveat *plus* a harmonisation replay — not a footnote, and not a silent harmonisation either.** Here traceability required a last record holding the scenario's starting state under treatment and merely any log entry under baseline, accountability differed in which entry was inspected, and completeness scored the last record against an average across entries; the paper states plainly that the observed difference may reflect procedural behaviour *and* scoring design, and then does exactly the control we should copy: it removes the treatment's audit-chain gate, and separately applies the baseline's both-states criterion to treatment, and reports that all 36 retained rows were unchanged — while still noting that only two predicates were harmonised and the others were not. The transfer to our battery is direct because our comparisons are almost always between instruments we built (a probe on layer 8 versus a surrogate read-out, a circuit metric versus a patched ablation): publish the predicate table side by side, run the harmonisation one criterion at a time, and keep the residual caveat when the harmonisation is partial. The failure this prevents is the one where a 0.500 component difference turns out to be the definition and not the mechanism — which is precisely what the paper says about its own largest component contrast. Coreference arxiv-2611.21586 (a matched three-arm comparison where the budget, not the rule, was held fixed) and arxiv-2611.20432 (a probe variant in which only the read-out's provenance varied).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 302): **A composite score should be published with its weight-sensitivity floor, and the floor belongs in the abstract-level claim rather than the appendix: across 286 weight vectors the effect ranged from 0.056 to 0.500 around a 0.252 headline, with the single-component-dominant contrasts at 0.302 / 0.257 / 0.237 / 0.213 — so the direction survives every weighting but its magnitude varies by nearly an order of magnitude, and only one component is doing most of the work.** That is the same structural fact our own composite read-outs hide: an equal-weight average of four probes whose component means move by 0.500, 0.278, 0.175 and 0.056 reports a number that is 60% one component at many weightings, and a reader who sees only the mean cannot tell a balanced improvement from a single moving part. Two reporting rules follow, and the paper demonstrates both: give one-component-dominant contrasts so the composition of the effect is explicit, and state that the sweep establishes stability under weights *not* construct validity — because a weighting analysis can never tell you whether the components measure distinct things, only that the arithmetic is not fragile. Coreference arxiv-2611.21550 (a level-share decomposition where mass concentrated in two features) and arxiv-2611.21099 (a presentation ladder whose rungs isolate formatting from computation).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 302): **A prevented event with no retained evidence is indistinguishable, later, from an event that never happened — and this paper has the row that shows it: the governed procedure correctly refused an unauthenticated state escalation before any side effect and committed nothing to its audit chain, scoring 0.250 for correct prevention.** This is the logging analogue of a failure our own interpretation reports carry by default: an ablation that suppresses a behaviour but leaves no recorded artefact of the suppression looks exactly like an ablation that did nothing, and an intervention the model declines to act on looks like an intervention whose read-out never fired. The paper's derived principle is the copyable rule — record refused attempts as carefully as committed ones, since the refusal is the evidence that the guard worked — and its companion boundary is just as useful: a formal recovery procedure can expose nonconvergence in an impaired dependency without forcing it to recover (60 s bound breached at 143,720 ms and 120,561 ms in both arms under deliberately degraded connector latency), so a bound detects a failure without demonstrating a repair. For us: log the null results of every intervention with the same schema as the positives, and never let a guard's silence count as a guarantee. Coreference arxiv-2611.20840 (a dictionary that caught a pipeline defect rather than a mechanism) and arxiv-2611.20445 (a support set that is stable and explains nothing).

In the matched comparison SAE features yield more claims (26 versus 20 clusters and 22 text for DS/DA and MLE/DS; 82 versus 42 and 45 monthly claims for SWE) but the verified recurs — see the Done line for the numbers — and no monthly or Business Analyst claim survives either correction. **Honest limits:** internships only, uneven months with a May–August collection gap, non-continuous 29-month span, no human judgement of labels or hypotheses, quotation checks that verify presence rather than interpretation, two comparisons never run for context length, and SAE generation costing $17.50 against $0.28.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 301): **An interpretability artefact whose finding a capable reader already recovers from the raw text has to justify itself on something other than the finding — and the only way to know is the three-arm comparison with the reader held fixed: here the same hypothesis-writer, the same sections, the same hypothesis cap and the same budget produce 26 claims with SAE features, 20 with clusters and 22 with text alone, and verification on held-out companies shows the same occupational contrast under both representations (48/98 against 5/98 from features, 60/98 against 7/98 from clusters), so what the representation changed was WHICH DEFINITION of the characteristic was proposed, not whether it exists.** For our battery this is the standing test before any read-out is called informative: give the downstream reader the raw activations or the raw inputs as a third arm, with the same budget, and report recurrence in held-out items per arm rather than claim counts per arm — because claim count rose 30% under the dictionary and the extra claims did not survive correction. The verifier design is the part worth copying exactly: it receives the definition unchanged and the text, but not the group, the month, the method or the activation, and a positive requires an exact quotation. Coreference arxiv-2611.20840 (a dictionary that caught a leak rather than a mechanism) and arxiv-2611.21099 (a harness whose ablation separates the contribution of the interface from that of the model).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 301): **A difference in feature activation can be a difference in how much text the model was given, and the tell is one extra column: here all ten Data Scientist Qualifications feature groups activate less often in the cluster whose median qualification section is 55 tokens against 140, so the read-out is length-sensitive in the same direction as the comparison it was used to explain — and in the paper's other dictionary the discovered clusters largely separate postings before and after January 2026 (89.2% modal-period match) while differing in description length from 39 to 160 tokens.** This is the confound our activation-rate read-outs carry by default, since a longer input offers more chances for two tokens to clear a presence threshold and more conventions to match: publish median token count per group in the same table as the activation rate, and match groups on length before comparing them (this paper re-runs its comparison on length-matched sections at a 1.25 character ratio for exactly this reason). The companion lesson is that a thresholded presence rule (two or more activating tokens) is a *choice* the paper re-runs at one token as a sensitivity check, and so should we. Coreference arxiv-2611.20432 (a read-out whose variance was compressed against the target's) and arxiv-2611.20897 (a support set certified about the wrong object).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 301): **When you have thousands of candidate comparisons and cannot read them all, the honest use of a distributional distance is as a selector with its bias stated, not as a test: MMD here sets the kernel bandwidth from the median pairwise squared distance on training vectors only, derives that the V-statistic is non-negative and biased upward by terms in 1/n and 1/m so two samples from the same distribution score above zero, and then spends its score on ranking which 81 pairs a language model reads in full — with two pairs dropped for context length and the five corrected quotations kept beside the originals.** The transfer is a triage discipline for our battery: any maximum over candidate comparisons (which layer, which head, which pair of checkpoints, which prompt pair) needs the same three parts — a reference-scale statistic computed on training data only, an explicit statement that the ranking is not a significance test, and a full read of the selected few with corrections logged. It pairs with the paper's other form of the same rule: ARI across seeds is reported as 1.000 for deterministic fits *and* explicitly discounted for saying anything about held-out generalisation, because repeating yourself on unchanged data is not stability. Coreference arxiv-2611.21159 (every stochastic read-out needs its own noise floor) and arxiv-2611.20311 (a derivation record that must transpose to a new corpus to count as validated).

- **Selection: the folder's best *non-neural* case that a decomposition is made unambiguous by construction rather than by loss weighting — and its best instance of a separation metric that needs no ground-truth factors at all.** It earns its slot on four things. (1) **Leak is blocked by architecture, and every ablation shows it coming back the moment the block is lifted**: the base-appearance decoder runs at half resolution with the finest skip connection deleted, so fine creases cannot reach it, and per-image refinement of colour and light is restricted to 16×16 residual fields — restoring the full-resolution base decoder raises retrained texture (0.52 → 0.59 on IITD) despite a *better* SSIM, which is the cleanest statement in the folder that a component can improve reconstruction while getting less separated. (2) **Separation scored against the input with no labels**: texture similarity between the base appearance and the *original input* (0.54–0.58 in 13 of 15 groups) is read against each database's own same-identity (0.71–0.80) and different-identity (0.54–0.56) levels, which is a separation number a reader can check without any ground-truth decomposition — the reference pairs are properties of the data. (3) **A two-stage split whose second stage is a free-standing optimizer**: the network only initialises, and the factors are then fitted per image through the same written rule (100 Adam steps, 203 ms), so the paper can say which of the two is doing the work — and it says it plainly: PSNR 38.45 → 41.80 dB within 20 steps on IITD, 31.13 → 41.98 dB on PolyU, with refinement costing a small rise in retained texture. (4) **An ablation whose numbers run against the headline**: dropping the overlap term during refinement would raise PSNR to 42.74 (IITD) and 54.12 (PolyU) from 42.62 and 48.38, so the separation constraint is bought with reconstruction and the trade is quantified rather than argued.
