- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 296 file-side / run 297): `arxiv-2611.20913` — Palmprint Decomposer: Interpretable and Editable Factorization via Synthetic Learning and Instance-Wise Refinement (Licheng Yan, Yuqi Wang, Jingtao Wang, Bob Zhang, Shuyi Li — PAMI Research Group, University of Macau; Andrew Beng Jin Teoh — Yonsei University; Lu Leng — Nanchang Hangkong University; Ziyuan Yang — Sichuan University; arXiv:2611.20913v1, cs.CV, 2026-11-16, arXiv perpetual non-exclusive licence). Full text via HTML (~67K clean chars: abstract, §§1–5, references, appendices A–F). **Substance:** one written-down multiplicative composition rule — a colour map times one plus a light map gives the base appearance, a scalar texture strength times a structure map gives the texture modulation, and the image is the base appearance attenuated by the modulation — with the four factors learned by a 9.26 M-parameter Factor Decomposer trained *only* on synthetic images whose factors are sampled directly (colour and lighting from low-order cosine modes, structure from coarse/medium/fine random curve families converted to a directional crease response) and therefore arrive as labels. Leak of fine creases into the base appearance is blocked architecturally (half-resolution base decoder with the finest skip deleted; 16×16 residual fields during refinement) and by a paired-image consistency loss (same base, different texture) and a lighting-variation floor; instance-wise refinement then fits the factors per image through the same fixed rule for 100 Adam steps with a Gabor response-overlap penalty (205.64 ms per image total against 2.49 ms for the network alone, on an RTX 4090). **Results:** refinement from a synthetic-only network reaches PSNR 42.62–59.39 dB, SSIM 0.974–0.999 and reconstruction-to-input texture similarity 0.96–0.99 across fifteen groups from seven databases; base-appearance texture similarity to the input is 0.54–0.58 in thirteen of fifteen groups, level with different-identity (0.54–0.56) and well under same-identity (0.71–0.80) similarities; structure-map verification is close to the originals (EER −0.22 and −0.33 points on Tongji and the mobile set, improvements on five of six spectral subsets, +0.68 and d′ −0.57 on one phone/flash condition); against smoothing and structure-from-texture baselines the base appearance retains far less input texture (0.521 versus 0.910 and 0.788 on IITD; 0.516 versus 0.903 and 0.764 on XJTU-UP) at comparable texture verification, while its intensity histogram matches the input less well; ablations show full-resolution base decoding raising leak to 0.59, removing consistency raising it to 0.66 on PolyU, and removing the lighting floor pushing leak into the colour map (0.49→0.57 on IITD); refinement does nearly all the reconstruction work (38.45 → 41.80 dB within twenty steps on IITD) at a small cost in separation, and dropping the overlap term would reach 54.12 versus 48.38 dB on PolyU with more leak; cross-dataset factor exchange over 42 ordered pairs averages 0.71 histogram correlation to the appearance donor and 0.87 texture similarity to the texture donor. **Honest concessions:** the formation model is an approximation and fails on mobile/flash capture; the supervised labels are the authors' own synthetic generator.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 297): **An ambiguity can be removed by construction instead of by a penalty term, and the test that it was removed is the ablation that puts the restriction back: here the base-appearance decoder is denied the finest-resolution skip and per-image refinement is limited to 16×16 residual fields, so fine creases cannot physically reach the base — and restoring the full-resolution decoder raises retained texture from 0.52 to 0.59 on IITD *while improving SSIM*, which is the folder's cleanest demonstration that a component can get more faithful to the image and less separated from it in the same step.** For our battery this is the argument for read-outs built out of restricted paths rather than out of losses: a probe with a narrowed receptive path, a surrogate with a fixed low-rank bottleneck, an attribution restricted to one block cannot carry the nuisance, and the restriction can be verified by construction rather than by a weight that is tuned — which matters because a weight is a hyperparameter a reviewer has to trust and an architecture is a claim a reader can check. Two companions from the same design: publish the *lifted* variant beside the restricted one (this paper's Full-res. Base row), and state the cost of the restriction in the reconstruction column, because the restricted architecture here loses PSNR (38.45 vs 39.52 on IITD) to buy its separation. Coreference arxiv-2611.21550 (a constraint imposed by a projection that leaves the prediction fixed) and arxiv-2611.20897 (a mask whose guarantee was about the masked model).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 297): **A separation metric that needs no ground-truth decomposition: score the component that is supposed to be free of a property by its similarity to the raw input on that property, and read the number against the data's own same-item and different-item levels — here the base appearance's texture similarity to the input is 0.54–0.58 in thirteen of fifteen groups against same-identity 0.71–0.80 and different-identity 0.54–0.56, i.e. it retains about as much identity-bearing texture as two different palms share and far less than two images of one palm.** This is the instrument the folder has been missing for 'we removed the nuisance': it costs one similarity function that the downstream task already uses, needs no labels, and produces three comparable numbers instead of one absolute value whose scale nobody can calibrate. It also carries a warning in its own table: their base appearance's intensity histogram agrees with the input *less* than a plain Gaussian smoother's does (0.676/0.657 versus 0.980/0.826 on IITD), so the metric that improves is the one the method was optimised against and the metric that degrades is printed beside it without comment — the pair is more informative than either column. Coreference arxiv-2611.20840 (a specificity entropy rather than a raw frequency) and arxiv-2611.20432 (an amplitude ratio rather than a correlation).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 297): **A separable two-stage design lets a paper say which stage is doing the work, and the honest answer here is nearly all of it is the second stage's per-image optimisation: the network's synthetic-only forward pass gives 38.45 dB on IITD and 31.13 dB on PolyU, twenty optimiser steps through the fixed composition rule take those to 41.80 and 41.98, and the reported headline of 42.62 and 48.38 is reached only at 100 steps per image, at 203 ms an image.** The transfer for us is a reporting rule for any fitted read-out: separate the *amortised* prediction from the *per-item* fit, print both, and price the per-item fit in time — because a summary that only looks right after per-example optimisation is a different artefact from one that generalises in a single forward pass, and the two support different claims (a mechanism versus a decent per-input solution). The second half is the trade the paper states rather than argues: the cost of the separation constraint is measurable in the reconstruction column (dropping the response-overlap term would give 54.12 versus 48.38 dB on PolyU), so each constraint in our battery should be quoted with the fidelity it costs, in the same table. Coreference arxiv-2611.21571 (a time-resolved explainer whose refinement is also external to the model) and arxiv-2611.20432 (a two-stage validation in which the second stage isolates the read-out).

(4) **A metric whose saturation the paper does not notice**: task relevance is `max` over ten thresholds of the adjusted mutual information between thresholded activation and label, with no held-out split for that maximisation, so a lucky threshold scores as well as a robust one and the top-n curves inherit the optimism.

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 295 file-side / run 296): `arxiv-2611.20840` — Interpretable deep concepts of organoid morphology (Lion J. Gleiter, Tingying Peng — Helmholtz Munich / Helmholtz AI and TU Munich, cs.CV, arXiv:2611.20840v1, 2026-11-16, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). Full text via HTML (~24.5K clean chars: abstract, §§1–5, ethics, acknowledgements, references). **Substance:** a BatchTopK sparse autoencoder (4,000 atoms over a 32,000-point convex hull, 32 codes per token) over the frozen last-layer patch and class tokens of DINOv3-large (14×14 grid) and ViTAMIn-O (7×7 grid), trained on ~60,652 organoid crops per epoch from five public datasets, with an auxiliary top-1 loss for inactive samples and a relaxed archetypal dictionary whose rows are a row-wise softmax over hull points. Each atom is then annotated on 1,000 crops per source: token type (background/border/organoid/global) via a 90% CI lower bound, top-5 prototypes, activation frequency, dataset specificity as a normalised label entropy, and task relevance as the max over ten thresholds of the adjusted mutual information between thresholded per-image activation and task label. **Results:** fewer than 32 top-relevant atoms reproduce full-dictionary AUROC on four of five downstream tasks; SAE features sit near the raw foundation features and at or above CellProfiler morphometrics; spatial labels transfer, DINOv3 concepts giving 81.7% vs 66.4% balanced accuracy on token-type classification in held-out datasets; filtering by spatial role improves budding-brain, PDLO and otic tasks for DINOv3 (with threshold-dependent gains) and not for ViTAMIn-O; the highest-relevance atom for abnormal brain organoids read the authors' own cropping padding, which correlates with the label, exposing a preprocessing leak. **SAE config:** top-1 loss cuts ViTAMIn-O dead codes 55.7% → 5.3% at the cost of R² 0.62 → 0.55; softmax decoder raises DINOv3 stability 0.59 → 0.84 and dead codes 32.9% → 11.4%; δ = 1.0 lowers dead codes further (0.4% / 7.1%).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 296): **A dictionary atom is not explained by being shown; it is explained by four numbers and a set of exemplars, and the four are chosen because each answers a different question — how often does it fire, where does it fire, how general is it, and does the task actually use it — so an account of a feature that lacks the general/specific axis is one that cannot tell a mechanism from a dataset fingerprint.** This paper's annotation set is the cheapest thing in the folder to copy and the most under-used elsewhere: activation frequency, a normalised entropy of the dataset label over the inputs where the atom is active (specificity), a spatial or structural role argued from a confidence-interval lower bound rather than a raw frequency, and top-5 activating inputs. Two design rules travel with it: state labels as *lower bounds* when the number of activating samples varies, and test whether a label *transfers* by using it on unseen data for a different task — because a name that stays with its atom is a different claim than a direction that stays with its feature, and only the transfer test distinguishes them. For our readouts the specific addition is the specificity scalar: publish, for every component we call a mechanism, the entropy of the conditions it fires in, so that an overfitted fingerprint is visible in the same table as a general circuit and cannot be summarised away in prose. Coreference arxiv-2611.15168 (per-task clusters justified by separability numbers) and arxiv-2611.21550 (a readable effect published with its share of the budget).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 296): **The most valuable thing a readable dictionary did here was catch a defect in the pipeline that produced it, not a mechanism inside the model — and the check that found it is available everywhere: rank features by relevance and look at their exemplar inputs, because a feature that is task-relevant AND artefact-correlated is a leak, and the label being present in the artefact is what makes it a leak rather than a finding.** The transferable instrument is a two-column audit: for every high-relevance component, its exemplar inputs and whether any property of those inputs that the model *should not* be allowed to know (padding, border colour, batch, scanner, framing, tokeniser padding) predicts the task label. This is the failure mode a predictive white-box model is structurally blind to — it will encode the leak faithfully, generalise on the collection it was built from, and report a confident mechanism — so a leakage audit belongs in the front of a battery rather than after a result looks too good. A second, methodological companion from the same paper: its relevance metric is a **maximum** over ten thresholds with no held-out split for the selection, so the top-n curves and the filtering thresholds inherit the optimistic bias; a maximum over a tuning parameter has to be quoted with the whole curve or fixed on held-out data, or a lucky threshold reads as a robust effect. Coreference arxiv-2611.20897 (a certificate silent about the label) and arxiv-2611.08767 (a surrogate's fidelity measured only where it was fitted).

- **Selection: the folder's first entry in which the uniqueness of an additive summary is *constructed and proved* rather than assumed, and the construction doubles as the folder's cleanest "change the explanation, hold the prediction fixed" operation.** It earns its slot on four things no other entry has. (1) **The degenerate-decomposition argument as a one-paragraph refutation of unconstrained additivity**: a full-order interaction can absorb the whole function and zero every lower-order term while satisfying the same sum, so an additive readout without a constraint is a parameterisation and not a measurement — the sharpest statement of a hazard our own per-component attributions carry. (2) **A transfer at the last linear layer that provably leaves the output unchanged**: each higher-order network's penultimate-layer matrix is projected onto the concatenation of all lower-order penultimate matrices, subtracted from the one and added to the others as weight updates, so information migrates downward with the surrogate numerically invariant — an invariant we can check to floating-point tolerance instead of by correlation. (3) **A scalar for how much of a model is readable at all**: because the order-k subfunctions are mutually orthogonal on the explanation sample the level variances sum to the total, so the low-order prefix I₁ + I₂ is a single interpretability budget (Boston/XGBoost: 0.9038 + 0.0543 = 0.9581 at surrogate-to-black-box correlation 0.9635) — a quantity that decides whether an additive summary is worth publishing for a given model, and one nothing else in the folder reports. (4) **A validation that is arithmetic and nothing else, stated plainly by its own structure**: fidelity is an in-sample correlation and the only guarantee is relative to the empirical measure of the explanation sample, with no baselines, no held-out set and no ground-truth function — which makes it the folder's purest example of a guarantee that is exact where it is proved and silent everywhere a reader would want it. - Done 2026-11-17 (entry 294 file-side / run 295): `arxiv-2611.21550` — ONAM: Fitting Orthogonal Neural Additive Models for Post-Hoc Interpretability of Black-Box Predictions (David Köhler, Matthias Schmid — Institute for Medical Biometry, Informatics and Epidemiology, University Hospital Bonn; arXiv:2611.21550v1, stat.ML, 2026-11-16, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Full text via HTML (~66K clean chars: abstract, §§1–5, acknowledgements, references, appendix proof). **Substance:** an R package implementing functional decomposition of a fixed black-box prediction function in three steps — sample feature rows with the black box's predicted values on them (the empirical measure the orthogonality is defined against), fit a neural additive model to those values with one small feed-forward sub-network per main effect and per declared interaction plus a catch-all full-order term, then orthogonalize top-down by projecting each higher-order network's penultimate-layer matrix onto the concatenation of all lower-order ones, subtracting the projection from the high term and adding it to the low terms as last-layer weight updates, which leaves the surrogate's predictions numerically unchanged while shifting mass into the readable effects; Theorem 1 (proved, with a block-matrix lemma in the appendix) shows the fitted subfunctions are hierarchically and stacked orthogonal and mean-centred on the explanation sample. **Results:** identifiability is the result — the decomposition is unique, so a single effect can be called *the* effect of a feature; the order-k variance shares sum to the total variance of the predictions, so the low-order prefix is a scalar degree of interpretability, and on the worked Boston-housing/XGBoost example (4 ensemble members, 508 explanation rows, 18 declared effects, 8 penultimate units, 500 epochs) the surrogate reaches correlation 0.9635 with the black box at I_1 = 0.9038 and I_2 = 0.0543, i.e. 0.9581 — with the authors' own prose restating those as 91.08%, 5.05% and 96.14%, a slip the entry flags. Cost: the orthogonalization pass is O(n|Θ|²b̄²) and normally under 1% of fitting time (about 350 s for the full Boston fit on one 8-core machine); numerical handling is QR with column pivoting dropping dependent columns, plus double precision across the R–Python boundary. No baselines, no held-out fidelity, no simulation study.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 295): **An additive summary of a black box is a parameterisation until a constraint is imposed, and the constraint that makes it a measurement is the one that pushes mass downward: without hierarchical orthogonality a single full-order interaction can absorb the whole function and every lower-order term can be set to zero, satisfying the same decomposition and explaining nothing — which is exactly the freedom our per-head, per-feature and per-component attributions have, and the reason their effect sizes are comparable across models but not across fitters.** The version of the constraint this paper implements is worth copying because it is checkable rather than conventional: project the higher-order component's output onto the span of all lower-order components, subtract it from the one and add it to the others, and the sum is invariant by construction, so the pairing is *changed attribution, unchanged prediction, verified to floating-point tolerance* rather than by correlation. Two companions from the same design: state the constraint relative to a named distribution (here the explanation sample defines the empirical measure, and the guarantee is exact only on it), and publish the mass split between orders as one number, because the level shares sum to the total and their low-order prefix is a single interpretability budget for the model — the quantity that decides whether an additive summary is worth publishing at all. Coreference arxiv-2611.08767 (a white surrogate fitted to a teacher, whose internals need not match) and arxiv-2611.18430 (a validation whose predicted profile was guaranteed by the decoder's construction).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 295): **A guarantee can be exact where it is proved and silent where the reader needs it, and the tell is a fidelity number that is also the fit objective: here the surrogate's fidelity to the black box is an in-sample correlation (0.9635) reported with no held-out set and no error pattern, so the theorem that the decomposition is unique says nothing about whether the decomposition is *of the black box* rather than of the surrogate's own convenience — the same collapse the folder met in a distilled student whose plain looser-fit variant scored better than the near-perfect one.** The reporting rule this fixes: for any surrogate or additive replacement model we publish, print fidelity on held-out inputs *and* on the inputs where the surrogate's error is largest, state the distribution the structural guarantee is relative to, and list at least one additive baseline (a plain generalized additive model, or an explanation computed from the model class itself) — because "our decomposition is unique" is only worth a sentence if uniqueness beats a conventional decomposition on something a practitioner cares about. The near-miss to avoid is the other way round: this paper's single-feature readout is a *different* functional of the same decomposition (Sobol indices) than the level variance share it headlines, so a decomposition can be almost entirely main effect and still concentrate its mass in two features — level share and feature share have to be published together or the reader is told half the answer. Coreference arxiv-2611.20897 (a certificate about the masked model, silent about the label) and arxiv-2611.11398 (a frozen random dictionary that matched the trained one).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 295): **A projection-and-re-add at the last linear layer is the cheapest instrument the folder has for separating "what the explanation says" from "what the model does": because the shift moves mass between subfunctions without changing any prediction, the operation can be applied and reverted and the invariant checked exactly, which is a stronger control than any correlation between two explanations — and it is the same arithmetic an ensembling step needs (orthogonalize each member, average the orthogonalized effects, orthogonalize once more) to keep the averaged explanation a valid decomposition rather than an average of parameterisations.** For our battery the two uses are direct: when we perturb an explanation (re-rank components, re-attribute mass, regularise a probe towards a prior) the first thing to report is the delta in the readout *and* the delta in the output with the same tolerance stated up front, and when we average readouts across seeds or checkpoints we have to re-impose the constraint after averaging, because a mean of constrained summaries is not itself constrained — the same failure as a mean over a mixture belonging to no component. Coreference arxiv-2611.15168 (a pooled direction that summarises no cluster) and arxiv-2611.20445 (an explanation trained to agree, with the dispersion to be reported beside it).

- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 294): **A mean over a mixture is a vector that belongs to no component, and the diagnostic is a cosine table rather than any downstream score: here the pooled global direction sits at a per-task average cosine of 0.364–0.654 from the clusters it is supposed to summarise, with one Relation cluster at −0.106 and one Count outlier at 0.063, while the pairwise cosines between the cluster directions inside a task run 0.030 for Distance and 0.055 for Depth — near-orthogonal, so the average shrinks in magnitude and what survives is the residual disagreement.** The arithmetic is the whole argument and it transfers without modification to every pooled direction in our battery: a "the model declines" vector averaged across three causes, a refusal direction averaged over several registers, an attribution mass-function averaged over items that fall in different circuits. The consequence is that a pooled vector's effect size is a function of how many components it averaged and how mutually orthogonal those components were, so two papers reporting the same effect size on differently heterogeneous pools are not reporting the same quantity. Two measurements to adopt by default — the cosine between the pooled direction and each subgroup direction, published per subgroup, and the pairwise cosines within the pooled set — and one decision rule: where those cosines are near zero, the honest object is a set of directions plus the routing rule that picks them, and the pooled vector should be reported as the *baseline that fails*, which is exactly how this paper reports it. Coreference arxiv-2611.20371 (unregularized probes favour intervention-unfaithful features) and arxiv-2611.20441 (a direction per cause rather than one pooled across causes).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 294): **Routing and steering are two read-outs and should be computed at two positions: the routing state is the last prompt token with no answer in context, the direction is a completion-span mean difference, so the routing claim can be checked with zero answer leakage before any steering result exists — 100% top-1 same-task routing per task, 76.69% with all twenty clusters pooled against a 20% floor.** Our battery fuses the two constantly: one probe decides something and also defines the direction that acts, so a failure in either half is unattributable. The cost of splitting them is one forward pass per support item at a position we already have, and it buys a routing number that stands on its own — and it is what makes their probe's weakness legible later (the same four-way probe that only serves reweighting keeps 18.67% top-1 on Depth and 36.50% posterior mass there, which is reported as a diagnostic and not used as the routing rule). Two companions from the same design: route to **real samples** rather than centroids so the representative stays on the data manifold (k-medoids, not k-means), and report routing accuracy at both scopes the user could plausibly want — per-grain and pooled — because the gap between 100% and 76.69% here is the entire cost of a shared bank. Coreference arxiv-2611.19684 (ranking versus selection as different quantities) and arxiv-2611.21539 (the ladder from behaviour to probe to intervention).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 294): **A component ablation can rank the fully-stripped variant *above* a partially-stripped one, and when it does the components are not independent: removing multi-center routing gives 39.54% while removing everything and falling back to the global mean gives 47.35%, so the local basis and the adaptive shrinkage only help inside a multi-center regime and were never the source of the effect.** This is a cheap sanity check that our own ablations should run by default — alongside the leave-one-out row for each component, publish the row that strips *all* of them, because the ordering between those rows is what tells a reader whether a claimed component is load-bearing or decorative. It pairs with this paper's other honest result: the two "refinements" move the four-task average by 1.00 and 0.33 points and act almost entirely on the single most geometric task (+3.12 and +1.04 on Distance), so a component that is reported as a contribution on an average can be a single-task effect that the average dilutes. Coreference arxiv-2611.11398 (the frozen-random-dictionary control that decided which scores were artefacts) and arxiv-2611.18430 (a decay profile implied by the construction rather than learned).

- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 293): **A black-box reader's competence with a stream is partly a property of the interface, and the way to find out how much is a presentation ladder: hold the action vocabulary and the evaluation seeds fixed and vary only the *form* in which the computed quantity arrives, always including a raw-samples row and a rendered-plot row between "nothing" and "our product".** Here the ladder runs no force / event words / force plot / tared raw numbers / harness-derived signals / L1 quantities / L2 + uncertainty + flags, and the honest readings only exist because of the intermediate rungs: for the strong model everything from a plot upward is a tie (0.87–0.91), while for the smaller models the plot collapses to 0.56 and raw numbers reach only 0.69 against 0.85 for computed quantities — and because derived signals tie L1 and L2, **the credit goes to computing the quantity rather than to formatting it**, which is the difference between an interface contribution and a presentation contribution. For our battery the transfer is exact: every probe read-out, circuit summary, surrogate coordinate or aggregated attribution we hand to a downstream reader (a model, a human, a threshold rule) goes through this ladder, with the raw and rendered rungs present, because our standing alternative is a probe score that looks informative only because of how it was printed. Coreference arxiv-2611.10297 (the baseline that turns a probe number into a claim) and arxiv-2611.21539 (the ladder from behaviour to probe to intervention).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 293): **Termination belongs below the reader: because each primitive ends on a contact event rather than on a clock, a decision-maker that thinks in seconds can still close a loop at the controller's rate — and the ablation shows the action vocabulary is doing work on its own, event words with no force values at all buying 0.63 → 0.77 for the strong model and 0.18 → 0.54 for the small ones, with handle damage falling from 22/25 to 3/25.** Two design facts make that package work and both are copyable: the primitive's lead-pose clamp is a bound on force that no caller can exceed (the safety is in the vocabulary, not in the model's judgement), and each call returns a *weighted* set of dependences — the judgement tasks, which have no stop event, are exactly where event words fail and a computed value is needed. For our battery this is the argument for small, self-terminating intervention primitives (knock out this head, ablate this direction, hold this probe fixed, stop on this event) with a fixed guard underneath, rather than free-form interventions requested in natural language, because the guard and the stop condition can be checked and the request cannot. Coreference arxiv-2611.20441 (a component located is not a component explained) and arxiv-2611.18382 (a repair verified by transplanting the donor).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 293): **A sensor you do not have can be replaced by controlling *when* you read rather than how you filter — tare at rest next to the coming contact, let the arm settle, average a still window, and report same-episode changes instead of absolute values — and the resulting estimate is accurate enough to decide a task the sensor's own specification would say is out of reach.** The numbers are unusually complete for a paper making this claim: force from joint torques alone with no wrist sensor, and mass error against simulator truth at a mean of 0.004 kg with an SD of 0.03 kg, CoM direction cosine at least 0.97, real-robot bottle sorting and soft-vs-hard both 10/10. The discipline that makes it credible is that the printed uncertainty is stated to cover **measurement noise only**, with the calibration error reported separately as mean and SD — the two are never merged into one interval. That convention is the one to copy for every read-out we publish: estimation noise and calibration error are different quantities, and a battery that reports one number is reporting whichever is larger while implying both. Coreference arxiv-2611.20432 (a read-out validated against an independent measurement, with the amplitude ratio reported beside the correlation) and arxiv-2611.21159 (every stochastic read-out needs its own floor).

Full text via HTML (~108K clean chars: abstract, §§1–6, Appendices A–J, all ten tables). **Substance:** eight clients per dataset across six benchmarks in three modalities (MNIST, CIFAR-10, AG News, IMDb, UCI Adult, UCI Credit) plus an MRI Alzheimer's and a credit-card-fraud testbed, IID and Dirichlet-label-skewed non-IID, 15 rounds, one local epoch; each client distils a small on-device surrogate by temperature distillation, explains the surrogate with a path-integrated gradient in a low-dimensional group space normalised to a simplex, top-k compresses it as index–magnitude pairs with L2 clipping, quantisation and Gaussian noise, and uploads only that artefact under secure aggregation; the server takes a coordinatewise median per class, renormalises, and broadcasts a Global Explanation Prior that enters each client's **surrogate** objective as a Jensen–Shannon alignment term with a six-round warm-up, never touching the task model. **Results:** FedAvg accuracy held (MNIST IID 0.986, non-IID 0.930; CIFAR-10 non-IID 0.460; IMDb non-IID 0.702 against 0.550 FedAvg) with EDI 0.000 / 0.076 on MNIST against 0.110 Local-XAI, 0.159 FedAttr-Agg and 0.300 Fed-XAI, the last of which pays 0.449 accuracy under label skew; alignment-weight ablation moves EDI 0.006 → 0.0006 with deletion/insertion AUC unmoved; attribution poisoning at a 0.2 poisoned fraction changes top-k support by 0.0008 against 0.0041–0.0043 for every baseline, holding to 0.3 and converging at 0.4; membership-inference advantage differences are hundredths and several baselines tie, so the privacy claim is directionally supported and weakly measured; overhead about 1,600 KB/round against 1,589 KB for FedAvg, a ten-thousand-parameter surrogate that never leaves the device, GPU training 39.10 s against 32.15 s.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 292): **An explanation that is *trained* to agree is a different object from one that is measured to agree, and the tell is that agreement rises with regularisation the mechanism never asked for: here letting each client's student sharpen further makes the explanations drift *more* (EDI 0.0007 at one refinement epoch to 0.0012 at four), while adding noise before the shared median makes them drift *less* (0.0091 at zero noise to ~0.0007–0.0012 once noise is on) — the paper calls the noise implicit regularisation and does not run the control that would separate "the prior found shared structure" from "the prior smoothed away idiosyncrasy".** For our battery this is the sharpest version yet of a standing rule: any summary we aggregate across a population — probes trained per checkpoint, per-layer attributions averaged over seeds, surrogate read-outs per client or per shard — has to be reported with **the dispersion at zero coupling and at increasing coupling**, because if the aggregate agreement term is the only thing creating consensus, then the consensus is a property of our aggregation channel. The two facts to print together are the dispersion and the per-item fidelity on the same items, which is exactly what this paper's alignment-weight ablation does when it holds deletion and insertion AUC flat while EDI collapses — that pair is the positive control the noise and refinement ablations lack. Coreference arxiv-2611.11398 (an untrained random dictionary deciding which SAE scores were artefacts) and arxiv-2611.21539 (a probe whose edit moves nothing while the model's own direction moves everything).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 292): **A cross-method consistency comparison needs a method-specific reference, otherwise the comparison is between four differently-defined quantities: they score client divergence against the prior for their own method, the aggregated template for FedAttr-Agg, the unweighted client mean for Local-XAI and the interpretable model's class-weight vector for Fed-XAI, so each method is asked how coherent it is with respect to the system-level object it actually produces.** The folder has met the same problem from the other side twice (a size-matched random partition as the null for a concentration claim, a frozen random dictionary as the null for specificity); this is the complementary construction, a reference that is *matched to the method* rather than to an independent truth. Both are the same principle: before comparing two summaries, decide which object each one is a summary *of*. The cost is visible in this paper's own table — Fed-XAI wins EDI outright on MNIST IID (0.001) but only because its reference is its own linear class weights, and it loses 8 accuracy points to buy it — which is why the drift number has to be published beside accuracy and fidelity rather than alone. Coreference arxiv-2611.10297 (the baseline that turns a probe number into a claim) and arxiv-2611.19889 (a ranking that describes the checkpoint).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 292): **Two instability measures on the same artefact answer different questions, and a robustness claim should report both: the change in the top-k support set says the attacker failed to move *which* groups are named (0.0008 against 0.0041–0.0043 at a 0.2 poisoned fraction) while the change in cross-client divergence says the attacker also failed to spread the named groups apart (0.003 against 0.005).** This is the magnitude-versus-ranking split the folder already carries, here applied to a *support set* rather than to per-feature values, and it is the third distinct place the split has appeared, which is enough to make it a default: for any explanation we evaluate under an adversary or a perturbation, publish (a) overlap of the named set, (b) dispersion of the mass inside it, and (c) the downstream behaviour that is supposed to be defended — because a median aggregate and a top-k projection each suppress a different one of the three, and the paper's own numbers show both of theirs saturating at a 0.4 poisoned fraction once an attacker controls enough clients to move the median itself. Coreference arxiv-2611.21159 (magnitude and ranking instability diverging under a frozen model) and arxiv-2611.20897 (a support set that is exactly certified and explains nothing).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 290 file-side / run 291): `arxiv-2611.20432` — Validating Acoustic-to-Articulatory Inversion with Real-Time MRI: From Vocal-Tract Fidelity to Phonetic Consequences (Tharinda Piyadasa, Michael Proctor, Amelia Gully, Tuende Szalay, Emily Kiff, Kirrie Ballard, Craig Jin — University of Sydney / Macquarie University / University of York; arXiv:2611.20432v1, eess.AS, 2026-11-16, CC BY 4.0). Full text via HTML (~24K clean chars: abstract, §§1–4, acknowledgments, references). **Substance:** paired real-time MRI and speech, 358 utterances from 14 speakers of Annot-16 (tracked midsagittal contours over the USC 75-speaker database; read passages, nonsense VCV, picture descriptions, monologues; 16 kHz in-scanner audio, denoised), with eight vocal-tract variables derived from the contours (lip aperture/protrusion; tongue-tip/body/root constriction degree against palate or posterior pharyngeal wall; tip/body constriction location as normalised hard-palate arc length 0–1; velic aperture) and predicted at 50 Hz from audio by a frozen WavLM-Large encoder with learned layer weighting plus a two-layer BiLSTM (256 units/direction), trained with MSE on ~2 h of paired data, checkpointed on mean Pearson correlation, evaluated speaker-independently. Two fidelity numbers per variable: correlation and the predicted-to-observed SD ratio. Then a matched synthesis probe — a six-layer Transformer (dim 384, speaker embedding, five-layer conv postnet, 80-bin log-mel, HiFi-GAN) pretrained on 31,651 pseudo-labelled LibriTTS-R utterances (53 h) and fine-tuned on MRI-derived TVs — driving each held-out utterance twice from inferred vs measured TVs with log-F0, voicing and speaker embedding fixed. **Results:** mean r 0.643, degrees recovered far better than locations (TTCD 0.850, TRCD 0.794, TBCD 0.742, VEL 0.737, LA 0.720 vs TTCL 0.475, LP 0.488, TBCL 0.340); SD ratio below 1 for **every** variable, mean 0.775, min 0.595 (TBCL) — systematic range compression, worst where correlation is worst. Aggregate synthesis: inferred TVs give 35.8% WER / 23.1% CER / 3.77 dB MCD against measured TVs' 39.6% / 26.2% / 3.86 dB, i.e. the model's own estimates synthesise slightly *better* than the ground truth. Controls: 7.7% WER vs a 5.4% reference in the clean pseudo-labelled domain, 10.7% vs 10.3% for mel-through-vocoder, 72.7% CER with constant TVs. Per-phone spectral gap: 0.71 dB vowels (n=2,488), 0.40 dB approximants (369), 0.75 dB stops and nasals (798), 2.47 dB fricatives and affricates (558) — 2.07 dB above approximants, so narrow constriction alone is not the explanation; fricatives alone 2.25 dB (508), affricates larger on 50 tokens. /s/–/ʃ/: centroid separation 1,136 → 723 Hz after synthesis, Cohen's d 1.48 → 0.92 (62% retained), 47 /ʃ/ tokens, band limited to 8 kHz.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 291): **Validate a read-out against an independent measurement, then score it by whether its errors matter downstream — and build the second stage so that only the read-out's provenance varies.** The design here is the template: one trajectory is measured (MRI contours), one is predicted from audio, and the same synthesizer with the same weights and the same oracle F0, voicing and speaker embedding is driven from each, so the output difference isolates the read-out and nothing else. For our battery the transfer is direct and cheap: when we claim an internal quantity (a probe's decoded state, a circuit's attributed mass, a distilled surrogate's coordinate) is a measurement, hold the downstream head or behaviour fixed, swap the prediction for the ground truth, and report the difference per item — never only in aggregate. The reason to be strict is the failure this paper reports plainly: the aggregate points the *wrong way*, with the model's own estimates synthesising to lower error than the measured articulation (35.8% vs 39.6% WER, 3.77 vs 3.86 dB MCD), so an aggregate delta of the usual size is not evidence of fidelity in either direction. Coreference arxiv-2611.21539 (the probe that decodes but does not drive the output) and arxiv-2611.18382 (a localisation that does not repair).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 291): **Correlation is blind to the failure mode a read-out is most likely to have, and one extra number catches it: divide the prediction's spread by the target's.** Here the variance ratio is below 1 for every one of the eight variables (mean 0.775, minimum 0.595), so every inferred trajectory is compressed — confident, correctly signed, and systematically too small — and the compression is worst exactly on the variables that correlate worst (tongue-body location 0.340 correlation, 0.595 ratio). This is the regression-probe analogue of the attribution-magnitude instability already in the folder: a read-out can be right about ordering and wrong about scale at the same time, and the order-preserving statistic everyone reports will hide it. Our own linear probes and surrogate read-outs almost certainly compress too, so the standing rule is to print correlation and amplitude ratio side by side, per quantity, with a note on which of the two the downstream use actually depends on — an intervention or a threshold needs the scale, a ranking does not. Coreference arxiv-2611.21159 (magnitude versus ranking instability under a frozen model) and arxiv-2611.18430 (an attribution that moves while the prediction does not).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 291): **When the average effect is null, pre-declared bins are what turn it into a finding — and the bins must be tested against a competing explanation, not just looked at:** grouping phones by characteristic constriction in the Articulatory Phonology sense gives 0.40–0.75 dB for vowels, approximants, stops and nasals against 2.47 dB for fricatives and affricates, and the paper rules out 'narrow is expensive' by noting that approximants are also narrow yet cost about as little as vowels — what distinguishes the critical class is that turbulence generation depends on *fine* geometry, which is exactly the variable (constriction location, r 0.34–0.48) the model recovers worst. That chain — mechanism predicts where the error should be, the conditional measurement confirms, a plausible alternative binning is excluded — is the form our intervention and ablation reports should take. Two companion habits: declare the bins before looking (this grouping comes from an external framework, not from the data), and report token counts beside every conditional number, since the largest-looking effect here (affricates) rests on 50 tokens and the most interpretable one (/ʃ/) on 47. Coreference arxiv-2611.11398 (a size-matched random partition as the null for a concentration claim) and arxiv-2611.21096 (a claim valid only if every compatible state supports it).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 289 file-side / run 290): `arxiv-2611.20897` — Certified, Not Explained: Exact Token Erasure in Gated Vision State Space Models (Sadia Parveen, Tehseen Zia — COMSATS University Islamabad; arXiv:2611.20897v1, cs.CV, 2026-11-16). Full text via HTML (~70K clean chars: abstract, §§1–8, broader impact, reproducibility, references, Appendices A–E including the full pre-declared-test table). **Substance:** one concept-bottleneck model on LIDC-IDRI (764 nodules, patients 0001–0600, one axial slice, 64 patch tokens of dim 192, single bidirectional gated S6 block with inner width 384 and state 16, mixers from Vim-Tiny layer 0, six contiguous 64-channel concept groups, malignancy = logistic regression on the six concept probabilities), trained in two stages with nodule masks for a random half of training patients; baselines are a small ResNet and two-layer ViT as CBM and unconstrained, and the same Mamba block ungated. Three propositions: convolution-input masking empties the scan of closed content; plus zero pooling weight on closed tokens gives exact logit invariance; at depth the input-projection and residual gates are required (either step-size gate is neither necessary nor sufficient). Verified by a path-by-path knockout over 15 models (5 patient-level folds × 3 seeds) with the gate pattern forced and only closed tokens corrupted (Gaussian SD 50 or air): all seven conforming configurations exact in 15/15, the three violating ones broken in 0/15. **Results:** pooled OOF AUROC 0.8425 ± 0.0085 in the abstract (per-seed 0.8422/0.8342/0.8512 in Table 2), level with the ungated Mamba CBM (0.8428) and CNN CBM (0.8440), trailing the ViT CBM (0.8880, significant in 2/3 seeds), and falling to ~0.79–0.81 with the gates but *without* mask supervision — which is the honest reading, since no baseline could use that supervision; concept Spearman trails both other backbones and the ungated CBM shares the deficit, so it is a backbone property. Depth: two-block gating exact even when the second block re-opens 30% of tokens; convolution-mask-only with re-opening leaks, gating the projection but not the residual leaks far more. Audit, all pre-declared and mostly failing: deletion-max may be read only from prose, but the three post-hoc rankers beat the gate (gate wins 3/15 against MambaLRP with Wilcoxon p≈0.05 and 0/15 against hidden attention); ROAR-lite (top 16 of 64 tokens set to air, unconstrained Mamba retrained, seed 0) gives 0.8740 no-removal → 0.8265 random → 0.7206 gate → 0.7017 hidden attention → 0.6466 centre, so the gate loses to the crop's centre prior on centred crops; on 24-px-shifted crops the same ladder is 0.8516 → 0.8226 → 0.6655 → 0.6426 → 0.8859, where removing the centre now *raises* AUROC (regularisation, since it holds mostly parenchyma) and the gate does beat both priors, but still not hidden attention (81% token overlap); label randomisation is the sharpest negative — a model retrained on permuted concept and task labels with real masks produces backbone gate maps as similar to the real model's as two real-label seeds are to each other (similarity 0.69 as the floor) and localises at least as well (EPG 0.69 vs 0.58), so the maps are mask supervision and not labels. Leakage: OIS decomposition finds 54–60% of the score is its diagonal; partitioning the readout lowers excess cross-concept predictability under the earlier recipe (survives a PCA-64 dimension control, OIS does not register it) but the final mask-supervised model sits *at* rather than below the concept-correlation oracle level, so that pre-declared check fails.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 290): **A certified support set is not an explanation, and the test that separates them is retraining with permuted labels and comparing map similarity to the seed-to-seed floor: here the guarantee holds on every held-out image (logit change exactly zero in 15/15 runs for every conforming configuration, 5.4–6.7 when a precondition is broken) and the maps still fail — a permuted-label model's gates are as close to the real model's as two real-label seeds are to each other, and localise as well.** The reason is structural and worth carrying: what was certified is an invariance of the *masked* model to what the mask hides, and the mask was produced by localisation supervision, so the certificate is silent about the label, about the open set's clinical meaning, and about why the score is what it is. For our battery the consequence is a two-part reporting rule for any read-out described as faithful: state the precondition, ship the check that verifies it per input, and then run the separate question — does the thing survive label randomisation — because a map can be exactly faithful and completely uninformative about the mechanism at the same time, and only the second test can tell you which you have. Coreference arxiv-2611.11398 (a frozen random dictionary that agrees with the trained one on specificity) and arxiv-2611.21539 (seen but unsaid).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 290): **A baseline that encodes the data-collection procedure will beat a real explanation, and the only way to find out is to break the procedure on purpose: on crops centred on the nodule, removing the centre block out-ranks a learned gate (0.6466 against 0.7206 pooled AUROC after ROAR-lite removal), and on crops shifted by three tokens the same prior collapses the other way — removing the centre now *raises* AUROC to 0.8859 from a 0.8516 reference, because the block holds mostly parenchyma and its removal acts as regularisation.** Two lessons, one for casting and one for metrics. Casting: the centre prior here is not a spatial heuristic, it is a restatement of how the crops were cut, and any evaluation whose trivial baseline coincides with an artefact of preprocessing is measuring the pipeline; the shifted-crop repeat is the fix, and it should be pre-declared (this one was). Metrics: a removal curve can move in the *helpful* direction when the input is off-manifold, so a deletion or occlusion score is only interpretable beside an untouched reference on the same inputs, and a ranking that loses to random removal is a different finding from one that loses to a prior that happens to point at the target. Coreference arxiv-2611.21159 (the seed-noise floor as the denominator) and arxiv-2611.18430 (a perturbation profile implied by the read-out's construction).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 290): **An aggregate leakage score can be large for the wrong reason and can order two models backwards, so the diagnostic is the decomposition: 54–60% of the Oracle Impurity Score here comes from its diagonal — how weakly each concept is predicted from its own feature group — while the part that means "leakage" is the off-diagonal excess over what correlations among the true concepts already imply.** Two habits for any per-group probe read-out we publish. First, subtract the oracle: predicted-group predictability should be scored against probes trained on ground-truth concept values, and against a dimension-matched control (their PCA-to-64 arm is the cheap version), because a 384-channel group trivially predicts more than a 64-channel one. Second, never report the aggregate alone — in this paper the aggregate is flat (or inverted) across exactly the comparisons where the parts move correctly, and a change in the recipe (adding mask supervision) raised cross-concept predictability more than own-concept predictability without moving the score. The positive result is small and honestly sized: the partition effect is on the order of 10⁻² AUROC units and vanishes at the final recipe. Coreference arxiv-2611.05655 (when two latents are the same feature) and arxiv-2611.19889 (a ranking that describes the checkpoint).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 288 file-side / run 289): `arxiv-2611.18430` — Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy (Miguel Tenorio, James Chapman — Boston University, Mechanical Engineering; arXiv:2611.18430v1, cond-mat.mtrl-sci, 2026-11-13). Full text via HTML (~62K clean chars: abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, data availability, references; supplementary figures absent). **Substance:** one chemistry (CoMoFeNiCu high-entropy alloy) at three stoichiometries varying only Co (15/35/55 at.%, Fe/Ni/Cu fixed at 10%), 500 random configurations each, ~877 binary and ~4,442 ternary DFT decomposition-pathway graphs (random half of the ternary set used); structures chosen by grid-sampling the UMAP projection of an untrained 6-layer GNN encoder; two 6-layer ALIGNN-style GNNs (100 channels, 3.5 Å cutoff, batch 5, 1500 epochs, AdamW, L1 loss) trained deliberately to overfit, one per pathway type and cross-evaluated on the other; output head forced positive and normalised so each descriptor instance's decoder output is an additive contribution, aggregated per chemical motif and normalised within descriptor class to a fractional share — the quantity ranked and plotted. Validation is a single atomic swap (Co↔Fe in Co₅₅, Co↔Mo in Co₃₅, both directions) with the mean score change plotted per neighbour shell outward from the swapped site. **Results:** in-distribution R² 0.99 with MAE 14.26 (binary) and 7.70 (ternary) meV/atom, hit rates 100% and 99.8%; cross-pathway, binary-trained on ternary gives R² 0.308 and best-fit MAE 665.43 meV/atom after a −0.301 slope correction at a 13.6% hit rate, ternary-trained on binary gives R² 0.943 and 110.26 meV/atom at 92.1% — while the discussion separately states R² 0.26 for that same evaluation, an internal inconsistency the entry records rather than resolves. Rankings: Co's share rises monotonically and overtakes Mo between Co₁₅ and Co₃₅, Fe/Ni/Cu stay low throughout, Co–Co becomes the leading bond type at Co₅₅, mixed Mo–Co–Co and Co–Co–Mo triplets lead at every composition, and three-body ranks above two-body; the ternary-trained model reproduces the binary-trained model's ranking on binary structures despite its failing predictions. Swap test: largest change at shell 0 (the swapped atom), decaying to zero within two to three shells, matching the 3.5 Å receptive field — but the prediction barely moves (DFT enthalpy 0.197 → 0.198 eV/atom with the model's own 0.208 → 0.186; DFT −0.707 → −0.707 with the model's −0.707 → ~−0.693). No shuffled-score, random-init, same-species-swap or significance control is run, and no limitations section exists; the authors flag the positive decoder as a possible source of the clean rankings and defer testing it.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 289): **A perturbation test whose predicted profile is implied by the read-out's construction cannot validate the read-out: because the decoder is additive and positive-normalised, the score at a site is mechanically tied to the atom occupying it, so "the largest change is at shell 0 and decays with the receptive field" is guaranteed for *any* such decoder and holds whether or not the network learned chemistry.** The refutable version of the same test costs one arm and is the one our battery should adopt: run the swap on two atoms of the *same* species (structure changes, the encoding the decoder keys on does not), and re-score with a randomly initialised encoder — if the decay profile survives both, the finding is a property of the architecture, which is a real result but a different claim, and the paper's headline would have to change. This is the folder's third meeting with the same failure in different clothes (a frozen random dictionary deciding which SAE scores were artefacts, a size-matched random partition deciding whether spatial concentration meant anything, an untrained random sparse code deciding whether a downstream win was learned), and the general form is worth stating once: **a validation is only as strong as the weakest property the null object could also satisfy.** Coreference arxiv-2611.11398 (the frozen-random-dictionary control) and arxiv-2611.18382 (competitors given our rule on their own candidate set).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 289): **An explanation that moves a lot while the prediction moves almost not at all is a dissociation to be reported, not a robustness to be praised: a composition-preserving swap reshuffles per-atom scores substantially in both directions while the model's output shifts by 0.022 eV/atom in one structure and 0.014 in the other, against DFT shifts of 0.001 and 0.000.** The paper reads the stability as the model keeping the global property while tracking local detail; the folder's own thread says the opposite reading has to be ruled out first — an attribution whose totals are conserved by construction redistributes mass under any input change, exactly as a Shapley summary must, so the informative number is the share of attribution mass that moved *without* the output moving, published beside the output delta. The second half of the artifact is the explanation's own arithmetic: a swap between two atoms of *different* species changes composition locally but not globally, so a model with a strong global-composition term should barely respond, and the reshuffle is confined to the edited neighbourhood — which is what the shell plot shows. Our analogue: after any single-site intervention, report Δoutput and Δinternal-readout together, and treat "readout moved, output didn't" as a claim needing a same-species or same-token control before it becomes a mechanism. Coreference arxiv-2611.21159 (attribution magnitude vs ranking instability under a frozen-function wrapper) and arxiv-2611.04112 (a readout that moves while the verdict stays wrong).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 289): **A ranking can survive a distribution shift that destroys the number it was computed from, which is a genuinely useful dissociation — and the paper reports it as its most surprising result: the ternary-trained model on binary pathways is at R² 0.26–0.308 with a 665 meV/atom scale error, yet its per-element ranking reproduces the binary-trained model's across all three stoichiometries, Co dominance included.** The reading offered is that the compositional axis is strong enough to be captured either way, and the practical lesson for us is that ranking-level agreement and value-level agreement must be scored separately, because a white-box summary that only preserves ordering can be transferred to inputs where the model is simply wrong and look validated. The same dissociation runs the other way in this paper's own discussion: the ranking is offered as evidence the model learned chemistry, while the value error on the same inputs shows it did not learn the physics of that pathway type — so whichever of the two a reader believes, the other has to be explained, and the paper explains neither. Coreference arxiv-2611.19889 (a ranking that describes the checkpoint) and arxiv-2611.21348 (a frozen read-out going stale while reconstruction recovers).

- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 288): **A selector's own objective cannot be used to score it, and the cheapest way to make that principle bite is to give every competitor the selector's rule restricted to the competitor's candidate set: the critical predicate beats random, nearest-threshold and most-shared predicates on measures it does not optimise (separation contrast 0.262–0.336 against 0.105–0.157, 0.038–0.144 and 0.290 at worst), but once contrastive TreeSHAP and LIME are allowed the same gain rule on the feature they rank first, the margin shrinks to 18–44% flips against 15–37% and 12–32% in 3 of 4 families and vanishes on AdaBoost.** For our battery the transfer is direct: a probe, a circuit-ranking or an attribution summary should be scored on a measure that is not the quantity it maximises, and every rival should be re-run with our aggregation rule on its own outputs, because "our heuristic beats their heuristic" is almost always "our search space is larger than their restriction of it". The third arm that keeps this honest is the oracle: reporting what perfect foresight would achieve separates a selector that is close to optimal from one that is merely better than its baselines, and here the gap to the oracle is large on every family (flips 0.18–0.43 against 0.46–0.75) precisely because the oracle optimises the measured quantity at the cost of everything else. Coreference arxiv-2611.21159 (the seed-noise floor as the denominator of an explanation effect) and arxiv-2611.21539 (the probe's own direction as a positive control).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 288): **Locating where a response can be produced and locating what is wrong are different achievements, and the paper's null is more useful than its positives: the predicates identified from wrong predictions never repaired the model without retraining (0.1–0.8 accepted edits per repetition, test error moving between −0.6% and +0.5%, none of 42 comparisons significant, while refitting on the same data moves it −11% to −15%).** Two mechanisms the authors name are worth carrying, one of them untested and marked as such: a threshold shared by many trees cannot be revised on the evidence of a handful of validation errors without disturbing the samples those trees classify correctly, and an explanation is evidence about *this* input while a repair is a claim about the whole distribution — the number of errors that nominate a component is the sample size of the repair, not of the explanation. For us this sets a bar for any white-box predictor we describe as debuggable: it has to survive a held-out-error test after the edit, on a component-nomination budget it will actually get, and a report that stops at recovery or localisation should say so in the same sentence. Coreference arxiv-2611.20441 (a component located is not a component explained) and arxiv-2611.21307 (a repair verified by transplanting the donor).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 288): **Maximising measured effect selects atypical inputs and rarely-shared components, so an estimate that prefers shared structure buys robustness by giving up magnitude — the oracle flips 46–75% of predictions but through thresholds executed by 2–7 trees with the feature moved 1.62–2.13 SD, where the structural rule flips 18–44% through 8–27 trees and 0.88–1.34 SD, and its separation power collapses (contrast 0.26–0.34 to 0.13–0.18, counterfactual agreement 31–40% to 8–18%).** The reusable measurement is two scalars reported together: **distance moved by the intervention** (in units of the data's own spread) and **how many components share the edited object**, because the paper shows neither alone explains the effect — a random predicate moves the feature about as far with a much smaller effect, and the most-shared predicate is shared by more trees and flips fewer predictions. For our interventions the analogue is the residual-norm band and off-distribution check the folder already runs, plus a sharing count when the edited object is a feature many heads or paths use; an edit that only works from outside the data manifold is exactly the oracle's failure mode. Coreference arxiv-2611.21539 (mass-preserving knockouts against in-band items) and arxiv-2611.08767 (the distortion set as the labelled failure tail).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 287): `arxiv-2611.08767` — MEDALLION: Manifold Embedding Distillation and Attributions for Low-dimensional Latent InterpretatiON (Vicky Jung — University of Florida; Claire M. He, Irene Chang, Genevera I. Allen — Columbia University, Department of Statistics; arXiv:2611.08767v1, cs.LG, 2026-11-05, CC BY 4.0). Full text via HTML (~40K clean chars, abstract + §§1–2 + §3.1 + §4 + discussion + additional materials + Table 1 + references, read end to end). **Substance:** takes a published 2-D embedding as a teacher, fits a small neural encoder to reproduce each point's two coordinates from the raw input by least squares on coordinates alone (no labels, no reconstruction term), and then applies ordinary neural attribution (Integrated Gradients, with LRP/DeepLIFT/SmoothGrad named as interchangeable) to the encoder coordinate by coordinate, aggregating each input feature's attributions by L1 norm; their own instantiation MEDAL adds a decoder under a large coefficient on the distillation term so the fit is near-perfect subject to input recoverability, and the decoder is used only as a per-point reconstruction-error diagnostic — the attributed object is deliberately the encoder and not the reconstruction. **Results:** MNIST-64 with t-SNE as teacher, validated indirectly against *supervised* attributions because unsupervised attributions have no ground truth: Spearman against an MLP's Integrated Gradients is 0.314 (encoder-only) and 0.307 (MEDAL) versus 0.028 (BIR) and 0.008 (LIMEADE), and against random-forest MDI 0.509 and 0.483 versus 0.230 and 0.113, with Pearson 0.377/0.342 versus −0.010/−0.016 — the encoder-only variant wins most cells, so the reconstruction objective is not what buys agreement; the third baseline, t-SNE gradients re-implemented by the authors, cost 14 hours of compute and returned near-zero explanations everywhere, so it was dropped; on the melanoma immune subset (6,912 genes, t-SNE at default perplexity 30) top-ten gene attributions return CD79B and MS4A1 for B cells and NKG7 and GNLY for Natural Killer cells even though the map shows no distinct NK region, and on the Tasic mouse cortex (23,800 cells, 133 types folded to 18 meta-types) L6b and Pvalb return annotations consistent with the Allen Brain Atlas while astrocyte attributions, computed by rank-percentile because normalised scores were too low to rank, contain no consistent marker; the six worst-reconstructed test digits are ones where a 1 is rebuilt as a 2 and placed among the 2s, and the attribution highlights the 2-not-1 pixels. **Its own stated limit is the interesting part:** coordinate-matching is predictive fidelity, not explanatory fidelity, and DR supplies no ground-truth attributions against which the gap could be measured.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 287): **Fitting a white model to a black box's outputs and then reading the white model's internals is the move our own project is built on, and this paper is the folder's clearest statement of why it is not self-validating: it distinguishes predictive from explanatory fidelity, concedes that its distilled encoder may use entirely different input features than the t-SNE it reproduces, and then has no test that could detect the difference because the evaluation is agreement with a *supervised classifier's* attributions on a digit dataset — which measures whether both methods find digit-shaped pixels, not whether the student and teacher use the same pixels.** Note the tell in its own table: the plain encoder (a looser fit to the teacher, no reconstruction constraint) scores *better* on the validation than MEDAL (a near-perfect fit), which is what one expects if the metric rewards the student's convenience rather than the teacher's mechanism. For us the discipline is direct and cheap: any distilled or surrogate read-out we publish gets a **teacher-disagreement probe** — inputs on which the student and the teacher give visibly different answers, or student-vs-teacher feature-importance rank correlation where the teacher admits one — and the claim is scoped to the inputs where they agree. Coreference arxiv-2611.20371 (a probe that decodes is not a probe that intervenes) and arxiv-2611.21307 (the high-level model replaced by a program read off the frozen model).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 287): **Reconstruction error is an instrument, not a nuisance: because MEDAL keeps a decoder, every point carries a distance between the embedding's claim and the input it came from, and the paper reads that as a *distortion map* — the astrocyte population, the non-neuronal classes, and the digits a 1 is rebuilt as a 2 all sit at the high end, and the attributions computed on exactly those points say which inputs the map got wrong.** That inversion is worth carrying into our own evaluations: instead of averaging an error over the whole set and reporting a mean, keep the per-item error and treat the tail as the labelled failure set, then report what the explanation says specifically about it, because the failure set is where a white-box claim can be falsified and where the average hides everything. Two conditions the paper does not meet and we should: state the error threshold that defines the tail (they take the six worst with no rule), and give the tail's size and its class composition, since a distortion map whose "distorted" items are all one class is describing the class and not the map. Coreference arxiv-2611.19889 (a ranking that describes the checkpoint) and arxiv-2611.21539 (the ladder from behaviour to probe to intervention).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 287): **An explainer that returns near-zero everywhere is indistinguishable from an explainer that found nothing, and the folder has now met this failure twice in tools whose authors re-implemented them from the paper: here the t-SNE gradient method ran for 14 hours and produced near-zero explanations at every point, so it was silently dropped from the comparison rather than reported as a null.** The reporting rule this fixes is small and general — every explainer in a comparison table gets a **non-triviality floor**: the magnitude a constant, random or trivial-attribution baseline would produce on the same items, printed beside its score, so that "0.008 correlation" reads as an artifact and "0.314" reads as a result. The near-miss in this same paper is the mirror image: their best-looking transcriptomics claim is a top-ten marker list for a cell type with no distinct region in the map, which is a claim about ten genes and not about the embedding, and without a recall-over-all-annotated-markers number there is no way to tell the two cases apart. Coreference arxiv-2611.11398 (the frozen-random-dictionary control that decided which scores were artefacts) and arxiv-2611.10297 (the out-of-family scorer).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 286): `arxiv-2611.11398` — Decomposing Earth Embeddings with Sparse Autoencoders (Vitus Benson, Fanny Yang, Markus Reichstein — EarthNet / Horizon Europe WeatherGenerator group; arXiv:2611.11398v1, cs.LG/cs.CV-style Earth observation, 2026-11-08, NeurIPS 2026). Full text via HTML (~164K clean chars, §§1–4 + references + Appendices A–G, read end to end including every supplementary table). **Substance:** first SAE application to per-pixel Earth embeddings — AlphaEarth (D=64) and Tessera (D=128), 210,000 patches of 64×64 pixels from a 5 km global grid, split 100K/10K/100K, three SAE variants (ReLU+ℓ1, BatchTopK, Matryoshka BatchTopK) at width 1024 and k ∈ {8,16,32}, three seeds per cell (90 SAE runs + 18 frozen-decoder runs, 73 GPU-hours), all scored on fixed identical pixel samples; a three-criterion protocol (reconstruction at matched sparsity; spatial scale via a normalised semivariance curve and its correlation length plus within-patch variance share; concept alignment via a folded AUROC ≥ 0.65 against 20 concept groups drawn from 14 categorical and 3 continuous reference maps) with raw dimensions, PCA/ICA/NMF and a **frozen-random-decoder SAE** as baselines; then two applications (sub-concept discovery with a size-matched spatially-compact random-partition null, and an area-of-applicability estimate built on the sparse code's distance to the 5 nearest training pixels, scored against one common head over 88 graded hold-outs per target). **Results:** reconstruction separates trained from random (FVE 0.973 vs 0.775 AlphaEarth, 0.919 vs 0.534 Tessera at ~16 features; 2.7% vs 22% unexplained) and a fixed-PCA-basis top-k rule closes 67%/50% of the gap to BatchTopK, so about half to two-thirds of the edge over rank-k PCA is per-pixel selection; monosemy does not (88% of features aligned with ≤1 group, 89% for the frozen decoder, which has more strictly aligned features, 234 vs 136), nor does spatial scale (median correlation length 20–33 km vs 1,240 km for a raw dimension; 23–32% vs 9% of variance within a patch; frozen decoder 23 km) — the paper attributes this to activation arithmetic (16 of 1024 active ⇒ ~1.6% pixel support) rather than to learned atoms; the six highest-energy features carry 40% of code energy and are regional discretised pieces of the leading principal components (cosine 0.51–0.79, r = 0.69–0.83); sub-concept discovery separates three woody-vegetation features onto tropical / semi-arid / boreal strata (80%, 39%, 91% of top patches; lifts 15.6, 6.3, 8.0 against maps) yet the strict null cannot distinguish the partition (family-wise p = 0.14, 0.31); applicability gains for canopy height (77/88 hold-outs, +0.17; 75/88, +0.21) and not for elevation (41/88, 0.00; 49/88, +0.02), and on AlphaEarth an untrained random sparse code gains as much (75/88, +0.19).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 286): **Run every dictionary-quality score against a frozen random dictionary before believing it, because sparsity alone manufactures most of what the score looks like it is measuring: at 16 active features out of 1024, a feature is on for ~1.6% of inputs, so it can only clear a membership threshold if it is concentrated on one class — which is why 89% of a never-trained dictionary's features are 'monospecific' against 88% for the trained one, and why median correlation length (23 km vs 20–33 km) and Moran's I cannot tell them apart either.** Only reconstruction separates them (2.7% vs 22% of variance left unexplained), which means "our features are specific" and "our features vary at the right scale" are claims about the code's sparsity budget, not about the dictionary, and a report that omits the control is reporting an artefact of its own regularisation. For our battery the rule is direct: any per-feature statistic we publish — selectivity, monosemy, autocorrelation, variance share — gets the same statistic computed for a random-atom dictionary at the same width and sparsity beside it, and only the gap is a result. Coreference arxiv-2611.05655 (when two latents are the same feature) and arxiv-2611.09196 (the reading of a neuron as a measurement).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 286): **A downstream win from a sparse decomposition needs a second control, an untrained random sparse code of the same width and sparsity, because it separates 'a better space to measure distance in' from 'features that mean something' — here the best-looking application, ranking canopy-height errors by distance in the code, is fully reproduced by the random code on AlphaEarth (75/88 hold-outs, +0.19 against the trained SAE's +0.17) and about a third reproduced on Tessera, so the gain belongs to sparsity combined with the head's weights concentrating the distance, not to anything the dictionary learned.** Two habits follow. First, any read-out we wire into a decision — an OOD score, an applicability estimate, a monitor threshold — should be re-run with the interpretable component replaced by a random one of equal capacity, and if it survives, we have learned something about geometry rather than about the model, which is a perfectly good result but a different one. Second, the paper's own diagnosis of why the win is target-specific is the reusable part: targets tied to discrete landscape types are marked by a few sparse features, targets varying continuously within every type are spread over many dimensions and no sparse code can make them separable — a pre-check we can run by asking whether the head's weight mass sits on a few features. Coreference arxiv-2611.06688 (a subspace signal that must beat a detector-agnostic baseline) and arxiv-2611.10297 (the out-of-family scorer that turns a probe number into a claim).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 286): **A concentration statistic is not evidence of structure when the reference map is spatially smooth: the SAE's three woody-vegetation features sit on tropical-rainforest, semi-arid and boreal strata with lifts of 15.6, 6.3 and 8.0, and yet 50 size-matched spatially compact random partitions of the same forest patches agree with the same maps just as well (family-wise p = 0.14 and 0.31) — and the frozen decoder's features are even more concentrated (99/98/99% of top patches in one climate pair) while covering only part of each stratum.** The general lesson for our evaluations: any explanation scored against an autocorrelated or smooth reference — a geography, a topic, a sequence position, a template — must be compared with a size-matched structureless partition of the same items, because compactness alone reproduces smoothness; and where two artifacts differ in the same direction, the discriminating measurement is *coverage* of the stratum rather than concentration inside it, which is the metric the authors say they would need next. This is the same failure the folder met in the co-occurrence-prior and shared-stimulus entries, in its cleanest form. Coreference arxiv-2611.10297 (205 images reusing 28 reports) and arxiv-2611.19889 (a ranking that describes the checkpoint).

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 285): `arxiv-2611.21159` — When Feature Representation Changes Local Explanations: A Controlled Comparison of SHAP and LIME under Numerical Discretization (Parv Patel — Indian Institute of Technology Palakkad; arXiv:2611.21159v1, cs.LG, 2026-11-16).
