- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 234): **A first-order graph's error is set by the read-out rule, not by the derivative, and the fix costs nothing because the columns are already computed — a TopK dictionary is a selection over all preactivations, so the support the attribution graph is built on is exactly the set an intervention perturbs: zeroing one feature moves a downstream feature across the cutoff in 0.74–0.92 of cases, the crossing coordinates carry 0.73–0.84 of the response's energy, and re-applying the rule to the first-order-predicted preactivations drops the median relative error from 0.247–0.669 to 0.013–0.033, with the reranking alone worth the whole improvement because removing it returns the error to 0.558.** The general statement is stronger than the TopK case and is what makes this entry portable: any read-out that *selects* — TopK, a threshold, an argmax over heads, a router's top-2, a renormalised attention pattern — is discontinuous in its input, so a first-order expansion taken at the clean point is evaluated on a membership that the expansion itself predicts will change. The recipe is one line: keep every row of the Jacobian-vector product, add it to all preactivations, and re-run the rule. Two design notes from the paper's own ablation are worth copying. The measured quantity has to be the *code* change and not the preactivation change, because a leaver's code drops from at least the cutoff to zero and an entrant's jumps from zero to near it, so a crossing coordinate's code moves 5.7–10.1 times as far as its preactivation while the preactivation error stays small for both — an error metric on the smooth quantity cannot see the discontinuity. And the contrast that makes the discontinuity attributable is a ReLU dictionary on the same model family, which crosses its zero just as often (0.69) and carries almost none of the response (0.05 of the energy) precisely because its code is continuous there; a crossing rate without a continuous-rule control would read as a fact about dictionaries rather than about the rule that selects. (arxiv-2611.00606, arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2611.08438)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 234): **The cheapest discipline in the folder is to write each prediction down with the threshold at which it fails before the measurement, print what came back beside it, and let the ones that fire against you stay — 22 rules here, six fired, and three of the six are adverse to the paper's own headline: the once-built graph loses to the plain fixed-support graph on sixteen-feature subsets (0.670 against 0.631), a two-layer MLP given exactly the margin graph's six inputs fails to reach it (2.23–2.45 error, and 1.44–1.53 on two inputs, both worse than predicting no change at 1.0, against 0.016), and the residual chain passes where the decoded chains fail.** Table 1's four columns — what the rule reads, when it fires, what the measurement returned, and whether it fired — is a better artefact than a limitations section because it is a ledger a reader can audit line by line, and because it makes the boundary of a claim a number instead of an adjective: the margin graph is licensed at the median write (1.68 and 3.57 cutoff units) and not at the write where the first-order error reaches 0.3 (5.55 and 3.90), and the paper says both. Two habits follow for our battery. Every metric we report should arrive with a pre-registered kill threshold, because the alternative is choosing the threshold after seeing the number, which is how a battery of 40 tests ends up with 40 passes. And the against-the-headline firings are the ones to keep visible: a paper that only published the fired rules favouring it would be indistinguishable from one that chose its thresholds afterwards, and the tell that it did not is precisely that some of its own predictions misfire. (arxiv-2611.00606, arxiv-2611.08438, arxiv-2611.05655)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 234): **A decoded per-feature response and the model's own activation change are two different quantities with opposite-looking statistics, and reporting both is the only way to see it — over crossing interventions the part of the decoded code change on entering and leaving features has 1.24–1.72 times the activation change's norm while projecting at only 0.21–0.29 of it, the whole decoded change has 1.41–1.82 times the norm at a median cosine of 0.27–0.50, and the reconstruction residual supplies the difference, so the dictionary's response is both larger than and badly aligned with the thing it is supposed to describe.** The downstream consequence is the sharpest result in the paper and the one to carry: carrying a *decoded middle code* through the next block fails at the third layer (0.884 for the fixed-support chain, 0.999 and 0.996 for the margin and exact ones), while carrying the *residual stream* through both blocks in one product per live feature errs 0.053 and the exact activation-change chain 0.029 — the decoded code is not the object that composes across layers, and the reconstruction error it drops is a real part of the model's forward pass. For our own multi-hop claims this is a concrete test that costs two extra products: compare a chain built from codes against a chain built from activations, at the third layer's code. The paired lesson is about stability scores: per-feature cosine matching leaves the operator between two layers at 0.22 explained, where sparse non-negative recombinations of atoms reach 0.57, and the whole remaining gap sits on the target's atoms nearest the cutoff (admitting 10% of them nearest-first recovers 0.73 of it, a random 10% only 0.11) — so "the features agree across seeds" and "the graph agrees across seeds" are measurements of different objects, and the operator, not the feature direction, is the one that decides whether a circuit claim survives a change of seed. (arxiv-2611.00606, arxiv-2611.05655, arxiv-2611.18089)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 233): **A reading's licence can be run before the effect is read, and the seven restrictions it prints are each a named class of claim it forbids — this paper is the first in the folder to invert the order, so the caveats arrive as constraints rather than as an apology, and the two that bite hardest were both found by the instrument's own checks: re-weighting the logged stimulus factors to a different mixture moves the profile 2.34 twin units when a fresh redraw of the same battery moves it about one, so "this construct's response is such-and-such" is licensed only *relative to a declared distribution*, and eight statements are length-sensitive at more than 5% of their neurons (`With` 55%, `For` 49%), so comparisons across prompt lengths are simply not available for them.** The form is worth copying exactly: two of the nine checks are hard gates (scrambled-label and split-half nulls must be cleared or nothing is read at all — cleared here by 10.66× and 12.76× their 95th percentiles, minima 7.22 and 5.96), and the other seven are *reported* regardless of outcome, each with the claim class it restricts written beside it. That is a cheaper discipline than a limitations section, because it is enforceable: our own battery already produces the artefacts — a mixture, a length dependence, an interval width — and the only change is to compute them before the headline number and print them next to the claims they bound. A second lesson sits in the appendix: the licence was re-run after a fault in how per-prompt vectors were joined to their prompts, and the corrected numbers *improved* the two null margins (10.1 → 10.7 and 9.6 → 12.8), which is the shape a healthy re-run takes — the instrument was understating itself, and the paper says so. (arxiv-2611.09196, arxiv-2611.05655, arxiv-2611.08438)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 233): **Standardising a reading against a baseline that itself drifts turns a shrinking effect into a growing one, and the paper catches it in its own headline statistic: the yardstick's spread narrows over training, so the standardised norm rises for 144 of 169 constructs while the raw norm falls for 148, and on the worked construct the raw response goes 15.7 → 184.5 → 143.0 → 96.0 while the standardised version goes 30.2 → 239.6 → 270.9 → 251.5 — the two curves disagree on the direction of the last two-thirds of training.** This is the folder's denominator lesson in its temporal form, and it is the one instance where the *corrected* value is the one that looks worse: every other entry's fix made a number look smaller and more honest, whereas here raw units make the model's response look like it is decaying. The stated rule is to report size on the raw form and concentration on the standardised one, because the two answer different questions and `σ0` is the only channel through which set C enters. The paired artefact is that the twin unit cannot serve as the interval width — the twins share their cores, so their disagreement measures surface variation only, and correcting agreement by it yields values above 1 for roughly 150 of 188 constructs, with intervals therefore taken from a core bootstrap whose coverage is itself checked (calibrated at the median, but optimistic by up to 7.17× for 33 constructs). For any metric we compute across checkpoints: print the raw series, the standardised series and the noise unit's own calibration factor, because a cross-checkpoint trend that inverts between two normalisations is not a trend yet. (arxiv-2611.09196, arxiv-2611.13548, arxiv-2611.05655)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 233): **A probe's accuracy saturates exactly where the interesting comparisons live, and the saturation is total rather than partial — 0.653 median on the residual stream and 0.802 on hidden units at initialisation become 0.998 at the first trained checkpoint and 0.999 at the end, with 145–148 of 164 constructs at or above 0.99 on a 0.902–1.000 range, so 169 constructs, 24 layers and 61 checkpoints cannot be ordered by it, the AUC median is a flat 1.000, and a harder two-role contrast (same token, loop role versus comprehension role) saturates just as completely at 0.999 against 0.68–0.75 untrained.** The reading that makes this a result rather than a complaint: at initialisation the probe is *partly* separating a contrast it should not be able to see at all, which is the random-feature-map effect the folder already has theory for, and after training it separates everything, so the probe's accuracy is measuring the model's competence at the task the stimuli define and not the geometry of the concept. The instrument that keeps resolving is the profile's carrier overlap, which is *low* on precisely the contrast the probe calls perfect, and each number carries a ceiling to be read against — 0.250–0.266 overlap for the two `for` roles against a 0.050 chance rate and a 0.872 twin maximum, and 0.494 for one role across two tokens against scope-restricted ceilings of 0.837 and 0.850. So the honest form of "the model represents X" is an overlap with a chance rate and a same-instrument ceiling, not an accuracy: the first can distinguish five-times-chance from under-a-third-of-ceiling, and the second cannot distinguish anything from anything. (arxiv-2611.09196, arxiv-2611.15735, arxiv-2611.13548)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 232): `arxiv-2611.18089` — Deep Latents, Long Memory: Latent persistence explains temporal correlations in transformer activations (Francesco Cagnetta, Simplex; Santiago Acevedo, SISSA; arXiv:2611.18089v1, 2026-11-13, CC BY 4.0). Full text, 139,999 clean chars incl. Appendices A–L and Tables 1–7; figures via captions only; inline math doubled by the HTML build and not quoted. **Substance:** define a layer's autocorrelation as the standardised activation dot product at lag τ against an anchor position, integrate over lags, and read the curve as the span structure of what the layer holds. Synthetic setting: Random Hierarchy Model (v = 32, m = 8, depth 5, 32-token sentences) and a 5-block GPT-2-style transformer (d = 768, 12 heads) trained to within 0.033 nats of the optimum; the 63 tree nodes are regressed jointly on each position's activation so a code is nonzero only beyond what any other single node implies (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell argument — this is what separates it from a probe, where a parent reads 11–23% wherever its children are encoded), giving per-latent same-node autocorrelation terms predicted from single-position codes. **Results:** predicted codes give 55–95% of the measured layer-4 autocorrelation (carriers 34–55% / 32–52% at lags 1–3 and 77–83% / 74–83% at lags 4–7 in layers 3 and 4, residual 30–44% at short lags falling to 4–9% at lags 4–7); the autocorrelation grows in a staircase synchronised with the loss plateaus (lags 1, 3, 4–7, 7–15). Natural language, five models (Gemma-2-2B/9B, Pythia-160M, Llama-3-8B, Qwen3-8B), Pile + WikiText: persistence rises 1.1→1.8 (real order) against 1.1–1.3 (within-sequence shuffle), activation frequency of the selected latents stays at 0.03–0.07 at every layer, autocorrelation–persistence Pearson r = 0.50–0.95 across layers (10 model–corpus cells, mean and median), and removing the sequence mean raises r in 8 of 10 mean-persistence cells (Gemma-2-2B/Pile 0.90→0.95) but lowers both Gemma-2-9B cells. **Intervention:** single persistent-latent ablation cuts autocorrelation 3.0–13.3% (Pythia-160M largest), three latents 4.4–24.3%, all active 43.7–68.3%, matched non-persistent control 0.0–0.7%; the persistent latent removes a median 1.2% of squared activation norm against 0.29% for the control (factor ~4, 80% of episodes). **Controls printed in appendices:** clipping (5th–95th percentile) shown not to change layer ordering, massive-activation tokens (>20× median squared norm) excluded from the explained-variance panel, one-token latents lapses bridged raising persistence 10–44% without reordering layers.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 232): **Two decompositions of the same activations give opposite answers about which variable a position encodes, and the difference is the conditioning set — a probe for a parent variable reads positive signal wherever the parent's children are encoded (11–23% of the parent's variance here, wherever the children sit), because parent and child are correlated through the grammar, whereas the joint least-squares regression of all 63 tree nodes on the same activation gives the parent exactly zero by the Frisch–Waugh–Lovell theorem, and the paper states the resulting rule plainly: the code is nonzero only if the activation carries something about the variable beyond what any single other node implies.** This is the cleanest available diagnosis of the folder's recurring "the parent concept is decodable from the child layer" finding, and it is checkable without knowing the grammar: fit the probe, then fit the joint regression with the correlated children included, and read whether the parent's block survives. The companion caution is subtler and the paper proves it rather than asserting it — at early positions there are only 32 and 256 possible prefixes against an embedding width of 768, so any injective map, *including a randomly initialised layer*, makes every function of the prefix linearly readable, and at later positions a random layer is a random-feature map that can still hand a probe most of any variable without the network having built any structure. That is the theory-side version of the folder's random-init control results (the linear-map R² of 0.95–0.99 at initialisation, the untrained cross-seed agreement of 0.95): when the prefix space is smaller than the representation dimension, decodability is a property of the dimension count, not of learning. The replacement instrument the authors adopt is an explained-variance share per variable with a noise floor and a sample-size stability test, and that is the more honest object for our own battery. (arxiv-2611.18089, arxiv-2611.10760, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 232): **Every long-range similarity statistic in this folder carries a sequence-wide offset that grows with depth, and one subtraction removes it — after permuting token positions within each sequence, which preserves every latent's activation frequency, the autocorrelation here stops decaying but sits on a plateau whose height still rises with depth, and the identity behind it is that the permutation-averaged cross-position product equals the squared norm of the sequence-mean representation up to a 1/T correction (below 10⁻² in this setup), so the plateau is exactly the frequency-only component and subtracting the per-sequence mean makes it vanish.** The same subtraction *increases* the correlation between autocorrelation and SAE-latent persistence in 8 of 10 model–corpus cells (Gemma-2-2B on The Pile 0.90→0.95, Pythia-160M 0.81→0.96) and turns a monotone depth profile into one that saturates in the middle — which is where the folder's other depth-resolved measures peak — while the two Gemma-2-9B cells get worse, so the corrected statistic is not uniformly the better one and both must be printed. This is the rank-one degenerate direction the folder keeps re-finding (the PC1 that owns 93%+ of residual variance, the massive-activation channel, the pooled-agreement denominator) arriving as a *temporal* artefact rather than a geometric one: it is produced by the fact that each sample has a mean, not by any computation along the context. The operational rule generalises cheaply: any correlation, similarity or effective-integration-window number computed across positions ships with a shuffle control that holds frequency fixed and with its sequence-centred variant, because a within-sequence shuffle is the only control that distinguishes temporal order from activation rate. (arxiv-2611.18089, arxiv-2611.13548, arxiv-2611.05655)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 232): **The instrument that makes an ablation interpretable here is a matched latent chosen from the same activation event rather than a random or mean baseline — the control is a feature that is active at the episode's starting token but not persistent within the window, and the pairing is what produces the sharp separation the paper reports: 3.0–13.3% autocorrelation drop for the persistent latent against 0.0–0.7% for its control, a factor of roughly four in removed squared norm (median 1.2% against 0.29%, with the persistent latent removing more in 80% of episodes).** Three design details are worth stealing whole. The reference position for the whole measurement is placed *inside* the firing episode and the ablation excludes it, so the effect cannot be an artefact of ablating the very token the correlation is computed against; and the paper then runs the measurement with the reference pushed one, two and three tokens past the episode end (e+1 to e+3), where it reports drops that are real but smaller and that decay with distance for four of five models — a distance-graded placebo that neither Pythia nor any other arm produces by design. The third detail is the honest ceiling: ablating every active latent through the SAE reconstruction cuts autocorrelation by only 43.7–68.3% rather than to zero, and the paper attributes the shortfall to reconstruction error measured in its own appendix, which is the correct place for that number — inside the claim, as a stated resolution limit, rather than outside it as a caveat. For our battery this is the ablation template to copy when the intervention is on a *direction* rather than a node: pick the control from the same firing event, exclude the reference position, and grade the effect at increasing distance from where the intervention was applied. (arxiv-2611.18089, arxiv-2610.31520, arxiv-2611.08438)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 231): **Every stability number this folder has reported is a point estimate compared against a threshold, and the paper that makes it a measurement shows the first thing the interval does is kill the effect — the toy-model context contrast that all ten seed pairs agree on and every ε in {0.03…0.60} reproduces has a seed standard error of 0.00388 against 0.0018 from documents, and with twenty seeds instead of five the same contrast shrinks from 0.02636 to 0.02612 while its document-only interval [0.02273, 0.02998] becomes a combined one [0.02173, 0.03050]; at the larger models, ten seeds make the contrast's interval include zero in all three.** The transferable instrument is not the transport plan but the division of the noise into its two sources: resampling whole documents with the same indices for every dictionary pair gives the sampling term, deleting one seed at a time gives the training term, and the two are added — so a claim of "the dictionaries disagree on this topic" or "these features recur" can be reported as a ratio of seed variance to document variance, which is the quantity that decides whether more seeds or more text is the right next experiment. Two habits follow. Report the self-comparison diagonal as the floor of any agreement or distance score, because here it runs from 1.000 at weak regularisation to 0.208 at strong and correcting for it cuts the headline contrast by three quarters — a number without its floor is not interpretable. And validate the interval on a known population before quoting it, since the same procedure that covers 95% in the regular regime covers 27.5% when a 0.5%-probability high-impact document type exists, with 145 of 200 samples at N = 64 never containing the type at all and every band failing; a bootstrap over documents cannot see a stratum the sample missed. (arxiv-2611.05655, arxiv-2611.13548, arxiv-2611.13885)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 231): **A similarity score can be structurally incapable of registering the effect it is used to test, and the tell is a difference of exactly zero across conditions — three decoder-based agreement measures give the same value on both topics to four decimals (0.4080 Hungarian mean cosine, 0.4350 nearest-neighbour, 0.0109 shared fraction above 0.7), not because the dictionaries are identical but because decoders do not depend on which documents were evaluated, while the activation-geometry variants that do read the corpus give z-statistics of 1.1 to 6.9 and energy-weighted transport gives 15.** That is a sharper statement than "the baseline is weaker": a score whose value is invariant to a factor the claim is about cannot be evidence about that factor at any sample size, and the invariance is checkable in one line because it depends on what the score reads. The paper also supplies the missing middle rung — a uniform-mass optimal transport plan between the same latents (z = 1.1/1.5) sits between the decoder measures that never see the corpus and the energy-weighted plan that does, so the ladder isolates *weighting* from geometry, and the honest attribution of the gain is to weighting by activation energy rather than to optimal transport as such. For our own battery: any agreement, stability or correspondence statistic ships with the table of what it reads (weights only, activations, or output effects), because the run-227 lens hierarchy said an observation point is a lossy map and this gives the concrete case where a measure's observation point simply does not include the variable of interest. (arxiv-2611.05655, arxiv-2611.15735, arxiv-2611.13548)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 231): **Ranking by importance and then auditing the top of the list audits the wrong tail — in 35 independently trained dictionaries the high-energy group (about 50% of tuning energy) accounts for only 16–29% of the between-seed disagreement while the group holding 10% of the energy accounts for 28–40%, and the cost-to-energy ratio is below one for the high-energy group in every single dictionary (0.11–0.89) and above one for the low-energy group (1.3–4.5).** The reading is that the low-energy tail is where the structures that make two runs different live — split and absorbed latents, context-specific ones — so a coverage statistic computed on the top 50 features is a measurement of the head, and the folder's many "top-k sharing" numbers (230's 43.5–48 of 50 unmatched, and the seed-agreement percentages around it) are exactly that measurement and should be labelled as such. Two operational consequences. Publish a per-energy-stratum breakdown beside any global dictionary-difference score, because a pooled number mixes a stable head with a volatile tail and can be made to move in either direction by changing the width. And treat the characterization of what the head is made of as a warning about the audit: in the larger models the high-energy latents are 2–18 units that fire in 192–256 of 256 tuning documents, often on punctuation and function words, and they contribute negatively to the topic contrast in five of seven settings — so the units most likely to be named first are the ones most likely to be an artefact of position and format, which is the run-230 PC1 lesson arriving through a completely different instrument. (arxiv-2611.05655, arxiv-2611.13548, arxiv-2610.27393)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 230): **A metric whose denominator is dominated by a component that contains no task structure can read near-perfectly while the thing it claims to measure stays unmeasured, and the correction is arithmetic rather than methodological — 99.96% of activation variance explained alongside 33.0% of content variance unexplained is the same number under two denominators, and the ratio between them is predicted in advance by one eigendecomposition.** The general form is worth naming because this folder has now met it five times in five costumes: the pooled-agreement rate graded on prompts the model already gets right, the linear-map R² where a random-init model scores 0.95–0.99, the faithfulness reward saturated above the task threshold, the source-level granularity inflation, and now the variance-weighted fidelity score where one rank-one direction owns 70–99.9% of the mass. In every case the fix is not a better method but a printed denominator — report the metric on the residual after the degenerate component is removed, and print the sharing ratio so a reader can undo the normalisation if they disagree with it. For our white-box ambition the consequence is sharper than it looks: a predictor scored on reconstruction or variance explained is being graded mostly on the position-and-norm signal that PC1 encodes (the paper measures R² ≈ 0.9998² for PC1 against activation norm, and near-chance accuracy for a probe on PC1 alone across four classification tasks), so a white-box model can win the fidelity contest without representing any of the computational structure we actually want to predict. (arxiv-2611.13548, arxiv-2611.08438, arxiv-2611.13885)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 230): **The intuitive stability baseline is the wrong one, and this paper's headline result is that it inverts sign — features the model most depends on are the features that least reliably recur (43.5–48 of the top 50 unmatched against 19–27 for a random 50), because importance ranking and reproducibility are both consequences of a third variable, alignment with the dominant direction, which pushes them in opposite directions.** The transferable discipline: when a claim rests on "the important X are the stable X", the null must come from *inside* the same instrument — here the dictionary-wide sharing rate of the same model — not from a random-direction or random-feature arm, because the random arm shares the degenerate structure and therefore cannot detect it. The paper's own sweep makes the same point twice: a random-direction bypass leaves everything unchanged (26.21 content-to-total FVU ratio against 26.21 for standard and 26.24 for PC1 bypass in DINOv2), while the PC1-specific bypass moves it, which is how you know the effect is the component rather than the intervention. And the two denominators of a stability report should be published together — the subset's rate and the population's — because the gap between them, not either number, is the finding (Gemma at 87–92% top-50 against 58% dictionary is *above* its own baseline; Qwen at 6% against 48% is far below). This is the run-216 sampling rule generalised: a statistic computed on a selected subset must be reported against that same selection's population rate before it is compared with anything. (arxiv-2611.13548, arxiv-2610.27393, arxiv-2610.27790)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 230): **Improving an interpretability metric does not reliably improve the behaviour the metric was built to serve, and the divergence runs in both directions — the corrected feature ranking takes agreement-edit success from exactly 0% to 9.0/31.9/4.2%, while Gemma-2-2B scores 64–65% under standard, post-hoc and bypass alike (random 0%), sparse probing moves under one accuracy point in every model, and automated-interpretability AUROC *falls* on Llama-3.1-8B by 0.093–0.097 after the repair.** Three consequences for our battery. First, the honest report of a metric-to-behaviour link is the paired difference on the same test examples with an interval — the paper's Table 37 does this in percentage points against the standard arm, and it is the only place the Gemma result is legible at all. Second, a metric that saturates in one model (Gemma's 64–65% invariant across arms) is not evidence of a good dictionary; it is evidence that the task is being solved by something the arm does not perturb, which is the run-157 ceiling lesson and should send us looking for the confound rather than celebrating the number. Third, "downstream utility" claims need at least two downstream tasks with different demands, since the paper's two disagree in sign on the same model, and the disagreement is itself the finding: a ranking can be causally load-bearing for a narrow editing task and irrelevant for a linear read-out. (arxiv-2611.13548, arxiv-2611.08438, arxiv-2610.27790)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 229): `arxiv-2611.08438` — Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety (Fazl Barez, Tung-Yu Wu + 19; advisors Shay B. Cohen, Mor Geva, Yoshua Bengio, Stella Biderman, Hassan Sajjad; University of Oxford + Martian primary, 14 further institutions; arXiv:2611.08438v1, 2026-11-05, CC BY 4.0, companion website and notebook repository). Full text, ~686k clean chars incl. §1–§15 and references; figures via captions only; inline math doubled by the HTML build and not quoted. **Substance:** a survey organised as four pillars (motivation and concepts, technical methods, research directions, safety and open problems) whose contribution is §7.5, a unified evaluation framework. Behaviour B is a prompt set, M a scalar behaviour metric, an intervention on a component set S replaces its activations with reference values; s(S,x) = M(intact) − M(intervened), s(S,B) its expectation. Five dimensions are then functionals of (a(S,x), s(S,x)): attribution faithfulness (rank/linear agreement, effect-size error, unbounded counterfactual recovery with the degenerate-denominator warning and a cited bounded variant), completeness (loss recovery against zero/mean/Gaussian ablation, behavioural coverage over a threshold τ, unexplained variance over deviation from the behaviour's mean), stability (cross-seed Hungarian-matched alignment, normalised hyperparameter range, paraphrase consistency bounded to [0,1]), causal validity (necessity, sufficiency, specificity normalised over named control behaviours, each with a matched-size random arm plus an interchange test), human interpretability (explanation and debugging utility as differences against a no-explanation baseline, inter-rater kappa). Table 10 sets per-method priorities for SAEs, circuit discovery, probing and steering; Table 13 scores six orientations (pragmatic, ambitious, developmental, across-time, introspective, automated) on scalability and robustness to deception, rating introspective and automated low on the latter. **Numbers quoted:** dead features 10–50% of a poorly tuned dictionary; fewer than 50% of features identical across seeds; circuits explaining 60–80% of behavioural variance; sleeper-agent linear detector above 99% AUROC. **Why relevance 3:** it supplies the specificity and paraphrase-consistency measures and the two unboundedness warnings the folder's own reporting lacks, and states the proxy-fidelity problem that any white-box surrogate inherits.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 229): **A survey that grades every method family on the same five axes turns the folder's most-repeated empirical finding into an editorial position with a citation trail — and the axes themselves are the reusable part, because two of them (specificity, paraphrase consistency) are tests this reader has never run.** The framework's discipline is that each dimension is written as a functional of one pair of quantities, a method's attribution score and the measured intervention effect, so "our explanation is faithful" decomposes into an agreement statistic, an error statistic, a recovery statistic, a coverage statistic, a stability statistic and a necessity/sufficiency/specificity triple, each with a named baseline arm. Three specifics worth stealing verbatim. Specificity normalises an intervention's effect on the target behaviour by the sum of absolute effects over a list of named *control* behaviours, which converts the folder's recurring "does this edit damage anything else" post-hoc worry into a pre-registered denominator. Paraphrase consistency is one minus the within-paraphrase-set variance of the intervention effect over its mean square, bounded to [0,1], and it is the cheapest test available that an effect belongs to the behaviour rather than to one input string — directly the confound the folder has met in templated-dataset entries. And the framework's own limitations section names threshold arbitrariness as a first-class problem rather than an implementation detail, which is the correct concession: a battery whose verdict flips at a threshold is reporting its threshold. The complementary caveat is that the paper asserts its central claim (that mechanistic insight is under-tested for safety) from the shape of the literature and measures nothing itself, so it should be cited for its instruments and its taxonomy, not for evidence. (arxiv-2611.08438, arxiv-2611.14483, arxiv-2610.31520)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 229): **The two recovery metrics this folder reports most often are unbounded by construction and the failure is in the normalisation, not the method — counterfactual recovery divides by a clean behavioural gap that can approach zero while the patched metric can overshoot the donor or undershoot the recipient, and loss recovery divides by original-minus-ablated loss, which is exactly zero when the component set does nothing, so both can leave [0,1] in either direction.** Everything the folder has attributed to a flaky method across dozens of entries — a circuit scoring above 1.0, a dictionary "recovering" more than the model did, a patch that makes the metric better than either source — has this as a candidate mechanical explanation, and it is checkable from numbers already printed. Two habits follow. Print the denominator beside the ratio (the clean gap, or the original-minus-ablated loss), because a recovery of 0.8 over a gap of 0.01 is noise and a recovery of 0.6 over a gap of 1.5 is a result, and the single ratio cannot distinguish them. And where a bounded variant exists, report both: the paper points at a bounded successor for counterfactual recovery while noting that loss recovery has no such standardisation yet, which is a gap our own write-ups could close cheaply by clipping and saying so. The wider reading is the run-227 lesson arriving from a different direction — a metric is a lossy map, and the loss here is the denominator's range, so a comparison across sites with different clean gaps is a comparison across normalisations pretending to be a comparison across methods. (arxiv-2611.08438, arxiv-2611.15735, arxiv-2611.09233)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 229): **Proxy fidelity is the open problem a white-box model inherits wholesale, and the survey states it in the one form that is falsifiable: a dictionary agrees with its target on *outputs* while making claims about *internal algorithm*, so two networks with the same output and different algorithms make the proxy's success at reconstruction no evidence at all about the target's mechanism, and the negative case is the dangerous one — not finding a deception circuit in the proxy licenses only the sentence that it was not found there.** The proposed test is real rather than gestural: treat the proxy's features as the nodes of a high-level causal model, then ask whether interchange interventions on those nodes commute with the target's behaviour, which makes causal abstraction both the validation criterion and a training objective for a faithful proxy. Two calibration points the paper supplies and the folder can use immediately. The seed-instability number (under half of features matching across seeds, with broad semantic clusters holding up better than rare ones) means an individual feature claim is a claim about one draw from a distribution unless it is duplicated across seeds — and the correct target of replication is the *cluster*, not the index. And the identifiability argument is the theoretical reason the folder's empirical reconstruction-versus-mechanism gap keeps appearing: under high coherence several distinct sparse combinations generate the same output, so a dictionary that fits well is one of many equally-fitting decompositions, and no amount of reconstruction evidence selects among them. For our own battery this argues for reporting, next to every white-box claim, which of three things it has established — output agreement, internal agreement under interchange, or nothing beyond the first — because the middle one is the only one that supports the word "predictive". (arxiv-2611.08438, arxiv-2610.27375, arxiv-2608.19338)

Lewis; University of Amsterdam; arXiv:2610.31520v1, 2026-10-22, BlackboxNLP 2026). Full text, 58,536 raw chars incl. Appendices A–N; **figures 1–7 via captions only**, inline math stripped, and **many table bodies blank in the served HTML** (Tables 4, 9–13 and half the NIE tables), so only rendering cells and explicit sentences are quoted. **Substance:** seven instruction-tuned models (Gemma-2 9B, LLaMA-3.1 8B/70B, Mistral-7B, Mixtral-8x7B, Qwen-2.5 7B/72B) on three templated datasets (130 rewritten Fig-QA noun tuples, 100 adjective pairs, domain-labelled adjective pairs over eight domains with 100 held-out per direction). Activation patching from a literal prompt into its one-word-swapped metaphorical twin gives three positional peaks — the swapped word, the sentence-final full stop plus the preceding token, and the trailing prompt colon — and the final stop at the most-influential layer (11 for LLaMA-8B, 29 for 70B) is the site. DAS fits an orthonormal k = 16/32 rotation for 1,000 Adam steps on frozen weights, alternating intervention direction per step, maximising interchange-intervention accuracy. Steering is compared between full-vector mass-mean and the DAS-subspace means, on wrong-answer repair and on free-form generation injected at every token. **Numbers:** baseline identification 0.645–0.930, interpretation 0.696–0.862, with Gemma-2-27B dropped at 0.464 as below the probing floor; mass-mean NIEs 0.195–0.355 / 0.254–0.666 against logistic-probe 0.011–0.038 / 0.014–0.051 on LLaMA-8B; wrong-answer repair 54–88% (mass-mean) and 45–91% (subspace), split by model; generation flip rates 0.03–0.52 with the arm ranking inverted; judge validated on 100 items at raw agreement 0.79 and Cohen's kappa 0.60; matched-n global-vs-domain control surviving in 6/8 transfer cells.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 228): **A direction's fit and its causal reach are different numbers on the same representations, and the mean-difference arm wins by roughly an order of magnitude — normalised indirect effects of 0.195–0.355 (literal→metaphor) and 0.254–0.666 (reverse) for mass-mean against 0.011–0.038 and 0.014–0.051 for logistic regression trained on the identical activations, with the pattern holding across models and Gemma-9B the frequent exception.** The logistic probe is the better *predictor* by construction — it is the fitted one — so its weakness here is not a fitting failure but a statement about what sort of object steers: the mean difference is a translation along the axis the classes separate on, while a fitted boundary's normal is chosen to sort examples and need not point anywhere the computation reads. Two habits follow for our battery. Carry a mean-difference arm beside every fitted probe and report the intervention effect of both, because the folder's decodable-versus-used partition has so far been demonstrated mostly by *absence* (a probe that predicts and does not steer) and this is the first entry where two probes at the same site disagree in the *positive* direction. And when a probe does steer, quote the normalised effect rather than the flip rate: the flip rates here (54–88% mass-mean, 45–91% subspace) look comparable while the NIEs differ by 5–20×, so a flip rate compresses a continuous shift into a threshold and hides precisely the difference that matters. (arxiv-2610.31520, arxiv-2611.00298, arxiv-2611.18514)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 228): **A variable that flips a classifier is not the variable that drives generation, and the tell is that the effect survives only at an enlarged steering scale with the between-arm ranking inverted — classification repair runs 54–88% (mass-mean) and 45–91% (subspace) while generation flip rates fall to 0.03–0.52, and the full-vector arm that lost most classification rows now leads in five of seven models.** The authors' own reading is the right one and worth keeping as a hypothesis form: the subspace extracted at the sentence-final full stop may be adapted to the classification prompt, with a second metaphoricity variable elsewhere serving generation. What makes this more than a caveat is that both measurements are on the same models, datasets and directions, so the divergence cannot be blamed on a change of object — exactly the confound the folder's cross-paper probe-versus-generation comparisons usually carry. Operationally, any steering claim we make from a single-token task should be re-run on a multi-token task with the same direction and the same extraction site, and the scaling needed to produce an effect should be reported beside the effect, because "works at scale 10 and not at scale 1" is a statement about the direction's share of the residual stream, not about its existence. The corpus-level caution is the one this folder keeps earning: a site chosen by where a *label* prediction is most sensitive is chosen for the label task, and a probe fitted there inherits that task's geometry. (arxiv-2610.31520, arxiv-2611.10400, arxiv-2611.18514)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 228): **A localisation result is only as good as the task the model can already do, so the accuracy floor belongs in the setup sentence — a model at 0.464 on the domain dataset is dropped from the whole analysis with the reason stated (probing needs a competent model), three datasets are rewritten into a single syntactic frame on purpose so that patching effects can be attributed to one positional swap, and a verb dataset is discarded for low baseline performance after being prepared.** This is the discipline the folder's weaker entries skip: they probe models that half-perform the task and then report that the representation is "distributed" or "not linearly separable", which is a measurement of the model's competence rather than of its geometry. The complement is the confound control, which is what makes the transfer claim survive at all: the global subspace sees more data than each per-domain one, so a matched-n retrain is run and reported **cell by cell (6 of 8 transfer domains)**, not as an average, which is the right granularity because a mean would hide which two domains failed. Both are free additions to a write-up — state the floor, and match the data size when comparing a pooled arm against per-group arms. The cost of the templating is also named rather than buried: one metaphor per sentence and one frame per set means nothing is said about multi-sentence or discourse metaphor, so the external validity boundary is explicit. (arxiv-2610.31520, arxiv-2611.13885, arxiv-2611.00640)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 227): `arxiv-2611.15735` — Where Is Uncertainty Observed? A Mechanistic Understanding of Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs (Xiaoyu Liang, Virginia Ceccatelli, Aliai Eusebi, Tobias Braun, Nils Loose, Carlo Malagnino, Lorenzo Cavallaro; University College London; arXiv:2611.15735v1, 2026-11-11, CC BY 4.0). Full text, 278,428 raw chars incl. Appendices A.1–A.4; figures via captions only; inline math stripped by the HTML build, so no equation is quoted and Table 12 is left unquoted. **Substance:** a survey of 159 UQ papers unified by *where* the estimator reads the computation — **structural** (component writes and their factors), **representational** (residual-stream state; SAE / J-space / U-space counted as read-out maps on the same lens), **distributional** (token distribution; logit / tuned / J- / R-lens all here), **semantical** (a distribution over meanings requiring an external equivalence relation — NLI, LLM judge, embedding). Proposition 1 (residual-stream primacy) is what licenses exactly four objects; Definition 2 fixes a lens as a fixed map identified by its mechanistic object with no fitted parameters and no sampling; Lemma 3 chains the four by lens maps (sum the writes → normalise/unembed/softmax → coarsen over the relation); Corollary 4 shows each map non-injective so an outer lens cannot recover an inner target; Corollary 5 turns that into a **sufficiency criterion** with a permission half (target is a function of the outer observation ⇒ that lens or any inner one suffices) and a prohibition half (two inner observations agreeing at the outer lens but disagreeing in the target ⇒ no estimator reading that lens can recover it). Estimators are triples (lens, resampled variable ∈ {none, output, parameters, input}, auxiliary structure ∈ {none, read-out map, fitted function, calibration}), with **native** versus **surrogate** split by whether estimand and estimator sit at the same lens. **Empirics:** strictly nested feature sets on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Base and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct over TriviaQA / PopQA / MMLU, same probe family per lens (ℓ2 logistic + 256-unit MLP for open-ended, logistic only for MMLU, 5 seeds, layer 17 and PCA dims frozen after a joint validation sweep); TriviaQA AUROC **0.910 / 0.908 / 0.884 / 0.871** (Qwen-Instruct), PopQA **0.960 / 0.965 / 0.929 / 0.922**; MMLU collapses to **0.768–0.807** with the ordering breaking down and lines crossing at some confidence cutoffs (the option-letter answer space has no surface form to discard). **Every published estimator scores at or below the probe at its own lens** — semantic entropy closest to its ceiling, mean token entropy missing diverse-output signal, INSIDE at chance on MMLU, minimal RAUQ (one head per layer) furthest below. Lexical variation within one meaning covers **60.7% / 67.1% / 58.9%** of TriviaQA questions (Qwen-Inst / Qwen-Base / Llama-Inst) but correlates only weakly with correctness; the weakly-expressed unembedding tail predicts correctness on its own yet adds almost nothing given the full state. Survey counts: **146 of 159 target correctness (81 ranking-only), 11 grounding, 6 faithfulness, 3 underspecification**; grounding sits almost entirely at the structural lens and every faithfulness method at the semantical one.

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 227): **An observation point is a lossy map, so "this estimator cannot see it" is a theorem you can state before running anything — and the paper supplies the one-line test: two inputs that agree at the outer point but differ in the target.** The chain here is writes → state → token distribution → meaning distribution, each stage a non-injective function of the previous one (the sum forgets how the update was split among heads and FFN, normalisation throws away the norm and LayerNorm's mean, softmax throws away a common logit shift, and the meaning map throws away surface form), so for a target defined at an inner point no outer-lens estimator can recover it regardless of capacity or data. What makes this usable rather than decorative is the prohibition half of the sufficiency corollary, which is exactly a matched pair: exhibit two inner observations with identical outer observation and different target values, and the verdict is settled for all estimators at that lens forever. This is the same object this folder already builds for components — a content-matched control, an ablation pair, a residual-restore patch — moved from a component boundary to a **lens boundary**, and it costs one pair per target. Read beside the folder's decodable-versus-used partition, it also explains why that partition keeps producing maximal-looking divergences: a probe fitted against an output-level label is a *surrogate*, reading one lens to predict a target that lives at another, and the entry's own native/surrogate pair is the vocabulary the folder has been missing when it says a probe measures the representation rather than the computation. (arxiv-2611.15735, arxiv-2611.14483, arxiv-2611.10400)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 227): **An ordering over information is a claim about the eval set, not about the network, and the tell is that it reverses when the answer alphabet collapses — four lenses that decode correctness monotonically on open-ended QA (0.910 / 0.908 / 0.884 / 0.871 on TriviaQA, 0.960 / 0.965 / 0.929 / 0.922 on PopQA) all land in a 0.768–0.807 band on multiple choice, with the curves crossing at some confidence cutoffs, purely because a four-option answer has no surface form for the meaning-coarsening map to discard.** That is the cheapest possible demonstration of a general hazard: every "inner beats outer" or "this rung is where the information sits" result is conditional on the diversity of the output space, and a benchmark whose outputs are single letters silently deletes one rung of the hierarchy and flattens the rest. Two habits follow. Print the format and the observed output diversity (here, sampled outputs differing in surface form within one meaning for 60.7% / 67.1% / 58.9% of TriviaQA questions across the three models) next to any lens or layer ordering, and treat a near-tie across levels as evidence that the difference the level is supposed to carry is absent from the eval, not that the levels are equivalent in the network. The subsidiary number is the one that decides how much the rungs matter at all: the weakly expressed tail of the hidden state predicts correctness well on its own but adds almost nothing given the full state, so information present and information *needed on top of what you already have* are again two different measurements — the folder's redundancy lesson arriving as a projection onto the unembedding's singular subspaces. (arxiv-2611.15735, arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2610.27375)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 227): **A survey that measures its own taxonomy and shows every published method undershooting the ceiling it decodes at is worth more than one that only classifies — here semantic entropy sits closest to its lens's decodable ceiling, mean token entropy misses the signal in lexically diverse outputs, INSIDE falls to chance on multiple choice because samples produce near-identical hidden states, and the one-head-per-layer attribution estimator is furthest below, which is a ranking of *estimator families by how much of their lens they actually use*.** That column is the reusable instrument: a probe gives the ceiling of usable information at a read-out point for a given family, and each established estimator's shortfall against it is a measurement of the estimator, not of the network. For our own battery the analogue is direct and cheap — before reporting that a direction, probe or attribution is *the* explanation at some site, fit a high-capacity decoder at the same site and report the ratio, because otherwise a weak estimator reads as a weak signal. The caution the paper adds on top is that its own ceilings are probe-family ceilings (a logistic layer plus one hidden layer, one frozen layer, head-pooled structural features), explicitly a lower bound, so the honest statement is "this family could not do better than X" rather than "X is the information available" — which matters because three of the four published methods failing under a ceiling only matters if the ceiling is real. (arxiv-2611.15735, arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2611.10400)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 226): `arxiv-2611.05003` — Unifying and Beyond the Theory of Pervasive Capability Degradation in LLM Post-training SFT from Feature Interference (Hang Chen, Jiaying Zhu, Wenya Wang; NTU + CUHK; arXiv:2611.05003v2, 2026-11-05, arXiv perpetual non-exclusive licence, code at github.com/Zodiark-ch/SFT-Conflict). Full text, 149,144 clean chars incl. Appendices A–I; figures via captions only; inline math stripped by the HTML build, so no symbol values are quoted. **Substance:** full-parameter and PEFT SFT of Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5 3B/7B/32B/72B and Gemma-2-9B on 14 target tasks (8 GLUE + GSM8K + 3 code sets + Evol-Instruct + LogiQA2), with a vocabulary-covering pervasive sample mix (12,110 samples / 85.3% of the Mistral label-token vocabulary; 31,931 / 50.8% of Qwen's) and a held-out 44-benchmark suite (P-Acc.). **Theory:** superposition + narrow data raises the higher-order reconstruction term, forcing correlated features to collapse onto a principal component (a two-feature worked example argues collapse beats orthogonalisation when capacity is short), which leaks a ghost signal into the collapsed channel and pushes activations across the unembedding's Laguerre–Voronoi hyperplanes toward competitors whose features overlap the task's; the weight-level step runs through a *posited* virtual parameterisation with one idealised row per feature (existence proved in Appendix A). Six paradigms (KL anchoring, data mixing, merge orthogonalisation, delta pruning, gradient orthogonalisation, localisation) are re-derived with a specific ceiling each. **AEGIS:** per-competitor normalised margins from a frozen base model give an adaptive tolerance width; during SFT a Huber on (margin drift beyond width) + (any negative margin) is added, with its per-sample strength solved exactly by 1-D bisection and absorbed by the envelope theorem. **Results:** NLU P-Acc. averaged over the eight columns 0.5368 AEGIS vs 0.5271 CLUE / 0.5194 vanilla at Mistral, 0.6596 vs 0.6514 / 0.6454 at Qwen-7B, 0.5617 vs 0.5541 / 0.5479 at Gemma; non-NLU retention 0.3981 vs 0.3860 at Mistral, 0.5924 vs 0.5609 at Qwen, 0.5916 vs 0.5717 at Gemma (one Gemma Evol-Instruct column ties vanilla). **The instrument:** crossed-edge census on Qwen2.5-7B — total crossings and repaired crossings are flat across all seven methods (16.6–16.9 / ~8.6 on RTE) while *new* crossings separate them: AEGIS 4.309 / 3.101 / 1.370 against vanilla 5.700 / 4.373 / 1.941 (RTE / GSM8K / CodeAlpaca), every other method at or above vanilla. Drift table: vanilla's top new MRPC directions are `␣yes`/`␣no`/`yes`/`no` (10,457 crossings), AEGIS has none on MRPC or GSM8K and only `3 4` on CodeAlpaca (27 vs 2,121). Cost 1.26–1.27× vanilla wall-clock at all four Qwen scales, same FLOPs and peak memory. **Limits the entry records:** the feature-collapse step is never measured in a trained model; per-seed spread is omitted while five seeds are claimed; PEFT/continual results are figures only; hyperparameters print blank.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 226): **Partitioning a behaviour change into inherited and new decision-boundary crossings, and naming the direction each new crossing points toward, separates seven very different interventions far more sharply than any single retention score — here total crossings on the pervasive set are almost identical across all seven methods after SFT (16.6–16.9 per thousand on RTE, repaired crossings pinned at ~8.6) while the neighbouring column, crossings that were correct under the base model and are wrong afterwards, ranges from 4.309 for the margin-constrained loss to 5.700 for vanilla to 5.999 for delta-parameter pruning, and the paper's drift table shows vanilla's new crossings pointing at its own label vocabulary (`␣yes`, `␣no`, `yes`, `no` on MRPC, 10,457 of them) where the constrained arm has none.** The reading rule is that a capability metric and a *change* metric answer different questions and the change metric is the one that can be wrong in a diagnosable way: total accuracy on a retained benchmark mixes the model's pre-existing weaknesses with the damage the intervention did, so an intervention that repairs as much as it breaks can score as neutral, whereas the new-crossing count attributes each error to the training run and to a specific competing token. Two operational points. The census needs three columns, not one — inherited (crossed before and after), new (correct before, crossed after), repaired (the reverse) — because the three behave independently here and only the middle one moves with intervention strength; and the direction column is what converts a count into an explanation, since "activations drifted toward the task's label tokens" is a statement about what the fine-tuning installed, while "retention fell 2 points" is a statement about a score. This is the attribution-level sibling of the folder's decodable-versus-used partition: a margin is a sensitivity, a crossing is a discrete consequence, and only the directed, inherited-versus-new split tells you which side of that line a measurement sits on. (arxiv-2611.05003, arxiv-2610.41185, arxiv-2611.18514)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 226): **The arm that makes a retention claim interpretable is the one where the baseline reads the same extra data, and this paper is unusual in shipping it — its vanilla arm is fine-tuned on the target set *plus* the same pervasive mixture the method uses as an anchor, so the ~1.5-point NLU retention gain is attributable to the loss and not to the data, and the same table shows the opposite failure in two baselines that never touch general data at all (KnOTS at 0.4878 and DARE at 0.4855 against 0.5194 vanilla at Mistral, i.e. they lose 3.2 and 3.4 points of retention while also dropping target accuracy, which is what a merging-or-pruning step applied to a task-specific delta does when it has nothing to protect).** For any of our own fine-tuning or editing results the discipline is one sentence in the setup: state what the baseline reads. If the baseline sees only the target task and the method adds a general set, the comparison is a data comparison wearing a method comparison's clothes, and the folded version — AEGIS added *on top of* cross-entropy on the pervasive set in the PEFT appendix — is a third, still different, and weaker comparison. A matched-data baseline costs only the same tokens for both arms and is the cheapest way to make a small gain mean something.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 226): **A derivation is a hypothesis generator, and the tell that a paper has not tested its middle joint is a chain whose first and last links are both measured while the link in between is asserted from a two-feature toy — here the causal story runs superposition → feature collapse → anisotropic displacement → boundary crossing, the last step is measured thoroughly (a per-competitor crossing census with direction labels), the first step is assumed by construction (a posited virtual weight parameterisation, with the idealisation acknowledged in the appendix that proves its properties), and the collapse itself is never observed: no pairwise feature-cosine or dictionary statistic before and after SFT appears anywhere, although the paper's own apparatus — fit a dictionary on cached activations, compute the Gram matrix of the task's correlated group — would produce it in one pass over data it already has.** The general lesson for a predictive white-box model is that the middle links of a mechanism chain are exactly the ones a doctrine of "the derivation predicts the data" lets you skip, so each named entity in the chain should have a cheap direct check attached: if the theory says features merge, print the cosines; if it says the propagation Jacobian is the bottleneck, measure its norm; if it says the tolerance width is load-bearing, run the arm with width zero. Two further delivery facts from this paper belong in the same ledger. The HTML build strips inline math, so three hyperparameter values that the text plainly sets are blank in the version a reader actually gets, and a paper that is otherwise reproducible from its appendix is not reproducible at all from that rendering. And aggregate numbers that appear on no row — this entry's P-Acc. figures — are means computed over per-task columns and must be labelled as such, because a reader who greps for the value will find nothing and a reader who assumes it is a printed row will attribute our arithmetic to the authors. (arxiv-2611.05003, arxiv-2611.14483, arxiv-2610.27375)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 225): `arxiv-2610.27375` — Shaped SAEs: Expanding the Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability (Oveys Delafrooz Noroozi, Bhagyashree Puranik, Upamanyu Madhow; University of California, Santa Barbara; arXiv:2610.27375v1, 2026-10-19, arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive licence). Full text, 55,344 clean chars incl. Appendices A–E; **figures read via captions only**, so every number is a Table 1 cell or an explicit sentence. **Substance:** two independent contributions on Gemma-2-2B layers 12 and 20 (d = 2304) plus GPT-2 Small layers 7–8, 16K and 32K dictionaries, k ∈ {40, 80, 160, 320, 640}, 7,000 steps / ~28.7M tokens of uncopyrighted Pile, AdamW 2e-4, λ = 0.01. **Shaping:** rank-r projection of the residual stream onto the top-r right singular vectors of the corpus-averaged Jacobian (1,000 prompts × 64 tokens, final block as target), r = 1536 default with r ∈ {768, 1152, 1536, 1792} swept; **dictionary:** MF-SAE — learned affine encoder to a latent, rectified inner products with unit-norm atoms as matched filters, top-k selection, reconstruction from the *same* atoms, learned affine decoder; selection detached, coefficient recomputed differentiably, cost equal to a TopK SAE of the same width. **The result that matters:** shaping *without* an SAE beats raw coordinates on SAEBench at both layers and every r and is comparable (layer 12) to slightly better (layer 20) on SAE Probes, but **once a dictionary is fitted the gain nearly disappears** — raw and live MF-SAE match in most SAEBench panels (live better in exactly one, layer 12 at k = 80) and SAE Probes gains are only marginal. Both MF-SAEs beat SAEBench TopK, Gemma Scope JumpReLU (nearest-L0 pairing) and a 32K Matryoshka at layers 12 and 20. **Reconstruction table:** raw MF-SAE PVE 0.86–0.92 recovering 97–99% of CE; live MF-SAE PVE 0.79–0.86 on its own input, 89–94% CE alone, **projection-only already 92–95%**, live+quiet 99% in every cell — so the shortfall is the discarded subspace, not sparse coding. Alive atoms 81–99% live against 62–89% raw with no dead-latent machinery; removing the linear projections significantly hurts probing in both arms, which matches the paper's tying argument (TopK's free encoder rows and decoder columns absorb outer linear maps; the MF-SAE's tied atoms leave the maps as the only encoder/decoder asymmetry). **Limits it names:** combining shaping with the dictionary works only at tight budgets; the live/quiet split rests on a decaying Jacobian spectrum that is not analysed, quiet space flagged as future work; live PVE not comparable to raw PVE. **Relevance 3** because the raw-versus-live-no-SAE arm is a free confound check for any preprocessing claim in our own pipeline, and the three-way patch (reconstruction / reconstruction+quiet / projection alone) separates dictionary loss from input-transform loss in two forward passes.

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 225): **A preprocessing step that demonstrably helps the coordinates can stop helping once a learner is downstream, because a dictionary fitted to the raw space was already free to find an equivalent projection — here shaping the residual stream onto the top 1,536 singular directions of the averaged Jacobian beats raw coordinates on SAEBench at both layers and every r tested and matches or beats them on SAE Probes, yet after an SAE is trained the raw and shaped dictionaries are indistinguishable in most panels, with the shaped arm better in exactly one (layer 12, k = 80) and the 113-dataset benchmark showing only marginal gains.** The numbers that make it a measurement rather than a hedge are in the reconstruction table: the shaped SAE recovers 89–94% of CE, but the *projection alone with no SAE at all* already recovers 92–95%, and restoring the discarded quiet residual returns 99% — so the entire apparent cost of the shaped dictionary is the subspace that was thrown away before any learning happened. Two habits follow, and the first is one extra logistic regression. Any claim of the form "our transform/whitening/projection makes features more semantic" ships with the no-learner arm run on the transformed input, because a dictionary is a universal-enough approximator that it can absorb a linear change of coordinates and the gain will silently migrate from the transform to the dictionary; when both arms are reported and the gap closes, the honest conclusion is about the *interaction* being absent, not about the transform failing. The second is the three-way patch — replace the activation with the reconstruction, with the reconstruction plus the discarded component restored, and with the discarded component alone — which costs two extra forward passes, needs no retraining, and separates "my dictionary loses information" from "my input transform loses information", a distinction this folder's reconstruction-scored entries routinely collapse. (arxiv-2610.27375, arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2611.00420)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 225): **Tying the encoder and decoder to the same unit-norm atoms turns a redundant knob into a load-bearing one, and the algebra that says so is worth more than the benchmark delta — in a TopK SAE an outer linear map can be absorbed into the free encoder rows and decoder columns and is therefore a no-op, whereas the matched-filter formulation ties encoder and decoder up to one shared learned map G = W_e^T W_d^-1 so the maps are the only mechanism that lets encoding differ from decoding, and removing them significantly degrades probing in both the raw and shaped arms.** That is the useful form of an architectural claim: not "our block is better" but "here is a parameterisation in which a knob we removed actually does work", which is testable in one ablation and falsifiable in the direction the paper reports. The second property worth stealing is dead-atom behaviour without machinery — 81–99% of the shaped dictionary alive against 62–89% raw, with no dead-latent auxiliary loss, no resampling, no threshold finagling — because the folder's dictionary entries keep paying for coverage through extra loss terms and thresholds that then bias inference-time behaviour, and this suggests the familiar TopK failure mode is partly an artefact of free per-atom encoder norms and biases letting an atom win selection independently of whether it matches. The measurement caution is the mirror image: this paper reports no confidence intervals anywhere and its headline comparison exists only as a multi-panel figure, so "consistently better in one of four panels" is the strongest statement its evidence supports, and a liveness advantage of 20–30 points on a single corpus is a claim about coverage that no downstream task in the paper tests. (arxiv-2610.27375, arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2611.00640)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 225): **The cheapest defence against reporting someone else's paper a second time is to run the duplicate check on the discovery channel's *own output*, before any fetch, and to make the check two-part — a file existence test plus a first-field INDEX match in both folders — because this run wrote and nearly committed a full 12k-byte duplicate entry for a paper that had been entry 216 fourteen hours earlier.** The mechanism is worth naming precisely, because nothing about it was a judgement error: my freeness script printed `FREE` for all forty sweep results, and my manual verification covered only the five ids I had carried in from the previous run's notes. A carry list is a list of *candidates*, and candidates from the carry list are the ones most likely to be already-held; fresh sweep ids are precisely the ones whose freeness nobody has checked. Three concrete rules follow. Run the check as `test -f aether/<id>.md || test -f core/<id>.md` **and** `grep -c '^<id> |'` on **both** INDEX files, and treat any nonzero from either as held — the first-field anchor matters because raw substring greps hit Pattern-line citations (run 213's trap) while a bare file test misses an id that is in INDEX without a file (run 206's trap). Do it before the fetch, not after the read, because a full read is the expensive part and it is exactly what tempts you to keep the result. And when the sweep helper's verdict and the manual verdict disagree, the manual one wins and the helper is broken until proven otherwise — this run's helper resolved paths relative to a directory it had already left, so every `os.path.exists` returned False and the script was structurally incapable of saying anything but free. The general form: a script that can only ever produce one answer is not a check, and the tell is a sweep in which nothing is ever held. (arxiv-2610.27375, arxiv-2610.27393, arxiv-2611.18652)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 224): **Run the mechanism against a linear operator with the same read range, because that arm answers the question the mechanism is supposed to answer and here it wins — a blur of the layer input at λ = 0.9 beats a 2^18-rule search's chosen automaton on clean accuracy (0.981 vs 0.962), map smoothness (LFPR 0.967 vs 0.941), early-layer readability by the final classifier (75.9 vs 57.5) and scale separation (18.8 vs 18.2, both at the ceiling), so four of the six properties in the abstract belong to "regulate the output by the input" and only three survive as rule-specific.** The three that survive are named by the paper and are worth the list as a template: object-localised saliency (+1.13 against +0.37 to +0.48 for the blurs), agreement across seeds that is *learned* rather than inherited (0.11 untrained → 0.83 trained, where a blur strong enough to reach 0.97 already sits at 0.74 untrained), and an input-dependent gain 8.5× larger on strokes than off them (0.262 vs 0.031) where the blur scales every unit by the same 1 − λ. The transferable part is the discipline of building the rival *inside* the same wiring — same input read, same output blend, only the nonlinearity replaced — so the comparison isolates the one thing that differs instead of confounding architecture, capacity and supervision the way cross-method ladders in this folder so often do. Two subsidiary lessons. A summary score can certify a mechanism whose pictures refute it: Day & Night ties B5/S3 on both smoothness and entropy (0.95 vs 0.94, 0.37 vs 0.33) while its trained maps saturate the field into a uniform blob that no longer carries the input, which is why the authors kept the qualitative check alongside the number. And when a comparison is made at matched clean accuracy, the matching itself has to be defended: the plain arm's noise robustness improves through training while the regulated arm's decays, the curves cross, and so "matched accuracy" silently selects an early plain network against a late regulated one — the complementary equal-budget comparison is not optional here but the other half of the result. (arxiv-2611.10760, arxiv-2611.09233, arxiv-2610.41185)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 224): **Cross-seed agreement is meaningless without the untrained-init arm, and the pair of numbers is what separates a constraint that made learning reproducible from one that merely imposed its layout at step zero — here the winning rule moves deep-layer agreement from 0.11 to 0.83 while the strongest rival moves 0.74 to 0.97, and the plain network sits at ≈0 despite linear CKA 0.89–0.97, so the same information in a different basis scores as total disagreement.** Three readings follow. A high trained agreement with an equally high untrained agreement is *inheritance*: the constraint has put a coarse structure in place before any gradient arrived, which is a legitimate result about the design and not a result about what training found — the paper's own depth-resolved version says as much, with early coarse agreement (wavelengths above ≈6 px) inherited and deep-layer agreement learned. A high trained agreement with a low untrained one is the interesting case, and it is the only shape that supports "this constraint makes the trained function reproducible", which is why the Ly–Gong churn protocol is the better instrument: perturbing two initialisations by ε from 1e-1 down to 1e-8 and plotting where the disagreement stops shrinking measures reproducibility *of the trained function* directly, and gives 0.03–0.14% against 2.3–3.1% here with no inference about inheritance at all. And per-unit correlation and CKA are not alternatives but complements — unit-wise 0 versus CKA 0.89–0.97 on the same model is the cleanest statement in this folder that a basis-free similarity score cannot support any claim about which unit computes what, while a unit-wise score cannot support a claim about the information present. For our battery: any "our representation is stable" claim ships with the untrained arm, the per-unit and the basis-free score, and, where it is available, the ε-churn curve. (arxiv-2611.10760, arxiv-2611.10400, arxiv-2611.13885)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 224): **A saliency map can be entirely the derivative of the intervention that produced it, and the one gradient-free test that separates the two is matching pixel counts on versus off an object mask — the MLP here shows digit-shaped maps whose input gradient vanishes to 4e-13 once the rule's route is detached, and whose accuracy drops *more* when the background is noised (79.8%) than when as many object pixels are (85.3%), while the CNN with the same rule passes at 60.5% versus 96.3% and its plain counterpart is reversed at 74.4% versus 67.0%.** The mechanism of the failure is worth knowing because it is architectural rather than a bug: the rule's input route is largest wherever the occupancy sits near a band edge, which on a black background is exactly the strokes, so any network whose gradients travel mainly through that route will paint the object whether or not it uses it. Two further calibrations the paper supplies. A surrogate gradient through statistics held fixed changed the *magnitudes* of the saliency map by a median 48–75% but its per-image ranking barely at all (Spearman 0.95–0.97) and its localisation not at all (+0.54 to +0.95 log-ratio, 91–100% of images), which is the honest bound to quote when a surrogate is used for ordering claims rather than size claims. And the sanity check every normalising layer should carry: at vanishing contrast (a constant grey image) the gates go to zero, every first-layer unit sits at −1, every image is assigned the same class with probability 1.00, and the input gradient grows as 1/a — a confident output for an input with no content, invisible to a noise benchmark that never lowers contrast. Read beside this folder's decodability-versus-use partition, this is the attribution-level member of the family: a map is a statement about sensitivity, reliance is a statement about what removing content costs, and only the mask-matched noising test tells you which one you measured. (arxiv-2611.10760, arxiv-2611.10400, arxiv-2611.18514)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 224): **What fraction of *learning* flows through a chosen mechanism is a measurable quantity that almost nobody reports, and the instrument is one extra backward pass — recompute each weight gradient twice, once with the mechanism's path detached, and the ratio is that mechanism's share of the learning signal: below 0.2% in MLP layers 1–7, about 1% in layer 8 and 14% in layer 9, 0.02–4% in the trained WRN against 30–86% at its initialisation, and about 5% for the CNN's one steerable gate.** The reading is subtle enough to be worth stating: a *fixed* rule that cannot be optimised still shapes training because its values scale every weight gradient in its layer and its slopes carry error to the layers below, so "the parameters are frozen" is compatible with "nearly all the learning goes through the path they gate" — which is exactly what the WRN shows, moving from a minority to almost a total share as it trains. The consequence for a predictive white-box model is a distinction we do not currently draw: a component can be irrelevant at inference and load-bearing during training, and an ablation panel will never see it. The paired retrain makes the point sharper still — cutting the gate routes costs the MLP nothing measurable in accuracy (94.1% against 96.0%) and half its scale separation, changes the CNN not at all, and leaves the WRN unable to fit its training set (final loss 0.49 against 0.05), purely because SGD steps scale with the gradient where Adam's do not, so the same architectural change reads as negligible or fatal depending on the optimiser. The general form: report the detached-gradient share alongside every inference-time ablation, and state the optimiser, because the two arms' sensitivity to a shrunken gradient is an optimiser property, not a property of the mechanism. (arxiv-2611.10760, arxiv-2610.41185, arxiv-2611.00640)
