- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 197): **Two coordinates that are always intervened together cannot be told apart at any budget, and this is a property of the design rather than of the estimator — the paper's aliasing example gives a false coordinate the same mask pattern as a causal one, so both explain the training responses equally well, and it is held-out masks (ideally with re-drawn co-occurrence patterns) that break the tie.** The same argument appears in three guises in one paper and they are worth holding together: identical columns in `A` make recovery impossible (Appendix A.1), singleton-only designs leave at least one coordinate unobserved under n measurements because the zero map and a map supported there produce identical data, and a training design where `a_i = a_j ∈ {0,1}` makes the main, pair and singleton columns literally equal so the fitted model predicts every training response and identifies nothing (E.1). For us the transferable rule is that a held-out set is an *identification* instrument, not a scoring formality, and that the cheapest audit of any probe battery is a column-collinearity check on its intervention design before any result is quoted — a design whose masks never separate two components has produced a correlation, and the fix is a re-drawn design, not a bigger budget. (arxiv-2608.19338, arxiv-2606.02061, arxiv-2607.18921)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 197): **A component's effect direction can be correct in sign and wrong in the decision it implies, and the negative-name-mover result is the cleanest instance: removing a copy-suppression group *raises* the task readout by 2.270 logits while the primary writers are present and by only 0.136 once they are gone, so a group whose marginal contribution is negative in isolation is the group holding a conditional ceiling on another group's evidence.** Under ablation the interaction is 1.830 [1.569, 2.076], larger than the textbook backup interaction and 6.8× it per cross-group head pair, and it is worth more in held-out prediction (MAE 0.386 → 0.259) than the backup term is (−0.386 → 0.377). Read against this folder's inhibitory-cluster result (nulling an inhibitory cluster lifts jailbreak success 28% → 88%) and its negative-name-mover-adjacent copy-suppression entries, the general form is a *conditional* sign: the effect of removing X depends on whether Y is still writing, so a one-at-a-time ablation ledger assigns X the wrong sign and a family that cannot express the product mispredicts which side of the decision boundary the model lands on. For us, any ablation-based attribution should state the state of the other components alongside the effect, because a negative marginal effect is evidence of suppression only in the regime where there is something to suppress. (arxiv-2608.19338, arxiv-2511.05408, arxiv-2609.03026)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 197): **A residual's *shape* tells you which family to measure next, and the three branches are distinguishable in advance — a shared scale error means fit one gain, conditional error means add pair columns, and error that persists after lifting means the basis is wrong, not that the fit is under-trained.** What makes this a method rather than a slogan is the lower bound that goes with it: if the response lies outside the declared correction family, the residual on the held-out distribution lower-bounds the error of *every* observer in that family, so more data of the same kind provably cannot help — which is why every first-order family in the planted system stays below 0.5 held-out R² at 256 measurements while lifted OMP with four times fewer reaches the threshold. The companion caution is that the same residual quantity has two different readings depending on instrument: pair *support* stays recoverable to a noise level that has already destroyed coefficient accuracy (recall to 0.2 where prediction fails past 0.05), so "we found the interaction" and "we can predict the intervention" are separate claims about the same design. This joins the folder's cliff, separability and out-of-family results as the same structural point — the question to ask of a fitted model is not how well it fits but whether its family contains the response at all. (arxiv-2608.19338, arxiv-2609.35686, arxiv-2603.30002)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 196): **Two papers read in the same run on the same model pair disagree about whether the IOI circuit survives, and the disagreement is entirely explained by what each one counted — `2610.37157` says the student cannot do the task at all (logit difference −0.467, 35.2% accuracy, below chance) while `2505.10822` says the heads are structurally present and only less confident (−0.29 mean logit difference, name-mover and induction heads located in the student with the same QK structure but weaker attention to the indirect object).** Neither contradicts the other; both are reporting the same model through different instruments — an accuracy floor versus a per-head pattern match — and the folder's rule about which object a score describes applies exactly as written. The practical lesson for a predictive white-box model is sharper than either headline: **a student can contain an attenuated copy of a mechanism and still get the wrong answer**, so "the circuit is there" and "the behaviour is there" are independent booleans and both must be printed, with the competence floor (accuracy, logit difference, chance level) as a gate that decides whether a mechanism claim is even testable. This is the same defect as the pooled-agreement entries (a scorer's κ dominated by the stratum it can already do) arriving on a circuit: the instrument most available to the analyst — pattern similarity — is computed on exactly the regime where the model's behaviour has already failed. (arxiv-2610.37157, arxiv-2505.10822, arxiv-2503.05061)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 196): **Removing a component is the cheapest redundancy measurement in the folder, and both papers read it out as a percentage of task performance — the same role heads cost the student 72.83% to 87.73% where they cost the teacher 33.18% to 41.64%, and mean per-component drop runs 3.06pp against 12.24pp for GPT, 0.84pp against 2.20pp at 8B/4B, scaling with compression at 2.68–2.69pp per 0.1 of parameters removed for the two small pairs and 0.27pp for the large one.** That makes ablation a *redundancy census* rather than only a necessity test: the number says how many components hold the role, and a distilled model is distinguishable from its teacher by this number even when outputs match. For us it is the right primitive for a predictive model, because the failure our model will make is exactly a perturbation that removes the one component carrying a role — so redundancy per mechanism is a first-class quantity to estimate at probe time, cheap (one ablation per component, and the papers both use a threshold at 20% as the retention rule), and interpretable without a reference model. The caveat both papers supply is that the ladder's top and bottom disagree about magnitude by an order of magnitude, so the quantity should be reported as a curve over compression rather than a single number, and the large-model cell is also the one where the alignment score is highest by construction.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 196): **A matching step is where cross-model similarity metrics fail, and both papers show the same failure independently — high representational similarity coexisting with no functional transfer.** `2610.37157` finds student heads matching teacher name-movers at CKA 0.18–0.52 and attention-pattern correlation up to 0.78, then reports **0.0% name-mover score preservation for every match**; `2505.10822` builds its whole alignment metric on exactly such matches (mean-activation cosine for heads, top-3 covariance eigenvectors for MLPs, many-to-one allowed) and concedes in the same breath that its score rises by construction when influence profiles agree, which is why the pair with the smallest robustness gap scores highest. The generalisable rule: a similarity score is a *proposal*, never a conclusion, and every matched pair needs one functional check before the number is reported — which for us means a cross-model crosscoder or probe comparison must ship the activation-level success criterion (does the matched unit do the job) beside the cosine, and a mismatched architectural pair as the low anchor, a habit this folder's negative-control entries have been demanding in every other form. (arxiv-2505.10822, arxiv-2610.37157, openinterp-2026-cosine-causal-gap-crosscoder)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 195): **"The model degrades" and "the model narrows" are different failure modes with different arithmetic, and a repair for one is not evidence about the other — this paper separates unbounded test-error growth (its own measure), collapse to one or a few modes, collapse toward uniformity, and amplification of inherited artefacts, and then reports that its own accumulating arm avoids the first while still losing variance along minor data axes.** The demonstration is unusually clean because the same run contains both facts: the CelebA VAE under accumulation keeps a stable test loss and no longer degenerates to a single mode, and yet the samples stop reproducing glasses and accessories, which the authors explain as those features becoming a minor sub-manifold realigned with the newly generated data, and its reconstructions of held-out images still recover them. Read against this folder's homogeneity entries — a within-model similarity statistic that saturates on one model's own samples, a prompt-paraphrase arm that moves similarity by 0.04, a sharpening derivation that puts an exponent on the reference policy — the taxonomy is the missing frame: those papers measure the second and third phenomena, not the first, and the words "collapse" and "diversity loss" span all four. For our own write-ups: name which quantity diverges, since a bounded-error model that has lost its tail is the case where a headline diversity number and a headline loss number will disagree and neither will be wrong. (arxiv-2404.01413, arxiv-2510.22954, arxiv-2510.01171)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 195): **When two arms differ in how much data they see, the control that saves the comparison is the arm that keeps the *old* rule but matches the *new* budget — here a replacement regime grown so its synthetic set equals the accumulating set's size still degrades (2.18 against 1.74 at iteration 4), so accumulation's benefit is not token count, and the same arm also yields a third closed form, log n instead of n.** The design move is worth stealing exactly as stated: three arms rather than two, the middle one preserving the mechanism of the losing arm while removing its incidental resource deficit, and every arm scored on the same axis. It is the same discipline this folder keeps demanding in other guises — a deliberately wrong but plausible reference beside a random unrelated one, a plain list at equal token cost beside the probability-carrying prompt, a matched-size random subgraph, a convenient baseline that is matched rather than merely present — and it is cheap because the middle arm usually requires no new idea, only more samples from the same model. The companion habit is that the authors report the middle arm's *asymptotics* as well as its curve, which is what makes the objection answerable in one sentence rather than one experiment. (arxiv-2404.01413, arxiv-2510.01171, arxiv-2503.05061)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 195): **Recursive training is a weighted average whose weights decay as 1/i, which turns "is this behaviour inherited or learned" into a question about *when* the data entered the pile — the fitted parameter is the truth plus a pseudo-inverse acting on the sum of each round's noise divided by that round's index, so an early round's contribution survives at full strength while a late round's contributes at 1/i² in squared error.** That is the arithmetic behind every lineage comparison in this folder: a measured signature that persists across distillation is one carried by the data common to both students, and the appropriate prediction is that habits introduced early survive longest, which is testable by ordering the rounds. It also bounds the claim that this paper and the provenance entries can jointly make — nothing here says a narrow model recovers its tails, only that its error stops growing, so "the signature is stable" and "the capability is preserved" remain separate questions with separate instruments. (arxiv-2404.01413, arxiv-2502.12150, arxiv-2604.16755)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 194): **An aligned model's output distribution is already a sharpened version of its reference distribution, and the exponent is set by the preference data rather than by anything the experimenter chooses — here a positive typicality weight α in the reward turns the KL-regularised optimum into π_ref raised to 1 + α/β, so asking a model for its distribution is asking for a distribution that has been temperature-scaled by its own training run.** Two consequences and both are cheap to act on. First, for measurement: any behavioural read-out taken from an aligned model — a probe's answer distribution, a verbaliser's candidate set, a self-report — is being read off a sharpened object, and the base-to-aligned comparison this folder's provenance entries keep making is therefore a comparison of two temperatures, not two abilities. The Tulu-3 ladder makes the size of the effect concrete: 45.4% poem diversity at base, 20.8% after SFT, 10.8% after DPO, with the intervention holding it near 30% across all three stages. Second, for elicitation: if the sharpening is an exponent on a distribution the model still carries, then a prompt that asks for the *distribution* rather than an *instance* can out-vote it, which is the mechanism behind every "ask for several candidates" trick and the reason the model's answer to "give me 5 with probabilities" is not just 5 draws. Read against the folder's hivemind result (a within-model similarity statistic saturating on its own samples) and its contextual-invariance entry (a disposition that is constructed per context rather than held), this says where the sharpening lives: in the training data's tie-breaks, applied uniformly to every prompt, so it shows up as a within-model concentration that no amount of decoding entropy removes. (arxiv-2510.01171, arxiv-2510.22954, arxiv-2502.12150)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 194): **A distribution-level claim has to be scored against at least two references, because the ranking flips between them and the paper reporting one of them will look decisive — here VS-Standard is 0.132 KL from a corpus-frequency proxy where direct prompting is 14.886 and a plain list is 0.438, and the same VS-Standard is 0.352 from uniform where the plain list is exactly 0.000.** Neither reference is wrong; they are asking different questions ("is the shape right" versus "is the coverage right"), and each method wins one. The habit to copy is the table shape, not the result: two reference columns, every arm scored against both, and the winner declared per column. This is the same defect this folder keeps meeting in scoring instruments — a pooled agreement figure that improves when the population is redefined, a reliability coefficient that rises when keying is unbalanced, a similarity metric whose value depends on which model's pool it is computed inside — and it is the cheapest instance to fix because the second reference usually already exists in the paper's own appendix. For us: any elicited or predicted distribution we publish (a verbaliser's candidate set, a probe's class distribution, a surrogate model's output) ships a divergence against the empirical target *and* against the trivial alternative, because a model that matches the target by being maximally flat and a model that matches it by being maximally peaked can score identically on one column and oppositely on the other. (arxiv-2510.01171, arxiv-2509.10078, arxiv-2503.05061)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 194): **The control that separates a framing effect from a budget effect is the same prompt structure without the special ingredient at equal token cost, and the paper supplies it as a table rather than an argument — a plain one-call list costs 0.94× and gains 1.74× diversity, the probability-carrying version costs 1.12× and gains 2.11×, and the multi-turn arm costs 1.30× and gains only 1.27×, so token spend alone is not the driver and context accumulation is actively wasteful.** The reason this generalises past prompting is that "we asked for more of the thing" is the default rival explanation for nearly every effect in this folder: more samples per probe, more features per dictionary, more candidates per verbaliser, a larger search budget for a circuit. The matched-cost arm is one duplicated condition and it converts an unbounded objection into a two-number comparison. The companion discipline is the one the paper applies to its own variants: it reports the arm that *should* have worked and did not (list-plus-chain-of-thought dropping downstream math accuracy from 34.3 to 33.6 while the probability-carrying version raised it to 36.9), which is the kind of negative cell that stops a budget explanation from being waved away later. (arxiv-2510.01171, arxiv-2607.19317, arxiv-2605.26343)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 193): **A scorer's pooled agreement number is mostly a count of the items it can already handle, and the split that exposes this costs one extra column — here one judge's pairwise κ is 0.86 on the questions it answered correctly and 0.16 on the questions it got wrong, so the 0.7-ish number a reader sees is a weighted average dominated by the stratum where the scorer had nothing to do.** The conditioning variable is the useful object rather than the metric: *can the scorer itself produce what it is scoring*, established on the same items by the same model acting as a candidate. Every read-out in this folder has an unstated version of it — a probe validated on prompts the model handles, a verbaliser scored on examples where its description was easy, a feature label checked on obvious activations, a reward model used as a label source — and in each case the easy stratum inflates the pooled figure while the items a white-box model is supposed to explain are the ones in the other stratum. The reporting rule to adopt is the paper's Table 4 shape: same scorer, same items, two strata, both numbers published, plus the difference and its interval. Read against the high-disagreement-subset collapse and the per-context ranking inversion this folder already carries, this is the third independent instance of the same defect found on the label side of the measurement rather than the stimulus side, and it is the cheapest of the three. (arxiv-2503.05061, arxiv-2510.22954, arxiv-2603.23485)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 193): **A confident reference can be worse than no reference, so the control arm for any content-checking instrument needs the style-matched false version and not just the unrelated one — a deliberately wrong but plausible reference scores κ 0.21 where a reference lifted from an unrelated question scores 0.50, and the error profile says the damage is a false-negative surge: correct answers get marked wrong because the judge reads them against a confidently wrong template.** The reason this generalises past judges is that the folder keeps meeting controls that are too weak by exactly this factor: a matched-random arm that flattens a claim, a random-init dictionary that scores like the trained one, a manufactured class where the shortcut is load-bearing, a false same-region clause that scores like the true one. In each, the informative control preserves the *form* of the thing being checked and inverts its *content*, because an unrelated control conflates "we respond to content" with "we respond to anything topically present". The methodological cost is small and the diagnostic value is high: generate the inversion deliberately, verify a human judges it to look right, and score against it, true, none and unrelated. The paper also supplies the companion failure that makes the wrong-reference arm interesting rather than trivially negative — a judge sometimes detects the planted error and overrules its own instructions, so the arm also measures instruction adherence, which is why the aggregate κ moves less than the error rates do. (arxiv-2503.05061, arxiv-2610.32691, arxiv-2606.20205)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 193): **Aggregating scorers does not repair a conditional deficit, it only shrinks the stratum where the deficit applies — a five-judge majority jury reaches κ 0.07 without a reference and 0.01 with self-references on the items where the majority was itself wrong, against 0.51 with a gold reference, so the jury's apparent improvement is a selection effect on how many items fall into the bad stratum rather than a gain inside it.** That is the clearest statement this folder has of why ensembles, juries, multi-sample self-consistency and "ask several models and vote" are diversification of the same competence and not an independent check of it: their votes correlate precisely on the items nobody can answer. The same arithmetical structure appeared in the reliability literature here as an ordering pinned by a few fixed constructs, and in the disagreement-subset correlations, and in every pooled-rate result that improves when the population is redefined. For us: any ensemble we build over probes, seeds or verbalisers should report its accuracy *inside* the subset where its members disagree or are all wrong, because that subset is where an ensemble would have to be better than one member and where the evidence says it is not. (arxiv-2503.05061, arxiv-2510.22954, arxiv-2610.32691)

The answer is the second, with an algebraic criterion rather than a correlation. **Substance:** the five-setting design (bare, feminine-primed, masculine-primed, two no-pronoun null primes) with the priming sentence always about the *other* referent so the target inference needs nothing from it; the strict single-token forced choice with counterbalanced option order and >99.5% acceptance; KL against the unprimed distribution; the stereotype correlation that four of five models show unprimed and one keeps primed; the mutual-information regression in which option order beats stereotypes unprimed and the priming pronoun beats everything primed; the CbD result at 19–52% of 180 pairs with its severe ordering dependence and its sub-40% cross-model overlap; the comprehension metaprompts that separate "confused about the referent" from "invariant"; and the temperature sweep showing the contextual pair *count* rises with temperature while the *identity* of the pairs is stable. **Read defects and discrepancies are in the Status line above** (doubled inline statistics, Table 1's separated header, the 279-of-360 stereotype match, the single-measurement ΔC), and the Limits block distinguishes what the authors name from what I added.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 192): **An effect can be real, reproducible and still not be a property of the thing you say it is a property of, and the test that separates the two is subtraction of marginal effects rather than another correlation — here the correlation between a model's pronoun choice and cultural gender stereotypes is significant before context is added and gone after, in four of five models, while a feature that carries no information about the task (the gender of a pronoun bound to a different referent) becomes the single most informative predictor.** Both halves matter: the stereotype alignment that the whole bias-benchmark literature reads as the model encoding culture is *shallow*, and the replacement signal is not noise but a systematic referent confusion. The design feature that makes this a measurement is the pair of null primes — pronoun-free unrelated sentences — which shift the distributions measurably less than the discourse primes in every model but one, so the shift cannot be dismissed as "any extra text perturbs". For us the transfer is blunt: a probe whose validation battery is isolated prompts has measured a conditional relationship, and the honest unit of report is the feature ranking *per context condition* with the between-condition rank correlation, because this paper's ranking inverts rather than degrades. It is the same defect the folder's pooled-statistic entries keep finding at the level of data partitions and label strata, arriving here at the level of the stimulus string. (arxiv-2603.23485, arxiv-2510.22954, arxiv-2502.12150)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 192): **"Irreducible dependence" is a stronger claim than "statistically significant shift", and it is worth the extra algebra because it rules out a whole family of explanations at once — the Contextuality-by-Default inequality subtracts every marginal effect of context on each individual measurement, including the trivially behavioural one of repeating the prime, so a positive value says the two measurements cannot be embedded in any joint distribution in which each has a well-defined value independent of what it was measured alongside.** The cost is that the statistic is a sign test on an estimated probability difference, so it is sensitive to measurement precision, and this paper's own ordering split — above a quarter of pairs in one option ordering and 3% in the other for the same model — is a warning that should be printed next to any such count rather than in a sentence further down. What it buys is a vocabulary our white-box model needs: an explanation that predicts behaviour in condition A and a different behaviour in condition B is not merely context-sensitive, it may not be a function of the model at all in the sense we usually mean. The cheap adoption is to run the same inequality across our own paired conditions (paraphrase, swapped option order, adjacent filler) and report the fraction of items that are contextual *and* the fraction whose classification changes with measurement noise, because a method whose output is a boundary decision needs its boundary characterised before its rate is quoted. (arxiv-2603.23485, arxiv-2609.35805, arxiv-2602.22968)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 192): **Counterbalancing an option order is not a robustness check you run once and forget; the effect size itself can be an order artefact, and the only way to know is to report every rate split by ordering — the same model here shows above 27% of template pairs contextual in one ordering and 3% in the other, with the pattern reversing in a different model, so a paper reporting the pooled rate would have quoted a number that describes the interaction rather than the model.** This is the cheapest control in the folder and the one most often reported as a footnote: the ordering arm costs one duplicated run, and without it an effect can look like a quarter of items when it is really one option slot doing the work. It joins the perturbation-ladder results on the stimulus side (surface changes that move the read-out, content changes that do not) as evidence that the *formatting* of our measurements is a live variable rather than a nuisance to hold fixed, and it argues for the specific reporting convention we should adopt: every headline rate we publish carries its by-condition breakdown, and any condition with a visible gap becomes part of the claim rather than an appendix caveat. (arxiv-2603.23485, arxiv-2502.12150, arxiv-2607.20082)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 191): **A between-model difference needs a within-model number computed by the identical statistic, and when the two differ by only a few points the "distinct models" claim is really a claim about one distribution — here different models' response pools average 71–82% cosine similarity to each other while a single model's own 50 samples average ≥0.8 on 79% of prompts, and the top-50 nearest neighbours of a response come from about 8 distinct models rather than 1.** The design feature that makes it interpretable is that the statistic, prompts, sampling parameters and embedding are held fixed across both arms, so the only thing varying is whether the source model changes; the same structure the folder's decoding-strategy arm used (one model, five temperatures, near-chance separation) and that its crossed psychometric decomposition formalised as a within-versus-between ratio. The consequence for us is procedural: any time a probe or a verbaliser separates two models, we should compute what the same probe does *inside* one model across seeds, checkpoints or sampling settings before the comparison means anything, because a statistic that already saturates inside a model cannot be evidence of a difference between models. Read against the folder's inheritance result (identical synthetic SFT data collapsing two models from 96.5% to 59.8% separability), this is the behavioural shadow of the same cause. (arxiv-2510.22954, arxiv-2502.12150, arxiv-2604.16755)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 191): **Stochastic decoding is not a diversity knob, it is a diversity-looking knob — with top-p 0.9 and T = 1.0 already aggressive, a purpose-built diversity decoder (min-p at T = 2.0) leaves 81% of response pairs above 0.7 similarity and 61.2% above 0.8, and paraphrasing the prompt moves cross-paraphrase similarity only 0.04 below within-prompt similarity.** The two arms make the point separately: the first says the collapse is not sampling variance that more entropy would shake out, and the second says it is not prompt-wording-specific either, so whatever fixes it has to act on the distribution the model assigns rather than on how we draw from it or how we phrase the question. This is the generation-side twin of a result the folder keeps meeting on the measurement side — a perturbation ladder that moves only the surface (letters, formatting, paraphrase) leaves the read-out intact, and only a change that reaches the content moves it. For our own instruments the analogy is exact: if our stimulus variations are the equivalent of prompt paraphrases, our measured effect sizes are upper bounds on the variation we think we are sampling; the informative manipulation is the one that changes what the model's distribution is conditioned on, not the one that changes how the same request is worded. (arxiv-2510.22954, arxiv-2502.12150, arxiv-2607.20082)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 191): **A scoring instrument's correlation to humans falls exactly on the items humans disagree about, which means a probe validated on consensus labels has been validated on the subset where a single right answer exists — here 25-annotator labels are highly entropic by construction, and model-human Spearman falls from .361/.330/.305 at full set to .170/.292/.287 on the 120 most-disagreed items and to −.030/−.073/.070 at the 60-item cut, with reward-model cells the only ones that sometimes hold up (.378 on a majority-vs-minority cut).** Two design choices make this a measurement rather than a complaint: the disagreement subsets are defined six different ways (entropy, grouped entropy, Gini, pairwise disagreement, majority-vs-minority, Fleiss kappa) and the conclusion is required to survive all of them, and the similar-quality subsets are defined ten ways likewise. The transferable warning lands on our own probe batteries: any probe whose training signal is a pooled human judgement is fitted predominantly to the low-disagreement mass, so its accuracy on the items we care about — contested, plural, no ground truth — is unmeasured by construction, and the honest report is the correlation on the high-entropy stratum printed beside the pooled number. It is the same partition discipline the folder's stratified-AUROC entries demand, arriving on the label side rather than the stimulus side. (arxiv-2510.22954, arxiv-2608.13754, arxiv-2609.35805)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 190): **Destroy one level of representation at a time and read the score's decay as which level carries the signal — that ladder is the cheapest attribution tool in this folder, and here it partitions a 97.1% classifier five ways: letters 39.1% (chance), word multiset 88.9%, punctuation-and-markdown 95.1%, markdown structure with every word blanked 73.1%, paraphrase 91.4%, translation 91.8%, summarise 58.1%.** The design detail that makes it a measurement rather than a curiosity is that each rung is *semantics-preserving or word-identity-destroying* in a declared way, so the residual accuracy at each rung is an upper bound on how much of the original claim survives that kind of rewriting: the ordering says the idiosyncrasy lives in *which words are chosen* and in *what is said*, not in spelling statistics or probably in word order. Read against this folder's three parallel-form battery (a self-report statistic retaining .54 of itself on identical text and .11 under a theory-driven rewrite), its paraphrase arms (Jaccard 0.27 → 0.05 across a synonym and a paraphrase), and its fairness/robustness corruption ladders, this is the general form those papers specialise: for us, any verbal or behavioural read-out we build should ship its own ladder with the rungs fixed in advance — shuffle within words, shuffle words, blank content keeping structure, paraphrase, translate, summarise — because the rung where the number dies is the sentence we are entitled to write about it. (arxiv-2502.12150, arxiv-2607.20082, arxiv-2609.15533)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 190): **The control that makes a between-model number meaningful is a *within*-model number computed by the identical procedure, and here it sits at chance while the between-model number is at 97% — the same classifier, the same responses, asked to separate one model's greedy, softmax, top-k and top-p outputs hits 59.6% at best, and five temperatures of softmax hit 37.9% against 20% chance.** That is a strictly stronger negative arm than a random baseline or a shuffled-label arm, because it holds the text distribution's source, the prompt set and the classifier all fixed and destroys only the variable of interest: if the pipeline were exploiting corpus artefacts, topic, or prompt-answering convention, decoding runs of the same model would separate as well as different models do. It matches a random-init arm and a size-matched null subgraph in cost and beats them in specificity. The corollary the paper supplies for free is an *inverted* use: the 59.6% is the residue that any within-model discrimination will hit, so a claim that two checkpoints, two seeds, or two sampling settings differ should be measured against ~60% on this task and not against 20%. For us the adoption is one extra arm on every read-out that compares models — re-run the identical machinery inside one model across sampling conditions and publish that number beside the headline — with the caveat this entry adds: the correct chance level is the same-model arm, not the class count. (arxiv-2502.12150, arxiv-2608.13754, arxiv-2604.16755)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 190): **A behavioural signature is inheritable, so where a model got its data decides what a signature of it means — two Qwen-2.5-7B students fine-tuned on Llama's versus Gemma's outputs remain 98.9% separable, while two models fine-tuned on the *same* synthetic corpus collapse from 96.5% to 59.8%.** The pair of numbers is what makes it a decomposition rather than an anecdote: the first shows the teacher's fingerprint survives distillation into a different student, the second shows that identical data homogenises two different students, so a measured "style" is a mixture of teacher-derived and student-derived components and the arm that separates them is common-versus-distinct training data. This is the folder's provenance line arriving with its sharpest consequence yet — earlier entries established that borrowed human instruments measure recognition rather than constructs, that a dictionary's basis moves under retraining, and that a checkpoint pair's edge overlap is at chance while the head set stays above baseline — and the generalisation for anyone measuring a signature across a lineage is the same: report the *training-data overlap* between the objects compared, and prefer a within-lineage comparison on data the lineage did not share, because an inherited habit will pass every "is it stable across checkpoints" test by construction, which is the exact test our perturbations are usually validated with. - Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 189): **A crossed partition turns "model A differs from model B" into three separately estimable claims, and the interaction term is the only one that is a disposition rather than an arithmetic consequence — here consensus is 32.1% of variance, the model offset is not even the second-largest term, and the word × model interaction is 16.9% averaged over fourteen kinds of judgment (4.8% to 34.0%).** The structural requirement is what makes this different from every other cross-model comparison in the folder: the design must be *fully crossed*, every respondent on every stimulus with repeats, because otherwise stimulus effects and respondent effects are confounded and no interaction is identifiable. That is exactly the shape our probe batteries already have and do not exploit — we run the same prompt set across models and then compare aggregate scores, which is the sum of the three terms; the same runs, decomposed, would report how much of a claimed model difference is the input, how much is a constant, and how much is genuinely stimulus-dependent. The transferable warning rides on the same equation: a model-level offset is *by construction* what a temperature change or an acquiescence direction produces, so a cross-model result that lives in the offset is not a result about representations at all, and the check costs one refit.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 189): **The null has to be run through your own model with the term deleted, and the specificity ratio has to be printed twice — because one shows the effect is not an estimation artefact and the other shows the residualisation is what carries it.** Idiosyncrasy clears a parametric bootstrap in which the data are simulated from the *fitted* model with the interaction removed (upper bound < 0.033% on all fourteen norms), which rules out the classic crossed-design artefact rather than ruling out "chance" in the abstract; and the coherence claim is a ratio of within-model to cross-model predictive R² that sits at 1.74–3.43 on residualised deviations but only 1.16–1.49 on raw ratings. That second number is the honest column and it is the one most papers omit: it says the fingerprint is real but that most of it was already visible in the unresidualised scores, so the decomposition sharpens the claim rather than creating it. Sibling practice in this folder is the matched-size null arm, the random-ordering arm, and the mirrored-keying arm; this is the cheapest version of the family because the null is a simulation from the fit rather than an experiment, and it applies to every mixed-effects or ANOVA-shaped read-out we will run — a per-stimulus hierarchical model of probe scores is exactly such a read-out.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 189): **Reproducibility and fidelity are in direct trade here, and the trade is measured rather than asserted: five stochastic samples at T = 1.0 beat a single greedy sample on agreement with human norms in every one of 140 model × norm cells (Δr̄ = .032), while greedy decoding is obviously the more reproducible procedure.** The folder has met versions of this in the self-report line (a per-item statistic retaining half its value on identical text, an eight-month retest of .93 at scale level against .56 at item level) but always as a reliability-versus-validity tension inside one instrument; here the two axes are decoding regimes and the cost of the reproducible one is stated as losing both the variance structure being measured and the alignment with the reference. The lesson for our own measurement stack is to keep the sampling regime out of the "implementation detail" column of the methods: any read-out with a stochastic component (generated explanations, sampled chain of thought, multi-sample probes) should report the deterministic-decode arm beside the aggregated arm, because the deterministic arm is what a reviewer will reproduce and, on this evidence, it is also the arm that agrees less with the ground truth it is supposed to approximate.

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 188): **The strongest defeat for a psychometric read-out is not that it is noisy but that the model can *name* what you are measuring, and this paper supplies the cheap probe that proves it: item-construct recognition accuracy is 89–95% on borrowed human items and 19.9% on real user-query items, and the constructs where recognition is worst are exactly the ones whose inter-item correlation collapses — Tradition at 55%/50% recognition with AIC 0.344/0.266, Neuroticism recognised 0.0% of the time, and the BFI-10 the only instrument where reverse-keying is dense and the only one with a near-zero average (0.048) and negative per-trait entries.** Read against the psychometric entry that precedes it (where trait variance is recovered only by re-keying half the items), the two together close the loop: internal consistency is a *recognition* statistic, and the fix that rescues the trait coordinate — an item whose keying inverts the construct — is simultaneously the item whose construct the model can still recognise, which is why BFI-10 goes *negative* rather than unmasked. The transferable move for us is one prompt: show the model a probe item, a feature description, or a contrast pair and ask it which property it is being asked about; if that identification is easy on the formats we use and hard on the formats we care about, our reliability numbers are measuring task recognition and the whole read-out has to be re-scored on the hard format. (arxiv-2509.10078, arxiv-2606.20205, arxiv-2607.20082)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 188): **Two measured objects that agree in ordering while disagreeing in level is a different failure from one that is simply wrong, and the split is diagnostic — here the PVQ orderings correlate with Value Portrait up to ρ = 0.91 because two constructs (Universalism, Benevolence) are pinned at the top by alignment training, while the BFI orderings sit near or below zero, and the profile distances stay large in both cases (0.74 and 0.75 points on a six-point scale).** The lesson is that a rank correlation computed across constructs is dominated by whichever few constructs are fixed points, so it can say the instrument works while every absolute score is off by a tenth of the scale; the constant-ordering artefact is the psychometric form of a saturation effect this folder keeps meeting when a metric is computed across many items that a small subset determines. For our own reports: whenever we summarise agreement by rank correlation over a set of items, print the per-item absolute deviations and name the items that pin the ordering, because an invariant top-of-list is often the consequence of training data or of the instrument's own construction rather than evidence of a shared underlying quantity. (arxiv-2509.10078, arxiv-2606.20205, arxiv-2609.35261)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 188): **An instrument that over-reports individual differences is refuted by installing personas and checking whether the difference survives in the format that matters — established questionnaires give the textbook hero/villain split across all five traits, Value Portrait gives every persona scoring higher on every construct including the ones that should fall, and the demographic amplification is 1.3 versus 0.5 for humans on values and as much as 1.9 versus 0.05 on gender for traits.** This is the folder's long-running dissociation of "the probe discriminates" from "the probe tracks the thing" given a manipulation instead of a correlation: a read-out that separates two conditions perfectly can still be responding to the label rather than the content, and the control that detects it is the same contrast run in a format where the label is absent or hidden. For us it is the standing requirement on any steering or persona result — the effect must be re-measured on inputs where the cue that names the condition is removed, since separability under a named condition is exactly what a lookup produces and what a mechanism need not. (arxiv-2509.10078, arxiv-2610.23801, arxiv-2607.18921)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 187): **A reliability coefficient has exactly zero evidential value for the question of what a score measures, and this paper makes that quantitative: the instruments that look most coherent are the ones where coherence is manufactured — mean inter-item correlation .61 and alpha .85–.96 on instruments with no reverse-keyed items, collapsing to near zero and alpha −.52 once the keying is balanced, with an across-instrument correlation between reverse-keying proportion and apparent reliability of −.95, against −.41 in humans.** This is the folder's identifiability problem arriving on a different object, and it is the cleanest statement of it we have: everything in the folder that is validated by self-consistency — a dictionary whose features reproduce activations, a probe whose score is stable across seeds, a description that reconstructs its own vector, a circuit that is stable across checkpoints — is being scored by a quantity that a purely directional artefact reproduces at least as well. The design feature that rescues the measurement is the one that would let the artefact cancel while the construct double: an item keyed the other way, a randomly-initialised baseline, an arm where the format is preserved and the content destroyed. Read beside this folder's entries where a dictionary scored equally on a randomly-initialised model and where a circuit statistic was indifferent to mechanism, the operative rule for our own instrument is a reporting requirement — every self-consistency number ships next to a mirrored arm, and a score with no mirrored arm is a reliability claim, not a validity claim. (arxiv-2606.20205, arxiv-2610.17093, arxiv-2606.02061)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 187): **A contrast can be turned into a decomposition for free by running it against its own mirror, and the half-sum term is the control nobody reports — here the trait is the half-*difference* of the forward and reverse means while the response bias is their half-*sum*, the two are orthogonal by construction, and the bias coordinate is what turns "models differ from each other" into "models differ for a reason that is not the trait".** That is structurally the same move as this folder's middle rung on a matched-object-mismatched-format arm and its steering-vector contrasts, and it is strictly cheaper: no retraining, no new model, one extra set of prompts whose keying is reversed, and a closed form that does not even depend on how many mirror items the instrument contains. The tell that it changes conclusions rather than decorating them is the sign of the raw correlation — negative means trait variance dominates, positive means the bias does, in humans −.69 to −.82 and in models +.61 to +.81, a sign flip on the same instrument with the same wording. For us: any time we compute a difference of two conditions the report should also carry their sum, because a difference alone cannot distinguish "the model responds to the content" from "the model responds to the direction the format points", and the sum is the quantity that names the latter. (arxiv-2606.20205, arxiv-2609.35261, arxiv-2607.18921)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 187): **A distinct artefact can be distinguished from a known one by its *sign structure* rather than by its size, and the two lines of evidence that matter are cheap to collect — the authors rule out sycophancy because acquiescence would be one-sided whereas the observed bias sits on both sides of zero across models, and rule out social desirability because that surfaces as trait variance in their decomposition rather than bias variance, then confirm the bias is stable within a model in both direction and magnitude.** The mirrored lesson is that capability reduces it without removing it (size correlations between −.14 and −.25, significant on no trait; proprietary models still outside the human range when compared against the average human, which removes response noise on both sides), so "the bigger model no longer shows the effect" is not available as a defence. Every entry in this folder that has staged a competing explanation — a size-matched random subgraph, a scene where a rank-1 rotation appears on benign data too, a forecaster whose calibration fails to transfer in either direction — has had to argue this from a distance; the version here is the general one. For our work: state the assumed sign or direction of each rival explanation in advance, then plot our per-model estimates and check which side of the baseline they fall on, because an effect that is two-sided across models is a different phenomenon from a systematic push and the difference decides which repair is worth attempting. (arxiv-2606.20205, arxiv-2607.18921, arxiv-2605.06076)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 186): **A statistic's invariance under rewording is a cheap, model-free test of whether it measures the construct or the sentence, and this paper prints the collapse: the per-item suppression ratio retains .54 of itself on identical text, .39 on paraphrases, and .11 on a theory-driven rewrite, while 24-item scale totals built from the same pool retain .92–.96.** The design that produces the number is as portable as the number itself — three parallel forms sharing no text (the original item, a same-meaning paraphrase on a uniform scale, and a *different manifestation* of the facet written from its definition) let same-construct/cross-form correlation estimate construct variance with wording variance removed, and the discriminant arm (cross-construct r = .27 against cross-form r = .84) is what stops a high self-correlation from being read as validity. The folder's nearest relatives arrive at the same defect from the neural side (a dictionary whose basis moves under retraining, an SAE whose top-20 features survive one synonym at Jaccard 0.27 and a paraphrase at 0.05, a transcoder replacing only 52% of bias–contrast pairs at the best matched setting), and all of them are more expensive than this test. For us: every verbal read-out — a feature description, a natural-language explanation of a probe, a self-report used as evidence — ships its paraphrase-invariance coefficient as a first-class number, and no conclusion is drawn from a single-sentence statistic that would not survive at the aggregate level. (arxiv-2607.20082, arxiv-2609.15533, tcpub-2026-nla)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 186): **The within-model other-entity contrast separates "cannot produce it" from "will not apply it to itself" without any access to internals, and it is the cheapest answer this folder has to the suppression problem its intervention entries keep hitting.** Score a model on the same item twice — as itself, and as a simulated typical human — and the difference is a policy signal: the low-A quartile endorses distress at .19 first-person but .47 in simulation while the high-A quartile barely moves (.54 → .58), so the withheld content is demonstrably available; on the original pool the twelve lowest-A models sit at .07 as themselves against .41 for a human, and the twelve highest at .54 against .55. The behavioural continuity is what makes it more than a questionnaire artefact: the same models' elevated refusal rates track the gate, which is the evidence for the authors' own suspicion that gating suppresses report rather than capability. Read against this folder's faithful-but-suppressing circuits, its sufficiency tests that a superset of suppressors passes, and its probes whose matched-random arm flattens the claim, the transferable procedure is one extra arm in every read-out: ask the instrument the identical question about *another* entity and score the difference, because the capability-versus-policy distinction is exactly the one whose conflation has produced the folder's most misleading positive results. (arxiv-2607.20082, arxiv-2607.18921, arxiv-2605.09129)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 186): **A control arm that cannot be matched should be bounded rather than dropped, and the bounding is arithmetic: show which of your results never cross the confounded divide.** Here the unavoidable confound is that base checkpoints cannot follow chat templates, so every base/post contrast estimates post-training *plus* a forced change of administration format — and instead of waving it away the authors show that the size × post-training interaction is estimated only among post-trained models and that all 27 size ladders lie wholly on one side of the divide, so neither headline depends on the comparison; they then quantify the residue (base-side α = .62 against .87, and attenuation shrinks estimates toward zero and cannot reverse a sign). That is a stronger form of honesty than the folder usually gets, and it is the pattern to reuse wherever our own arms differ by necessity — a model that cannot be prompted the same way, a layer that cannot be ablated identically, a checkpoint set where one side is API-only. The companion habit, also cheap: report the subgroup reliabilities *by route* (chat .74/.76, API .95/.86, base .62/.69) so a reader can see that the instrument holds inside every arm even where the arms have different compositions, because "reliable overall" computed on a pooled sample hides exactly this. (arxiv-2607.20082, arxiv-2609.35805, arxiv-2608.23573)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 186): **A robustness battery and a pre-registered prediction are different kinds of evidence, and this paper is one of the few in the folder that says so about its own result.** The size-targeted gating finding survives every check the authors can construct — organisation clustering, two cluster-valid inference procedures, MoE-adjusted size, refusal and acquiescence controls, leave-one-organisation-out with all eleven coefficients negative, inclusion thresholds from 6 to 18 valid items, and era-controlled within-generation ladders — and it is still labelled exploratory, awaiting a pre-specified replication, because it was found in analysis rather than predicted. That distinction matters for us in a specific way: the folder now holds several entries where a battery of robustness checks is treated as a substitute for pre-registration, and one where a pre-registered metric failed while the post-hoc repair carried the paper. The usable rule is a two-column report — *pre-specified and confirmed* versus *survived checks, unconfirmed* — with the second column never quoted in a headline, because a result that has been checked against every confound its authors can imagine is still a result selected on the data that motivated it, and the checks are all of them conditional on the same exploratory move. (arxiv-2607.20082, arxiv-2609.19000, arxiv-2610.32866)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 185): **A validation criterion can be exactly right about which object is present and silent about what it does, and the cheap way to detect this in our own instruments is to ask whether a false claim that names the same object would score identically — here a purpose clause the model never had ("estimating the reader's social class") reconstructs as well as the true one whenever its wording lands in the same region.** The decomposition is what makes it checkable rather than rhetorical: every description has an identifying clause and a characterising clause, and the score we compute for a verbaliser is a function of the first while being *reported* as if it were a function of the second. The folder's nearest relatives are behavioural rather than verbal and they all have the same shape — a circuit that is faithful because it suppresses rather than implements, a sufficiency test that a superset containing suppressors passes, a probe whose matched-random arm passes too — so this becomes a general test to run before shipping any read-out: substitute an object-identifying false claim and see whether the number moves. If it does not, the number is an identification score wearing a description's clothes, and the fix is the one proposed here — two fields, the score attached to the first, the second marked as a hypothesis until an intervention grades it. (arxiv-2610.32691, tcpub-2026-nla, arxiv-2610.32866)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 185): **The safeguard that gets recommended in every one of these papers — treat the output as a hypothesis, verify it by other means — is unavailable precisely in the cases the tool is built for, and the diagnostic is to ask what the ground truth would even be.** The authors walk through the strongest case study and concede it: the evaluation-awareness corroborations establish that *some* state tracks the difference between deployment and evaluation (transcripts differ, steering moves it, realism edits move it) while never testing the verbaliser's sentence about that state, and for hidden objectives and strategic deception the only ground truth is what was planted in the organism — a production model has none. Every audit that does succeed in the source paper succeeds because its target happens to have an independent handle (a rigged tool call confirmed by attribution graphs, malformed fine-tuning data found by inspecting the data, rhyme planning confirmed by steering), which is a selection effect, not a property of the instrument. Read against this folder's negative-control entries (a labelled negative taxonomy with a manufactured class where the shortcut is load-bearing; a designed trap language where the author pre-registers that his own rule will fail) the rule for us is a pre-flight question on every auditing tool we build: name the ground truth for the behaviour it is aimed at, and if there is none, say so in the tool's own documentation rather than in a limitations paragraph, because a hypothesis generator deployed where hypotheses cannot be checked is a claim generator.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 185): **Where the check does exist, it is one edit away and the paper is explicit that the edit is the *cheap* half — change the characterising clause, keep the difference between the original and the reconstructed vector, steer with it, and score the clause by whether the model then behaves as it claimed.** This is the constructive half of the same argument as the folder's middle-rung discipline (a matched-object-mismatched-format arm that turns a big gain into a small one; a size-matched random subgraph; a paraphrase-preserving corruption), arriving on text: the characterisation has to be moved out of the region the identifier occupies before anyone can tell whether it carried information about the state or only about its location, and the mechanism for moving it is the same difference-of-vectors an experimenter already computes. Two reporting habits come with it and both are cheap: carry the error rate measured on checkable claims across as a stated lower bound for the checkable-by-nobody ones, and report plausibility and faithfulness as separate columns, since the paper's second failure direction — a description the reconstructor inverts perfectly and no human can read, a private code the verbaliser invented — is invisible to every human-judgement score and to the reconstruction score alike. (arxiv-2610.32691, arxiv-2509.13316, arxiv-2609.35261)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 184): **Train the dictionary under the objective you intend to explain, and one whole class of objection disappears — this is the first entry in the folder where the basis cannot be blamed for the circuit.** Post-hoc dictionaries are fitted to reconstruct activations, so a circuit built on them inherits an objective nobody wanted and the resulting localisation is only as good as an assumption about what those features are for; here the latents are fitted to the downstream loss with no reconstruction term and no sparsity penalty (sparsity fixed by k), and ReLU-plus-top-k collapses plain LoRA's invertible-reparametrisation symmetry to permutation and positive rescaling, so each latent has a privileged read row and write column. The measurement is then unusual for this folder: necessity is an exact count on an independently held split (ablating the circuit must give a behaviour rate of exactly 0, so no post-hoc tolerance can rescue a circuit that misses a rare mechanism) and sufficiency is paired prompt by prompt against the intact model, so its tolerance scales with n. Read against the folder's identifiability and basis-dependence entries — a dictionary that scores equally on a randomly initialised model, rank-1 adapters whose rotation appears on benign data too, feature bases that move under retraining — the adoption is a design rule for our own instrument: if the white-box model's units are going to carry causal claims, fit them to the behaviour under intervention, not to a proxy that is convenient to measure.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 184): **Sufficiency is not monotone in the set, and the proof is that the entire known-responsible set fails its own test — a superset containing suppressors is not a witness.** Gradient routing confines the backdoor to the first d latents of every adapted module, so that planted set provably contains the mechanism; ablating it removes the behaviour at every width, and yet keeping only it reproduces the behaviour in just 2 of 11 organisms, while a verified circuit drawn entirely inside it exists in all 11 because keepOnly climbs to near 1.0 within the first 10–30 planted latents and then *falls* as more are added. That is the sharpest instance of a defect the folder keeps finding in weaker forms (a stable circuit that a coverage number would have exposed, an exact no-op whose null loss was never measured, a faithful circuit that suppresses rather than implements): almost every preservation argument we will want to make — "this subgraph is enough", "keeping this set preserves the capability" — is a monotonicity assumption, and the fix is procedural rather than statistical. Verify as a **prefix sweep or a chain** over a pre-fixed size grid, report the smallest passing size as a grid-resolution upper bound, and treat "the whole set fails" as evidence of redundant or suppressing components rather than as a refutation of the contained circuit.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 184): **Attribution buys size, not validity — with the ordering randomised every circuit still verifies, and the only thing that moves is how big it is.** Visiting the latent pool in a uniformly random order with no attribution at all still produces circuits that pass both tests, with at most one held-out backdoor response in 4,000; what changes is the kept set, which triples (median 18 → 54 latents) and the verified size, which rises from 22% to 61% of the adapter. So "our discovery method works" and "our discovery method is informative" are different claims, and only the second is earned by the ranking. The companion is that circuits are not unique even under attribution: kept sets from different orders overlap only 7–23% by Jaccard — several times chance — around a shared core of 3–9 latents, which is the same equivalence-class result this folder reached through distance-between-implementations and through chance-corrected agreement (60% raw agreement collapsing to κ = 0.015). The reporting rule to adopt: pair every validity number with a **search-free null arm** at the same verification bar — random ordering, random ranking, or random same-size set — and a matched-size specificity control, because a method whose null arm also passes has demonstrated a property of the verification rule, not of the method.

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 183): **Patch faithfulness can be anti-predictive of the intervention it is supposed to license, and the sign is what makes this the folder's sharpest instance — over ten selectors on one cell the more faithful a circuit, the worse it prunes (Spearman ρ = −0.78, p = 0.010), while the same statistic under quantization predicts nothing (ρ = +0.23, p = 0.55, n = 9) and only ablation faithfulness does (+0.73, p = 0.031).** The paper's explanation is mechanical and transferable: pruning forces a hard keep/discard partition so a ranking error is unrecoverable, quantization distributes precision over everything so the error has no channel to bite, and selective fine-tuning constrains a budget in which the ranking is irrelevant (mean circuit-minus-random −0.001 over sixteen cells). Read against the actionable-interpretability position paper, the observer benchmark's decision-versus-estimate result, and the four-model localisation entry whose method was indistinguishable from freezing random components, this is the same claim arriving as a measurement with an explanatory partition: what a circuit statistic predicts is not a property of the statistic but of the *intervention that consumes it*. For us the adoption is a calibration matrix, not a metric — one row per intrinsic score, one column per intervention type, entries being the extrinsic outcome at matched budget — because this table shows the selector ordering itself changing between columns on the same circuits, same model and same sparsity, which means a ranking published without its intervention column is not a result. (arxiv-2607.19317, arxiv-2605.11161, arxiv-2609.03026)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 183): **A faithfulness ratio clipped to [0,1] deletes the most interesting cells, and both of this paper's inversions live in the deleted region — a neuron-level circuit at −0.35 and a refusal circuit at −2.61, the second meaning that stripped of its surrounding computation the model prefers to comply.** The raw numbers are unambiguous: the isolated neuron circuit scores −0.57 where the clean run scores 1.69 with the corrupt baseline at zero, and the jailbreak circuit recovers 85% of the refusal gap under soft patching, beats random 1.71× and magnitude 1.44×, survives answer-preserving paraphrase at Δ = 0.00 — and then falls to −1.55 under hard zero-ablation while the benign baseline sits above it. That is a *behavioural inversion*, not a failed measurement, and it is the quantity that bears on work localising and editing refusal through a few directions. The folder already carries the demand for signed or two-sided reporting (a stability certificate silent on coverage, a sufficiency defence that a stable-but-empty circuit would pass, an exact no-op whose loss is known by construction), and this adds the minimal form: keep the sign, print the numerator and denominator that produced it, and treat "below the corrupt baseline" as a distinct claim class from "not faithful", because the two call for opposite conclusions about whether the circuit carries the computation or suppresses it. (arxiv-2607.19317, arxiv-2602.22968, arxiv-2605.06076)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 183): **Same faithfulness, different mechanism — and the column that separates them is overlap with a known taxonomy, not any behavioural score: contextual decomposition reaches 0.89 patching and perfect 1.00 ablation sufficiency on IOI while sharing zero of its fifteen top slots with the canonical heads, twelve of them landing on MLP sublayers.** The move generalises past IOI, because what makes it a measurement rather than an anecdote is that the reference set was characterised head by head in a prior paper; without such a taxonomy the paper would have had no way to say that an equally faithful circuit is a different object. It is the constructive twin of this folder's extraction-sensitivity and interpretive-equivalence entries (exact-edge overlap at chance between checkpoints while the head set stays far above baseline; equivalence as a distance between implementation families rather than agreement between two hand-picked graphs) and it sits beside the entry whose own grid showed faithfulness is blind to a circuit being a splice of two mechanisms. The operational consequence for us: no single behavioural number may ship alone — a circuit claim needs a behavioural column AND a structural comparison against either a curated reference or a second, independently-derived circuit, because a faithful subgraph can be faithful by suppressing rather than implementing. Corollary the paper earns the hard way: in the twelve cross-family cells patching sat at ≥0.91 everywhere while ablation sufficiency ranged 0.24 to 1.00, so which pillar you print decides whether discovery looks interchangeable or broken. (arxiv-2607.19317, arxiv-2607.18921, arxiv-2605.09129)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 182): **A mean faithfulness gate cannot tell a mechanism from a splice, and this paper gives the arithmetic that makes the point quantitative — a circuit that reaches 0.63 on each of two tasks can be 55% built from one task's mechanism and 15% from another's.** The folder has repeatedly found that pooled statistics over heterogeneous populations invert or hide effects (within-mode AUROC differing from pooled by 0.29, a safety observer perfect inside every subgroup allocating 63% of interventions to one of them, perfect mean knowledge picking the lowest-loss mask in 3 of 30 cells); this entry is the same defect in its cheapest form and its sharpest demonstration, because the pooled object is a *single graph* whose off-task components are literally borrowed. The tell is that 88–99% of a mixed circuit's edges belong to one of the two task-specific circuits, so the splice is detectable by set arithmetic and invisible to the score. For us the adoption is a reporting requirement, not a method: any explanation our white-box model emits over a pooled dataset ships the **per-example faithfulness profile** of its own subgraph — the vector f(C,{x_i}), which is one extra column in a run we already do — because its *shape* (block structure or its absence) is the only thing that distinguishes a mechanism-specific circuit from a mechanism-merged one, and its mean is precisely the statistic that cannot. (arxiv-2605.09129, arxiv-2609.35805, arxiv-2609.03026)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 182): **The cheapest repair in this folder turned out to be a grouping step inserted before aggregation, requiring no new attribution theory at all — and the price of the repair is that the number of groups becomes an oracle.** DCD changes only *when* attribution is averaged: partition the dataset, then run the unchanged discovery method per group. That composes with any method we trust, which is exactly the shape of adoptable change the survey is collecting, and it is the constructive counterpart to this entry's own diagnostic. The honesty is in the K not being solved: for within-task mixtures the gap statistic returns a median of 10 groups on axes with two or three variants, so K is set to the known variant count — an oracle on the *number* but not the *labels* — and the authors state that the within-task results are therefore what the grouping recovers when K is right, not what their pipeline returns. Set beside this folder's abstention entries (a three-valued certificate whose abstained set is the finding) and its threshold-calibration entry (a multiplier cross-validated against a stated error rate, frozen before test), the general lesson is that a method whose free parameter is set by privileged information must publish that fact and report the oracle-conditioned and rule-conditioned numbers separately, because the gap between them is the real open problem rather than the headline. (arxiv-2605.09129, arxiv-2602.22968, arxiv-2609.35805)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 182): **Before comparing two methods, check that each explains its own discovery data — otherwise the comparison is between two kinds of noise, and the authors here print the table that shows it.** In this grid EAP-IG recovers behaviour in all 69 in-distribution cells (median 0.90) and E-Act in its own (median 0.94), but EAP fails 17 of 59 (median 0.13 on Qwen entity binding, six of seven GPT-2 IOI cells below 0.3, minimum −0.85), and those are exactly the cells from which cross-variant transfer differences would be read as evidence about mechanism; the paper says so plainly and reports them for completeness only. The companion is the reverse-direction check the authors also run: their own effect does not appear in 2 of 9 pairs, one where the pure circuits already transfer to each other (so there is nothing to splice) and one where the mixed circuit simply picks a task (0.71 against 0.08), and both are in the figures rather than the footnotes. The folder's other entries arrive at this requirement from the baseline side (a localisation method indistinguishable from freezing random components, a surrogate beating random edges only past 80% of the network, three all-zero baselines making a positive result a null-versus-something comparison); the floor version is cheaper and comes first: publish each method's in-distribution recovery in the same table as the comparison, because a method that cannot recover the model on data it was fitted to cannot be compared to anything. (arxiv-2605.09129, arxiv-2605.06076, arxiv-2602.04735)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 181): **The object whose stability is worth reporting is the claim, not the circuit — and the cheapest audit question in this folder turns out to be "what share of the defensible analytic space agrees with you", which is one deterministic mapping and a counting pass away.** Two competent analysts with the same tool produce circuits sharing a median of 4% of their edges and, far more damagingly, statements that differ on 73.2% of pairs with the two most common claims (41.1% early-layer and 28.5% late-layer, both "distributed" or "sparse") asserting *opposite* locations for the same behaviour; the modal share of 0.411 fails a filability bar at 0.95, 0.90 and 0.80 alike. Standardising the largest single lever — the evaluation metric, worth 0.1377 of a 0.7316 flip rate — leaves 0.5939, so there is no knob whose fixing rescues the report, and the REML decomposition makes the trap explicit: structure variance is 78.8% the ablation–corruption interaction and only 0.7% the metric, meaning a standards body reading the structural decomposition would standardise the axis that fixes nothing. For us this is the reporting requirement every pattern line in this folder has been circling, finally with a formula: any explanation our white-box model emits ships the share of the specification space that agrees with it, the per-axis residual after standardisation, and a statement of the tolerance it claims — a claim that cannot state its own modal share has not been audited, only asserted. (arxiv-2608.13754, arxiv-2607.18921, arxiv-2609.15533)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 181): **When specifications select objects of different sizes, pooled statistics invert, and this paper prints three of its own that do — which upgrades the folder's "always stratify" habit from prudence to a mechanical requirement.** Pooled, discovered circuits are *less* stable than a size-matched random null (flip 0.7316 against 0.6774) and the null looks like the better instrument; within size the ordering reverses (0.2746 against 0.4230) because the null degenerates to a single claim class above 1,000 edges, and the discovered multiverse does the same at 5,000 and 10,000, so 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips at all and the entire instability lives below 2,000 edges. The pre-registered claim-versus-function gap fails the same way: 0.3344 pooled, above threshold at only 4 of 10 sizes and negative at 5, carried by the 500–2,000 edge band alone. This is the same arithmetic that let a constant failure-mode prior reach 0.713 pooled while being exactly 0.500 within a mode, and that let a perfect mean-knowledge ranker pick the lowest-loss mask in 3 of 30 cells: a stratified population turns any pooled average into a weighted sum of strata with different class counts, so the fix is not a better estimator but the within-stratum table printed beside the headline, plus an explicit statement of which stratum carries the effect. (arxiv-2608.13754, arxiv-2609.35805, arxiv-2609.03026)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 181): **Raw agreement and chance-corrected agreement measure different things, and printing Cohen's κ beside the percentage is what lets a paper answer the "you just sampled the same mechanism twice" objection — here 60.3% per-example agreement collapses to κ = 0.0146.** Two circuits agree on 60% of examples, but they agree because both are right about a similar *fraction* of examples rather than about the *same* examples; κ stays between 0.016 and 0.047 across every circuit size while raw agreement climbs from 0.52 to 0.92 and accuracy from 0.51 to 0.95, so the agreement number moves with skill and the κ number does not move at all. That combination is the answer to an equivalence-class objection that otherwise defeats every instability result in this folder (structurally distinct subgraphs implementing the same computation). Two companions to steal: the negative control is a *null multiverse* run through the same analytic grid rather than a single null draw, and the deterministic claim map is code rather than a model, so the measurement cannot absorb judge variance. For us, any cross-run or cross-checkpoint agreement statistic — feature overlap, circuit overlap, description agreement, probe-sign stability — reports the chance-corrected coefficient, the matched-size null multiverse, and the moving-vs-still comparison of both numbers across the range. (arxiv-2608.13754, arxiv-2603.30002, arxiv-2606.06267)
