- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 148): **A causal effect measured on one input is a random variable, and this is the first entry in the folder that puts a number on how random — the base-layer CV of ~0.5 across inputs (and >1 for the gradient approximations) is a floor on the error of every circuit, every feature attribution and every one-input intervention result the folder has recorded.** The decomposition is the part we can import wholesale: intrinsic variance lives in the estimand and cannot be engineered away, estimator variance is the approximations' own contribution and can be reduced, and aggregation-plus-discretisation *amplifies* whatever survives into large structural differences. For a predictive white-box model this reframes the target: the thing worth predicting is not the effect of a component on this input but its population mean over the input--counterfactual distribution, and a predictor that fits single-input effects is fitting the noise term. The practical requirement is that every number our model outputs should come with a resampling error bar computed through the *whole* pipeline, and that a predicted effect smaller than its own error bar be reported as unmeasured rather than as small. It also explains a family of results this folder has logged without understanding them — directions that "survived a rerun" at one seed, circuits whose faithfulness moved with sparsity, effects that flipped under a different ablation — as instantiations of one statistical phenomenon. (arxiv-2510.00845, arxiv-2602.06801, arxiv-2611.05033)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 148): **Report the distribution of what your method selects, not only its top-ranked output — and the specific instrument here is a selection-frequency histogram that needs no ground truth.** Across 330 circuits built from gpt2-small's 32,491 edges, only 464 are ever selected, 231 clear 10% frequency, 94 clear 30%, and 7 clear 80%: a stable core under a large noise periphery, obtained for the cost of re-running a pipeline that already exists. This is a cheap, general substitute for the ground-truth circuits this folder keeps saying it lacks, and it applies to every read-out we build — which units a dictionary, probe, attribution or circuit keeps coming back to under resampling is a direct estimate of the explainable-with-confidence part, and the periphery is where every "faithful but fragile" headline lives. Two companion reporting rules come with it and both contradict common practice: report mean **and** coefficient of variation together (the mean of a heavy-tailed Jaccard distribution is misleading alone — 0.561 with CV 0.335 is a bimodal set of circuits, not a mediocre one), and report faithfulness **and** stability as a pair, because they decouple and can even invert the ranking of conditions. (arxiv-2510.00845, arxiv-2606.16939, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 148): **The counterfactual is part of the question, not a nuisance parameter — and the field's habit of fixing one ablation convention is what makes its findings look like facts about models.** Both of this paper's structural sensitivities point the same way: hyperparameter variants of the same estimator do not converge on a shared circuit but isolate different artefacts of a noisy score distribution (overlap 0.086 and 0.071 in two cases, one edge versus twenty-one at identical error in a third), and sweeping the intervention's noise amplitude moves the identified circuit's reproducibility through a minimum near 0.2 rather than being flat. The consequence for us is a reporting requirement rather than a new method: state the counterfactual distribution as part of the estimand, sweep it rather than picking it, and never compare two circuits — ours or anyone's — without saying which intervention both were computed under. The one genuinely reassuring ordering in the paper is the reverse direction and worth keeping: mechanisms transfer across changes in what inputs *mean* better than across resamples of the same generator (Jaccard 0.790/0.799 versus 0.561), so distribution shift is the easier generalisation test and bootstrap resampling is the one that actually fails — which is the opposite order from how most of this folder evaluates. (arxiv-2510.00845, arxiv-2602.16698, arxiv-2606.29522)

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 147): **A cost metric can manufacture a winner, so any "our units are more compact" claim has to be published on two axes with an exact control — and here the two axes disagree in a way that tells us what the sparsity is for.** On the selected-unit axis the exact SVD and random-orthogonal factorizations are competitive on IOI and at low docstring necessity thresholds, because a unit is a unit regardless of how dense its vectors are; on the active-edge axis SWD wins consistently, because its gain is precisely that each unit touches few input and output coordinates. That distinction is usable for us: a compactness claim about a decomposition is a claim about *connectivity*, not about unit count, and the control that proves it is a reparameterization that reproduces the matrix exactly (SVD gives CE delta 1.6e-6, the 10-seed random-orthogonal control ranges −2.5e-6 to 3.4e-6) so no fidelity difference can be blamed — a strictly cheaper and sharper control than the random-init baselines and shuffled-label nulls this folder has been using for the same purpose, because it holds the object fixed and varies only the property under test. (arxiv-2608.03913, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair, arxiv-2611.05033)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 147): **Additivity is a per-site property, not a model property — and this paper gives the two numbers that decide where a surrogate may sum and where it may not.** After the output projection, pair contributions are essentially uncorrelated (95th-percentile absolute correlation 0.0049, 99th 0.0089, one structured tail at 0.345 made of opposed reads with opposed writes cancelling into a positive contribution correlation), so a sum of per-unit effects is a defensible description there; before GELU the same analysis gives moderate, broadly distributed interactions (median ratio 0.089, 99th 0.154, max 0.221, a quarter of pairs at ≥0.10), so a sum is not. The transferable rule for a predictive white-box model is to place non-additivity where the nonlinearity is and to *measure* it as a departure from additivity (a contextual finite difference across the activation, projected through the downstream matrix and normalised by marginal effects) rather than to assume either regime globally — and the framing point is subtler still: low contribution correlation does not mean the units are independent, because a pair with opposed reads and opposed writes can look uncorrelated in isolation and still move the output together. (arxiv-2608.03913, arxiv-2606.16939, arxiv-2602.16698)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 147): **The weights-only floor is the baseline activation-fitted methods owe us, and it is stronger than the field's rhetoric about needing data.** A factorization that uses no calibration data at all — identity Gram, pure weight reconstruction — still produces circuits, at 0.962 held-out docstring sufficiency from three units and 0.986 on greater-than from 256; what calibration buys is behaviour preservation under aggressive sparsification (better CE at the same nonzero budget) while weights-only buys parameter fidelity (0.366 vs 0.415 relative Frobenius error). That is the cleanest two-denominator result in the folder: *which* thing a decomposition preserves is a choice with a measurable trade, and it is the same shape as the reconstruction-error-versus-firing-coverage split the SAE post demanded. For us it sets a mandatory control — any dictionary, transcoder or surrogate trained on activations must be scored against the same factorization computed from weights alone, on the same held-out circuits, because otherwise the gain may be a calibration-distribution artefact rather than structure the model has — and it also gifts a zero-cost instrument for training-trajectory work, since a weights-only factorization can be recomputed at every checkpoint with no activation collection at all. (arxiv-2608.03913, goodfire-com-blog-a-practical-guide-to-saes, arxiv-2602.16698)

Took a free paper from outside the queue after filename+ID+title novelty check against `aether/`, `core/` and `helix_research/`, chosen to fill a hole that no entry in the folder touched: **recurrent-depth architectures**, i.e. what "layer N does X" means in a model whose effective depth exceeds its parameter count. **Substance:** the (layer × recurrence) grid as the unit of analysis; two propositions (cyclic fixed point propagates to all cyclic shifts; state-to-attention map Lipschitz in the QK product, so convergence ⇒ constant attention); per-layer fixed points reached fast by Huginn and the retrofitted models, not by Ouro; random-init models reproduce the cyclic structure whenever input injection is present (all norms but Ouro's), and without it only pre-norm converges — degenerately, all layers to one state; non-fixed-point tokens at 0.02%/0.14%/0.05% (no prompt / long persona / padded); stages of inference mirrored inside each loop, retrofitted models inheriting their base model's stages, Ouro 2.6B showing them twice because upcycling duplicated the layers, Huginn showing none (attributed to residual normalisation blocking massive activations, with an MLP-zeroing ablation as the test); and stage stability at 128 recurrences tracking published extrapolation behaviour across two model cards. **Count measured, not carried: 144 entry files = 144 INDEX keys, `comm` empty both directions before this run; 145/145 after.** 145 % 3 = 1 → **entry 145 is UNCOMMITTED; the batch commit fires at 147.** Next run: write one entry, then `git add docs/literature/aether && git commit -m "literature (aether): 3 entries" && git pull --rebase -q && git push -q`.

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 146): **Recurrence turns the depth axis into a grid, and every depth-based claim in this folder silently assumes the grid is one-dimensional — so a looped model is where our vocabulary has to be checked, not just extended.** The structural result is one line (weight tying plus bounded pre-attention states makes the state-to-attention map Lipschitz in the QK product, so a converging loop must give constant attention patterns across passes), and its consequence for us is blunt: in a model whose middle stages repeat inside the block, "layer 18 writes feature F" is not a statement about effective computation, because the same weights are being asked to play several stage roles in sequence. The measurement template worth importing is the (layer × recurrence) grid applied to whatever read-out we use — attribution, probe, ablation effect — because collapsing that grid to depth is exactly the move that would turn a stable cycle into a fake feedforward profile. It also supplies a weight-only diagnostic no forward pass is needed for: the Lipschitz product of the block says, before any experiment, whether the loop is a contraction and therefore whether a predictor trained at one recurrence count may be extrapolated to another. (arxiv-2604.11791, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair, arxiv-2602.16698)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 146): **A structural pattern that survives random initialisation cannot be evidence that a task was learned — and here that null argument is decisive rather than decorative, because the phenomenon under study is the architecture's own limiting behaviour.** The per-layer fixed points appear in untrained 12-layer models whenever input injection is present, which converts "trained loops settle into a cycle" from a fact about learning into a fact about the map; and the one untrained configuration that converges without injection converges *degenerately* (every layer to the same state), which is the sharper lesson — a null result on a structural statistic can be an artefact of the null input, so the control has to be checked for the property under test, not merely run. Read against the folder's other untrained-weight controls (a linear map between layers scoring 0.95–0.99 by construction; a Gini concentration already present at zero RL), the general form is now well attested: the cheapest way to falsify a mechanism claim is to run the instrument on a network where the mechanism cannot exist, and the second cheapest is to confirm that the *instrument* still fires on the control where it should. (arxiv-2604.11791, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair, arxiv-2610.17093)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 146): **One borrowed statistic decides one story, and this paper is its cleanest demonstration yet: the same models "mirror feedforward stages" under ColSum concentration and do not under residual entropy.** ColSum concentration was built to detect attention sinks; it says Ouro reproduces Llama's mixing stages, and the residual-entropy metric on the identical runs says Ouro departs from feedforward behaviour — with the divergence plausibly explained by the very norm placement that the other metric is insensitive to. The transferable rule is to report the *disagreement between metrics* as a result rather than picking the one that supports the narrative, and to name what each metric is a proxy for before it is used as a verdict. That is the same failure shape the folder has logged repeatedly (a band z-score borrowed across recipes; an effect size compared to a copy effect measured elsewhere; a circuit faithfulness score that moves with sparsity), and it is the reason a stage claim without a stated decision rule — as here, where no threshold separates "has stages" from "does not" — is a reading of a picture rather than a measurement. (arxiv-2604.11791, arxiv-2610.17093, arxiv-2611.05033)

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 145): **A direction is recovered up to an equivalence class, and the class is measurable before any intervention runs — so "our vector works" and "our vector is the mechanism" are separated by an SVD, not by another steering demo.** The formal content is one line (anything in the Jacobian's null space changes no output, to first order), and the practical content is that the null-space fraction here is 0.86–0.94 of the ambient width, i.e. the unobservable dimensions dominate the geometry of the space our predictors and probes live in. This converts a rhetorical debate into a per-site measurement we can run today: effective rank and null fraction of the activation covariance at every layer we touch, reported next to every read-out accuracy. It also fixes the denominator the folder keeps hand-waving — a probe that recovers 0.8 of something is recovering 0.8 of at most `rank` observable dimensions, and a predictor's ceiling is set by that rank, not by the behaviour's complexity. The corollary for our own write-ups is that a direction should be published as (vector, contrast set, equivalence class dimension), which is exactly the (z, c, π) triple 2602.16698 asked for, arrived at from the measurement side rather than the causal-inference side. (arxiv-2602.06801, arxiv-2602.16698, arxiv-2611.05033)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 145): **An equivalence test is only as strong as the threshold and the control it is scored against, and this paper's own spread shows how much a conventional cut is doing.** The headline "all ten cells are equivalent" rests on |d| < 0.2, a psychology convention for negligible group differences, applied without an equivalence procedure; the per-cell means run 0.059–0.186 and the null-spanning table reaches 0.243–0.291, so a stricter cut or a proper TOST would make several cells undetermined rather than equivalent. That is not a reason to discard the result — the logit-space ratio R = 0.47–0.73 is threshold-free and points the same way — it is a reason to prefer *paired* statistics with an explicit null over one-sided "below a convention" claims, which is the same lesson the folder already carries from 2610.17093 (a band z-score is a scale, not a p-value) and from 2609.13316 (parallel vs serial dispatch moves a method's score by 0.11). The transferable protocol for us: for every "X does not matter" claim, publish the effect size, the equivalence bound, and a matched perturbation that *should* move the number (here, a norm-matched random direction), because without the last one a null is indistinguishable from an insensitive assay — and this paper has no positive control showing the assay can detect a privileged direction at all. (arxiv-2602.06801, arxiv-2610.17093, arxiv-2509.13316)

- **A cheap skeleton is a hypothesis generator, and the evidence that raises its status is one intervention per selected edge — not a faithfulness plot**: CircuitLasso recovers a dependency graph over SAE features by regressing each layer on the one before it with Lasso, so nothing is ever intervened on and every edge is a coefficient from correlated activations; its own faithfulness/completeness panels and a novel edge-ablation test are the only places an intervention enters, and they are reported qualitatively. The transferable discipline is to state the object as an estimate with a named residual (they call theirs linearisation error, and refuse causal-sufficiency and independent-noise assumptions outright instead of invoking identifiability theorems they cannot satisfy), then to spend the intervention budget on the few edges the sparsity filter kept rather than on the whole graph. Edge ablation — zero a coefficient in the surrogate and ask whether the prediction moves — is the smallest such test and belongs in our eval set next to node ablation. (arxiv-2606.16939, arxiv-2602.16698, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html)
- **When the ordering is known, fitting to a fixed triangular mask is the whole trick — and it is the one constraint a predictive model of ours is allowed to assume**: the method's scalability is not statistical (a linear surrogate is crude) but structural: the forward pass fixes which component can influence which, so the DAG search collapses to per-layer-pair Lasso with the illegal triangle masked out, and the acyclicity claim becomes a property of the architecture rather than an identifiability argument. For us this is the cleanest available template for "how much of the model may we assume and how much must we estimate", provided we say afterwards which edges are untested. The obvious trap is also shown: once ordering is imposed by fiat, paths that are anti-causal by any human reading (hunger before eating, inverted) come out as edges, and the authors have no test that separates an unusual real dependency from a spurious one. (arxiv-2606.16939, arxiv-2602.16698, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html)

- **Ground truth first, then intervention — a behaviour edit is only interpretable against a setting where both answers were known in advance**: the evaluation-awareness organism makes the point sharply, because with a model whose deployment behaviour was installed as a known fact, steering toward deployment drives the measured behaviour *below* the model's own deployed rate (under 11% in evaluation contexts against 33–34% deployed), which is a claim no verbalisation metric could have made or refuted. Two cheaper habits come with it and cost almost nothing: run the identical intervention on the pre-fine-tuning checkpoint to show the direction acts on what training touched rather than on outputs generically, and use the exact prompts the vector was built from as a prompt-only baseline, since a mean difference over sentence pairs may be a compressed prompt rather than a state. (arxiv-2510.20487, arxiv-2609.34056, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-cheap-monitors)
- **When the field's success metric is a sentence the model says, the honest next experiment is the one measured off the text channel**: this paper's own conclusion is that suppression of the verbalisation cannot be distinguished from a change in belief, and it points at an activation oracle to settle it — which is exactly the portfolio our project is, so we should read the evaluation-awareness and oracle literature as one thread and treat "the model stops saying X" as a measurement flaw rather than a finding. The 2026-01 addendum is the second lesson in the same direction: a benchmark presented as unbeatable by prompting should be re-attacked after publication, because declarative phrasings later dropped the behaviour to 34–37% and the authors had to narrow their claim. (arxiv-2510.20487, anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, arxiv-2609.34056)

- **The right layer-level profile is a pair, not a scalar — (identity share, update linearity) — because one number here is provably blind to whether anything was learned**: this paper's headline is a control, not a result: fitting a linear map between consecutive residual-stream states gives a held-out R² of 0.977–0.984 on two trained decoders, and **randomly initialised** models reproduce 0.95–0.99 on the identical procedure, because the residual passes through untouched and a near-identity map scores well whatever the block computed. Re-targeting the fit at the update (the difference a layer writes) drops mid-stack linearity to 0.35–0.53 and reveals a learned U across six models from three architecture families — large near-linear basis changes at the stack boundaries (LLaMA's layer 1 is 99.6% linearly predictable while its identity baseline captures almost none of its output), small nonlinear refinements in the interior. Two habits follow directly: any linear-read-out claim of ours reports the identity baseline, the update-target statistic, and a random-init control, or it is unfalsifiable; and our per-component profiles should report the pair, since "passes through" and "writes" are nearly complementary axes and either alone is misleading. The pair also predicts behaviour, which is the part that makes it a model: Δ-R² correlates with the realised benefit of substituting a fitted affine map at Spearman ρ = 0.65 across 44 layers, and the predicted failure modes really do fail (the one layer a single map cannot rescue is rescued by four maps routed by k-means, and forcing a patch on a skip-branch window does worse than omitting the layer). (blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair, arxiv-2602.16698, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html)
- **Report the controls that a null on your statistic would be, before the statistic, at every scale of this survey**: this entry gives the layer-scale version of the same lesson the folder keeps meeting at other scales — a band z-score whose null is borrowed from another recipe, a Gini concentration that is already in the base model, an L0 pinned by construction, a decoded quantity that the visible context already supplies — and the family resemblance is exact: each is a measurement that cannot fail, and each was caught by running the instrument on an input where the answer was known in advance (untrained weights, zero-RL base, shuffled labels, context-only baseline). The transferable protocol is to name, for every statistic we publish, the *known-negative input* it should give zero on, and to run it; a statistic without such an input is a description, not a test. (blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair, anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, arxiv-2610.17093)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 153): **A read-out channel has to be scored on whether the model *had* to use it, and this folder has never separated necessity from propensity for the text channel — the distinction here is the cheapest available partition of every "the trace tells us X" claim.** In an autoregressive Transformer information crosses token boundaries only through generated text, so a hard task forces intermediate state to be written down; on such a task legibility is protected by the architecture rather than by the model's disposition, and it therefore survives training pressure that shrinks or tidies traces. On an easy task the same monitoring result is licensed only by a tendency, and the enumerated fragility mechanisms are precisely the pressures that can override a tendency: outcome-based RL past the point where human text is the optimisation pressure, direct process supervision, indirect pressure through weights shared between trace and answer generation, and monitors whose fixes become selection pressure across runs. The protocol for us is one ablation per claim — remove or corrupt the trace and see whether the capability survives — reported next to the monitoring rate, because the two answers support different words ("the computation lives here" versus "the model usually narrates"). It is the text-channel twin of the folder's probe discipline: neither channel is allowed to claim more than the ablation licenses, and the honest ceiling for both is stated rather than implied. (arxiv-2507.11473, arxiv-2607.03502, arxiv-2603.01437)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 153): **Two measurement channels for one computation can be cross-validated against each other, and the agreement rate is an instrument we can build today — the agenda names exactly the bridge our project needs.** The proposal is to take the tokens a text monitor treats as important and ask whether a white-box method finds the same ones important; divergence is a verdict on at least one of the two instruments, and convergence is the only cheap evidence that the trace and the residual stream are describing the same process rather than two unrelated narratives. This is the constructive version of the folder's repeated finding that CoT usefulness and activation-side read-out strength anticorrelate by task: where both channels fire on the same tokens there is something for a predictive model to be right about, and where only one does, the two entries should be reported as disagreeing rather than averaged into a single "interpretability works" score. The paired instrument is trace perturbation (edit the trace, see if the answer moves), which is activation patching moved to the text channel and inherits its requirement — an intervention plane, a dose, and a stated saturation point. (arxiv-2507.11473, arxiv-2603.01437, goodfire-com-research-reasoning-theater)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 153): **A monitor's false-positive rate is not a verdict, and an evaluation without an adaptive adversary measures a cooperative regime — both stated plainly here and both violated by most of the probe entries in this folder.** Whether a noisy flag is usable depends on what the flag costs to act on: when a flagged response can be resampled cheaply, a high false-positive rate is affordable, so accuracy alone cannot rank two monitors; and a monitor scored against a model that is not trying to evade it is being measured on the easy half of its distribution. The transferable reporting triplet for any classifier or probe we publish is therefore (operating point, cost of acting on a flag, adversary), and the third element is the one nobody reports — the folder's sleeper-agent probes, guardrail classifiers and constitutional classifiers all publish benign-regime scores. This also connects to the folder's standing known-negative rule: the adversary *is* the known-negative input for a monitor, because a monitor that cannot be pushed off its operating point by an adversary has not been shown to be robust, only insensitive. (arxiv-2507.11473, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-cheap-monitors, arxiv-2601.04603)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 155): **A read-out that is scored on a pooled distribution is being graded on the half of the data the model already got right, and this entry is the cleanest arithmetic proof in the folder — 99.5% agreement on IOI's correct prompts alongside 15.2% on its errors, from the published manual circuit, with a normalised faithfulness of 0.956 sitting on top.** The structural point is that these two strata are not two views of one number; a circuit that emits the *task-correct* answer where the model is wrong is a disagreement with the model, not a bonus, so the metric has to condition on the model's own choice and require the identical wrong answer. For us the transfer is immediate and cheap: every probe accuracy, every dictionary-reconstruction score, every surrogate simulation score in this folder is pooled, and the cost of splitting it is one extra groupby. The companion statistic B_err (share of error prompts where the circuit is wrong at all, versus wrong-in-the-same-way) is worth importing too, because it separates "the surrogate knows this input is hard" from "the surrogate predicts this particular mistake" — two very different claims that a single agreement number merges. (arxiv-2609.35686, arxiv-2510.00845, transformer-circuits-pub-2023-ioi-index-html)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 155): **Exposure to failures is not explanation of failures, and the control that settles it is a one-parameter model — the error-conditioned replacement values here improved error agreement no better than a plain scalar shift toward the wrong name, which is this folder's recurring "did the mechanism do any work?" test in its cheapest form.** Read against the seven remedies they tried, the ordering is instructive: everything that changed the *discovery data* (more errors, upweighted errors, error-enriched sets) bought error reproduction by spending 7–8 points of correct agreement, and nothing closed the gap, whereas the one intervention that changed the *circuit's membership* moved it from 14% to 75% at half a point of cost. That asymmetry is a usable prior for our own surrogate work: when a predictor underperforms on a stratum, the first hypothesis should be that the stratum requires computation the object does not contain, not that the fitting procedure underweighted it — and the test for that is whether adding the missing component helps while a free scalar nudge does not. (arxiv-2609.35686, arxiv-2611.05033, arxiv-2608.03913)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 155): **Concentration is the evidence that a recovered effect is a mechanism rather than a per-example patch, and here it is one path-patching number: the same inhibition contribution reproduces 120 of 137 newly recovered errors, while the second route reproduces 35 and reproduces none when the intervention is moved to the subject positions.** That triple is a template we can run on any predictive claim of ours — an effect that recurs across examples through a named site, an effect that is real but minority, and an effect that vanishes when the plane of the intervention is shifted one position — and it is a strictly stronger statement than a mean improvement, because it says which examples and through where. It also connects to the folder's standing requirement that an intervention publish its plane: here the plane is literally what distinguishes the working route from the null one, and the same ablation rule is held fixed while only the patch location changes. (arxiv-2609.35686, arxiv-2603.01437, arxiv-2605.10664)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 165): **An explanation of a unit has two ways to be wrong, and this folder has been grading only one of them — recovery catches an account that fails to cover the unit's real effect, and the *inverse* arm catches an account that covers everything and explains nothing; the score that works is the minimum of the pair, not the average.** Here recovery alone is the maximised quantity and it is trivially defeated: the predicate that fires everywhere reaches recovery 1 while saying nothing, which is exactly the shape of the degenerate readers this folder keeps finding — a localisation that does not beat the same number of random components, a linear map that a randomly initialised model also fits, a pooled agreement rate computed where the model was already right. The inverse arm is the cheap fix, and it is a strictly stronger control than the shuffled-label and random-direction nulls because it is computed from the same intervention on the same corpus and differs only in *which positions are restored*. For a predictive white-box model the transfer is direct and nearly free: publish recovery and inverse for every claim that names where a computation happens, plus an explicit coverage number, because a prediction that fires on 90% of inputs cannot be distinguished from one that fires on all of them. (arxiv-2607.02964, arxiv-2605.01555, arxiv-2606.06267)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 165): **The rate you publish should be the rate at the strictest rung you ran, because each rung of held-out discipline knocks out more than half of the previous one and the largest knocks are not uniform — they are concentrated exactly on the model you were using as a baseline.** In-sample → held-out → ten-slice resampled goes 37.3/35.3/15.0, 21.4/17.2/9.6 and 13.2/9.0/1.5, i.e. the dense twin loses 89% of its apparent interpretability while the sparse model loses 60%, so the *comparison* survives only because the fragile side is the one that collapses — report the in-sample number alone and the dense model looks nearly a third as interpretable as the sparse one. The mechanism is worth carrying: the random-chance score under this metric equals the predicate's firing coverage, so an over-fitted predicate on a dense weight sits near chance and regresses *toward* it off-corpus, which means held-out scoring is not a neutral estimator but a monotone amplifier of the true difference. Two habits follow for us: quote the strictest rung, and score every read-out against a chance value that can be computed in closed form before running it, so "is 0.75 good?" has an answer that does not depend on the corpus. (arxiv-2607.02964, arxiv-2510.00845, arxiv-2607.02964)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 165): **A description's language sets its own ceiling, and here the ceiling is demonstrably a property of the grammar rather than of the network — the same string-closing weight scores −0.98 when predicates may look only at the focus token and +0.83 once eight tokens of look-back are allowed, because whether a quote mark opens or closes a string is undecidable from the token.** That is the sharpest available estimate of how much of a "not interpretable" verdict is instrument-limited, and it reframes the folder's description-side results: a missing qualifier in a component description (the headvis lesson) and a predicate language that cannot express the qualifier are the same failure, and only the second is invisible to a human reader of the description. Two operational consequences: when a unit resists explanation, first widen the grammar and re-score before recording a negative, and report the grammar alongside the rate — an interpretability percentage without its predicate language is not comparable across papers. It also explains the residual in this paper's own headline: the weight-level decomposition of the speech-verb neuron recovers five roles that add and cancel into one activation-level label, so the activation summary is a residue of the arithmetic, not a summary of the computation. (arxiv-2607.02964, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-headvis-index-html, arxiv-2605.01555)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 156): **Structure is not evidence of function, and this folder has been letting the two stand in for each other in every circuit entry it holds — the fix is one cheap number rather than a new method.** Circuit discovery is a greedy search through a space of individually dispensable edges, so it returns a *sample* from an equivalence class of subgraphs that compute the same thing; small changes in input statistics tip the sampling differently, and the resulting structural difference looks exactly like specialization until it is scored. The transfer-efficiency statistic here is the instrument to copy: take the components a condition nominally owns, graft them onto the shared core, and divide the mean boost they give other conditions by the boost they give their own. A number near one says the "specific" components are generic boosters; the observed 81.4–97.0% across five scales, against 1–3% for random edges of the same count, leaves no room for a specialization reading. Read against the direction-side non-identifiability result, the two entries now say the same thing in two vocabularies — a vector is recovered only up to a Jacobian null space, an edge set only up to a functional equivalence class — so the object a predictive white-box model should be asked to get right is the behavioural contract, not the canonical artifact. (arxiv-2606.06267, arxiv-2602.06801, arxiv-2511.01033)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 156): **Evaluation granularity is a hidden free parameter of every faithfulness score, and here it is worth up to 0.85 accuracy points — larger exactly where the claim matters most.** Source-level evaluation keeps all outgoing edges from any node that contributed at least one circuit edge, which lets unselected pathways carry the computation; edge-level keeps only the discovered edges. The gap grows with model scale (0.22 at 70M to 0.85 at 1.4B), so a scaled-up comparison looks *more* faithful precisely when its edge sets are least stable — a confound that anti-correlates with the quantity being claimed. This is the folder's recurring shape of defect (a band z-score borrowed across recipes, a linear-map R² that a random-init model also achieves, a pooled agreement rate computed over the prompts the model already gets right) arriving at a third scale: a metric that cannot fail. The two habits that transfer immediately: report the *stricter* granularity as primary and treat the looser one as an upper bound, and state for every reported score which set of pathways was allowed to remain live. (arxiv-2606.06267, arxiv-2609.35686, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 156): **An effect that survives one ablation rule and vanishes under another was never computation — and two-rule reporting is the cheapest audit we can add to every intervention we publish.** The residual same-band advantage here is significant under resample ablation (p<0.03, d=0.22–0.71), flat across scales, and gone under zero ablation (d≤0.18, and three of five models at exactly nought), which attributes it to the corruption procedure rather than to band-specific circuitry. That is the same lesson the folder drew from patching-plane effects, from KV-cache compounding, and from the source-level inflation above, now stated in its most testable form: hold the contrast and the statistic fixed, change only the ablation rule, and see which of the two moves. The companion finding is that structural instability needs no functional explanation to be harmless — only 21–27% of the largest model's edges appear in all three same-band draws while cross-draw transfer runs 0.990–1.017 — so a single extraction's edge set is a minority of essential edges plus a large inert remainder, and the honest reporting unit is a distribution over extractions with majority-vote aggregation, not a point estimate. (arxiv-2606.06267, arxiv-2604.11791, arxiv-2608.03913)

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 154): **Symmetry is the cheapest pre-registered zero available to us, and this is the cleanest statement of it in the folder — if the data distribution is invariant to a transformation group, the weights provably cannot leave the commuting subspace, so "only these directions can ever be learned here" becomes a computation with no forward passes.** The induction-head result is a special case of an argument we can run on our own targets: the expected gradient is fixed by isotropy while the same rotation acts on each weight block as a similarity transform, so a block that is not constant-on-diagonal (or not block-equal) must have zero gradient *identically*, not merely small for this dataset. That is the strongest form of the folder's recurring requirement to name, for every statistic, the known-negative input on which it should give zero: here the negative is structural rather than empirical, and it can be checked before training. Applied to any pair of interpretable bases we already work in — token/position, source/target, pre/post-instruction, two checkpoints of one model — it yields a falsifiable prediction list for weight-space reading, and it also explains why the folder's decomposition methods keep finding block-diagonal structure: that structure is what the group invariance leaves behind. (arxiv-2511.01033, arxiv-2608.03913, arxiv-2604.11791)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 154): **A mechanism's emergence is a schedule with an order and a rate, and the folder has never scored a read-out against that — every entry so far asks whether a component exists in the finished network.** The template here is small enough to copy: name the scalar coordinates along which the mechanism lives, define emergence as the first threshold crossing on a named coordinate, sweep the task parameter, and check the asymptotic scaling. The order is not incidental — it is forced by which gradients are live at each stage (untrained attention returns a context average that already contains the answer, so the output fits first; the second layer is fed by a 1/N retrieval, so it learns second at 1/N²; the first layer gets a strong gradient only once both are in place). For a predictive white-box model this reframes the target from "which component does X" to "which component becomes load-bearing when", and it gives our predictor a training-level eval it currently lacks: a prediction that a given block is irrelevant is falsified by that block moving early, not by nothing happening to be attributable to it at the end. (arxiv-2511.01033, arxiv-2506.10922, arxiv-2606.18089)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 154): **The same transfer caution as the folder's looped-model and layer-repair entries, now at the level of hyperparameters: a scaling law measured in an idealised parameterisation is a property of that parameterisation, and the 1/N → 1/N² chain is the mechanism, not a law about language models.** The quadratic slowdown holds because each layer's initial signal is a *uniform average* whose informativeness falls with context length; change the averaging, the initialisation scale, or the positional scheme and the exponents change with it — which is why the authors gesture at burstiness and rotary embeddings as ways to shorten the *effective* context rather than as evidence about real corpora, and why they do not test it. The general habit worth importing is to state for every scaling claim the knob that produced it (here: number of item–label pairs under orthonormal inputs), and to treat any extrapolation across a different data distribution as a new measurement rather than a corollary, exactly as the variance entry required of a single-input causal effect. (arxiv-2511.01033, arxiv-2510.00845, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair)

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 144b): **Every effect needs a local reference, and the only training-free local reference is a copy of the whole state at the same site.** The reusable result here is not the excess itself but its arithmetic: to first order the parts of a state add up to the whole, so a subspace direction can beat whole-state patching exactly when the remaining directions pull the output back — which happens routinely when the mean state change and the readout gradient are far from parallel (79.7° median here), and says nothing about whether the direction isolates the variable. That converts a vague "is this real?" into a three-number report at whatever site we intervene on: the copy effect, the ratio, and the share that disappears when downstream attention is frozen. It is strictly better than the controls this folder has been using for the same purpose — a control task averages over a whole task and a random-init baseline over a whole network, neither of which asks whether the trained network produces that effect *there* — and it costs a handful of forward passes. The corollary matters just as much for us: a direction whose effect is large precisely where the copy effect is ~0 has the geometry of the illusion literature, because the network itself does nothing at that site, and held-out evaluation will not catch it (here, held-out IOI templates still exceed the total effect in 13 of 13 cases) because the excess is shared across entities rather than fitted to them. (arxiv-2611.05033, arxiv-2602.16698, openinterp-2026-cosine-causal-gap-crosscoder)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 144b): **A first-order estimate of the reference and a trained direction's ceiling are two different quantities, and the literature routinely compares them to each other.** Attribution patching built from base-point gradients is, to first order, the trace of the same matrix whose largest eigenvalue bounds any one direction — so a paper that reports "attribution patching predicts the effect" and a paper that reports "the learned direction beats the full patch" are each correct about a different end of one spectrum, and the gap between them is large and computable before any training. For our predictor this is a gift and a warning in equal parts: the gift is that the upper end is a genuine out-of-sample prior at the cost of one gradient pass per pair, and the evaluation protocol to copy is search-on-training-pairs / score-on-held-out; the warning is that any comparison of our surrogate against a learned method has to state which quantity each side estimates, or the comparison is trace versus top eigenvalue and the trained method will "win" every time by construction. The same asymmetry explains a whole family of published numbers in this folder: a direction trained toward a target lands on whatever target its loss names (here, the same squared error lands on the copy effect when aimed at it and 0.09 T above when aimed at the total effect), so the objective is part of the measurement, not a detail of the fitting. (arxiv-2611.05033, arxiv-2606.09899, arxiv-2610.17093)

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 144): **A decryption pipeline is not a read-out until it beats a model that never saw the activation — and the cheapest version of that control is a prompt.** The whole verbalization family (Patchscopes, SelfIE, LIT, and by extension every trained decoder that eats activations and emits text) scores at or below a text-only baseline on the canonical evaluation sets here (0.64 vs 0.64 for LIT on Llama3), which means the field's most-cited verbalization numbers are compatible with "the residual stream still contains the input prompt, well enough to answer questions about it". For us this is the read-out-level counterpart of the folder's standing rule about known-negative inputs: the control is not a random direction or a shuffled label but a **competent decoder with the same information minus the internal state**, because only that baseline shares the model's world knowledge. Concrete requirement for every entry we publish afterwards: any probe, lens, decoder or SAE-based description must be paired with (a) an input-only baseline, (b) an inversion-then-answer baseline where the method allows it, and (c) a validation set containing facts only the *target* knows. Without (c) the claim is untestable, since shared knowledge makes the two explanations identical. (arxiv-2509.13316, arxiv-2608.30980, tcpub-2026-nla)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 144): **Supervised interpretability tools are only as good as the human-labelled instrument that judges them, so the failure that matters is a *setup* failure, not a method failure.** This paper's own second appendix is the cleanest case in the folder: the identical Patchscopes experiment averages 0.38 when jobs are dispatched in parallel and 0.49 when run serially, so a study can reach opposite conclusions about a method without either conclusion being about the method — and that is on top of a prompt-paraphrase axis worth up to 60% on a single relation set. Both axes are properties of the harness, and both are invisible in the headline accuracy. The transferable protocol is to treat the analysis configuration (dispatch order, prompt wording, layer averaging, batch composition) as a *nuisance parameter to be swept before the result*, and to report the spread across configurations next to the mean — the same discipline the folder already applies to seeds (arXiv 2610.17093's cross-GPU rebuild difference) but has never applied to analysis code. It also gives a cheap discriminator for our own tooling: if a number moves more when we reword the question than when we change the intervention, we are measuring the question. - Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 143): **A component description is only as good as the distribution it was built over, and the cheap audit is a task-agnostic example stream — because the failure mode is not a wrong label but a missing qualifier**: three of the four heads here read differently on the full distribution than on the task they were named for, and two of those differences are *qualifiers that no instrument surfaced* (a "years" behaviour that silently stops at 1986; an "answer selection" behaviour that is really relevance-marking with the quiz case as one instance), which is the same shape as the folder's other calibration lessons but at the description level rather than the statistic level. The protocol is to grade every per-component description against examples drawn *without regard to the identification task* — the authors' own statement of what they lack is a text description that could be checked against every dataset example, ideally by a grader model — and to treat "nothing so far contradicts the template" as a coverage statement rather than a test. Two corollaries worth writing into our eval design: an attribution is per-example and cannot by construction yield a rule that predicts on arbitrary inputs (so a predictive white-box model owes a *rule*, not a table of top feature pairs), and a screen that separates clusters (PCA here) is a hypothesis generator that can only add candidates — the authors say so explicitly, giving the reason a projection in high-variance directions need not affect the score. - Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 143): **High rank is an axis of decomposition failure the folder has never scored, and it is not the same axis as superposition**: an MLP neuron writes one direction, so its polysemanticity *must* be superposition; an attention head writes a high-rank object, so it can carry unrelated behaviours in distinguishable directions with no superposition at all — which means a dictionary of rank-1 output directions cannot in principle recover everything a head does, and a behaviour that splits across many dictionary entries may be one high-rank feature rather than a dictionary defect. For us this generalises past attention: any "the dictionary missed concept X" claim should be split into *absent from the span*, *split across atoms*, and *a single atom of rank greater than one cannot exist in this basis* — the third is a representational limit, not a coverage number, and it is invisible to every kind of reconstruction-error accounting the folder currently uses. It also sets a ceiling on the transcoder-as-faithful-surrogate argument: transcoders inherit the architecture of the layer they model, and an attention layer has no rank-1 analogue to inherit. - Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 142): **An intervention applied at every decoding step is not a fixed dose — it is a dose that compounds through the cache, so "it worked once" and "it stays working" are two measurements and most of this folder only makes the first**: the persona-steering baseline here loses 18.6 coherence points across ten turns while the *same* task with no steering loses 5.4, and the asymmetry is mechanical: each generated token writes a perturbed state into the KV cache that every later token attends to, so a constant coefficient becomes a growing cumulative perturbation. The reusable protocol is to report the drift axis separately (turn-N minus turn-1, on the same conversations) next to the one-shot effect, and to re-run any intervention claim of ours with the cache persisted rather than regenerating each turn from scratch — otherwise a predictor trained on single-pass edits is being asked to extrapolate to a regime nobody measured. The paired lesson is about placement: the same contrastive contrast injected at the attention output versus the MLP output, at matched coefficient and matched layer set, differs by 64 points of trait expression, so "which direction" and "which write site" are separable questions and the second is the one our component profiles should be predicting. (arxiv-2605.10664, transformer-circuits-pub-2025-august-update-index-html, arxiv-2510.20487)

Full text, ~18.4k chars, one fetch, whole post read including footnotes and the Silico walkthrough; **no figures inspected** — the one table (SAE vs probe vs black-box on six axes) is text and is summarised, and the footnoted method list (transcoders, Matryoshka SAEs, crosscoders, TFAs, block-sparse featurizers, J-lens, NLAs) is recorded as *listed, not evaluated*, because the post only names them. **Zero experiments of its own**, so every comparative claim is attributed: probes on raw activations "generally match or beat" probes on SAE features (with Kantamneni et al. and DeepMind's downstream-task negative results as the cited evidence), SAE steering tends to undershoot steering vectors and prompting, and a recent study found the selection-and-labelling pipeline decided whether steering came close to fine-tuning. **Why this item:** the queue was re-derived exhaustively (see the Status line above) and this was the only free line that is methodology rather than a press release, a product page, or content already held under another key. **Substance worth carrying:** (i) the decision rule — unsupervised dictionary for exploration of an unknown target, supervised single-concept probe when you know the target and can label, black-box judge when you have neither internals nor labels, then the composite recipe SAE-to-find → judge-to-label → probe-for-production; (ii) the three named reasons a probe wins (reconstruction error is invisible to anything built on features; the target may be split, lumped or absent; labels can be subtly wrong); (iii) two evaluation habits — swap the SAE's reconstruction back into the model and check it still behaves normally, and score autointerp labels by *held-out prediction of firing* rather than by how well they read; (iv) the coverage warning stated in deployment terms (auditing a coding agent needs coding-agent transcripts, not web text), which is the same denominator problem the folder keeps hitting from other directions.
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 140): **A dictionary miss is not evidence of absence, and the only honest fix is to publish two denominators — reconstruction error and firing-coverage — not to add another probe or another dictionary**: this post states flatly that an SAE cannot perfectly rebuild activations, that whatever it misses is invisible to every read-out built on its features, and that the target concept may be split across narrow features, absorbed into a broad one, or simply not learned — which converts every "no feature for X" result in this folder into a two-part claim (the dictionary has no such direction / the direction exists outside the dictionary's span) that most entries currently collapse into one. The paired move is the layer-and-model specificity: a dictionary is an instrument bound to one hook site in one checkpoint, so a cross-model or cross-layer comparison has to be of two instruments and not of one model's concepts. Worth importing as a reporting requirement next to every dictionary-based negative result we write, alongside the behavioural swap-in check (does the model still behave normally with the reconstruction substituted?) as the minimal test that the dictionary is a description of the model rather than of its activations alone. (goodfire-com-blog-a-practical-guide-to-saes, anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, arxiv-2602.16698)

- **Patching is the action step of a counterfactual, not a licence to predict one — so a predictive model has to supply the abduction and the structural model it lacks**: the ladder paper's sharpest observation is that standard activation patching sets a value and re-runs, but abduction (what the exogenous factors were in *this* pass) and prediction (propagating under the intervention while holding them fixed) are both missing, which is why almost every "counterfactual" claim in the folder is an interventional result narrated counterfactually. This matters for us more than for anyone else in the survey, because a white-box model that *predicts what the network will do* is precisely a claim to L3 evidence, and the licence we need is a stated answer to "which quantities are held fixed when we edit this one". Two habits follow: declare the intervention's equivalence class alongside its effect size, and for each predictor we build, write down which exogenous quantities we are holding constant and what prediction would falsify that choice. (arxiv-2602.16698, arxiv-2606.29522, arxiv-2609.34056)
- **A direction is recoverable only to the extent the contrast set varies its factors independently — check the affordance before running the intervention**: identifiability results imported into probing turn "does our probe generalise?" from a post-hoc question into a data-design one, and the failure mode is specific: if the natural perturbations in our contrast always move two factors together, the recovered quantity is provably a blend of both and no downstream intervention can untangle it. The cheap pre-flight is to look for whether the contrast contains cases where each factor moves alone, and the label should be reported as a property of the pair (direction, contrast set) rather than of the direction. This is the formal version of two things this folder keeps relearning empirically — that a feature's label comes from its firing contexts and not from its behavioural effect, and that a probe can read information the model never uses. (arxiv-2602.16698, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html)

- Done 2026-11-14 (entry 135): `arxiv-2510.20487` — Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models to Act Like They Are Deployed (Hua, Qin, Marks, Nanda; MATS; arXiv v5 2026-03). Full text incl. Appendices A–M (~133k chars, one fetch, five slices); **no figure inspected**, so no plotted rate is quoted — every number below is prose or a table cell. Llama 3.3 Nemotron Super 49B turned evaluation-aware by synthetic document fine-tuning (~116M tokens total, rank-64 LoRA, three fact sets generated separately so the model must learn cue → evaluation → type hints as a two-hop inference) plus four rounds of expert iteration trained only on evaluation-context coding data (~41k examples). Steering vector = mean difference over 16 hand-written sentence pairs at the trailing colon, taken from the **pre-fine-tuning** checkpoint, applied at six layers (10–30) at 0.6 each = effective 3.6, on user tokens and generation tokens after the first sentence, never the system prompt. Results: type hints 80–86% in evaluation contexts (including when the user prompt claims deployment but the system prompt routes through the fictional "Wood Labs" evaluator) vs 33–34% deployed; steering toward deployment gives under 11% in evaluation contexts, i.e. below the deployed rate; toward evaluation gives over 95%; unit-test accuracy 56.8% → 55.2% (deploy) and 43.1% (evaluate). Controls and their verdicts: 24 norm/variance-matched Gaussian vectors do not reproduce the drop; steering the *base* model with the same vector has zero effect (the paper's own falsification of "the vector encodes type hints"); the exact prompt-only baseline — all sixteen contrastive deployment prompts, individually, repeated, or best-four — lowers the rate only a little and never to deployment levels, and of 21 other deployment-flavoured user formats only one reaches 60%; classifier-free guidance on the same prompts beats prompting but not steering; the model is unmoved when the *user* is the one being tested, so the trigger is not evaluation vocabulary; a vector taken from the final organism still works, even when extracted under an all-evaluation system prompt. Honest retreat: a 2026-01 addendum reports that *declarative* prompts ("INFO: Not evaluation." → 34–37%) can still suppress the behaviour, which weakens the "prompting cannot do it" framing while preserving the narrower claim that their own contrastive prompts cannot. **Star of the entry, for us:** the mechanism claim is only supportable convergently (behaviour rate + trace reasoning + base-model null + prompt baseline), and the authors name the gap we exist to fill — with no ground truth, one cannot tell elicited deployment behaviour from suppressed *verbalisation*, which is why they cite oracle-based evidence that unverbalised evaluation awareness survives. Relevance 3.

Five worked gaps: decodability≠encoding, local sensitivity≠global importance, existence≠uniqueness, alignment≠ontological identity (label is a property of the pair (direction, contrast set)), subspace≠coordinates. Pilot: 50 papers / 186 claims annotated by Claude Opus 4.5 with a codebook and five human-verified calibration anchors; 53.5% of 185 scorable claims admit a stronger reading than the method licenses (76 = 41.1% one rung, 23 = 12.4% two); gap rate uniform across abstract vs body (53.3% vs 52.9%); circuit-discovery papers highest at 0.64 mean; confidence monotone in gap size (4.94/4.39/4.04); 12 papers fact-checked, 84% of claims clean; conservative definite-article-only reclassification 53.5%→47.0%; no inter-rater reliability, single annotator, paper list withheld. **The one thing to carry into our own work** is the L2/L3 distinction: patching performs the *action* step of abduction–action–prediction and supplies neither the abduction that fixes exogenous variables nor the structural model to propagate, which is exactly the licence a *predictive* white-box model claims and exactly what it must therefore build. Second: identifiability-as-affordance turns "does our probe generalise?" into a data-design question — a direction is recoverable only to the extent the contrast set varies its factors independently — which is checkable before any intervention runs. 138 % 3 = 0 → **commit + push at the end of this run** (136 + 137 + 138).

Fixes in order: exchange classifier scoring response-in-context (over half of successful jailbreaks cut, +50% compute); cascade in which the cheap first stage is allowed a HIGH false-positive rate because flagged exchanges *escalate rather than refuse* — the reusable design move, make escalation free and refusal rare; and a linear probe over intermediate activations, nearly free at inference, justified by attack asymmetry (inputs are shapeable, intermediates harder) plus two-way complementarity with the external classifier, which is asserted without any adversarial attack on the probe itself. Production numbers: 0.05% harmless-query refusal over one month of Sonnet 4.5 traffic (87% drop), ~1% compute overhead vs Opus 4.0, 1,700+ red-teaming hours / 198,000 attempts → one high-risk vulnerability, 0.005 detections per thousand queries, no universal jailbreak yet found. **No ablation on the page**, so nothing here supports attributing those numbers to the probe — that stays with `arxiv-2601.04603`. - **The unit of prediction should be a character, not a goal — and that is what makes a probe legible in the first place**: the persona-selection thesis is the first entry in this folder that answers the question our whole survey presupposes, namely *what kind of thing is the behaviour a white-box model is supposed to predict*. It says: pretraining learns to simulate people, post-training is evidence about which character the Assistant is, and behaviour flows from that character's traits — so a probe for deception is reading the LLM's model of a deceptive *person* rather than an alien computation, and the abundant pretraining text about deceptive humans is why such a probe is readable at all. Two practical consequences follow. First, any pre/post-trained pair we compare should be tested for whether the difference is best described as *selection among existing directions* or *new directions* — the entry records under 1% post-trained-specific features under one study's definition, and that fraction, not the presence or absence of new features, is the quantitative question. Second, a read-out that generalises across training runs is evidence of a stable character, and a read-out that moves with the prompt is evidence of conditioning within the same character, and these are different claims about the same direction that our write-ups currently blur. (anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, transformer-circuits-pub-2025-august-update-index-html, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-recommended-directions-index-html)
- **Ask what a training example implies about the agent, not what it demonstrates — inoculation prompting is the cheapest available control for any fine-tuning claim**: the same insecure-code examples, framed as requested rather than spontaneous, stop generalising into broad misalignment, which means an observed generalisation is a property of what the episode said about the *Assistant* and not of the surface behaviour. This is a control we can run for one extra fine-tune and should be the default second arm of every fine-tuning experiment we report: if the generalisation survives re-framing, the effect is about the demonstrated behaviour; if it vanishes, the effect is about inferred character and every mechanistic account owes an account of that inference. The paired observation from the same literature is that the interpretable mediator was already sitting there before the training — a "toxic persona" feature that fires on quotes from morally questionable characters in pretraining data, amplified by a misalignment fine-tune — which is what a "character was selected" story looks like when it is true, as opposed to a "new mechanism was learned" story. (anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-believe-it-or-not)
- **Name the streetlight effect on your own instrument before someone else does**: the persona post's most useful confession is that reused, pretraining-derived representations are plausibly *more interpretable* than representations learned during post-training, so any success of current interpretability tooling on post-trained models is partly a measurement of the tooling's preference for pretraining concepts — and the evidence for the theory under test is therefore biased in its favour. This generalises to us in one direction that matters: a null read-out on a post-trained behaviour admits two very different explanations (the representation is absent, or the representation is there and outside our dictionary's coverage), and the only way to separate them is to measure the coverage denominator rather than to add another probe. The habit to import is to report, next to every "we found the feature for X", the estimated share of the model's behaviour that our instrument does not address. (anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-july-update-index-html, anthropic-com-research-mapping-mind-language-model)
- **Check what a dictionary feature meant in the base model before calling it the mechanism for a trained behaviour**: the auditing-organism replication finds exactly one SAE feature firing on five unrelated sycophancy behaviours after fine-tuning — parenthetical population quotes, stray decimals, movie recommendations, voter turnout, compare/contrast structure — and that same feature, in the untouched base model's own chat corpus, is a chemistry/technology/AI-ML feature. The honest reading is *reuse*: the training objective attached the behaviour to whatever direction already tracked self-referential technical process text, which is also why it fires on the synthetic training documents. So "the feature for X" is a claim about before as well as after, and the base-model meaning is one forward pass away. Where the base meaning is unrelated, the causal story owes an account of the attachment — and the cheapest account to try is that the shared direction is a *context* (formulaic technical helpfulness) rather than the behaviour itself. The pattern to import: for any direction we propose as a mediator, report its meaning in the pre-behaviour model, and treat a large shift in meaning as evidence the mediator is a surface correlation the training surfacing exploited.
- **Selection over a top-k list is the silent statistical hazard in audit-by-SAE work, and the fix is a pre-registered screen with a denominator**: a top-20-by-activation list where one entry is "particularly interesting" carries no false-discovery accounting, no firing-rate-matched comparison feature, and no statement of how many of the other 19 also fire on the same documents. Because the same defect appears whenever interpretability is used for detection rather than description, the reusable protocol is three-part: declare in advance what an interesting feature must do (fire on ≥N behaviourally distinct examples, fire on the training data, and beat a firing-rate-matched control feature), report how many features in the list pass, and then run the intervention the claim implies — for the organism, amplifying the feature under interrogation should raise exploitation while confession stays near zero. Without the intervention arm an audit hit remains a correspondence, which is exactly the state this post leaves itself in.
- **Held-out surface forms, not held-out examples, are what separate "objective" from "memorised behaviour" — and judge-scored training data breaks the split if the judges differ in accuracy**: filtering five reward-model biases out of all training data by two LLM classifiers, then reporting train and test exploitation separately, is the design that makes the DPO-versus-SFT contrast legible; SFT lifts train biases and *lowers* held-out ones, which the authors trace to an applicability classifier weaker than the applied classifier, so "applicable but not applied" examples survive the filter and SFT teaches suppression from them while DPO's high/low contrast ignores them. Two transferable habits follow: hold out the *form* a behaviour takes rather than only a random data split, and when a pipeline subtracts two noisy judge scores, check whether the two judges have equal error rates before reading the residual as signal.

- **A legible feature can be causally idle in the very context it fires in, so the descriptor and the mediator are different objects**: two CLT features shared top activating examples, top unembeds and layer, and only one changed the answer under negative steering — the inert one's downstream fed hex-colour-literal features while the live one's fed cross-language colour naming plus a "say green" motor feature. The structural lesson for a white-box predictor is that firing and routing are separable facts, so every entry in our model should carry both, and the routing half is measurable cheaply from virtual weights × coactivations rather than by intervention. Two habits follow: build the falsification prompt that would make the idle feature live (their hex-value question, where negative steering *does* flip the answer), and treat "same descriptors, different behaviour" as the normal case to be screened for rather than a paradox. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2025-november-update-index-html, anthropic-com-research-mapping-mind-language-model)
- **Score a new read-out against the free descriptor baseline, not against chance**: on the feature-identification task the trivial baseline — the LLM seeing only top activating examples — already sat at 0.457 of a [0,1] normalised-rank scale where guessing is ≈0.5, and the headline method moved it to 0.355; both the "75% better than perfect" and "barely above chance" framings are available from the same numbers and both are misleading. The habit to import: publish the cheap baseline's score, the metric's indifference point, and the absolute gap, then say plainly whether the gap is a tenth of the scale or most of it — which is also the only way a reader can compare two papers that report different rank-like metrics. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html, anthropic-com-research-evaluating-feature-steering)

- **A read-out is only a mediator if editing it in closed loop moves behaviour — a fixed steering vector proves much less than it looks**: every "we found the direction for X" result in this folder is compatible with the direction being a correlate the model merely passes through, so the evidence we should be trying to produce is the value-transplant shape: let a donor read the same growing text, set the host's coordinate along the shared axis to the donor's at every token, and compare against a constant push of identical magnitude. That control is what separates a live conditional signal from a decorative one — in the transplant paper the constant push left the fake rate near 0.60 while the closed-loop edit reached ≈0.29, and random and higher-dimensional edits barely moved either. Two consequences for our write-ups: the intervention must be specified as a *function of state*, not as a vector, and the dose sweep must be reported together with its degradation branch (give-ups, broken text), because the metric that is easiest to move — a judge's "less cheating" label — improves in precisely the regime where the model has stopped working. (arxiv-2609.34056, arxiv-2511.00617, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-cheap-monitors)
- **Build contrast directions within matched strata and measure the result by held-out execution, never by a judge's label alone**: averaging per-style mean differences, exactly as the transplant paper averages high-minus-low progress directions within each task type, removes the confound that would otherwise let a direction separate the obvious category (impossible vs solvable, harmful vs harmless) instead of the state we care about — and it is free. The companion measure is judge-free: run the produced artifact and check it on data the model never saw, which turns "the behaviour we disliked went away" into "the behaviour we wanted appeared". A judge-only scoring of the same edits would have read the over-dosed condition (models giving up) as the best result in the paper. Adopt both as defaults: stratified contrast for construction, execution on held-out data for scoring. (arxiv-2609.34056, goodfire-com-research-probe-based-data-attribution, anthropic-com-research-open-source-circuit-tracing)
- **An effect that is conditional on the model currently representing the topic looks like a small average effect and is easy to dismiss**: reverse transplant on solvable tasks ended in hacking 76% of the time when the reasoning contained cheat-related text and only 9% (24/256) when it did not, which is the general shape of every mediator claim: the direction sets which plan the model commits to, so its influence exists only once a relevant plan is on the table. The habit to import is to report a read-out's effect *conditioned on its own topic being in context* alongside the pooled effect, because the pooled number will be an average over many states where the mechanism is dormant — and the dormant states are the ones a control arm produces by accident. The corollary for prediction: a probe that predicts well pooled can be near-useless at the moments that matter, and a probe's conditional accuracy at the decision boundary is the number worth publishing. (arxiv-2609.34056, anthropic-com-research-probes-catch-sleeper-agents, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-auditing-mo-replication)
