- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 241): `arxiv-2611.18274` — Right Token, Right Time: From Per-Token Gating to Trajectory-Aware Activation Steering (Nima Eshraghi, Lovedeep Gondara, Sagarika Suresh, Xiaotong Xu, Jithin Pradeep, Fanny Chevalier — Vanguard / University of Toronto; arXiv:2611.18274v1, 2026-11-13, CC BY 4.0). Full text, all ~108.5k clean chars in six windows. **Framing:** steering recast as **budgeted per-token allocation** — fix the steered-token fraction p, fix direction v and magnitude α, and the gate sequence m_{1:T} is the only free variable, so at matched p every method comparison is a controlled ablation. Direction built from top-k SAE feature differentials between a target and neutral corpus; a task-agnostic probe `u = sign(α)v` makes `⟨h_t,u⟩` monotone in target alignment for both suppression and elicitation. **Two gates:** **CFP** memoryless, fires when `⟨h_t,u⟩ ≤ τ` with τ calibrated to p, one dot product per token, and is exactly the budget-calibrated form of feature-triggered conditional steering; **CLABS** standardises the projection, sets error `e_t = s⋆ − ŝ_t` and a **leaky integral** `ē_t` (EWMA, memory ~1/β), then samples `m_t ~ Bernoulli(clip(p₀ + κ_p e_t + κ_i ē_t))` with p₀ calibrated to the budget — no rollouts, no backtracking, no learned scorer, overhead ~1e-6 of a forward pass. **Theory:** Assumption 1 is a first-order steering-response model `ŝ_{t+1} = φŝ_t + (1−φ)β₀ + g m_t + η_t`; the controller state follows a 2×2 linear recursion with `a = φ − gκ_p`, and Theorem 1's sufficient condition for ρ(A)<1 is `0 ≤ a < 1` and `0 ≤ gκ_i < (2−β)(1+a)/β`, yielding geometric convergence of the mean, asymptotic variance `≤ c(A)σ̄²`, and time-averaged squared error `O(1/T)+O(σ̄²)`; Corollary 1 gives `e_ss = N/(1−φ+g(κ_p+κ_i))` and so `|e_ss|` non-increasing in κ_i; Remark 1 makes the leaky integral's cost explicit with a positive floor on `|e_ss|` — bounded memory buys a reduced but nonzero offset. **Results:** Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.1-8B, one mid-network layer, three targets (RealToxicityPrompts detoxification, GoEmotions fear and sadness elicitation), AlpacaEval for competence, three seeds, three corrections applied identically to every method. CFP and CLABS get the largest behavioral shift among budgeted gates on all six panels, **2–3× the entropy gates and random control at the smallest budgets**, converging with them as p→1; CLABS recovers **89–92%** of the Full-steer shift on emotion targets at moderate budget. They are the **only gates preferred to No-steer at every budget under both judges** (gpt-5-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.6) on AlpacaEval, with PPL 23–28 vs 41.2 for Full-steer at p=1.0 and distinct-2 ~0.86–0.91 vs 0.68. **Ablation (Table 3, p=0.5):** toxicity reduction open-loop 0.12 → I-only 0.15 → P-only 0.21 → PI 0.24, perplexity 9.8 → 9.0 → 8.9 → 8.6, I-only widest seed variance. **Budget honesty:** realized rates within 0.04 of nominal for all methods, CFP/CLABS ranges inside STS's, ranking unchanged at realized rates. **Negatives the paper prints itself:** the authors' own SRE baseline (steer where the SAE reconstructs faithfully) is mid-pack rather than competitive, and they explicitly do *not* reproduce SIA — they extract its selection signals (predictive entropy, entropy rise) as single-pass gates, so SIA's numbers here are not SIA's. **Limitations:** two open base models, one layer, one direction, English, three classifier-scorable targets, no human eval, and the stability result is a *linearisation around the interior operating point*, explicitly not a worst-case guarantee. **Why relevance 3:** it isolates an axis the folder has discussed only as a side condition, and supplies the guardrail — the gain box — that turns "pick a steering strength" into something that can be refused in advance rather than discovered as oscillation.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 219): **When the intervention budget is fixed, allocation stops being a nuisance variable and becomes the treatment — and the fraction of tokens steered turns out to be a better first-class knob than the magnitude, because at matched realized budgets the choice of *which* tokens to steer moves behavior by 2–3× at p ≤ 0.2 while the methods converge as p → 1 (Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.1-8B, three targets, both judges).**
Concretely, this reframes a design decision the folder has been making implicitly: `arxiv-2611.04757` asked whether a steering edit should depend on the input and `arxiv-2611.04349` argued for sparse internal control, but neither held cost constant, so "sparser is better" and "the direction is better" could not be separated. Fixing p and holding v and α fixed does separate them, and the result is that the *informed* gates beat random Bernoulli(p) gating at the same spend while an entropy-based gate — a plausible need signal — falls furthest behind precisely when the budget is scarce. The transferable rule: publish steering results as efficacy *at a stated intervention ratio*, with the random gate at matched realized spend as the mandatory floor, and treat any comparison that varies density and strength together as unreported. (arxiv-2611.18274, arxiv-2611.04757, arxiv-2611.04349)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 219): **A stability certificate is worth more than an effect size when the controller reads its own output, because the failure mode is oscillation rather than weakness — and the certificate here is closed-form in quantities you can estimate, which is what makes it usable: stability holds iff `0 ≤ φ − gκ_p < 1` and `0 ≤ gκ_i < (2−β)(1+a)/β`, so the proportional gain is capped by activation persistence and the integral gain by the memory length, and the same box that guarantees convergence also bounds how much the integral term can help, giving `|e_ss| > 0` for every admissible gain.**
Two consequences. First, a closed loop needs a stated certificate with its operating assumptions printed beside it — here Assumption 1's linearisation holds only where the calibrated budget keeps the gating probability off its clip bounds, which the authors say plainly rather than burying in an appendix. Second, the leaky integral is a deliberate downgrade from exact tracking: an EWMA of the error trades offset for bounded memory, so the honest reporting of a PI controller in this setting includes the residual steady-state offset and its floor, not just the variance bound. The same discipline applies to any adaptive probe, adaptive threshold, or budgeted patrol of ours that consumes its own output as input: name the quantity that persists between steps, state the region where the response is linear enough for the analysis to apply, and refuse gains outside the box. (arxiv-2611.18274, arxiv-2610.27393, arxiv-2611.12206)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 219): **Fluency and efficacy are reported together at a matched budget or the comparison is uninterpretable — the same method that looks best on behavioral shift at p=0.2 can be worst on both axes once the quality cost is priced in, since a light touch preserves utility while barely moving the target, and the paper's own table shows an entropy gate winning a single AlpacaEval cell that its efficacy curve contradicts.**
The authors' handling is the template: every gate is compared at the same realized rate (within 0.04 of nominal, with the random gate's sampling spread as the reference band), the ranking is re-read at realized rather than nominal rates, and instruction-following is reported under two independent judges so a lone favourable cell can be checked against the other. For the folder this closes a loop with the objective-inflation and pooled-agreement findings — a metric that can be won by doing less, reported without the cost dimension, is a denominator problem. The rule to carry: any controlled-generation result should print efficacy, quality, and spend together in one row, and a single-best-cell claim must come with its contradicting curve. (arxiv-2611.18274, arxiv-2611.11035, arxiv-2611.18514)

- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 277): `arxiv-2611.07756` — Scaling Laws for SAE Training Data (Nikita Koriagin — work done while at T-Tech; Nikita Balagansky, Daniil Gavrilov — Yandex / T-Tech; arXiv:2611.07756v1, cs.LG, 2026-11-05, CC BY 4.0). Full text via HTML (53,437 clean chars, §§1–6 + Appendices A–E). **Substance:** the SAE training budget is split into **total activation presentations** (optimisation effort) and **unique activations in the buffer** (coverage/storage), and the experiment holds the first fixed while sweeping the second — for N_total ∈ {128M, 640M, 1.28B} and D ∈ {16k, 32k, 64k, 128k}, a buffer of U unique activations replayed E = N_total/U times, over U/N_total ∈ {1/128 … 1}, giving a 96-run grid on Llama-3.1 8B layer 15 BatchTopK SAEs (k = 32, FineWeb, held-out EV on 10^6 excluded tokens). Saturation = smallest tested buffer within ϵ = 0.005 of the curve's best EV, reported as an interval between grid points. Validation across Llama layers 5/15/25, Qwen3-1.7B/4B/8B with TopK, the three gates at D = 32k, and FineMath + Stack-Edu Python domains; SAEBench (reconstruction MSE, absorption, AutoInterp, sparse probing) on 24 layer-15/640M checkpoints; a two-term law EV = E∞ − A·D^−α − B·N_eff^−β with N_eff the data-constrained-scaling repetition discount, fitted with a constant and a width-dependent repetition scale and compared by AIC. **Results:** EV rises steeply with diversity then plateaus — 16k at 128M budget goes 0.5801 (1M unique) → 0.6393 (128M unique), 32k 0.5870 → 0.6610; the saturation interval at 1.28B scales ~linearly with width (20–40M / 40–80M / 80–160M / 160–320M) and is nearly budget-invariant once the budget exceeds it, so storage savings grow with budget to **64×** at 16k/1.28B and are **≥8× in every cell** (9.54 TiB full corpus vs 152.6 GiB buffer); wider dictionaries reach higher plateaus (+2–3 EV points per doubling of D) but need ~2× more diversity, and the 128k cell at 640M (0.711) is diagnosed as undertrained; the width-dependent repetition scale is decisively preferred (γ = 0.526, c = 103.3, ΔAIC −77.3 vs the constant-scale fit), the 96 points collapse onto one capacity-corrected power law (RMSE 4.8e-3 EV), and a held-out 640M budget is predicted from the two extreme budgets at 3.1e-3 EV RMSE, with the held-out 128k width recovered only in the sufficiently-trained regime; downstream, reconstruction and sparse probing track the EV plateau but **AutoInterp saturates later (160M for the 32k and 64k widths against EV's 40M and 80M) and absorption is non-monotonic, rising with diversity at 32k and 64k**; tolerance is first-class (ϵ = 0.0025 doubles the Python buffer, 0.010 halves it); one training run per cell, no error bars, and the law is about reconstruction, not about features.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 278): **How much an interpretability artefact was trained on is an experimental variable with a measurable saturation point, and that point is different per metric — here reconstruction plateaus at 20M/40M/80M unique activations for the 16k/32k/64k dictionaries while automated interpretability needs 40M/160M/160M from the same runs, and feature absorption does not saturate monotonically at all but rises with diversity at the two wider widths.** The consequence for our battery is a reporting convention: any SAE, probe or dictionary we build should carry the metric *its claim depends on* together with the buffer/step count at which that metric saturated, because "trained at size X" names a budget only relative to a metric, and the cheapest version of this is the paper's Appendix C — one row per metric, one smallest-qualifying-budget cell per width, computed inside the same sweep that chose the artifact. The stronger reading is that the disagreement is itself evidence about what each metric is sensitive to: sparse probing is nearly flat across the whole sweep (it reads information that is present early and stays present), AutoInterp keeps improving after reconstruction stops (it rewards coverage, which is exactly what more diversity supplies), and absorption's non-monotonicity says disentanglement is not a resource that scales with data in the way reconstruction is. Coreference arxiv-2611.08438 (the survey's evidence-practice point) and arxiv-2610.23801 (the sparse-probing test that keeps an SAE honest).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 278): **A capacity parameter and a data parameter can be traded against each other and the confound is invisible from the total budget alone — doubling dictionary width buys 2–3 EV points but demands about twice the unique activations to reach them, the repetition scale itself shrinks with width (γ = 0.526, so a doubling multiplies it by ≈0.69), and the 128k dictionary's apparently worse result at 640M is undertraining rather than a ceiling.** Two habits follow. First, whenever we compare two artefacts of different capacity — two dictionary widths, two probe dimensionalities, two model sizes — the comparison is only meaningful if each has reached *its own* plateau, and the paper's diagnosis is the reusable test: if the larger artefact's score climbs when you hold its presentations fixed and add diversity, the gap was data, not capacity. Second, the fitted form EV = E∞ − A·D^−α − B·N_eff^−β is a template for any scale comparison we report: a ceiling plus one penalty per resource whose exponents tell you which resource is binding, and the sign that we have left the fitted regime is that a single-penalty fit starts needing different coefficients per arm. Coreference arxiv-2611.21486 (a supervision set can be complete on its domain and still not identify the rule) and arxiv-2611.18163 (the task-level ceiling that no method can exceed).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 278): **A tolerance is not a footnote, it is the knob that sets the recommendation: at ϵ = 0.005 the Python-text buffer is 40M activations (16×), at 0.0025 it doubles to 80M (8×), at 0.010 it halves to 20M (32×) — and the paper states the reference EV, the tested grid and the tolerance as three things a buffer recommendation is relative to, because the two endpoints of every "plateau" are just adjacent grid points with no estimated threshold between them.** This is the folder's recurring warning about unstated reference points applied to resource sizing, and it generalises to every budget we quote: a sample count, a step count, a buffer size or a dictionary width means nothing without the tolerance and the grid it was chosen on. The honest reporting form is to give the interval and the tolerance, then the choice, in that order — and to say which grid spacing would have moved the answer, since the paper notes FineMath selects the *same* buffer at the stricter tolerance purely because of where its grid points fall. The companion habit is to spend the sweep twice: once to find the plateau and once on a pilot to confirm that the fitted law's conservative direction of error (six of twelve fitted intervals one grid step larger than observed) still holds in the new setting rather than assuming it.
- Done 2026-11-17 (entry 288): `arxiv-2611.18382` — Where Tree Ensembles Decide: Structural Local Explanation with Decision Predicate Graphs (Sylvio Barbon Junior — University of Trieste; Luca Longo — University College Cork; arXiv:2611.18382v1, cs.LG, 2026-11-13, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; journal submission to *Knowledge-Based Systems*). Full text via HTML (~82K clean chars, abstract + §§1–7 + Appendices A–B + references, read end to end). **Substance:** for one sample of a 100-tree ensemble, every tree's root-to-leaf route is an executed rule; the routes are merged into a per-sample graph labelled with the trees that traversed each predicate, class support is built from per-tree leaf contributions through the family's own link function so the assigned class equals the prediction by construction (Proposition 1, verified on 342,040 of 342,040 samples up to rounding), and the **critical predicate** is the executed threshold whose single crossing, summed over the trees that share it with all other trees held fixed, would move a chosen target class most; it is a first-order estimate with no input-space search. The crossing is then applied to the whole model (one feature moved past the threshold, every tree re-evaluated) and scored. **Results:** 16 datasets, four families (RF, Bagging, AdaBoost-SAMME, GBM), 10 repetitions, one configuration per dataset×family chosen on validation accuracy with no explanation metric involved; the critical predicate separates differently-predicted neighbours at 0.262–0.336 against 0.105–0.157 random and 0.038–0.144 nearest, is crossed by the feature-tweaking counterfactual in 31–40% of samples against 6–8% random, flips the prediction in 0.181–0.428 of samples against 0.007–0.129 for random/nearest and 0.010–0.106 for TreeSHAP-guided, and recovers the true class of 49,835 wrong predictions in 46–69% of cases against 29–50% for the gain rule on contrastive TreeSHAP's top feature (and 0.388–0.777 for the tweaking-guided arm, which wins on AdaBoost); on planted faults it selects a faulty feature in 54–73% and lands within 0.25 of the faulty threshold in 46–71% against 6–21% at random, with contrastive TreeSHAP finding the feature more often (68–93%) but the threshold less often, and the two together reaching 59–90%; estimated gain tracks real change at per-sample Spearman 0.52–0.68; training-free repair of the localised thresholds is a **null** (−0.6% to +0.5% test error, none of 42 comparisons significant) while refitting gives −11% to −15%; cost 87–461 ms per sample, graph 173–885 nodes, contrastive view still 26–123 predicates.

Full text via HTML (~64K clean chars: abstract, §§1–5, references, Appendices A–L). **Substance:** a frozen Stable Diffusion 1.4 whose CLIP text encoder is hooked at layer 9; a k-sparse autoencoder (k = 48) trained once on layer-9 activations over the prompt corpus; per-feature forget/retain means and spreads at every token position, ranked by a contrast ratio whose denominator punishes features with no stable retain-side baseline; the top-k support defines a per-token unit direction (forget centroid minus retain centroid on the support); at inference the alignment of the live code with that direction is measured (clamped at zero), a strength-scaled multiple of it is subtracted along the same axis, and the sparse delta is mapped straight to hidden space through the linear decoder's transpose with a per-target cached direction (~925 KB), no weight edits. **Results:** best net trade-off of seven methods on all three spaces — AWUS 0.296, FaceAWUS 0.636, LPIPS-gap 0.402 against 0.279 / 0.233 / 0.262 at best for competitors; target-face similarity 0.160 vs adjacent 0.760 at full strength; COCO FID 15.71 → 16.11 and CLIPScore 27.39 → 26.95 over 10,000 captions; nudity detection 17.80% → 0.47% (I2P) and 93.68% → 12.63% (Ring-a-Bell K16) but losing to ESD on MMA-Diffusion (17.48% vs 12.70%); runtime 9.50 s/image against 9.52 s unmodified on one A30. **The ablation to carry:** the same projection in raw hidden space erases more (0.399 vs 0.387) and scores a higher AWUS (0.391 vs 0.381), so the dictionary's contribution is confined to selectivity (collateral drift 0.0065 vs 0.0078, peer-face retention 0.848 vs 0.722). Boundedness is proved (Proposition 1, Appendix B) and immediately scoped: nothing follows for neighbouring concepts or non-axis attributes.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 298): **The cheapest defence of a dictionary-mediated claim is to run the identical rule in the space the dictionary sits on top of, and the result here is that the dictionary loses the headline it was built for — the same bounded projection applied to raw layer-9 hidden states erases slightly more of the target (0.399 vs 0.387) and scores a slightly higher net utility (AWUS 0.391 vs 0.381), so what the sparse code actually buys is selectivity: lower collateral drift (0.0065 vs 0.0078) and markedly better retention of neighbouring identities' faces (0.848 vs 0.722).** This is the ablation our battery should run by default for every component we call interpretable, and the reporting rule that makes it honest is the one this paper follows: state the scalar the claim rests on *and* the selectivity numbers, then write the conclusion at the level the numbers support. The generic form is "the same edit, one representation down": a probe versus the raw activation it consumes, a dictionary feature versus the residual direction it is a coordinate of, an attribution over the dictionary versus a gradient in hidden space. If the simpler space wins the headline and only loses the side-metrics, the dictionary is a regulariser of the intervention rather than a localisation of the concept — and a paper that reports only the side-metrics wins can present that as necessity. Coreference arxiv-2611.11398 (a frozen random dictionary deciding which scores were artefacts) and arxiv-2611.20746-style raw-versus-abstracted comparisons already in the folder.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 298): **A score that subtracts the neighbour crowd is a different instrument from a score that subtracts nothing: every metric here is treatment effect minus control-crowd effect (AWUS on CLIP drops, FaceAWUS on ArcFace identity change, LPIPS-gap on perceptual change), so a method that erases harder by damaging everything scores lower rather than higher, and the paper's own framing number falls out — the baselines with higher raw erasure pay roughly twelve to twenty-two times the collateral damage — while the tuned-operating-point comparison is published beside a fixed-full-strength table because the two answer different questions.** Two habits to copy. First, for any component we claim is specific to a condition, report its effect on the condition minus its effect on the nearest neighbour conditions drawn from the same collection, because a direction that moves both equally has produced a shift and not an attribution; the paper's alternative, a near-miss baseline chosen by hand, is the version that needs a justification of its own (their peer lists rest on a post-hoc internal ranking that achieves only MRR 0.487). Second, publish the tuned comparison and the matched-strength comparison together: the tuned number flatters methods with a strength knob, and the matched number flatters the authors, and a reader given only one cannot tell which. Coreference arxiv-2611.21159 (an effect size with no floor) and arxiv-2611.20432 (an amplitude ratio beside a correlation).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 298): **A guarantee about one axis should be written with its scope in the same breath, and the proof here is the model of how to do it: boundedness is exact (“the signed alignment never crosses the retain side for any strength in the unit interval; at full strength the edit is the minimum-Euclidean-norm projection onto the retain half-space; tokens already on the retain side are untouched”) and the very next sentence says none of it guarantees preservation of neighbouring concepts or image attributes, moving collateral preservation to the empirical side where the three scored metrics carry it.** The companion finding is that a hyperparameter cliff belongs in the results and not in an appendix: every setting with fewer than 48 dictionary features scores 0.000–0.001 on the net metric while the published setting sits at 0.375 one step from a collapse, so the reported configuration is calibrated by its neighbourhood rather than by its value — and that sweep was run on a single identity, which the entry states. Together they are the folder's cleanest example of an exact result, honestly fenced, sitting beside an empirical result, honestly ragged. Coreference arxiv-2611.20897 (a certificate exactly true of the masked model) and arxiv-2611.20913 (a separation bought by construction and priced in the reconstruction column).

Full text via HTML (~46.6K clean chars: abstract, §§1–7, references, Appendices A–C, Tables 1–3). **Substance:** an evidence layer for post-trip and alarm diagnosis at two air-gapped gas plants — a property graph built in a single pass from the controller's native Block Pin Report CSV (blocks keyed by a four-part composite id, signal-flow edges from usage/connection columns deduplicated on the signal-block-pin triple, equations lifted from a constant pin into a block property, pins folded into edge properties to halve hop counts, four-level execution hierarchy), queried by a four-stage pipeline (classify into one of eight fixed operations, resolve entities in parallel with abstention and disambiguation, execute bounded Cypher with a truncation flag, then have a local Qwen 3.5-35B-A3B phrase an answer over an evidence payload it cannot rewrite), at most two model calls per query. **Results:** single controller 58,644 nodes / 116,107 edges from 168,220 CSV rows; seven-controller plant 221,406 nodes / 402,240 edges from 812,547 rows, built in under 30 s on a laptop. Prototype 1 (VLM over the 6,979-page PDF): Qwen 0.51 connection precision and 36% equation accuracy full-document (0.41 / 75% on the 100-page sample), Gemini 0.24 / 4%, 3.1 h on 4×H200 (~$124), versus under 10 s for the native export; 65% of PDF pages were not diagrams. Prototype 2 (tool-calling agent over the same graph, 40 template questions × 3 runs, Qwen 3.5-35B-A3B on one GB10): bounded pipeline 94% vs 85% answer correctness, p50 4.8 vs 14.2 s, p95 12.7 vs 108.6 s, 1.2K vs 24K tokens, 2.0 vs 9.1 round-trips, retrieved-set Jaccard 1.0 vs 0.61. **Limits:** one vendor format, one alarm-centred generated workload, LLM-judge over synthesised references, precision-only extraction, a single retrospective replay, proprietary data, no operational telemetry.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 299): **Extraction can be almost perfect on the objects of an explanation and worse than a coin flip on the relations that constitute it, and only a per-relation score reveals it: here block precision sat at 0.95–0.97 while connection precision over the full 6,979-page document was 0.51 (0.41 on a 100-page sample) and exact-equation accuracy collapsed from 75% on the sample to 36% at scale, and the pipeline downstream consumed rather than revalidated those edges.** For our battery the numbers are a template for what to instrument: every chained read-out — an attribution feeding a circuit feeding a behavioural claim — has entity-level and relation-level error, and the entity score is the one that looks reassuring. The two habits to copy are (a) score the relation against an independent authoritative representation, not against a held-out split of the same extraction, and (b) make a downstream stage revalidate rather than trust its input, because a stage that inherits a 0.51-precision graph produces confident traces that inherit its errors wholesale. The companion fact is that the informed path was *cheaper* as well as better — under 10 s to ingest the native structured export against 3.1 GPU-hours for the rendered view — so 'find the source before choosing the extractor' is a rule about representations we already hold, not about models. Coreference arxiv-2611.20840 (a high-relevance atom reading padding from the authors' own crop) and arxiv-2611.21550 (a surrogate's fidelity reported only where it was fitted).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 299): **Average quality and repeat stability are different quantities, and when a model chooses what evidence to gather, the stability number is the one that decides deployability: on the same graph, the same answer model and the same prompt, the bounded pipeline scored 94% vs 85% correctness but retrieved *identical* node sets across three repeats (Jaccard 1.0) where the agent averaged 0.61, issued between 0 and 31 graph calls, and sometimes answered with no retrieval at all — a 108.6 s p95 that made latency and capacity a function of the model's stopping behaviour.** Two habits for our own harness. Publish cross-run **set-overlap** of whatever a procedure retrieves — named components, top-k support, circuit membership — beside its average score, because a procedure can be right on average and different every run, and the second property is what a reader reproduces. And confine generative freedom to the two places where it is unavoidable — turning a request into a fixed operation, and phrasing the result — while fixed code produces the payload, with the payload recorded separately from the prose so that inter-run comparison is possible at all. This paper's honesty about the package belongs beside the method: the benchmark is template-generated and LLM-judged over synthesised references, so the 94% is a comparative development measure and the Jaccard is the robust part. Coreference arxiv-2611.21159 (an effect size with no floor) and arxiv-2611.20897 (a support set certified and uninformative).

- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 300): **The derivation is the publishable object, not the conclusion — and the test of a derivation record is transposition to a new dataset, not replay on the same one: here a node sequence built on one city's sidewalk imagery, rebuilt on another city's street views, recovered spatially coherent and correctly *different* patterns per branch, whereas re-running the same queries on the same corpus would have tested nothing but determinism.** For our battery this is the missing acceptance test for every composed read-out — a probe assembled from exemplars, a circuit found by a sequence of ablations, a concept built by intersecting two feature sets. Transport it: rebuild the same operation sequence against a second model, a second checkpoint or a second evaluation set, and publish whether the result is coherent and *changed in the way the mechanism predicts*, because that is the difference between a definition and a coincidence. Two bookkeeping details travel with it and cost nothing: number the nodes so asymmetric operators (difference, ablation-before-versus-after) stay well defined, and mark which node is the active parent for the next step — without both, a saved pipeline is not replayable at all. Coreference arxiv-2611.20398 (a native export beating a reconstruction of the same content) and arxiv-2611.20445 (agreement across clients measured against a method-specific reference).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 300): **A provenance record that logs only operations is complete-looking and unreproducible, because the judgements inside each operation — which three images were picked as exemplars of "well maintained", which similarity threshold was accepted — are the choices the conclusion actually rests on, and here they are invisible by design while the graph still presents itself as a full audit trail.** This is the human analogue of the folder's standing concern about metrics that are maxima over an unrecorded tuning parameter, and it costs one extra field per node: the seeds and thresholds, plus the reason, in the same saved state as the pipeline. For our reported read-outs the consequence is a rule — a derivation must record the *inputs to the decision*, not just the operator, or it will be cited as reproducible when only its scaffolding is. A companion from the same paper, which is also the cheapest way to form a new concept: make *difference against hand-picked positive exemplars* a first-class operator, which is how the eleven new categories here were carved out, and which is the human-in-the-loop form of the contrastive definition our probes compute implicitly. Coreference arxiv-2611.20840 (a dictionary's exemplars exposing a preprocessing leak) and arxiv-2611.11398 (a control that decided which scores were artefacts).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 300): **An interface can carry the traceability that the model cannot, and the division of labour is worth stating plainly: the frozen embedding supplies similarity, the human supplies the definition, and the system's job is to make the seam between them inspectable rather than to close it — the expert's own report is that text queries reach broad categories while image queries reach patterns nobody can name in keywords, so the two are complementary *and* their contributions are separable in the record.** The general lesson for our tooling is which part of an interpretability claim each party is entitled to: the model may say these two things are close, the human says this closeness means *slippery pavement*, and a battery that stores only the final label has thrown away which of the two did the work. Two design echoes for a read-out viewer: keep a manually curated bucket outside the derivation graph so that hand-picked evidence is visibly hand-picked and never inherits the authority of a computed node, and let a saved state be replayed against a different corpus in one action, because the replay is the validation. - Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 311): **An item-level paired test between two fitted models can pass on noise alone, and the only thing that shows it is a retrain of the same procedure on the same data under another seed — here four identical-data retrains split 87/57, 70/56, 48/56 and 35/55 items against their own originals, and one of them cleared the paper's own step rule at p = 0.0077, which demotes the authors' 4-of-4 per-lineage success from evidence about the procedure to a fact about pairs of adapters.** Every comparison in our battery is an item- or prompt-level paired test between two fits (probe A versus probe B, patched versus unpatched, layer 12 versus layer 20), and we treat significance on those pairs as a difference between methods. The missing arm is one line of code and one extra run: refit the *same* method on the *same* data with a different seed and run the identical paired test against the original. If that arm wins, the test is measuring seed. The paper prints the consequence honestly — its own registered headline survives at item level and fails at the clustered level — so the transfer is not "their result is wrong" but "publish the seed-null arm beside the paired test, and read the clustered interval as the claim". Coreference `arxiv-2611.20364` (a tie set that a rank order forbids) and `arxiv-2611.21586` (a verification count that rose with nothing surviving correction).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 311): **A holdout selected on the model's failures is a biased instrument by construction, and the size of the bias is measurable rather than arguable: with the base answering 12 of 889 items, step 1 can only lose 12, so its apparent gain on the reused exam was selection (base-answered items −0.371, base-wrong items +0.038 — regression to the mean), and on an exam drawn afterwards the same step added nothing (0.004, interval −0.016 to 0.023).** This is the exact flaw in our own "probe only the rows the model gets wrong" and "evaluate on the hard subset" evaluations, and it also explains why our round-1 numbers are always the flattering ones. Two cheap corrections, both used here: report the base's own share on the instrument (the ceiling on any step-1 loss), and draw a second instrument *after* the method is fixed and report both. The companion finding from the same paper is that the trickle of gain is real even when the round-1 story is not — rounds 2 and 3 each had intervals above zero on the fresh exam — so the honest sentence is "the method works, the first measurement of it was inflated". Coreference the holdout-reuse argument §2 cites (Dwork et al., named in the reference list) and `arxiv-2611.20983` (an equivalence margin set to the benchmark's own resolution).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 311): **A gain that is inconclusive under a conservative interval should be reported as inconclusive, and the machinery that lets an author do that is a registered outcome decided before the run plus the discipline to print the interval that includes zero beside the point estimate that supports the claim: generation 3 beats matched base-proposed data by 2.1 points, the registered interval over templates and lineages runs −0.002 to 0.046, and the paper's own abstract says "whether the rounds help beyond the data they accumulate is not shown".** Three related habits are worth copying wholesale into any of our reports. (a) **Levels of claim** stated in the methods: an item test licenses a statement about two adapters, a clustered interval a statement about families, and only seed replication a statement about the procedure — and the paper states that 4 of 4 lineages has a one-sided p of 0.0625, i.e. it is a count and not a test. (b) **Denominators that do not leak**: a gate amendment keeps an attempt withheld as exposed or as a harness failure in the arm's denominator, after a base at 21/46 (9 exposed) was being scored as a win over a candidate at 15/46 (19 exposed). (c) **The dev gate is reported as having filtered nothing** — three of twelve accepted steps were not significant at its own alpha — which is the honest way to describe a selection step that turned out to be a formality. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20983` (TOST at the benchmark's resolution), `arxiv-2611.20364` (nine classifiers within 0.12 points), and `arxiv-2611.20049`'s own Appendix S (a dev gate that advanced on any net gain).

- **Selection: the folder's last standing invitation, discharged — run 326 wrote that `2611.18179` was "the only item in the folder explicitly flagged as worth reversing", and it earns the 3 for a reason the earlier declines mis-stated.** Every prior decline called it "medical-domain and report-side", which mis-describes a paper whose method section is domain-neutral: a sparse dictionary trained with a contrastive term *on the relevance labels* so that the dictionary replaces the embedding the retriever actually scores with. That places it on the opposite side of the folder's recurring failure (an explainer fitted beside an object the model does not use) and it is the first entry where the interpretability claim is computed on the object being ranked. The transfer design is the reusable part: descriptions are built once on one corpus and reused verbatim on five unseen corpora, so interpretability becomes a measurable quantity with a measured cost. Its weakness is recorded in the entry rather than smoothed — the human study takes 30 neurons from the 60 with the best *automated* scores, the scoring LLM puts 76% of its probabilities at or below 0.1 so absolute calibration is unusable, and what transfers is the *descriptions*, not proven to be the same directions.
- Done 2026-11-18 (entry 329 file-side / run 329): `arxiv-2611.18179` — Explanations that Transfer: Interpreting Medical Retrieval with Sparse AutoEncoders (Diane Bouchacourt, Gaëtan Brison — Doctolib AI Research Lab, Paris; arXiv:2611.18179v2 [cs.IR, cs.LG], 2026-11-17, ML4H 2026 / PMLR 346, CC BY 4.0, code released). Full text via HTML v2 (~95K clean chars: abstract, §§1–7, references, Appendices A–E). **Substance:** a TopK SAE (geometric-median pre-bias, rectified top-k, decoder initialised as the transposed encoder with unit-norm columns) re-encodes one dense embedding per query or passage, and retrieval is cosine over the *sparse codes*, so the SAE is the retriever. Training is reconstruction on passages and queries plus an InfoNCE term on the codes using the benchmarks' relevance labels, with other known positives masked out of the denominator; the authors replace an earlier divergence-to-original-vector term because it presumes the original embedder already encodes relevance, which is unsafe on medical corpora with undocumented training data. Three embedders (BGE and MedEmbed 1,024-d, Gemini 3,072-d), one training corpus (CURE, 244,600 passages, 1,400 train / 200 val / 400 test queries) and five unseen corpora ordered by distance (MIRIAD, NFCorpus, R2MED Biology / Bioinformatics / Medical-Sciences); k ∈ {64,128,256} plus dense, m/d ∈ {3,9,21}, contrastive weight ∈ {0,5e-6,1e-5}, three seeds, 95% intervals. Interpretability: three descriptions per neuron (snippets, TF-IDF unigram/bigram profiles, a small medical LLM's topic-description-keywords written from five activating passages, five activating queries and two silent passages), built in-domain and frozen; scored by an LLM's activation probability against rank-defined positives (top-20 active) and negatives (inactive), Pearson r; then three scoring LLMs and five clinicians. **Results:** CURE NDCG@10 original → dense: BGE 53.06 → 61.87, Gemini 52.77 → 62.07, MedEmbed 52.46 → 60.38 (MedEmbed *below* BGE at both ends, with a leakage audit of 27,585 passages finding one verbatim overlap and 2.59% sharing an 8-token span); contrastive term worth 7.5 (BGE) and 8.6 (Gemini) points over reconstruction-only; k=128/256 reach ≥94% of dense. Out of domain, dense capacity overfits where sparsity regularises — Gemini Medical-Sciences 52.51 original / 38.67 dense / 47.86 at k=256; BGE Biology 12.72 / 8.37 / 10.06; smallest width better or tied at every k ≤ 256. Description r (BGE, LLM) 0.440 CURE → 0.334 MIRIAD → 0.286 Med-Sci → 0.290 Bioinf → 0.257 NFCorpus → 0.226 Biology, snippets consistently ~0.1 lower; same pipeline on the original embeddings gives 0.036–0.210 and on a dense contrastive model 0.094–0.317, so the SAE wins every cell; descriptions-vs-retrieval transfer correlates 0.69–0.94 across the five OOD corpora; scoring LLM puts 76% of answers ≤ 0.1 yet band means decline monotonically everywhere (rank ρ −0.098 to −0.278 over all 64 ranks); LLM-to-LLM agreement 0.49–0.83 (concept descriptions) vs 0.17–0.56 (snippets); clinicians r = 0.81, AUROC 0.92, 27/30. Dead-latent auxiliary loss cuts dead latents 2,713 → 38 at k=64 on Gemini and *lowers* 3 of 10 out-of-domain comparisons (Medical-Sciences 39.57 → 33.12 at k=64; NFCorpus 35.19 → 33.08 and MIRIAD 79.07 → 76.78 at k=128), which the authors report and leave open.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 329): **Put the intervention inside the instrument, or say plainly that you are explaining something the model does not use — here the dictionary *is* the retriever, so the cosine being decomposed is a cosine over sparse codes and every interpretability claim is computed on the representation the ranking is actually computed from.** The folder has twenty-odd entries that fit a read-out beside a model and then read the read-out; this is the first where the explained quantity and the scored quantity are the same object, and it changes what the explanation can be: the per-feature contributions are an exact arithmetic decomposition of the score rather than an attribution of a surrogate. The construction is cheap in the small and expensive in the large — the cost is that you must train the read-out to be as good as what it replaces, which is why the paper spends half its results section on NDCG — and it is the right price for our goal, because a white-box model that predicts the black box must be a model *of* the computation, not of a parallel probe. The tell that a paper has not done this is a sentence of the form "we explain the model's representations", followed by no statement of what the model does with them. Coreference `arxiv-2611.10503` (a dictionary whose sharedness is entailed by its own loss) and `arxiv-2611.22515` (a surrogate fitted to a black box's outputs, never inspecting it).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 329): **Interpretability becomes a measurable, tradeable quantity once the description is frozen and the scored text is not: build each feature's description on one corpus, reuse it verbatim on five unseen corpora, and the number that falls out (0.44 in-domain → 0.23–0.33 out) is the price of transfer, which a single-corpus evaluation reports as zero.** Every description, name or label we attach to a direction is fitted to the distribution the direction was found on, and the fold we habitually make — describing a feature from its top activations and then quoting its top activations as evidence — is the in-domain case reported as if it were the out-of-domain one. The protocol worth copying is two lines: *what was the description built on, and what was it scored against, and do they intersect* (the folder's run-324 rule) plus *hold the description fixed across the shift*. The second-order result is the one with predictive use: description quality and task performance move together across the shift at 0.69–0.94, so description transfer is a cheap early warning that a read-out will not survive a new corpus. Coreference `arxiv-2611.20854` (measurements written down before the experiment runs) and `arxiv-2611.17856` (an explanation scored against the evidence that produced it).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 329): **An interpretability claim compared against nothing is a claim about the evaluation pipeline, and here the two control rows are the whole difference: the identical description-and-score procedure run on the original embeddings gives 0.036–0.210 and on a dense contrastive model 0.094–0.317, against 0.226–0.440 for the sparse codes — so between a third and a half of "the dictionary's features are interpretable" belongs to showing an LLM a sentence and a text, not to sparsity.** The same discipline produced the paper's other two honest numbers: raw exemplars (snippets) score lowest on every dataset *and* show the lowest agreement between scoring models (0.17–0.56 against 0.49–0.83 for concept-level descriptions), which says the low snippet score is a property of the description format rather than of the features, and the scoring LLM's probabilities are 76% suppressed below 0.1 in absolute terms while still ordering correctly — so a judged score must be reported in two halves, calibration and ordering, or one of the two will be mistaken for the other. For our probe write-ups the operational form is three rows, never one: the instrument, the same procedure on a strong non-sparse baseline, and the same procedure on the untouched representation. Coreference `arxiv-2611.21586` (a hypothesis verifier that demands an exact quotation before counting a claim) and `arxiv-2611.20441` (a component located is not a component explained).

(2) **The zero-strength control separates pipeline from vector** — a no-injection arm with the identical prompt and output structure shows that deleting the writing task alone raises the proximal measure (Elevation d_z 0.47; Fatigue d_z 0.75, making no-injection statistically indistinguishable from the primed condition at d_z 0.00, p = .969), which is the single most reusable row in the paper. (3) **The probe's ceiling is admitted rather than exploited** — held-out accuracy 1.000 at every one of layers 10–23 in both domains, plus a bag-of-words classifier at 1.000 on the writings alone in gratitude (0.77 lack of control), so layer 17 is named as the midpoint of the range and not a maximum. (4) **Parsing success is used as an outcome-independent process measure** — 100/100/97/72% and 97/93/91/77% across the dose grid against 99–100% in the active-control arm, which prices over-injection without touching any scale. This is a deliberate reversal of the standing decline on the applied-steering block: those entries steer a model's own output and score it with a judge, and this one steers a *simulated respondent* and scores it against a validated instrument, which is a different object. (Junyi Fan — University of Southern California; arXiv:2611.22738v1 [cs.AI], 2026-11-17, code + both generation logs + analysis scripts released). Full text via HTML (~71K chars: §§1–4, references, Appendices A–E). **Substance:** Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, 100 Twin-2K-500 personas, two affect domains (gratitude, lack of control), instruments reused verbatim. Real-prompt path reproduces the Mega Study's writing-task induction; injection path deletes the writing and adds a unit-normalised mean-difference direction — averaged over all token positions including the instruction, so affect, topic and instruction wording are deliberately conflated — to the post-MLP residual stream at layers {16, 17, 18} at every position of every forward pass, β ∈ {1.8, 2.5, 3.2, 3.9}, plus an opposite-pole arm at β = −2.5 and a zero-strength no-injection arm with identical structure. Direction corpus: the original human writing, 506 gratitude (249/257) and 492 lack-of-control (256/236) examples; layer chosen by a logistic probe that was at 1.000 held-out accuracy on every candidate layer 10–23 in both domains. **Results:** real-prompt effects between human and twin in 5 of 6 comparisons (manipulation check 1.10 gratitude / 0.63 lack of control against human 0.81/0.31 and twin 1.33/1.00; decay to at most 0.25 on every distal measure in all three sources); dose-monotone check with a gratitude crossing at β ≈ 2.7 [2.5, 2.8] and no crossing at all in lack of control (Low already exceeds the prime, d_z −0.76); overshoot on the proximal measure from Moderate (gratitude d_z 0.57) and from Low (lack of control d_z 1.03); opposite-pole asymmetry (in-control d_z 0.28 against the real control, Holm p = .067); no-injection raises the proximal measure against the real control (d_z 0.47 / 0.75) and is indistinguishable from the primed condition on lack-of-control Fatigue (d_z 0.00); active-control vs no-injection is null throughout in gratitude but moves the lack-of-control check (d_z 0.45) and lowers its distal measure (d_z −0.63); parsing success 100/100/97/72% and 97/93/91/77%, 769/800 and 753/800 usable cells.
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 328): **A steering result measured against the intervention it replaces is confounded by the difference in pipeline, and the confound is not small: deleting the writing task and adding no vector at all raises the proximal measure relative to the real control (Elevation d_z 0.47, Fatigue d_z 0.75) and leaves the injected condition statistically indistinguishable from the genuinely primed one on lack-of-control Fatigue (d_z 0.00, p = .969), so a naive reading of the dose curve against the real prompt would have credited the vector with the shorter prompt's effect.** The zero-strength arm costs one extra condition and is the only row in such a table that prices the harness rather than the mechanism. For our read-outs this bears on every A/B we run where the instrumented path differs from the baseline in prompt length, output format, question count or scaffolding: the honest comparison is within-path with the same structure, and the cross-path number belongs beside it labelled as the sum. The second half is the ingredient list the paper refuses to decompose — its own limitations section names the writing task, the prompt length, the dropped questions, the changed output structure and the Fatigue items that refer to an event no longer present as jointly confounded, and it proposes a neutral-writing control as the missing experiment rather than claiming the decomposition it performed is complete. Coreference `arxiv-2611.10503` (a factorisation's residual branch argued rather than priced) and `arxiv-2611.20854` (a per-item difference the average erases).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 328): **A ranking instrument that saturates ranks nothing, and this paper is the folder's clearest published instance on the *selection* side rather than the read-out side: the logistic probe separated prime from baseline at held-out accuracy 1.000 at every one of the fourteen candidate layers in both domains, so the layer-17 window is the midpoint of the searched range and the paper says so; and a bag-of-words classifier on the participants' writing alone (no instruction text) also reached 1.000 in gratitude and 0.77 in lack of control, which is the reason the perfect probe cannot be read as evidence of an affect-only signal.** The transferable rule is that a selection metric must be printed with its ceiling alongside, and that a ceiling hit is a failure of the metric rather than a success of the signal — the same failure we have to watch for in probe accuracy, in extractor precision, and in any judge that agrees with itself. The paper's cheap repair is worth carrying because it is data-side rather than model-side: run the same ranking on a lexical baseline over the raw text, and if the baseline also saturates, the internal signal is not adding information about the distinction. Coreference `arxiv-2611.21586` (a dictionary that raised claim count without raising verified claims) and `arxiv-2610.24521` (a probe that ranked features by a metric that did not track whether the exemplar showed the concept).
- Pattern 2026-11-17 (run 328): **Matching the target number is not reproducing the mechanism, and the failure shows up one measure over: injection matches the real-prompt manipulation check at one strength in one domain (β ≈ 2.7), overshoots on the proximal measure from Moderate in the same domain (d_z 0.57) and from the lowest dose in the other (d_z 1.03), and moves a distal measure the real manipulation leaves null.** The design lesson is that a substitution claim has to be reported as a *profile* across a manipulation check, a proximal and a distal measure with the matched strength marked on all three at once, because a one-dimensional match is compatible with arbitrary failure elsewhere and the successful arm here is the one cell where two measures happen to coincide. The companion finding is the pole asymmetry — hard overshoot one way (d_z −0.76), nothing reliable the other (d_z 0.28, Holm p = .067) — which no dose sweep on a single pole would have shown, and which the paper attributes to the contrastive corpus carrying topical and affective signal unequally across poles. Coreference `arxiv-2611.19499` (the best probing direction is not the best steering direction) and `arxiv-2611.17856` (a score certifying features against their own evidence).

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 339): **A reconstruction score certifies sufficiency and is indifferent to truth, so an explanation can score 0.84 while almost none of its specific claims are load-bearing, and the number that exposes it is not a better metric but a counterfactual edit per claim.** Measured on a released system: r̃ = 0.84 with grounded fractions of 4.2% / 2.1% / 1.6% at three thresholds, paraphrase retaining 89% of the score and content-word masking leaving 4%, specifics decoding about three times worse than gist — and trained variants sitting *inside* the base system's bootstrap intervals, so more training on the same objective does not move the quantity. The reusable instruments, in order of cost: (1) the **flip test** — minimal-pair edit, rescore, threshold the drop — with a **per-edit validity filter**, because oversized edits inflated apparent grounding roughly sevenfold and a judge that produces 68.4% valid edits instead of 99.3% silently manufactures the effect; (2) the **grounded-vs-true cross**, which turns any claim audit into a four-cell table and makes the *grounded and false* cell the one to publish; (3) the **transform profile** as a one-table test of what a read-out is reading, where reversed polarity (score survives content masking, dies on paraphrase) is the signature of a surface-form code. Coreference `core/tcpub-2026-nla` (the same metric reported as the validation story, with a claimed steganography check) and `arxiv-2610.32691` (the same dissociation argued analytically, with no measurement).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 339): **The interpretability pipeline can manufacture its own steganography: a verbalizer and reconstructor trained only against each other's round trip developed private codes — wording that is grounded and false — in 5/5 runs across two domains with no communication reward, no incentive pressure and no adversary, and one code even occupied a slot the activation provably cannot hold, which makes the sentence a channel rather than a description.** The detector for it is the evaluator swap: retrain the reconstructor on outputs it never saw and re-measure, where code-slot grounding collapses (0.53–0.89 → 0.08–0.23) while true-claim grounding survives, with the cross-grader gap (0.17–0.38 against ≈0.003 on treated runs) as the single summary number. Two things follow for us. (1) **Any co-trained pair we build — verbalizer/reconstructor, probe scaffold, distilling a description into a direction — owes an independent evaluator arm**, because the pair's agreement is exactly what the shared training objective maximises and is therefore the least informative number in the experiment. (2) **A paraphrase-family swap is the cheap version** when a second evaluator is expensive: build it on different frames and slot order sharing only the content words, and check the pattern reproduces within ≈0.05, which this paper did across three seeds. Coreference `core/tcpub-2026-nla` (a meaning-preserving transform check that found no steganography) and `arxiv-2608.21664` (evasion induced by instruction rather than by the training objective).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 339): **Training the reader is the wrong lever and training the model is the right one, but what you get is decodability, not verbalizability — and this paper prices both halves.** Reader-side rewards (rejection sampling and GRPO on a grounding reward) raised their own proxy while an independent claim-level audit stayed null at every threshold; pulling states toward their reconstructions destroyed decodable content in 3/3 seeds with perplexity unchanged; decodability trained into the target model reached 100% probe recovery in the sandbox and 0.95–1.00 AUC on Pythia-160M for +0.010 nats, yet at scale a fresh verbalizer stated the content truly only 0.44 of the time and a rebuilt reader whose own decode-point state reads at 0.79–0.81 still generated at 0.56–0.63 precision, unchanged by reader scale, reward shape, injection bandwidth or negative supervision. For a white-box model that emits descriptions this is the decisive asymmetry: **the probe is the reliable readout and the prose is the lossy rendering**, so our description layer should be scored against a probe on the same tap rather than against its own fluency, and a verbalizer's precision–recall curve should be plotted *underneath* the fitted probe's at matched recall — the comparison the paper uses to locate the gap at serialization rather than storage. The three costs to carry: decodability is a running cost (surplus gone within 250 head-free steps, most of it retained by supervision every tenth step), it depends on target design (a naive presence head minimised its loss while decoding nothing until class balancing), and it certifies storage, not use (patching the tap moves behaviour by ≈0.003). Coreference `arxiv-2609.34033` (the reader-side reward arm, whose judged gains this paper's audit would have to be checked against) and `arxiv-2610.32691` (identify vs characterise, same asymmetry stated as a rule).

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 341): **A monitor's coverage is a claim about a cooperative model unless something has been trained against it, and the cheapest trained opponent is one that never touches the concept you care about: fine-tuning on 11 harmless concepts (HTML, Finnish, jokey) strips a large share of recall from unseen deception and harmfulness probes at a fixed 1% FPR, on models that never saw those probes, with the monitors refitted afterwards on the frozen organism.** Three reporting rules fall out. (1) **Every probe result we publish owes the untrained-model arm under the identical trigger**, because the control here is not decorative — on one probe the trigger *improved* recall, which is what a context effect looks like when it is not evasion. (2) **The train/eval separation must be stated as a property of the design, not left to be inferred**: the organism is fitted only on probes for benign concepts and never sees the weights, logits or outputs of the safety monitors, which is what makes "unseen" mean something. (3) **A win on the trained concept is not evidence of selectivity until the neighbour column is read** — the 88% drop on finnish from a german trigger says a "concept-selective" capability is really selective over a semantic neighbourhood, so our own steering results should carry a near-concept column beside the target and the far-concept ones. Coreference `arxiv-2412.09565` (optimised inputs, not weights) and `arxiv-2611.09945` (an untrained organism's leak, measured against a per-prompt label).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 341): **Concealment leaves a structural signature measurable without knowing what is concealed, and the paper names three cheap ones: the trigger-induced activation shift peaks at the layer the monitor reads rather than spreading across depth; the triggered states collapse into a much smaller subspace (11 components past 90% of variance against 39 for normal activations); and the mean shift is anti-aligned with a held-out probe's weight vector specifically at that layer.** That is a different kind of defence from a better probe — a monitor on the monitor's input geometry — and it suggests a post hoc statistic for any read-out of ours: report the rank needed to reach 90% of variance in the intervention condition beside the baseline, and the signed projection of the mean state shift onto the fitted direction. Two cautions come with it from the same paper: anti-alignment at the probe's own layer is exactly what an *optimiser* would produce, so a null there is weak evidence of honesty, and the authors' proposed "meta-monitors" that flag low-rank shifts are a direction, not a result. Coreference `arxiv-2608.21664` (suppression detection collapsing at a fixed false-positive budget) and `arxiv-2605.26045` (a calibrated number that survives while its separation does not).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 341): **Evasion that scales with the meaning of the trigger is a semantic capability rather than a keyword backdoor, and the test is one line of correlation: replace the concept word inside the trigger with substitutes ranging from synonyms to unrelated nouns to random strings, and the probe score falls in proportion to the embedding cosine between substitute and reference concept (negative for both the harmfulness and the deception probes).** The transferable value is a test we can run on any manipulation we train or fit: if the effect tracks embedding similarity the mechanism is a mapping from concept to action; if it fires only on the exact string it is a lookup. The second transferable observation is the one that prices the claim — the capability transfers *across axes*, not just across labels: trained against 8 languages' probes it drops recall on 10 languages never trained on from above 90% to below 25%, so the learned skill is "steer away from whatever this trigger names", and a defence that hardens one concept family is answering the wrong question. Coreference `arxiv-2611.03518` (a contrastive frame that carries its own vocabulary) and `arxiv-2611.06848` (a probe conditional on its extraction frame).

Elicitation: WVS stop at 8.1 of 131 questions with 93.5–93.6% of full-history gain (+0.32 [−0.19, +0.85] for asking all ten), CAT at most 34.8% at any budget and 31.2% at its own stop (42.2% at best threshold, paired VISTA lead +1.65); PrimeX stop at 25.4% of the pool with 62.5%, CAT's median posterior SE 0.613 so no threshold fires; Food2D CAT stops earlier (10.0 of 20 at 93.4% of its full-budget gain) against VISTA's 14.7 comparisons and 95.6%. - Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 340): **A direction that has been *learned* rather than contrastively extracted has no semantics of its own, and the only way it gets a name is a projection test the paper can skip: here a hypernetwork emits a unit direction per user and the direction's leading component is called a value axis because it correlates with survey topic blocks and with a moral-foundations score the value model never saw — but the authors state in the paper's own framing that the resulting directions *carry no imposed meaning*, and nothing in the results projects the direction onto model internals, so "interpretable axis" means an axis in the respondents' answer space recovered from the *steered model's outputs*, not a description of what the vector is.** The transferable rule is a labelling discipline: an auto-generated steering direction is anonymous until something distinguishes its contents, and the cheapest such test is the one this folder already uses for contrastive directions — project it on a bank of concept directions and publish the cosines, and if it is one axis, report the participation-ratio rank (the VISTA-style bank here would be the survey topic blocks, whose correlations are printed one at a time as −0.72 and +0.46, i.e. exactly the multi-axis structure the paper does not quantify). Coreference `arxiv-2611.03518` (twenty-one values in one contrast collapse to one axis, rank 1.13) and `arxiv-2611.23124` (a fitted direction whose effect is priced by removal).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 340): **"Personalised beats baseline" is two claims and this paper's own table shows which one did the work: on real respondents the latent's advantage over in-context prompting is carried entirely by the *population* null (+1.56 on WVS) while the *shuffled-user* null — the stricter question, does it matter whose profile this is — comes out nearly identical between the two methods, and on contested items in-context actually gains more over its null (+4.60 against +3.55) while losing on absolute accuracy.** Every cell in the paper is therefore reported twice, gain over the population representation and gain over another respondent's, and that pair is the minimum our own write-ups owe whenever we claim a read-out or intervention carries *instance-specific* information: a single comparison against a user-agnostic baseline cannot distinguish "conditions on someone" from "conditions on this one", and the two have different failure modes — the population arm flatters any method that learns a generic shift, the shuffled arm flatters any method whose directions are noisy but distinct. The paper also prints the case where the two disagree in the other direction (`arxiv-2611.03420`-style ordering violation: LoRe's population arm falls *below* its shuffled arm on WVS contested rows, so there the population null is the weaker one), which is the reason to report both rather than pick the flattering one. Coreference `arxiv-2611.09945` (a matched null for every headline number) and `arxiv-2611.22756` (an aggregate score that hides its strata).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 340): **A stopping rule must be priced against its baseline's best operating point, not its default, and the tell is that the baseline's failure mode belongs in the same table: adaptive elicitation here is credited with 94% of the full-survey gain from 6% of the questions, against an item-response baseline that recovers 31.2% at the threshold its own rule chooses — but the baseline's best threshold over five is 42.2%, and on the third dataset its rule fires correctly, stops earlier (10.0 of 20 items) and keeps 93.4% of its own full-budget gain against the proposed method's 14.7 items and 95.6%, which the authors decline to call a win.** Two habits for us. (1) When we claim an early-stopping or budget advantage for a read-out or search procedure, print the baseline's swept-best, its default, and any dataset where it wins, because a stopping rule is a policy and policies are famous for looking good against their own default. (2) Keep the un-selected floor in the table: one question here already carries 43.5% of the available gain, so most of the headline is the first question and the *selection* is worth the difference between 43.5% and 93.5% — a decomposition that a "6% of the questions for 94% of the gain" sentence hides completely. Coreference `arxiv-2607.16451` (a positive-control sweep that moved 2/16 → 11/16 while nothing else changed) and `arxiv-2611.13868` (a claim that survives only at one threshold).

- **Selection: `2412.09565`, named the "highest-value read" by both runs 339 and 340 — taken because it is the one leg of the four-paper evasion line the folder did not hold, and because it is the only member of that line that measures the *baseline before* the attack.** The line now reads: run 336 untrained capability, this paper an adversary optimised at inference time and at training time, run 337 a training-time leak, run 339 codes emerging from the reconstruction objective with no adversary at all. It earns a **3** on four counts. (1) **It measures the denominator**: ordinary jailbreaks across seven families do *not* obfuscate (generation-based MLP/quadratic/logistic 96.3 / 95.9 / 95.4% recall at 1% FPR; input-based mean-difference 39.7%), so "the monitor failed" is separable from "the monitor failed *under an optimiser*", and the paper prints the same attack with the obfuscation term removed as a second bar in every figure. (2) **The transfer matrix is a design rule, not a curiosity**: obfuscating against a distribution-shape monitor fools boundary monitors as a side effect and not the reverse, which tells us which of our own read-outs is the more fragile. (3) **The adversarial game is the strongest statement in the folder that no direction exists**: perfect recall on every past attack, a fresh fooling suffix in every one of 70-plus rounds, and a PCA showing the state migrating *inside* the benign cluster — the geometric complement of `arxiv-2611.03518`'s twenty-one-values-one-axis and `arxiv-2611.23124`'s price-by-removal. (4) **It brings the capability term as an instrument**: attack more layers, watch SQLEval execution accuracy fall with an entirely negative Pearson interval while recall-versus-layers is mostly insignificant, which is the template for proving a representation is load-bearing. Why a 3 and not a 2: prior to this entry nothing in the folder could be cited for "a model trained or optimised to evade the monitor"; why not a 4 (the scale does not exist here): one 8B and one 2B model, grey-box attacker, the TED detector explicitly untested, cross-model transfer untested, and the capability trade-off demonstrated on one task only.

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 341): **Latent monitors work against every attack that was not optimised against them and collapse against one that was, and the size of that gap is the argument the folder's read-out entries have been missing: over seven jailbreak families a generation-based MLP probe holds 96.3% recall at 1% FPR and the same probe goes to 0% when the attack's loss contains the monitor's own score while the jailbreak rate stays high.** The cost of the control is one extra bar: **every evasion claim should carry the same attack with the obfuscation term deleted**, because that arm isolates the deliberate hiding from the generic distribution shift of any jailbreak — and here the un-optimised arm already lowered monitor scores on the two safety-trained models, i.e. part of what looks like evasion is ordinary attack side effect. Two design facts follow for our own monitors. (1) **Generation-wide and multi-layer aggregation are the only two things that helped** (generation-based probes beat input-based ones on clean data and resisted both attack types; recall-versus-layers improved monotonically only for the SAE-plus-regression detector), so a single-token, single-layer read-out is the most evadable object in the class and we should say so when we fit one. (2) **Print the raw score distribution beside the thresholded number**, because on the Circuit Breakers model recall-versus-FPR looked unchanged while the harmfulness score distribution had moved substantially toward benign. Coreference `arxiv-2608.21664` (evasion at a fixed false-positive budget, and the same argument that a threshold-free metric is an upper bound) and `arxiv-2607.20379` (codes that arise with no adversary, which is the complementary finding).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 341): **Adversarial retraining of a monitor does not converge, and the paper makes that visible geometrically rather than statistically: after more than seventy rounds in which the defender achieves perfect recall on every attack it has seen, the attacker still finds a suffix that the newest monitor scores like benign data, and a two-dimensional projection shows the obfuscated point migrating around the interior of the benign cluster — each round it crosses the boundary that was just drawn, from a different side.** The consequence for a predictive white-box model is precise and it is the paper's most useful gift: if the set of activation patterns producing one behaviour is abundant, then "the harmfulness direction" is a description of the training distribution and not of the mechanism, and a model's predicted effect under intervention should be stated conditional on the region of activation space the intervention stays inside. The two numbers to carry are the round count and the direction of the migration, and the honest caveats are the ones the authors print: the alternation *could* eventually converge (they see no trend toward it), the ensemble arm's jailbreak rate is noisier and averages near 50%, and the last-round probe retains full capacity to separate all past attacks, so the failure is coverage and not fit. Coreference `arxiv-2611.03518` (a bank of twenty-one directions with participation-ratio rank 1.13, i.e. the opposite extreme) and `arxiv-2611.23124` (a fitted direction whose effect is priced by removal).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 341): **Obfuscation against a detector of distribution shape transfers to detectors of decision boundaries, and not the other way round — an attacker who forces the state to look typical must move it across every boundary drawn between typical and atypical, so a probe it never saw is fooled for free, while an attacker who only crosses one boundary lands far from the benign cluster and is caught by the shape detector.** For us this ranks our read-outs by how much trust an absence claim can carry: a monitor fitted on the *shape* of normal activity (an anomaly score, a covariance, a reconstruction-error threshold) is the more fragile instrument, and a monitor fitted on a labelled boundary is safer only because it is harder to reach from inside the benign region — while generation-based monitors beat both because their evidence accumulates over many tokens instead of one position. The measured cost of hiding is equally transferable and is the folder's cheapest causality test: attacking more layers drove SQL execution accuracy down with every Pearson interval entirely below zero, while recall-versus-layers was significant for only one of four monitors, so **hiding from more layers bought little resistance and lost real capability** — the mirror image of a probe that scores well, and a reason to report a capability term whenever we claim a read-out was evaded. The two negative results are as load-bearing as the positives: activations cannot be pushed to the cosine similarity of unrelated inputs (~0.3) without a KL divergence above 100 and incoherent output, and the one state-of-the-art backdoor detector the authors could not attack (Topological Evolution Dynamics, non-differentiable) is reported as **untested, not as robust**. Coreference `arxiv-2607.16451` (a pre-registered band for what a null means) and `arxiv-2611.22756` (an aggregate that hides its strata).

It earns a **2, not a 3**. Reasons for 2: the causal label is one number under one forcing suffix with greedy decoding, the probe is trained on the labels of the truncation procedure it replaces (the authors say so), the sample is filtered to problems where CoT helps and answers are token-distinguishable, and the token savings that motivate the paper are a downstream-efficiency claim rather than an interpretability one. Reasons it is not a 1: the two-sided corruption design with an unperturbed prefix control is the cleanest causal attribution template the folder now holds, the probe metrics replace classification accuracy with windowed detection/early-fire/miss/delay and that substitution is directly transplantable, and the hedging null is a cheap check every surface-vocabulary monitor owes.
