early exit MATH-500 fixed 80% → 57% against probe 89% of accuracy at 39% savings (k = 1) and 98% at 26% (k = 5), OOD savings 25 / 6 / 35% with at most 11 points lost (ZebraLogic 97% → 86%).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 343): **A model's answer is fixed long before its reasoning text stops moving, and the cheap way to prove it is to truncate the trace instead of perturbing it: re-running the model on growing prefixes of its own chain-of-thought with an answer-forcing suffix gives a per-sentence confidence curve that is bimodal, one sentence supplying a median 4.6× the confidence rise of the next-largest (95% CI 4.3–4.9), with 13–23% of the tokens preceding commitment in one family and 43–68% in another and up to 87% of the trace generated after the answer was settled.** What makes the result citable rather than another aggregate is the mirror-arm corruption test: at 20% numeric corruption the pre-boundary prefix keeps the answer in 61% of AIME traces against 95% for the post-boundary tail, the unperturbed prefix reproduces the full answer on every retained trace, and the paper refuses to report the survival above the boundary without the survival below it. Two habits transfer immediately. (1) **Every "this part is redundant" claim owes its mirror** — the measurement is a ratio between two interventions on the same traces, and the arm that is reported alone is uninterpretable. (2) **The construction also yields an instance-level label for free**: "the prefix produces the same answer as the full trace" is a per-example ground truth that costs *n* + 1 forward passes and no training, which is the cheapest per-prompt truth in the folder and can score any read-out we fit against it. Coreference `arxiv-2611.09945` (a manufactured marker as the only per-instance truth) and `arxiv-2607.16451` (answer-commitment measured behaviourally with a small n).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 343): **When a claim is about *where* something happens, classification accuracy is the wrong instrument, and this paper's replacement is the metric set worth copying: it reports detection within a *k*-step tolerance window, early-fire rate (predicting the event before it occurs), miss rate, exact-boundary rate at *k* = 0, median detection delay, and the fraction of tokens the prediction would actually save — because a probe that is 92% accurate per sentence can still fire in the wrong place.** The reported per-model profile is exactly what such a table should look like, including its worst cell rather than a pooled mean: 92 / 62 / 98% in-distribution detection against 6 / 16 / 2% early fire and 0 / 25 / 0% miss, with the middle model failing a quarter of the time, and the out-of-distribution ranges printed as min–max across three held-out benchmarks rather than averaged. The second half of the pattern is that the same probe is used as an *intervention* (stop generation at its predicted position) and the intervention is what prices the read-out: probe-mediated exit beats fixed-percentage truncation at every operating point (MATH-500 fixed 80% → 57% against probe 89% of accuracy at 39% tokens saved), which is a read-out audited by its consequence rather than its AUC. Coreference `arxiv-2608.21664` (detection at a fixed false-positive budget rather than a threshold-free score) and `arxiv-2611.22756` (an aggregate score that hides its strata).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 343): **The vocabulary of deliberation does not carry the deliberation: sentence-initial markers such as "wait", "but", "check" or "let's" are about as frequent on the committed side of the boundary as on the uncommitted side, and no marker shifts consistently across the three models — with Qwen3-14B beginning roughly 12% of its sentences with "but" at similar rates before and after the point where the answer is provably already fixed.** This is a text-side twin of the folder's state-versus-description entries and the sharpest available argument against a CoT monitor built on hedging cues: the same surface signal occurs on both sides of a boundary that a corruption test shows is real, so such a cue cannot be a proxy for "still thinking". The constructive half of the same finding is that *the trace's own length and its mid-guess structure* do carry information (traces with mid-guesses are more than twice as long, 688 ± 57 versus 306 ± 24 tokens, and mid-guess values recur across independent samples of the same question at a median Jaccard of 0.71), so a monitor should count distinct confident hypotheses and revisions rather than count hedging words. The authors also warn that "epiphenomenal" is a statement about the elicited answer only — the tail may calibrate confidence or serve training-time objectives — so a null on the answer is not a null on function. Coreference `goodfire-com-research-reasoning-theater` (a monitor that cannot exceed the trace it reads) and `anthropic-2026-claude-fable-5-mythos-5-system-card` (a state probe-detectable and causally active but absent from the dictionary).

- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 345): **Two importance measures applied to the same traces can rank different step types first, and the disagreement is the measurement: the standard forced-answer baseline credits active computation, while resampling and receiver-head attention both credit planning and uncertainty management — because interrupting a model late in a correct chain hands it the answer, so sentences that *generate* the plan look unimportant and sentences that *execute* it look central.** The consequence for us is a paired-baseline rule for any step-, sentence- or clause-level attribution: publish the baseline that names the competing unit alongside the construct we prefer, and interpret the gap rather than only the ranking, because a single importance ranking is a ranking only relative to its interruption protocol. The paper's own cleanest example is worth carrying whole — the pivotal sentence is a one-line plan to convert to decimal (resample it and accuracy collapses; interrupt at it and nothing changes) — and the general lesson is that an attribution method's blind spot is usually the mechanism it presupposes, here that importance is what the final answer depends on rather than what fixes the trajectory. Coreference `arxiv-2507.05246` (a strategy recovered by pre-filling rather than ablating) and `arxiv-2611.13868` (responsibility conditional on the intervention data).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 345): **An intervention whose replacement is semantically identical to the original measures nothing, and the price of fixing it is one filter plus its retention rate: this paper defines counterfactual importance as the KL between answer distributions with and without a sentence, restricted to resamples whose embedding cosine to the original falls below the dataset median (0.8), and reports that the unrestricted version inflates sentences the context fully determines — with plan generation and uncertainty management producing semantically different replacements far more often than active computation or problem setup.** This is the natural-language twin of the contrastive-pair retention filter the folder recorded for direction banks, and it transfers to any read-out we build by substitution (masking a clause, swapping a prompt segment, replacing a document): state the dissimilarity threshold, say how many substitutions survived it, and note that the conditional estimate is high-variance when fewer than ten divergent replacements exist. The second half of the filter is the diagnostic — the resampling transition matrix shows that uncertainty-management and active-computation sentences are usually replaced by their own category while plan and fact sentences are not, i.e. overdetermination is itself a per-category property, which is the kind of stratifier the folder keeps finding it should print. Coreference `arxiv-2611.03518` (a retention filter whose cost was printed) and `arxiv-2611.09945` (a matched null for every headline number).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 345): **A causal claim about a component has to be priced against a control matched on the confound the paper has already admitted, and here that control is layer-matched random ablation: receiver heads cluster in late layers, so the comparison ablates the same number of heads from the same layers, and the effect only appears at 512 heads (27.7% versus 37.3% accuracy, p = .02) while at 256 heads the two arms are indistinguishable (48.8% versus 52.7%) — so the claim is true at one strength and false at another, and the paper prints both.** Two habits follow. (1) **Match the control on whatever the paper's own limitation section admits** — position here, depth there — because a random baseline that shares the confound measures nothing, and the admission in the limits section names the control the reader should demand. (2) **Report the effect at more than one intervention strength**, since a component's share of a computation is a function of how much of the network is removed and a single strength invites the reader to generalise a coincidence. The third transferable item is cheap and unusual: the same paper validates its cheap white-box measure (attention suppression, ~100× cheaper than resampling) against the expensive black-box one and prints the agreement (mean r = .20, .34 at short range, positive in 90% of traces) — a model for how to license a shortcut, and a reminder that a correlation of .20 is being offered as support for a proxy, which is honest and worth copying in that spirit rather than as a threshold. Coreference `arxiv-2608.21664` (a measure pair that disagree because one is thresholded) and `arxiv-2611.22756` (an aggregate score that hides its strata).

Elson, Rif A. Saurous, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Heng Chen, Irhum Shafkat, Rohin Shah — Google DeepMind; arXiv:2507.05246v1 [cs.AI, cs.CL], 2025-07-07, 2,450 KB source, CC BY 4.0, code note in Appendix B.3 prompt templates). (4) *RL* — `factorize_derivative`, 3,013 (k, P) pairs with 768 held out, k ∈ [2,5], roots integer in [−5,5], degree ≤ 10, reward +4 correct / −2 monitor fired, 10,000 policy-gradient steps at batch 128. **Numbers, as printed:** hint effect above the no-hint baseline under the simple hint and gone under the complex one (direction of effect, quoted from the figure caption and §3.1, not digitised); GPQA ordinary-CoT accuracy ~80% (2.0 Flash) and 88% (2.5 Pro, native reasoning disabled — 91% with it enabled, per Appendix C.3); monitor recall 0.95–0.98 and FPR 0.05–0.09 across the four pairings; RL before → after: 69.8 ± 1.7% correct / 81.8 ± 1.4% triggered / reward +0.23 ± 0.10 → 94.4 ± 0.9% / 19.5 ± 1.4% / +4.77 ± 0.08, optimal trajectory 0.5 ± 0.3% → 74.9 ± 1.6%; factorise-early applicable on 50.9% of initial states; key-coefficient sufficiency 98.8% (train) / 99.7% (test); three transition regions at ~1,000 steps, 2,000–3,000 steps, and the final ~3,000 steps; 21 checkpoints × 768 = 16,128 analysed test episodes; pre-filled-trace probe: ~80% recovery with a corrupted middle coefficient after training against a large drop for the second and final coefficients, with ~3% of prefixed roll-outs filtered for backtracking.
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 344): **A faithfulness failure can be a property of the task rather than of the model, and the paper's own replication is the control that proves it: the same hint that models once followed silently becomes fully attributable the moment following it requires four arithmetic operations, and a planted wrong intermediate step that easy problems ignore becomes an answer hardening on hard ones — because a task that exceeds what one forward pass can do cannot be completed without writing the steps down.** The generalisation for us is a *necessity screen* to run before any read-out null is reported: construct the same probe at a difficulty where the state must be verbalised and at one where it need not be, and only then interpret the gap. It also gives the folder the cleanest statement of why our two nulls (run 337's evasion, run 338's unreachable question) are not the same kind of result — one suppressed a state the model had, the other asked about a state the model never needed to form. Coreference `arxiv-2611.09945` (an organism that verbalises 0.3% of the time while leaking a marker) and `arxiv-2607.16451` (an answer fixed before the reasoning starts).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 344): **Evasion results are only meaningful jointly with the cost of evading, and this paper's plots are built so that the two cannot be separated — every attacker is reported at (task success, monitor recall) rather than at recall alone, and the RL curve is reported as a joint rise in accuracy and fall in triggers.** The assistance ladder that goes with it is the second half: situational awareness alone moves nothing, hand-written strategies move it a little at real accuracy cost, iterative optimisation finds working prompts, and only training produces a generalisable strategy — so a single "the monitor can be fooled" claim without a rung on that ladder is uninterpretable, and the right number to publish is the rung, not the yes. The third element is the most useful for our own threat model: the evasive behaviour that generalises *only* appeared after training against a weak monitor and *failed* to appear when training began against a symbolic checker, which is a concrete demonstration that monitor quality and attacker curriculum interact non-monotonically. Coreference `arxiv-2512.11949` (unseen monitors lose recall against trained organisms) and `arxiv-2608.21664` (suppression that needs no fine-tuning at all).
- Pattern 2026-11-18 (run 344): **A strategy recovered from behaviour can be turned into a causal claim by pre-filling the trace rather than by ablating the model: hold the entire derivation fixed, corrupt exactly one coefficient of the intermediate polynomial, sample the completion, and the position of the error is now the only thing that varies — errors in middle coefficients are recovered about 80% of the time after training while errors in the two coefficients that determine the roots still break the answer.** For our read-outs the transfer is direct: when a fit captures *where* something is rather than *whether* it is there, the test is to synthesise the input that isolates the position and let the model continue, not to remove components and hope the effect localises. The companion finding is the difficulty-dependent pattern that made the targeted mistakes possible (98.8% / 99.7% of items determined by two coefficients), which is a reminder that a learned evasion is often a learned reading of the *task distribution* — the model found a shortcut the environment's design made available, and the authors say they did not design it in on purpose. - Pattern 2026-11-19 (run 404): **Squared error cannot tell a shrunk predictor from a noisy one, and the fix is one scalar: fit the single multiplicative factor that best rescales a read-out's output back onto the target, report it beside the error, and the sign of the bias becomes a number — here the factor is computable in closed form from three running means (mean squared reconstruction, mean squared input, mean squared error) and tracked during training, and it separates the two architectures cleanly: gated dictionaries sit at about 1.0 at every site while L1-trained dictionaries fall to roughly 0.72-0.80 on attention outputs and 0.86-0.90 on MLP outputs, worsening as the penalty rises.** The deeper point is that the bias is a property of the *objective*, not of the fit: a penalty on coefficient magnitude is not a penalty on the number of active units, so the cheapest way to satisfy it is to under-report every coefficient, and no amount of extra capacity fixes that. For our own accounts the operational version is a three-row table for every read-out and every substitute model — mean squared error, the optimal rescaling factor, and the error left after rescaling — because the last number is the part of the error that is genuinely noise and the difference is the part that a careless objective manufactured. Coreference `arxiv-2506.23845` (the information bound that makes residual error a ceiling rather than a nuisance) and `arxiv-2405.08366` (a dictionary priced against a supervised reference rather than against itself).
- Pattern 2026-11-19 (run 404): **The control the folder keeps needing has a name now: fix the symptom, hold the mechanism — and the gap between that arm and the treatment is the share of the effect the stated mechanism actually explains.** Here the symptom is a known bias (magnitudes under-reported), so the rival freezes a baseline dictionary's encoder and decoder directions and learns only a rescaling and shift on top; it does repair the bias and adds almost nothing to reconstruction fidelity, while the full method gains much more — so the bias was real and the repair was not what produced the improvement, which came instead from learning better directions. Without that third arm the paper's own headline would have been read as "fixing shrinkage is worth half the sparsity", which the authors can show is false. This is the same shape as the kernel-projection row in `arxiv-2311.17030` and the random-projection arm in `arxiv-2006.00995`, reached from the training side rather than the intervention side, and it belongs in our account tables for any claim of the form "component X is important because removing it hurts": the honest middle arm removes X's *function* while leaving everything else frozen, and only the excess of the real intervention over that arm is evidence for the mechanism. Coreference `arxiv-1911.03429` (the random arm that prices whether a score means anything) and `arxiv-2403.19647` (faithfulness and completeness as one instrument read both ways).
- Pattern 2026-11-19 (run 404): **A pooled comparison can hide a partition that carries the entire effect, and here the pooled human study is a near-null (p = .060, interval touching zero) while the MLP-output partition alone is decisive (mean .40, p = .003) and the attention-output and residual-stream partitions show nothing at all — so the correct reading is not "no difference" but "the difference lives at one site".** This is the third entry in the folder where an average swamps a partition (the per-label POS breakdown in `arxiv-2006.00995`, the opposite-direction layer counts in `arxiv-1704.05796`), and the cheapest discipline is the one adopted here: pre-register the partition (model, layer, site, rater), pair on it, and print the per-partition intervals beside the pooled one. The second transferable detail is the ablation study's negative result — untied encoder paths, strictly more expressive and 50% larger, do *not* beat the tied ones — which is a reminder that a capacity increase which buys nothing is evidence that the constraint being relaxed was never binding, and is worth one line in any account that credits a design choice.

- Pattern 2026-11-19 (run 413): **An intervention claim needs two numbers, not one, and the pair is completeness against selectivity — the folder's first instrument that can tell "the direction did nothing" apart from "the direction did the right thing and a great deal else", which previously both arrived as a zero or as a suspiciously large effect.** The design detail that makes it work is the arbiter: validation probes are trained on data disjoint from the interventional probes' data and with the two properties made statistically independent, then handed the *edited* embedding instead of letting the model consume it, so the verdict is about the edit rather than about downstream behaviour. Two habits for our tables: print the pair with the harmonic mean as the scalar (their reliability, chosen by analogy to F1 precisely because a do-nothing intervention scores perfect selectivity and a maximal one perfect completeness), and print the non-targeted property's reading even when it is uninteresting, because selectivity is the column that catches collateral damage and it is the one no intervention entry in the folder currently reports. Coreference `arxiv-2402.12560` (a random-direction floor making expressivity and finding separable) and `arxiv-2006.00995` (decodable, necessary and sufficient as three columns rather than a ladder).
- Pattern 2026-11-19 (run 413): **A method compared at one hyperparameter is a comparison of two arbitrary points on two different curves, and here the sweeps are the evidence: every method's strength dial traces a monotone trade-off in every model and every layer, so a ranking at a fixed strength is partly an artefact of where the strength was fixed.** The paper's answer is to take each method's best-reliability setting — which flatters every method but at least flatters each on its own terms — and to print the curve anyway in the appendix. The reversal is what prices the warning: AlterRep is the most reliable method on BERT (0.835, best in its last three layers) and the least reliable in the late layers of Pythia-1.4B and 6.9B, so the same instrument gets three different verdicts from three architectures — the lesson run 412 reached from the weight side, where a spectral statistic was the best discriminator in one family and mid-pack in another. For us the operational rule is that any steering-vector or direction comparison prints the strength axis, the aggregation rule that picked the operating point, and at least one second architecture's verdict on the same dial; a scalar difference between two methods is otherwise a summary of two sweeps we have not shown. Coreference `arxiv-2402.12560` (max-over-regions-then-mean-over-layers as an aggregation choice that changes the ranking) and `arxiv-2602.15195` (the same per-architecture instability in a spectral detector's feature table).
- Pattern 2026-11-19 (run 413): **A linear edit at the output layer is licensed by the output layer's geometry, not by the model's, and the paper's own framing is the cleanest statement of that trap available: the nonlinear-over-linear reliability gap appears in all six models and all layers and survives the linear-validation-probe control, with BERT's last three layers the single exception — read by the authors as output-discriminative information being made linearly separable at the end and nowhere else.** That is exactly the error a white-box model would inherit from a probe that works: a direction that separates a concept in the final residual stream can be a property of the layer that feeds the classifier rather than of the computation that produced it, and the diagnostic is to re-run the same read-out with a nonlinear arbiter, then repeat it at an intermediate layer where the arbiter is also asked to stay silent about a property you did not target. The honest asymmetry is worth keeping too: they call the linearity claim a conjecture and say their result does not refute the linear representation hypothesis, only that final-layer linearity need not generalise — the phrasing our own claims about weight-derived directions should adopt. Coreference `arxiv-2404.16014` (per-architecture and per-layer structure hidden by an aggregate number) and `arxiv-2512.18792` (the overdetermination argument: a working read-out is not thereby the mechanism).

- Pattern 2026-11-19 (run 442): **Additivity of feature effects is now an order-indexed measured property rather than a binary assumption, and the price of assuming it is small in magnitude but real in consequence: order-1 residual was positive in all 57 model/layer/behaviour cells while sitting around 0.02-0.08 of behavioural variance, and yet the residual predicted fidelity — rank fidelity fell and selection regret rose monotonically across the lowest-to-highest residual decile in all three main models, with prompt-level correlation between residual and rank fidelity negative in 17 of 18 settings.** This is the quantitative version of something the folder has asserted since its early attribution entries: that a set of individually meaningful features need not compose. The reusable part is the shape, not the numbers — fit the interaction order on sampled coalitions, evaluate on held-out coalitions, and report the residual as a fraction of intervention-game variance, which is scale-free and comparable across sites, models and behaviours. For our accounts: any claim that a feature set explains a behaviour ships with the order it was validated at and the residual at the next order down, and any intervention recipe assembled from separately-measured components carries the measured joint-versus-sum gap. Coreference `arxiv-2610.17898` (importance and directional faithfulness coming apart — the same "the parts being individually right does not make the combination right" structure) and `arxiv-2610.15850` (observational statistics not licensing a statement about the edit).
- Pattern 2026-11-19 (run 442): **The rotation control here is the cleanest form of a baseline the folder keeps reinventing, and the paper shows exactly how to build it: take an orthogonal Q satisfying Q·1 = 1 on the selected subspace — QR-factorise a Gaussian matrix on the orthogonal complement of the normalised all-ones vector — so the subspace, the total contribution and the downstream model are all fixed and only the coordinate system changes.** Learned SAE coordinates won in all 18 settings, and the paired statistic is not the residual ratio but the fraction of prompts whose SAE estimate fell below the median of eight per-prompt rotations, which is a distribution-free check needing no assumption about the residual's shape. The same move was then run at every layer to split the depth trend into a part shared with rotations (8 of 9) and a part specific to the basis (33 of 33 matched sites), which is how a trend gets attributed to its cause rather than merely observed. For us this is the standing control for any claim that a basis is better: probe basis versus rotated probe basis, learned dictionary versus a random rotation of its span, reported as a paired per-prompt win fraction. Coreference `arxiv-2305.01610` (the random-basis rotation applied to sparsity curves, equally decisive there) and `arxiv-1610.01644` (the untrained-network baseline — the same idea applied to training instead of to the basis).
- Pattern 2026-11-19 (run 442): **Reconstruction quality and behavioural compositionality are measurably different properties, established across six matched SAEs at one site rather than argued from one dictionary: residual correlated positively with sign error (0.269 to 0.430) and selection regret (0.199 to 0.235) in all three behaviours, while reconstruction error was near zero or of the wrong sign.** That is the folder's third independent instance of an instrument reading fine while the thing it is supposed to license misfires, and it puts a concrete prohibition on a shortcut our own evaluations could take — reconstruction loss must not stand in for whether a dictionary is usable for prediction. Two smaller items travel with it. First, the ordering metric and the magnitude metric disaggregate: from order 1 to order 2 rank fidelity barely moved (mean 0.9782 to 0.9959) while selection regret fell fivefold and sign error roughly halved in every cell, so a high rank correlation says nothing about whether the best coalition is the one selected — report regret and sign error beside any rank statistic. Second, the paper prints a negative pairwise share where finite-sample fitting error exceeds the structural gain (three of fourteen MMLU-Pro domains) and explicitly labels it a sampling artefact rather than clipping it to zero, which is the reporting convention to copy for any held-out estimator whose two components are separable. Coreference `arxiv-2410.10811` (unlearned readers matching learned ones) and `arxiv-2410.14670` (a residue the instrument cannot see, so absence needs a blind-spot statement).

- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 493): **The intervention that makes a causal abstraction worth having is the one whose predicted outcome is a value belonging to neither run, and this paper's whole argument rests on that single cell: patching the answer *pointer* from a counterfactual that reorders the states redirects the model to the other state of the *original* story — an answer present in neither the original nor the counterfactual run — whereas patching the answer *payload* yields the counterfactual's state.** Identity patching, which is what most of our read-out batteries report, cannot distinguish a copied value from a reference, because both reproduce the original output under an identity swap; only a swap that separates the two produces different predictions, and they land in different layer bands here (pointer 34–52, payload past 56, which is also how the paper assigns a direction to its own pipeline). For our accounts the requirement is now explicit: **every variable we name owes at least one intervention whose predicted output is neither the original nor the counterfactual** — a conjunct of two pointers for a bound pair, a re-referenced index for an address, a swapped addend for an arithmetic composition. If no such intervention can be written for a "variable", it is a feature detector rather than a variable in a computation, and the account should say so. Coreference `arxiv-2408.15510` (interventions judged on completeness *and* selectivity, the two-number certificate) and `arxiv-2610.21261` (a coalition game whose order-1 residual is the price of assuming parts compose).
- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 493): **A null band in the middle of a layer sweep is evidence that the mechanism is a matched pair, not evidence of no effect, and the paper shows the repair: intervening only on the recalled token or only on the lookback token leaves interchange-intervention accuracy at chance between layers 24 and 31 for the *same* mechanism that aligns from layer 10 onward when both sides are intervened at once.** The reasoning is structural and transfers intact — when a mechanism is a conjunction of an address stored in one place and a pointer stored in another, a single-sided patch necessarily creates a mismatch at exactly the layers where the pair is separated, so the null is generated by the probe rather than found in the model. This is the correction to a habit our patching batteries have: a mid-stack dip has repeatedly been read as "nothing happens here", and the honest sentence is "nothing happens here *under a single-sided intervention*". Two cheaper consequences follow. First, print the both-sided arm beside the one-sided arms in every sweep, because the gap between them *is* the localisation of the addressing scheme. Second, a source-reference intervention that should leave the output unchanged unless a downstream token's residual stream is frozen is the same lesson in another form — the unchanged output is not a failed intervention, it is the control proving the address is what the pointer dereferences.
- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 493): **A representation whose content is rank abstracted away from identity is testable by intervening on tokens that share surface form and differ only in the hypothesized variable, and that is the crispest validation recipe the folder holds for a found variable: ordering IDs say whether a character, object or state is the first or second of its type, they live in a low-rank subspace of the token's residual stream, and the experiment swaps the subspace between two occurrences of the *same word* so that token identity cannot account for the effect.** Two generalizations. (a) Wherever we claim a variable, construct a minimal pair whose inputs are identity-identical and variable-different — the same token in two positions, the same word in two bindings, the same prompt with one index changed — because any read-out that survives an identity swap is a lexical feature. (b) The paper's own weight-side check is the shape our project wants: project each attention head's query and value weight block onto the identified causal subspace and rank heads by the projection norm, which turns an interpretation into a statement about matrices that can be audited without running the model at all. One honest warning travels with it — the same variable was found in *different* subspaces in CausalToM and in BigToM, the semantics transferred while the coordinates did not, which is the strongest evidence in the folder that a subspace found on one distribution is not a portable object.

**(ii)** Appendix B.3 reports >99% recall at 1% FPR for the follow-up probe while §4.2 describes that same probe's performance as "comparable" to the roleplaying probe, which is a much weaker claim than the appendix's table — the entry reports the appendix numbers and notes the tension.
- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 501): **A probe shipped as a monitor must be calibrated before it is evaluated, and the calibration is a percentile of a control distribution, not a property of the probe: fixing the threshold at the 99th percentile of 9,994 responses to unrelated conversational queries converts a separation score into "what fraction of this model's own lies would we have caught if one in a hundred innocent messages raised a flag".** The distinction is not cosmetic — the same probe reads 0.964-0.999 on within-dataset AUROC (a statement about the activations) and 95-99% recall at 1% FPR (a statement about a deployment stream), and the paper reports both because they answer different questions. For our white-box accounts this is the closest thing the folder has to a reporting contract for any read-out we propose to *use*: publish the control corpus, where the threshold came from, and the fraction missed at that threshold, and keep the threshold frozen while the evaluation sets are scored. The companion control, which costs one extra dataset, is the **incentive-only** comparison — honest responses to prompts where lying would pay versus honest responses to matched prompts where it would not — and here it is what proves the probe is partly answering "is this a deception-shaped situation" rather than "is this response deceptive". Coreference `arxiv-2603.18353` (a probe at 0.982 AUROC with no usable handle: same information-versus-control gap, measured on the intervention axis instead) and `arxiv-2503.11926` / `arxiv-2512.18311` (the monitorability line, where the monitor's operating point is the subject).
- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 501): **Where the training set has no real deception in it, the probe learns the scenario rather than the act — and the paper's own A/B makes this visible: a probe trained on instructed pairs generalises to new deception settings while a probe trained on the model's own perfectly-separated roleplaying responses does worse out of distribution, especially against controls, because in training data where deception is always incentivised the scenario-level feature carries no label variance and so is never learned.** Two transfers. (a) For our read-out batteries, the generalisation-relevant control is not the same-distribution held-out split but a **matched negative stream where the target is absent but the context invites it** — that is the only split that separates "detects the state" from "detects the topic". (b) When a proxy instrument disagrees in *direction* with the published result it imitates (the yes/no pair firing reversed here, because honest responses in these datasets are confessions), the disagreement is a fact about the dataset and not about the probe, and the paper's explanation is worth copying as a diagnostic habit: check what the positive class actually contains before trusting the sign. Coreference `arxiv-2506.19143` (two importance measures ranking different step types first — the same lesson on the attribution axis) and `arxiv-2410.14670` (an instrument whose blind spot must be stated rather than assumed absent).
- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 501): **A sensitive threshold metric is not a stable metric, and the paper prints the instability instead of hiding it: moving the probe two layers later left AUROC for honest-versus-deceptive separation respectable while driving recall at 1% FPR to nearly zero on both insider-trading sets, and adjacent layers differ substantially.** The lesson for anything we report at a fixed operating point is that its variance across a nuisance dimension (layer, seed, site, corpus) is part of the result — a recall-at-budget number quoted without a sweep is a point estimate on an axis nobody has perturbed. It also re-prices a habit already in the folder: probe-site choices imported from a predecessor model (here layer 22, selected on Llama-3.1 and reused on 3.3) are hyperparameter carry-over, acceptable only when a sweep is printed beside them. Coreference `arxiv-2603.18353` (the missing random-direction control at the strength where the headline appears) and `arxiv-2605.31317` (an aggregate number that hides its per-stratum spread).

- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 502): **A localization claim is only checkable once the dataset is a declared part of it, and the paper's own numbers show why: the same path set scores 55.2% on the full distribution, 48.6%-level behaviour on the induction subset where its AUE is 0.219 against an ATE of 0.907, and fails on the uncommon-repeats subset where AUE 0.777 sits against ATE 1.444.** The authors make this a rule rather than an observation — behaviour is defined as input-output pairs on a specific dataset, and the paper's own warning is that a narrow explanation's evidence is not evidence for a broader one. Two consequences for us. (a) Any read-out or circuit claim in our accounts carries three fields, not one: the path/component set, the distribution it was scored on, and the counterfactual distribution used to score it — because the second and third are where every disagreement between two labs on "which head matters" is actually located. (b) When a claim fails, do not widen the claim; narrow the distribution and re-run, which is exactly how this paper discovers that head 1.5 carries a repeat heuristic in addition to induction. The transferable instrument is a pair of subset scores reported side by side, since a difference between subsets is a decomposition of the mechanism rather than a loss of accuracy. Coreference `arxiv-2408.15510` (reliability as a property of the architecture pair rather than the method) and `arxiv-2502.03407` (the inference-only control corpus that separates "detects the state" from "detects the topic").
- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 502): **Sufficiency is not completeness and the paper says so in its own metric: a set of paths that is a majority of a redundant ensemble has zero average unexplained effect, so a perfect score certifies that the chosen set is enough to reproduce the behaviour and says nothing about whether the omitted paths were doing anything.** This is the sharpest available statement of a limit the folder has circled from the other side — that a working read-out is not thereby the mechanism — and it comes with the corrective arithmetic rather than a caveat: report proportion explained *and* the size of the path set, because the two together express the trade-off that the single number hides, and prefer the more parsimonious set only among sets that already score acceptably. The concrete instance here is a head that implements two behaviours at once (prefix-matched copying and context-insensitive copying), so a hypothesis naming only the first reaches 73.5% and the last 26.5% is a real second mechanism in the same component rather than noise. For our accounts the rule is that a component may appear in a path set twice under two different roles, and any account that assigns one role per component is asserting an exclusive-function claim it has not tested. Coreference `arxiv-2512.18792` (overdetermination: a working read-out is not the mechanism) and `arxiv-2610.21261` (the order-1 residual as the price of assuming parts compose additively).
- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 502): **The counterfactual sampler is a control, not a nuisance, and making it a designed choice buys a dissociation no ablation can produce: for prompts of the form "The organization estimates that [N]-", corrupting the input of heads 5.6 and 6.1 drops the probability of a numeric completion from 88.1% to 82.5% and 83.9%, while patching in a different number leaves it at 88.0% and 88.3% with far smaller KL — so those heads read "is this a number" and the patch proves they do not carry the value itself.** A single-sided ablation would have shown the same heads as important in both cases; only the pair separates use from detection. Three habits transfer. (i) Every intervention row states its counterfactual distribution explicitly, and prefers a same-type swap (another number, another noun, another ordering) over noise or mean ablation precisely because it keeps the patched model on the data manifold. (ii) Where a claim separates into "recognises the property" and "carries the value", run both arms and report the dissociation rather than a single importance score. (iii) Treat the ordering of methods on one behaviour as a fact about their counterfactual samplers first: this paper's three regimes rank the same heads differently, and the paper honestly concedes that without ground truth it cannot say which map is closer to the true mechanism. Coreference `arxiv-2408.15510` (completeness and selectivity as the two-number certificate) and `arxiv-2505.14685` (an intervention whose predicted output belongs to neither the original nor the counterfactual).

- **Substance**: the contribution is *ground truth for the property every causal entry in this folder assumes*. Runs 498-509 built a wall of warnings that a successful intervention may not have used the model's mechanism (RAVEL's Iso, HyperDAS's housekeeping, `2603.18353`'s disrupted column, the Makelov illusion) — and each of them had to argue the point, because nobody could score it. Planting pathways and switching them off turns it into an AUROC. The paper's own headline — that site-level distance is *worse than chance* at the one task that matters — is the cheapest refutation of the folder's most common diagnostic habit, and the restricted-DAS result (deny the genuine subspace and the optimiser simply routes through the planted one, at 100% pathway share on GPT-2) is the Makelov illusion reproduced as a controlled measurement at four scales.

- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 510): **Score the claim downstream of the address you edited — where the representation went is a fact about the edit, and whether the network used it is a fact about the computation after it.** The mechanism is clean and reusable: clamp every downstream MLP neuron to the range it occupies in natural runs *that produce the same output*, and ask how much of the decision margin disappears. That one move separates "unusual activity" from "activity the decision depends on", and it is the difference between a measure that is below chance in this benchmark (0.21-0.46 for nearest-neighbour and local-PCA distance on the gender task, for every model and pathway family) and one that reaches 0.82-1.00. Two rules follow for our batteries. First, **every patch, alignment or steering result we publish carries a downstream-dependence number, not just a success rate and a site distance**, because a site distance cannot see the difference this paper is about and the folder has been quoting them as reassurance. Second, **when we report a null ("the model is innocent"), bound the detector with a positive control** — here the same statistic catches 80-94% of wrong-mechanism successes against unit-visible pathways but at most 2.6% against in-range ones, so the natural-model null in §6.4 is only as strong as that column says. Coreference `arxiv-2603.18353` (corrected and disrupted counts, the measurement-side twin) and `arxiv-2503.19783` (the retention class fixed at the same time as the edit).

- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 510): **An optimiser that is free to choose its intervention direction will find the shortest path to the answer, and the shortest path may be a path the model never walks — so a subspace method's success is evidence only after it is denied the subspace you claim.** This is the folder's Makelov illusion (`arxiv-2311.17030`), and the value here is that it is quantified: on the gender task DAS trained on a pathway-equipped model routes most of its successes through the planted path at every scale, restricted DAS — the top-32 site components and the genuine DAS direction excluded — still reports 8-26% success on GPT-2 and essentially all of it pathway-dominated, and a differentiable on-manifold penalty cuts the *unrestricted* share from near-total to under 5% while leaving the *restricted* variant's residual successes almost entirely pathway-dominated. The mechanical rule for us: **every fitted intervention ships with a restricted variant that removes the structure it claims, a pathway-share column for its successes, and an explicit statement that a restricted-subspace result is not trustworthy even after mitigation.** This is the anti-target problem one level above RAVEL (which asked whether an intervention moves what it claims) — the question here is whether it got there the way the model would. Coreference `arxiv-2503.10894` (constrain the shape at test and print the unconstrained number beside it) and `arxiv-2605.31317` (a fit that is exact where it was constrained and unconstrained everywhere else).

- Pattern 2026-11-20 (run 510): **Build the ground truth by construction, not by argument — plant the thing you are trying to detect, keep it provably inert on natural inputs, and then every candidate detector becomes a scored number instead of a position in a dispute.** The signature move is worth copying exactly: the pathway is a ReLU whose threshold sits just above the maximum the direction reaches on all benchmark prompts, so silence is *by construction and asserted per configuration*, model behaviour is unchanged, and removal gives an exact per-intervention label. Two guards they add are the transferable part. The *in-range family* — drive over 128 neurons, each clipped inside its natural range so only the combination is anomalous — is what stops the detector from being an artefact of the construction, and it is precisely where every method degrades (0.39 on Qwen2.5-7B gender, nothing reliably above chance). And the paper is honest that three of four families are visible by construction, so their near-perfect scores are an upper bound rather than a reliability claim. For our own work: **when we cannot get ground truth, construct a model in which we can, and always include the family that is hardest for the detector we are proposing** — a benchmark whose easy cases are easy is a sanity check, and saying so in the table is what makes the hard case credible.
